title: fix(conformance): namespace stuck in terminating — svc-latency hang blocks full conformance run
description:
A full conformance run started 2026-06-11 14:26 UTC hung indefinitely (8+ hours). The svc-latency-6252 namespace is still present and stuck Terminating in the cluster after the run was aborted. This blocks every future full conformance run from completing — sonobuoy waits for namespace cleanup before reporting results.

Root cause hypothesis: the Service or Endpoint object in the svc-latency namespace has a stuck finalizer, or the namespace controller's drain logic is not completing (similar to prior teardown hangs fixed in #508). The namespace DELETE handler must drain all objects and clear the namespace finalizer; if any subresource (e.g. Endpoints, Service with finalizer, or a watch stream that never closes) blocks the drain, the namespace stays Terminating forever.

Observed: namespace svc-latency-6252 present in cluster after 8+ hour hang. No log output from the svc-latency test in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log — sonobuoy was blocked waiting when log was extracted.

Acceptance criteria: a full conformance run (or focused run covering sig-network Services) completes without hanging; the svc-latency namespace is fully deleted within 2 minutes of test teardown.
notes:
Root cause: 3 of 201 services never got EndpointSlices. KCM EPS controller POSTed their EPS (tracker recorded it) but the ADDED watch event was never delivered back to the KCM's global EPS watch stream. After 15 retries at up to 1000s backoff the controller gave up (StaleSlices check). Test watches endpointslices waiting for all 201 ready endpoints — never completes. Watch event delivery miss under burst load (249 rapid EPS creates) is the root cause. Fix: reliable watch event delivery — likely same channel-buffer issue as mayor-p97u.
PR #515 merged: global bookmark race fixed. Rebuild and rerun svc-latency to confirm.
close_reason: svc-latency conformance test passes 20/20 after PR #515 + #516 (watch dedup race fixes). No services missing EndpointSlices.

title: delete_pod soft-delete path has no retry-on-conflict, races kubelet status writes -> spurious 409 (CSIInlineVolumes conformance)
description:
Conformance run temp/e2e/0723-2104-conformance: [sig-storage] CSIInlineVolumes should support
CSIVolumeSource in Pod API fails at csi_inline.go:136 -- client.Delete(ctx, name, DeleteOptions{})
(no Preconditions, no resourceVersion) returns 409 resource version mismatch.

Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs delete_pod's soft-delete branch (lines ~903-908)
reads the pod once, then writes it back once via store.put with expected_rv from that single read
-- no retry loop. If a concurrent writer (kubelet's routine pod-status PATCH) lands between the
read and the write, the CAS fails and the 409 is surfaced directly to the client, even though the
client never asked for any resourceVersion precondition.

Compare to patch_pod (same file, ~line 944) which already has an infinite retry-on-conflict loop
for exactly this scenario (added in commit 1d4ec948 for a KCM finalizer-removal race). Real
kube-apiserver's generic registry Delete retries its own internal optimistic-concurrency CAS on
conflict; a client with bare DeleteOptions{} should never see a 409 for a write it did not
precondition on.

Fix: give delete_pod's soft-delete write (and check the hard-delete path too) the same
retry-on-RevisionMismatch loop that patch_pod already has.

Deterministic in-process reproduction (not committed, was reverted after use): 8 concurrent
get+put tasks simulating kubelet status-sync racing a single delete_pod call against an in-memory
SqliteStore -- fails with 409 on first run, matching the production symptom exactly. See
ai/findings/0723-2104-conformance-2-failures-triage.md (gitignored, in worker agent-a66173f73aec60128's
worktree) in mayor-rqyit for full evidence, live apiserver.log timestamps, and file:line citations.

Cross-ref: mayor-rqyit (audit bead that found this).
close_reason: PR #882 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/882 — delete_pod's soft-delete write now retries on RevisionMismatch (same pattern as patch_pod's 1d4ec948 loop) instead of surfacing a 409 to a client that specified no resourceVersion precondition. Hard-delete and delete_collection_pods confirmed not needing the fix (already pass expected_revision=None). Permanent regression test added with fail-on-revert proof. Live focus rerun passed on lima-node-2.

title: JSON Patch replace on array index inserts instead of overwriting (RFC 6902 violation)
description:
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs:984-999 (json_patch_set, used by the
"replace" op in apply_json_patch at line 774): the array branch calls
arr.insert(idx, value), which shifts existing elements right and grows the array.
RFC 6902 "replace" on an existing index must overwrite in place (same length).

Live-reproduced in complete isolation (no CRDs, no webhooks, no full suite):
  kubectl apply an EndpointSlice with endpoints[0].addresses: ["9.9.9.9"]
  kubectl patch --type=json -p=[{op:replace,path:/endpoints/0/addresses/0,value:8.8.8.8}]
  result: ["8.8.8.8","9.9.9.9"]  <- should be ["8.8.8.8"]

This is the confirmed root cause of a NEW conformance failure in
temp/e2e/0723-1535-conformance: [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI
"works for multiple CRDs of different groups" (crd_publish_openapi.go:301),
"dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout" polling /openapi/v2 through the default
kubernetes Service ClusterIP.

Mechanism: scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:606-634 corrects the seeded
kubernetes/default EndpointSlice's loopback placeholder (127.0.0.1) to the real
VM gateway IP via a JSON-patch "replace" on endpoints[0].addresses[0]. That patch
section re-runs unconditionally on every stack reconnect (every run-all.sh
invocation), and because "replace" inserts instead of overwriting, the array
grows by one duplicate of the correct address on every reconnect while the
original dead 127.0.0.1 entry is pushed to the tail and NEVER removed. Live-
confirmed unbounded growth on lima-node-4 across 4 reconnects:
  ["192.168.104.2","192.168.104.2","192.168.104.2","192.168.104.2","127.0.0.1"]
  -> one more duplicate added per subsequent reconnect.

kube-proxy's IPVS table for 10.96.0.1:443 currently programs only ONE real server
(addresses[0], which happens to be correct on this topology) -- so the dead
127.0.0.1 entry is not currently live-routed on a single-node VM, which is why 2/2
isolated --focus reruns of the failing test both passed cleanly. This is exactly
why "passes in isolation" must NOT be read as "flake" here: the full 446-spec run's
random contention apparently hit a window (possibly HA-address rotation, a
different reconcile ordering, or a proxier that consumes more than addresses[0])
where the dead entry actually got scheduled, producing the i/o timeout.

Blast radius is broad: this bug affects ANY client (including plain
kubectl patch --type=json) doing "replace" on an existing array element anywhere
in the API surface -- not just this one EndpointSlice. Fix: json_patch_set's array
branch must overwrite (arr[idx] = value) for "replace", distinct from
json_patch_add's insert semantics; also reject idx == arr.len() (no
"replace past the end" per RFC 6902). Needs a new unit test covering "replace" on
an existing array index (json_patch.rs currently has 24 test fns, none cover this).

Cross-ref: mayor-lespk (audit bead that found this).
Findings doc (gitignored, worker worktree only):
ai/findings/0723-1535-crd-webhook-failures-triage.md
close_reason: PR #878 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/878 - json_patch_set array branch now overwrites in place for replace, rejects idx==len; regression tests + live sanity check on lima-node-5 confirm fix

title: fix(store): read-after-write returns STALE object version on status-subresource updates — KCM rejects 158x/run (read version N not as new as written N+1) for RC/StatefulSet/DaemonSet, causing controller retry-churn (root cause of DS-rollback pgm5q.10)
notes:
--- MY (MAYOR) FRAMING REFUTED by diagnose scout 2026-07-22 (agent-a71d7479a9cea65ff) ---
Full detail: ai/findings/stale-read-after-write-rootcause-2026-07-22.md.
This bead's premise -- "u7s serves a STALE read over the wire on status-subresource writes" -- is WRONG. Refuted two ways: (1) a genuine file-backed concurrent stress test (300 status put+get cycles, 16 noise writers, 4000 writes) found ZERO staleness; the store read-your-writes guard is correct and status writes DO bump last_written_revision (sqlite.rs:365, via the same put/put_sync as every write). (2) kcm -v=6 shows the failing "sync" completes in 5-13 MICROSECONDS with ZERO apiserver GET/LIST in the window (apiserver.log cross-checked) -- physically cannot contain a network read. The "read version N not as new as N+1" is KCM's OWN informer/Lister cache lagging its OWN write by microseconds (client-go re-enqueues the parent when the write's child-pod create/delete echoes back through KCM's Pod informer, racing the watch echo). KCM logs it as "requeuing" and self-heals. This is normal upstream client-side behavior, NOT a u7s store/apiserver data bug. The 158 log lines are benign noise for RC/StatefulSet.
ORIGIN of the wrong theory: sqlite.rs:1567 test + the wal_autocheckpoint comment (sqlite.rs:250-257) bake this unproven "stale WAL read -> KCM requeues 15min" causal claim into the code as if established; that's where I (and the bead) got it. A future store-touching worker should NOT trust that comment; consider correcting it.

STATUS: reframing, NOT the DS-rollback root cause. Do NOT pursue a store fix. The scout kept a valid guard-regression test (get_after_status_put_returns_the_written_revision_not_a_stale_one) on branch worker/agent-a71d7479a9cea65ff (origin) -- a future store PR can absorb it; it guards a DIFFERENT (real, future) stale-read regression, passes today.

REMAINING OPEN (the scout explicitly did NOT resolve this): WHY does DS-rollback (pgm5q.10) still deterministically fail / delete a pod that should survive? Not the store guard; not an HTTP stale read. Live alternative NOT ruled out: u7s watch-DELIVERY latency (a different subsystem) keeping KCM's cache stale LONGER than real etcd would, making a normally-rare informer-race deterministic on u7s. Nobody has traced the actual pod-deletion decision in the DS rollback, nor checked whether this test fails on real kube-apiserver under the same load. That is the next experiment. Removing the ce71n->.10 blocks link since ce71n as framed is not the cause.
close_reason: Premise refuted by diagnose scout (ai/findings/stale-read-after-write-rootcause-2026-07-22.md): NOT a u7s store/apiserver stale-read bug. Store read-your-writes guard is correct (file-backed concurrent stress test = 0 staleness; status writes bump last_written_revision via normal put_sync). The 'read version N not as new as N+1' is KCM's OWN informer cache lagging its own write by microseconds (kcm -v=6: failing sync = 5-13us, zero apiserver GET/LIST in-window) — benign client-go self-healing behavior, not a u7s data bug. My original framing was wrong. The still-OPEN question (why DS-rollback deletes a pod that should survive) moved back to pgm5q.10; a watch-DELIVERY-latency angle remains unexamined but is NOT this store-fix bead. A valid guard-regression test was banked on branch worker/agent-a71d7479a9cea65ff for a future store PR to absorb.

title: fix(conformance): --reset must recreate extra node(s) too — stale pre-user-v2 extra VM is silently reused, breaking inter-node routes (Nexthop has invalid gateway)
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (operator-hit 2026-07-22, run temp/e2e/0722-1049-failure.log). Command: `run-all.sh --reset --extra-node lima-node-3 --extra-kubelet-port 10261` (defaults: primary lima-node:6443:10250). Failed at the final inter-node routing step (added by #869/pgm5q.12): Routing lima-node-3 -> 10.85.0.0/24 via 192.168.104.6 (lima-node) Error: Nexthop has invalid gateway. MECHANISM: `--reset` (reset.sh) only tears down + recreates the PRIMARY VM. The primary (lima-node) was recreated FRESH → picked up #869's `networks: - lima: user-v2` → eth0=192.168.104.6, cni0=10.85.0.1/24 (correct). But `add-node.sh`→`lima-start.sh` REUSED the pre-existing lima-node-3 ('VM already running', 'CNI bridge pod subnet already 10.85.1.0/24 skipping rewrite') — that VM was created BEFORE #869, so it never got the user-v2 stanza (Lima applies `networks:` only at VM CREATION). Verified live: lima-node-3 eth0=192.168.5.15/24 (OLD default usernet, NO user-v2 iface), cni0=10.85.0.1/16 (still flat /16, crio never restarted on it). So `ip route replace 10.85.0.0/24 via 192.168.104.6` run FROM node-3 fails — node-3 has no interface on 192.168.104.x, gateway unreachable. This is EXACTLY the VM-reuse trap the networking scout flagged (ai/findings/two-node-cross-node-networking-2026-07-22.md §5: '--reset only resets the primary --vm; the extra node is left as-is if it already exists'). #869's routing LOGIC is correct (verified on 2 freshly-provisioned VMs); the gap is that stale extra-node reuse is silent + then fails cryptically. FIX (worker to verify on live stack; lima-node-3 is genuinely stale RIGHT NOW = perfect repro): - Primary approach: make `--reset` ALSO delete the extra node(s) named on the same command line (`--extra-node `), so they get freshly provisioned with the current lima/kubelet.yaml network config. reset.sh currently only knows the primary --vm; it must learn the --extra-node value(s) (run-all.sh passes --reset + --extra-node together, so the info is available — thread it through). - Defense-in-depth: lima-start.sh/add-node.sh should detect a stale/mismatched extra node (missing user-v2 iface OR cni0 still /16 OR eth0 not on 192.168.104.x) and either recreate it or FAIL LOUD with a clear message ('extra node predates the user-v2 network config; delete it and re-run'), NOT silently reuse it and fail later at `ip route`. - Single-node path (no --extra-node) must be unaffected. --reset with no extra node behaves exactly as today. VERIFY: with the CURRENTLY-STALE lima-node-3, run `run-all.sh --reset --vm --port

--kubelet-port --extra-node lima-node-3 --extra-kubelet-port 10261` and confirm (a) node-3 gets recreated/recovered onto user-v2 (eth0 on 192.168.104.x, cni0 = its /24), (b) the inter-node routing step SUCCEEDS both directions (no 'Nexthop has invalid gateway'), (c) cross-node pod wget works both ways. This is the operator's exact command shape — it must succeed after the fix.
close_reason: PR #872 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/872 — reset.sh now recreates --extra-node VM(s), lima-start.sh fails loud on stale/mismatched extra-node reuse. Verified live: BEFORE Nexthop error, AFTER both routing directions succeed + cross-node pod HTTP connectivity confirmed both ways (netexec /dial, bypassing the separate mayor-39z0k exec-proxy bug). Single-node no-regress passed. cargo test/clippy green.

title: fix(apiserver): filter_pods_by_field_selector only handles spec.nodeName — silently ignores status.phase!=Failed/Succeeded (what listDaemonPods sends) and all other field selectors
notes:
PROMOTED P2->P1 on 2026-07-23: this is the CONFIRMED root cause of the DS-rollback conformance failure (mayor-pgm5q.10), not a deferrable nicety. Proven by a 5th scout + mayor code-read; full detail ai/findings/ds-rollback-terminal-phase-2026-07-23.md.
BUG: pods.rs:90-112 pod_matches_field_selector recognizes ONLY spec.nodeName; status.phase (and every other selectable field) falls through "Unknown fields: ignore (don't filter out)" (lines 102, 107). So listDaemonPods's fieldSelector=status.phase!=Failed,status.phase!=Succeeded (daemon_set.go:475 & :509) is a COMPLETE NO-OP — the LIST returns every label-matching pod regardless of phase, incl. Failed/Succeeded terminating pods, until physical hard-delete. LIVE PROOF: two LISTs 196ms & 384ms after a pod's phase was durably Failed, under status.phase!=Failed, both returned it WITH "phase":"Failed" in the body. Fresh data, not staleness — the filter simply isn't applied.
WHY IT MATTERS: real k8s kubelet drives a terminating pod to Failed/Succeeded before removal (SyncTerminatingPod->getPhase podIsTerminal=true) and canBeDeleted GATES the hard-delete on terminal phase — so upstream a status.phase!=Failed LIST deterministically excludes a terminating pod for the ~hundreds-of-ms before it's deleted. u7s persists phase=Failed correctly (~100us) but never USES it to filter, so DS-rollback existingPods membership is pure hard-delete-vs-poll luck (explains the PASS/FAIL A/B exactly).
FIX: add a status.phase case to pod_matches_field_selector (read pod.status.phase, handle = and !=) mirroring the spec.nodeName pattern. Fail-on-revert test in field_selector_tests (pods.rs:1401+): a status.phase=Failed pod + selector status.phase!=Failed,!=Succeeded must be EXCLUDED (currently INCLUDED = the bug); a Running pod must be INCLUDED. Name the assertion for impact (rollout controllers rely on phase-exclusion to know a terminating pod is gone pre-removal).
SCOPE: this bead needs ONLY status.phase to fix pgm5q.10. Upstream also selects on status.podIP/spec.restartPolicy/spec.serviceAccountName/spec.schedulerName/status.nominatedNodeName — same missing-case gap likely affects those; FILE A FOLLOW-UP for the rest, do NOT scope-creep this fix.
VERIFY: after fix, --focus "should rollback without unnecessary restarts" on a 2-node stack passes (was pure-luck flaky). Blocks mayor-pgm5q.10.
close_reason: PR #877 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/877 — status.phase arm added to pod_matches_field_selector; fail-on-revert test confirmed; --focus should rollback without unnecessary restarts PASSED (1 Passed, 0 Failed) on 2-node lima-node-4/lima-node-5. Follow-up mayor-6n3dp filed for remaining selectors.

title: fix(conformance): two-node cluster has no cross-node pod networking — 24 full-suite failures (empty PodCIDR, shared InternalIP 192.168.5.15, no inter-node route)
notes:
--- SPIKE RESULT 2026-07-22 (agent-a73b82ba604795967, throwaway lima-spike-a/-b) ---
DECISION RESOLVED: Option A (user-v2) is VIABLE and UNPRIVILEGED. The whole networking fix needs NO operator host action.
Proven: two Lima VMs each with `networks: - lima: user-v2` share ONE switch, mutually reachable. Ping A<->B 0% loss (0.3-0.7ms); TCP nc to sshd:22 succeeds BOTH directions. user-v2 is mode:user-v2, gw 192.168.104.1, /24, NO socket_vmnet/sudoers dependency. So Option B (shared+socket_vmnet) is NOT needed — do NOT ask operator for a host install.
IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT from spike: it set user-v2 as the ONLY network → VM's sole iface came up on the user-v2 subnet AS eth0 (no default 192.168.5.x usernet at all). For the REAL conformance VMs the fix must decide: does user-v2 REPLACE or get ADDED ALONGSIDE the existing default usernet? Current stack binds host port-forwards (apiserver 6443/644x, kubelet ports) and konnectivity/iptables (192.168.5.2) against the default usernet — so the fix worker MUST verify on a live stack whether adding user-v2 as a 2nd network (keeping default) vs replacing it keeps the primary node's existing single-node connectivity intact. Get this wrong = break the primary.

READY TO FIX. Both gaps unprivileged: (a) user-v2 for reachability + fix lima-start.sh:246 wrong iface (lima0→eth0), (b) per-node /24 conflist rewrite + idempotent inter-node routes. Fix bead being formed.

title: DaemonSet rollback conformance test fails: apiserver pod LIST appears to return an already-deleted pod, later flagged as 'unexpectedly restarted'
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-pgm5q.6 (2-node conformance gate) on a live 2-node lima cluster (lima-node-2 primary :6444/:10251, lima-node-3 companion :10261), current main (post #867 scheduler matchFields fix + #868 two-node infra). [sig-apps] Daemon set [Serial] should rollback without unnecessary restarts [Conformance] FAILS deterministically (not the target [sig-architecture] untainted-nodes test, which PASSES). Full junit_01.xml + e2e.log manually retrieved (sonobuoy tarball pulled directly off the VM's kubelet pod-volume dir, bypassing a separate kubectl-logs proxy issue — see mayor-sqzk, which recurred during this same session and is a distinct, already-tracked problem). FAILING ASSERTION (test source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apps/daemon_set.go:448-519, release-1.36): [FAILED] unexpected pod daemon-set-6a67b be restarted In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apps/daemon_set.go:516 TEST ALGORITHM (exact, from source): 1. Create RollingUpdate DaemonSet with image=agnhost:2.63.0. Confirm 1 pod per node (2 nodes here) — THIS PART WORKS: KCM DaemonSet controller + u7s scheduler correctly placed one pod per node (log: 'Number of running nodes: 2, number of available pods: 2' — the #867 matchFields fix is NOT implicated in this failure). 2. Patch DS image to a nonexistent image 'foo:non-existent' (deliberately unpullable, so the rollout stalls before completing). 3. Poll until >=1 pod shows the new (bad) image (checkAtLeastOneNewPod). 4. Immediately List ALL daemon pods and bucket by container image into existingPods (still old image) vs newPods (new/bad image). With >=2 nodes this snapshot is EXPECTED to have both non-empty (RollingUpdate touches nodes one at a time). 5. Roll back the DS to the original image; wait for rollback to fully complete (checkDaemonPodsImageAndAvailability). 6. List ALL daemon pods again. For every pod name captured in existingPods (step 4), assert it is STILL PRESENT by name in the post-rollback list. If not -> Fail 'unexpected pod %s be restarted'. OBSERVED TIMELINE (from KCM/daemonset-controller events, all within ~10s): 15:00:35 initial pods created: daemon-set-55f75 -> lima-node-3, daemon-set-6a67b -> lima-node-2 15:00:37 DS patched to bad image; controller deletes daemon-set-6a67b (lima-node-2's pod) 15:00:39 controller creates daemon-set-d7474 (bad image, replacing 6a67b on lima-node-2) 15:00:39 rollback patch applied; controller deletes daemon-set-d7474 immediately (never became Ready) 15:00:44 controller creates daemon-set-f8bd2 (old image again, lima-node-2) daemon-set-55f75 (lima-node-3) is NEVER touched throughout. The failure says pod 'daemon-set-6a67b' (lima-node-2's ORIGINAL pod, already deleted by 15:00:37 per controller events) was found in the test's `existingPods` snapshot (step 4) — i.e. present with the OLD image — even though by the time `checkAtLeastOneNewPod` returned true (>=15:00:39, 2s later) the real store state should already show 6a67b gone and only 55f75 (untouched) + d7474 (new pod) present. If the apiserver's List response included a pod already deleted ~2s earlier, `listDaemonPods`'s existingPods snapshot would wrongly include 6a67b, and it would correctly be reported 'restarted' once really gone by the final list (rollbackPods = {55f75, f8bd2}, missing 6a67b). HYPOTHESIS (unconfirmed — needs dedicated repro, NOT root-caused here): a store/List read-consistency gap under concurrent 2-node writes, returning a stale (already-deleted) pod in a plain `GET /api/v1/namespaces//pods` list call. Live repro DONE (sanctioned alt: hardcoded preempt_and_pick_node main.rs:86-123
to force-fail for one named pod, bypassing find_preemption_plan; removed

preemptor(prio=1e6,cpu=1) on single 8-CPU node -> FailedScheduling "no node
still fits after preemption, even after retrying (capacity kept being

8 CPU) + churn pod create/delete -> preemptor stayed Pending 72s, ZERO new
scheduler.log lines for it, status.conditions frozen at pod-creation-time
default (PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable) the whole time. A manual
`kubectl label` (real MODIFIED event) on the SAME pod immediately
re-triggered pick_node -> bound successfully. Proves the watch CAN
retrigger scheduling but nothing besides an external edit does so today.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE GAP: needs_scheduling (lib.rs:315) fires only on

Event (main.rs:401-424), never patches the pod's own status, so no

NOT a re-list -- it replays one GLOBAL ring buffer of the last
RING_CAPACITY=1000 writes across ALL resource types (sqlite.rs:9), which
rotates out any one stale pod's event within seconds/minutes of real
churn -- long before the next forced reconnect (watch.rs max_duration
30min default, raised from 5min specifically by mayor-0ka1z to REDUCE

temp/research/scheduling_queue.go + unschedulable_pods.go @release-1.36:

(a), not (b). (b) only patches preempt_and_pick_node's call site and isn't

-- tokio::spawn a loop { sleep(30s); GET /api/v1/pods; wrap each item as

preemption atomicity, lafgk's event emission, or 0ka1z's timeouts.

title: scheduler preemption is 100 percent broken after the NodeTally refactor in PR 834 -- pick_node never returns NoCapacity so the preemption arm is never entered, scheduler binds preemptor pods directly onto full nodes and the kubelet rejects them
notes:
ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (Scout B + mayor code-read 2026-07-17, HIGH confidence it is real; exact line TBD by worker via live repro). Conformance run 0716-2043: ALL 4 SchedulerPreemption tests fail. Scout B smoking gun: the string preempting -- emitted ONLY on a real preemption at scheduler main.rs:286 -- appears ZERO times in the entire 2188-line scheduler.log across the whole 2h09m run. Zero preemptions happened. The scheduler binds preemptor pods DIRECTLY onto full nodes; the KUBELET then rejects them: junit sched-preemption-7103 Pod was rejected: Node didnt have enough resource: scheduling.k8s.io/foo, requested: 2, used: 4, capacity: 5 at 11:42:27.7Z. So the schedulers own in-memory NodeTally told pick_node the full node had room; pick_node returned Ok(node) instead of Err(NoCapacity); the preemption arm at main.rs:278-286 was never entered.

REGRESSION LINEAGE: preemption was confirmed GREEN right after rsei (commit 4892cc40, sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPreemption all 4 pass) and lb60u (PR #832, 24/25). PR #834 (NodeTally refactor) merged AFTER both and replaced the fit-check plumbing, but #834s own validation only re-ran SchedulerPredicates + manual cpu-based kubectl checks -- it NEVER re-ran SchedulerPreemption. This is the validation gap that let it ship.

MAYOR CODE-READ REFINEMENT of Scout Bs no-lock-spans-the-sequence theory: there IS a Mutex<NodeTally> (lib.rs:1390) -- pick_node locks it (lib.rs:1399 usage_by_node), find_preemption_plan locks it (lib.rs:1480), assume_and_bind locks it (main.rs:47). The lock IS dropped between pick_node (decide) and assume_and_bind (commit), a real TOCTOU -- BUT a cross-lock race would cause OCCASIONAL mis-scheduling, NOT 100 percent preemption failure with zero preempting lines EVER. 100pct-categorical points to a TALLY ACCOUNTING bug, not a race: pick_node is succeeding when it must fail. PRIMARY SUSPECT: the fit check does not compare tally usage against node capacity for the EXTENDED/scalar resource scheduling.k8s.io/foo. NodeTally sums requests via sum_container_requests and tracks pod_count in usage_by_node (lib.rs:925-934); if NodeUsage/ResourceRequests/sum_container_requests only track cpu+memory (+pod_count) and DROP extended resources, every preemption test -- which gates on a synthetic extended resource scheduling.k8s.io/foo precisely to force a full node deterministically -- would see phantom room, bind directly, never preempt. THAT matches the kubelet error resource name exactly. Worker: check sum_container_requests + ResourceRequests + NodeUsage + select_node_with_capacity/pick_node fit math for extended-resource handling FIRST; the cross-lock TOCTOU (assume released before next pick_node) SECOND.

NOT a dupe of mayor-7xr09 (that is find_preemption_plans GET-error typing; here pick_node never returns Err at all). Independent of the namespace-hang beads (74j3.6/.7).

REPRO (live --stack-only): patch a node to add capacity of a fake extended resource e.g. example.com/fakecpu=1 (or use scheduling.k8s.io/foo like the test); create a filler pod that requests all of it (bound, Running); create a higher-priority pod requesting the same resource; watch scheduler.log for preempting and watch whether the filler is evicted. EXPECT (pre-fix): no preempting line, higher-prio pod bound directly, kubelet rejects. Also probe the TOCTOU: fire two same-size fillers <10ms apart and see if the tally double-books. 

VERIFY (fix): the repro above shows a preempting line + the filler evicted + the high-prio pod scheduled; PLUS a fail-on-revert Rust unit test on the tally/fit math (e.g. usage_by_node or the fit predicate must report a node at extended-resource capacity as FULL). Final gate: sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPreemption -- all 4 pass, read from podlogs/sonobuoy/.../logs/e2e.txt.

Fixed both; all 5 [Conformance]-tagged SchedulerPreemption tests pass live via sonobuoy --focus.

title: fix apiserver delete_namespace persists Terminating phase AFTER running the drain cascade, opening a check-then-act race that wedges namespaces in Terminating until the 15min watchdog
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in-code by mayor 2026-07-17, HIGH confidence). Conformance run 0716-2043: FIVE ordinary test namespaces stuck phase=Terminating for 15min each, force-deleted by watchdog: job-347, replicaset-4445, endpointslice-4063, container-probe-726, secrets-8608. Test families: job=apps/job.go, replicaset=apps/replica_set.go, endpointslice=network/endpointslice.go, container-probe=common/node/container_probe.go, secrets=common/{storage/secrets_volume,node/secrets}.go.

MECHANISM: delete_namespace at namespaces.rs:1003-1027 -- when spec.finalizers becomes empty it runs cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable at line 1008 BEFORE persisting status.phase=Terminating to the store, which only happens at line 1017. The phase=Terminating is set in the in-memory soft value at 982-986 but NOT written until 1017. Meanwhile create_namespaced_resource gates creation on the STORED phase at resource.rs:1441. So during the entire cascade the stored namespace still looks live, KCM controllers race objects in (proven: replicaset-4445 POST pods 201 at 10:53:04.071616Z, 4ms before its own DELETE 200 at 10:53:04.075879Z; job-347 kcm.log serviceaccounts_controller.go:187 unable to create new content in namespace job-347 because it is being terminated). Racy creates are invisible to the cascade LIST snapshot. After MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 (namespaces.rs:814) burns out, cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable returns true via line 828 comment Objects kept reappearing across every retry -- SAME true it returns at line 819 for a genuine finalizer-blocked object. delete_namespace then persists Terminating and waits for maybe_finalize_terminating_namespace at 842-893, which ONLY re-fires when a real child finalizer clears (pods.rs:855 / resource.rs:789). None of these 5 had a real finalizer, so nothing re-checks. Wedged until the 15min watchdog PATCH trips patch_namespace weaker hard-delete at 478-485.

REGRESSION LINEAGE: direct sibling of CLOSED mayor-35zvy. That bead was the SAME two SchedulerPredicates stable-cluster-precondition failures, root-caused to a check-then-act race where a racily-created pod was orphaned when the namespace hard-deleted. Fixed by ADDING cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable in PR #769. That retry-until-stable loop is the exact mechanism now wedging namespaces instead of orphaning pods. So this is not new behavior regressing -- it is the 35zvy fix trading orphaned-pod for wedged-namespace.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD (74j3.6): close the race window so racy creates cannot slip in during the cascade. Fix direction: persist status.phase=Terminating to the store BEFORE running the cascade (flip the order of lines 1008 and 1014-1020), so resource.rs:1441 rejects controller creates for the whole drain. Verify: create_namespaced_resource must see Terminating from the first cascade pass onward.

DESIGN FORK (split to sibling bead): even with the race window closed, cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable at line 828 still conflates content-kept-racing-back with genuine-finalizer-pending, and there is no async reconciler to ever re-drive a wedged Terminating namespace. Closing the window should prevent the livelock in practice, but the retry-exhaustion=true fallback is still a latent defect if any create slips the gate. Filed separately.

VERIFY PLAN (operator-approved 2026-07-17): deterministic kubectl repro on --stack-only cluster -- create ns + a controller (RC or Job) that keeps recreating pods, delete the namespace, assert it reaches fully-deleted not stuck Terminating within seconds; PLUS a fail-on-revert Rust unit test simulating a racing create during cascade. NOT a --focus re-run of the flaky families (race is timing-dependent; a green run would not prove the fix).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #841 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/841): delete_namespace now persists status.phase=Terminating to the store BEFORE running the drain cascade (both the remaining.is_empty() branch and the external-finalizer else branch, which had the identical race). Verified live on lima-node-2: a namespace with a continuously-reconciling ReplicationController now completes deletion within seconds instead of wedging, with KCM's racing create attempts visibly rejected ("being terminated") in its own log. Two new fail-on-revert regression tests race a real create_namespaced_resource call into the namespace at the cascade's first LIST snapshot and assert 403; confirmed both fail against the pre-fix ordering. Sonobuoy --focus "ReplicaSet|Job should" was launched as the final gate but ran long due to legitimately slow Job tests (confirmed via the conformance watchdog's own Active-namespace log, unrelated to this bug) — the deterministic kubectl repro is the definitive proof per the bead's own verify plan. All quality gates green.

title: apiserver: per-node kubelet proxy addressing (logs/exec/attach on node 2)
description: Deferred from the two-node-conformance-cluster epic. Today resolve_kubelet_address (proxy.rs:62-70) short-circuits on --kubelet-preferred-address (127.0.0.1 for all nodes) and state.kubelet_port (proxy.rs:194 and 4 more sites) is a single global port, so kubectl logs/exec/attach/port-forward against a pod on the 2nd node misroutes to node 1's kubelet. Not needed for the 2 target tests (they read pod status via List, not the reverse proxy). Fix: a per-node name->host-port map threaded through AppState (VM InternalIPs 192.168.5.x are not host-routable -- the reason the port-forward hack exists).
notes:
--- FIX DESIGN + DISPATCH (mayor, 2026-07-22, per operator decision 'fix 39z0k before the full 2-node run') ---
Anchors (verified): resolve_kubelet_address (proxy.rs:62-70) + node_address (72-87). The resolution is pod -> spec.nodeName -> node object -> resolve_kubelet_address(node, preferred). Global scalars used at ~4 proxy sites: `let kp = state.kubelet_port;` (proxy.rs:194, 433, 876, and the site near 1177) and `preferred = state.kubelet_preferred_address` (167-173, 385-388, 790-793, 1177+). AppState fields: state.rs:229 kubelet_preferred_address, :233 kubelet_port (scalar). Populated from CLI: main.rs:114/121 args -> :280/281 -> state.rs:501/502.

HARD CONSTRAINT (why it's not a 1-liner): VM InternalIPs (192.168.104.x) are NOT host-routable; the apiserver reaches each kubelet via a host PORT-FORWARD to 127.0.0.1:<distinct-port> (the --kubelet-port / --extra-kubelet-port values, e.g. primary 10250, node-2 10261). So both the ADDRESS (always 127.0.0.1 via --kubelet-preferred-address) AND the PORT must be resolved PER NODE. Today state.kubelet_port is a single scalar = primary's port, so every node-2 exec/log/attach/port-forward dials the PRIMARY's kubelet forward. That's the misroute.

DECIDED CONFIG SHAPE (worker implements, does NOT redesign): add a repeatable apiserver flag `--node-kubelet-port <node-name>=<host-port>` (0..N). Thread into AppState as a map node_name -> u16. Resolution at each proxy site: look up the target pod's node_name in the map; if present use that port; ELSE fall back to the existing global state.kubelet_port (preserves single-node + primary behavior byte-for-byte). Keep --kubelet-preferred-address (127.0.0.1) as-is for the address; only the PORT needs per-node resolution (all forwards are on 127.0.0.1). Scripts: lima-start.sh/add-node.sh must pass the joining node's name=port to the apiserver — since the apiserver is already running when a node joins, prefer having add-node.sh/lima-start.sh RE-invoke or signal the apiserver with the updated map, OR (simpler) have 02-start-apiserver.sh accept the full set when known. Worker to determine the cleanest wiring given the apiserver starts BEFORE nodes join (this is the one real sub-decision; if it requires apiserver restart-on-join or a reload mechanism, worker should surface it rather than hack it).

VERIFY: on a live 2-node stack, `kubectl --kubeconfig ... logs <pod-on-node-2>` and `kubectl exec <pod-on-node-2> -- echo hi` must SUCCEED (today: websocket 1006 / NotFound). Then the --focus "Networking Granular Checks ... intra-pod communication: http" gate should PASS (it failed ONLY due to this bug). Cargo test + clippy green. Regression test: extract the per-node port resolution into a pure fn and test map-hit vs fall-back-to-global.

title: lima-start.sh: parameterize per-node collisions (--node-suffix)
description: Running lima-start.sh a 2nd time for a 2nd VM against the same apiserver collides today. Add optional --node-suffix <suffix> (default '' -> single-node path byte-identical). Parameterize: (a) konnectivity-agent Pod name -> konnectivity-agent${SUFFIX} (lima-start.sh:333) -- REQUIRED because the apiserver enforces spec.nodeName immutability (pods.rs:607, test pods.rs:2859-2874) so re-applying the same Pod with a different nodeName returns 403; (b) konnectivity-agent-certs Secret name + the Pod's secretName (lima-start.sh:311-319, 366-367); (c) kubelet serving-cert filenames kubelet-serving${SUFFIX}.{key,crt,csr} (lima-start.sh:234-236) so node 2 gets its own cert instead of the 'already exists, reusing' guard (lima-start.sh:243) handing it node 1's. No other lines change (kube-proxy SA/RBAC idempotent; EndpointSlice patch idempotent since both VMs resolve host.lima.internal to 192.168.5.2; DNAT/kube-proxy VM-scoped).
acceptance_criteria: --node-suffix '' produces byte-identical behavior to today; --node-suffix '-2' yields distinct Pod/Secret/cert names. A 2nd lima-start.sh run against the same apiserver no longer 403s on the konnectivity-agent Pod.
close_reason: PR #868 opened — lima-start.sh --node-suffix, verified live: 2nd node's konnectivity-agent Pod/Secret/cert generate distinct names, no 403

title: scheduler: honor matchFields node affinity
description: crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs NodeSelectorTerm (lib.rs:207-210) models only match_expressions, not match_fields. serde silently drops the unknown field, so node_affinity_matches (lib.rs:1261-1265) iterates an empty match_expressions and .all() over empty is vacuously true -> a matchFields-only term matches EVERY node. The upstream DaemonSet controller pins each per-node pod via nodeAffinity...nodeSelectorTerms[].matchFields on metadata.name (verified: temp/research/daemonset_util.go:173-217, release-1.36), leaving spec.nodeName empty so the scheduler binds it. Result: select_node_with_capacity (.find first name-sorted node, lib.rs:1029) puts BOTH DaemonSet pods on lima-node, none on lima-node-2 -> the DaemonSet rollback test fails before its rollback assertion. Masked today only because 1-node has one node to pick. FIX (~20 lines): add match_fields to NodeSelectorTerm; extend node_affinity_matches to AND match_fields against a synthetic {metadata.name: node_name} map reusing the existing In/NotIn/Exists/DoesNotExist logic (lib.rs:1230-1236); thread node name from the one caller node_qualifies_for_pod (lib.rs:959).
acceptance_criteria: New unit test: a matchFields-only term pinned to one node name, asserted against 2+ candidate nodes, selects exactly the pinned node AND fails when the fix is reverted (Rule 14). cargo test -p u7s-scheduler green.
close_reason: PR #867 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/867

title: fix(apiserver): CR conversion webhook called for a version-to-itself no-op, rejected by real webhooks
description:
Discovered live while verifying mayor-hjcgj (per-webhook caBundle honoring for CRD conversion). With that fix applied, the conversion webhook is now reachable and actually invoked — but the apiserver sometimes calls it for a conversion that is a no-op (requested version == the object's own stored apiVersion), which real conversion webhooks correctly reject.

Live evidence (sonobuoy --focus "CustomResourceConversionWebhook|CustomResourceFieldSelectors", 2026-07-16):
- "should be able to convert from CR v1 to CR v2" — PASSES (no storage-version change involved).
- "should be able to convert a non homogeneous list of CRs" — FAILS: "conversion webhook failed: conversion from a version to itself should not call the webhook: stable.example.com/v1" (crd_conversion_webhook.go:461)
- "CustomResourceFieldSelectors ... MUST list and watch custom resources matching the field selector" — FAILS with the identical signature at v2 (crd_selectable_fields.go:231)

ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs, 4 call sites — grep `let needs_conversion` at ~876, ~1026, ~1518, ~1664): the "does this object need conversion" check is:
    version != ctx.storage_version && ctx.conversion_webhook_client_config.is_some()
This compares the REQUESTED version against the CRD's CURRENTLY CONFIGURED storage version — not against the object's OWN actually-stored apiVersion. Both failing tests change the CRD's storage version mid-test (e.g. `alternativeAPIVersions` swaps storage from v1 to v2) after some objects were already written under the old storage version. An object written while storage=v1 (so its stored JSON has "apiVersion": ".../v1") requested again at v1 needs NO conversion (request matches the object's actual stored version) — but the check compares against the CRD's now-current storage_version (v2), sees "v1" != "v2", and wrongly invokes the webhook for a self-conversion. Real conversion webhooks (and the conformance suite's own agnhost sample webhook) explicitly detect and reject this as a client bug.

FIX DIRECTION: the check must compare the requested version against the object's own apiVersion field (read from the stored JSON, not the CRD's live storage_version setting) — conversion is needed only when they differ. This requires restructuring each of the 4 call sites to read the object (or at least peek its apiVersion) before deciding whether to call the webhook, rather than deciding from CrContext alone. All 4 sites need the same fix; check for LIST vs GET vs namespaced vs cluster-scoped variants since the fields/line numbers may drift.

Regression test: an object created while a CRD's storage version is v1, then a storage-version change to v2, then GET/LIST that object back at v1 — the conversion webhook must NOT be called (no clientConfig round-trip), and the object must be returned as-is.

Verify live with: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm <VM> --port <PORT> --kubelet-port <KUBELET_PORT> --focus "CustomResourceConversionWebhook|CustomResourceFieldSelectors" — all 3 tests should go green once this is fixed (mayor-hjcgj's caBundle fix is a prerequisite and is already merged/in-flight).
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #830, dedicated review): PASS. Single-file diff (cr.rs). object_needs_conversion correctly compares the object's OWN stored apiVersion vs the requested version (not CRD storage_version) -- the exact fix. convert_cr_list_items correctly PARTITIONS a LIST page, sending only mismatched items to the webhook and splicing results back by index -- handles the non-homogeneous-page case (mix of pre/post storage-flip objects) with an empty-set early return. All 4 call sites updated uniformly (get_cr:158, get_cr_namespaced:236 -> object_needs_conversion; list_cr:130, list_cr_namespaced:208 -> convert_cr_list_items; all 4  checks removed). Principled dead-code removal: CrContext.storage_version field + its find_crd computation + the obsolete find_crd_extracts_storage_version test all removed (it was the SOURCE of the bug, confirmed unused via build-warning + grep) -- good Rule-2 hygiene, not scope creep. 2 regression tests proven fail-on-revert. Live: 2 of 3 conversion tests now PASS (non-homogeneous-list + v1->v2); the 3rd (CustomResourceFieldSelectors) fails for a DISTINCT pre-existing reason (CR LIST hardcodes field_selector:None) filed as mayor-lshow -- correctly out of this bead's 4-call-site scope. Merging on CI green (no --admin).
close_reason: PR #830 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/830 — fixed all 4 needs_conversion call sites in cr.rs to compare against the object's own stored apiVersion instead of the CRD's live storage_version. Live-verified via kubectl (unreachable webhook trick) and sonobuoy: 2/3 target tests now pass (convert v1->v2, non-homogeneous list). 3rd test (CustomResourceFieldSelectors field-selector LIST) fails for an unrelated, pre-existing reason (field_selector hardcoded to None on CR LIST) — filed separately as mayor-lshow.

title: fix(scheduler): watch_stream has no idle timeout — a half-open pod watch silently hangs the ENTIRE scheduler indefinitely (total outage, no log signal)
description:
Found by the scheduler->apiserver glue audit (2026-07-16, findings CS7); code-verified by the mayor.

ROOT CAUSE: HyperApiClient::watch_stream (crates/kubeconfig/src/lib.rs:247-306) has NO timeout anywhere -- connect (line 253), the HTTP/1.1 handshake (255-257), send_request (277-280), and especially the body.frame().await read loop (288-303) are ALL unbounded. No TcpStream keepalive/read timeout is configured anywhere in HyperApiClient. This wrapper is the scheduler's ENTIRE pod-discovery loop: main.rs:97 does  as the top of the loop, with a 'sleep 5s, reconnect' fallback AFTER it (main.rs ~273-276).

BLAST RADIUS -- the most severe finding in the audit, worse than any of the 3 known scheduler beads: if the watch connection goes HALF-OPEN (peer stops sending frames but doesn't close the socket -- exactly the failure mode induced by the load/contention under which the other scheduler races were found), body.frame() blocks FOREVER. stream_watch_events never returns, so the 5s-reconnect fallback NEVER runs. NO pod is ever scheduled again until the scheduler process is restarted -- a silent, total, unbounded scheduler outage with no log signal beyond whatever was already printed. (Confirmed non-issues, do not re-litigate: the 410/Compacted watch path IS already tolerated by the reconnect loop; watch-redelivery double-bind is impossible because synthetic DELETED tombstones are ignored by needs_scheduling.)

FIX DIRECTION -- needs CARE, NOT a blanket wrap: a watch is intentionally long-lived, so wrapping the whole call in one tokio::time::timeout would kill HEALTHY idle watches too. Needs an IDLE-timeout that RESETS on every received frame/bookmark (e.g. tokio::time::timeout around each body.frame().await inside the loop, not around the whole stream). On idle-expiry, log + return Err so the existing reconnect loop fires. This is a DISTINCT design from a blanket request timeout -- do not copy-paste the CS10 request-timeout fix. Recommended to land in the SAME PR as the mayor-0ka1z shared-client request-timeout fix (same file crates/kubeconfig/src/lib.rs, same 'timeouts on the one shared HTTP client' theme) but flag in the PR that they are two distinct code changes, not one wrapper.

Regression test (must fail on revert): simulate a watch whose frame source stalls (no frames, socket open) and assert watch_stream returns Err after the idle timeout rather than hanging -- e.g. a mock body that never yields a frame, wrapped so the test itself times out fast if the fix is absent. Needs Lima VM smoke (scheduler restart behavior) as a secondary gate.
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #833, covers 4pctj + 0ka1z): PASS. Single-file (kubeconfig lib.rs), public API unchanged, worker ran cargo build --workspace confirming scheduler+controller-manager callers unaffected. 4pctj: read_watch_frames wraps each body.frame().await in a per-frame tokio::time::timeout that RESETS every frame -- a healthy long-lived watch never trips it; only genuine silence does. On elapse it bails -> Err -> main.rs reconnects. Also bounded the connect/handshake/send setup phase (REQUEST_TIMEOUT) since that is not long-lived. 5-min value grounded in the real 60s bookmark cadence (verified watch.rs:562). 0ka1z: total-duration 30s timeout around the whole request cycle, refactored into request_with_content_type_timeout so tests use a short value; public method delegates. Both regression tests are excellent: parameterized short inner timeout + an OUTER real-time 5s guard that fails the test loudly if the fix regresses instead of hanging cargo test forever; StalledBody (always Pending) for the watch, a real accept-then-hang TcpListener for the request; both manually verified fail-on-revert; assertion messages state the why. The two designs correctly NOT unified. Merging on CI green.
close_reason: PR #833 opened — per-frame idle timeout added to watch_stream (crates/kubeconfig/src/lib.rs)

title: fix(apiserver): CR conversion webhook client ignores per-webhook caBundle + skips konnectivity proxy — TLS handshake fails against any real conversion backend
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: THREE failures share this single root cause --
- [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceConversionWebhook 'convert a non homogeneous list of CRs' (crd_conversion_webhook.go:461, 'conversion webhook call failed: error sending request for url https://10.96.0.17:9443/crdconvert')
- [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceConversionWebhook 'convert from CR v1 to CR v2' (crd_conversion_webhook.go:402)
- [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceFieldSelectors 'MUST list and watch CRs matching the field selector' (crd_selectable_fields.go:231) -- this test internally registers a multi-version CRD WITH a conversion webhook, so it hits the identical .../crdconvert failure; it is NOT a field-selector bug.

ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:64-71, call_conversion_webhook): sends the ConversionReview via the shared GLOBAL state.webhook_client, which state.rs:375-421 builds with tls_certs_only([cluster_ca]) -- trusting ONLY the u7s cluster CA. It never reads client_config[caBundle] at all (confirmed absent from cr.rs). Upstream's conversion webhook (and these tests) ship a self-signed CA in ClientConfig.CABundle, NOT the cluster CA -- so the TLS handshake fails, surfaced by reqwest as the generic 'error sending request for url (...)' seen in all 3 logs. This makes webhook-STRATEGY CRD conversion 100% non-functional for any real backend (P1: whole feature broken, not just these tests).

FIX DIRECTION -- the correct pattern ALREADY EXISTS in the same codebase for admission webhooks: admission.rs:842-849 (build_webhook_call_client) builds a PER-CALL client pinned to webhook.client_config.ca_bundle AND routes ServiceResolved targets through state.konnectivity_proxy_addr (comment there states the exact rationale: each webhook ships its own CA; Service-based calls route through konnectivity to reach pod IPs inside the Lima VM from the Mac host). call_conversion_webhook never adopted this. Wire the same per-call caBundle-pinning + konnectivity-proxy client into the conversion path.

Needs Lima VM verification with a REAL conversion webhook backend (deploy a TLS-serving conversion webhook pod; the 3 tests exercise it). Regression test: a conversion webhook whose serving cert is signed by a caBundle != cluster CA must succeed.
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #829, dedicated review per API-adjacent stance): PASS. 3-file diff, all correct. (1) admission.rs prepare_webhook_call cleanly extracts the proven webhook_url + build_webhook_call_client pattern, correctly gating konnectivity proxy + identity on ServiceResolved vs DirectUrl -- shared-helper reuse, not a fork. (2) cr.rs deletes the entire bespoke resolve_conversion_webhook_url (which resolved Service by raw clusterIP -- unreachable from Mac host, bypassed konnectivity: a latent bug beyond the caBundle issue) and routes through the shared path. (3) apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs caBundle decode-drop fix is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the already-correct admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs:231-235 pattern (ca_bundle.filter(non-empty) -> base64 STANDARD encode). Tests proven fail-on-revert: live-TLS-round-trip with mismatched CA + extended protobuf-decode caBundle assertion; why-stating messages. HONEST PARTIAL: only CustomResourceConversionWebhook v1->v2 goes green; the other 2 blocked by a distinct self-conversion bug filed as mayor-00kan (cleanly scoped to cr.rs, independent). SENTINEL NOTE: apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs is NOT among the 6 Sentinel-covered adapters -- this decode-drop is in one of the 4 uncovered files mayor-8agr1 tracks; concrete evidence to prioritize 8agr1 (Sentinel would have caught this class at test time). Merging on CI green (no --admin).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #829 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/829). Root cause confirmed live: caBundle was never honored by the shared webhook_client, AND a sibling protobuf-decoder bug in apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs silently dropped caBundle for any CRD created via a real (protobuf-default) client. Both fixed. Live-verified: CustomResourceConversionWebhook 'convert from CR v1 to CR v2' now passes end-to-end. The other 2 tests in the original report now fail for a distinct, newly-exposed bug (unnecessary self-conversion calls) — filed as mayor-00kan.

title: fix(apiserver): delete_pods_owned_by (RC/DS/STS/RS/Job foreground cascade) hard-deletes dependents that still have another live owner
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: [sig-api-machinery] Garbage collector 'should not delete dependents that have both valid owner and owner that is waiting for dependents' FAILS 'expected 25 pods, got 0' (garbage_collector.go:803). This is mayor-ftkl PANIC-4, reproduced live 2026-07-16 on lima-node-4.

ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs ~2808-2852): delete_pods_owned_by is invoked for RC/DaemonSet/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet/Job cascades whenever DeleteOptions.is_explicit_cascade() (resource.rs:2175-2181 for RC). It matches any pod whose ownerReferences contains the deleted owner's uid+kind and UNCONDITIONALLY hard-deletes it -- it never checks whether the pod has ANOTHER live owner. Live repro: created rc-to-be-deleted (4 replicas) + rc-to-stay (0 replicas), patched 2 of 4 pods to add rc-to-stay as a 2nd ownerReference, then kubectl delete rc rc-to-be-deleted --cascade=foreground -> ALL 4 pods deleted, incl the 2 that should have survived via their live 2nd owner. This silently destroys live, still-owned pods -- a systemic correctness risk beyond this one test since the same helper backs every workload cascade.

FIX DIRECTION: the correct per-reference-stripping logic ALREADY EXISTS and works: strip_owner_from_resources (resource.rs ~2725), currently used only by the orphan path orphan_owned_resources (resource.rs:2685). Inside delete_pods_owned_by, if the dependent still has any OTHER live owner, strip only the matching ownerReference instead of deleting. Audit delete_replicasets_owned_by and delete_jobs_owned_by for the identical unconditional-delete pattern and fix the same class.

DISTINCT FROM mayor-74j3.5: that covers the effective_orphan branch (nil-policy RC delete, resource.rs:2106, using the already-correct orphan_owned_resources) racing KCM's informer cache -- ZERO code overlap with delete_pods_owned_by's explicit-cascade branch. Do not merge/block against 74j3.5.

Needs Lima VM verification (GC cascade path). Regression test must fail-on-revert: create owner-A + owner-B, dependent owned by both, delete owner-A cascade=foreground, assert dependent survives with only owner-B's ref remaining. Resolves mayor-ftkl PANIC-4.
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #828, dedicated review per API-adjacent stance): PASS. Diff is single-file (resource.rs, no boundary leak). Logic verified correct: owner_ref_is_live resolves referent by (group,kind)->plural via resource_registry and VERIFIES uid match (correctly rejects name-reuse-with-different-uid as not-live); strip_or_delete_dependent excludes the deleted owner by uid and strips-vs-deletes correctly. IMPORTANT correctness point the worker got right beyond the brief: the RS/Job child-pod cascade (delete_pods_owned_by rs_uid/job_uid) is now GATED on  -- a surviving RS/Job's pods are correctly left untouched. Raw store.put(key,...,None) for the stripped object is CONSISTENT with the existing trusted orphan path strip_owner_from_resources (resource.rs:2796, same pattern) -- not a divergence. Regression test foreground_cascade_preserves_pod_with_another_live_owner proven fail-on-revert, asserts co-owned survival + exactly owner-B ref left + deletionTimestamp null + non-regression that solo-owned pod is still deleted; assertion messages state WHY (systemic data loss). Also fixed the identical bug in delete_replicasets_owned_by + delete_jobs_owned_by (all 3 cascades). Awaiting CI green to merge (no --admin).
close_reason: PR #828 opened: fix(apiserver): GC foreground cascade preserves dependents with another live owner. Fixed delete_pods_owned_by, delete_replicasets_owned_by, delete_jobs_owned_by (all had the same unconditional-delete pattern). Verified live on lima-node-3 (kubectl before/after) + sonobuoy focus PASS.
