title: fix(watch): implement set-based label selector 'in'/'notin' in live event and list filter paths
description: The watch test '[sig-api-machinery] Watchers should observe add, update, and delete watch notifications on configmaps' FAILS IN ISOLATION (one test, quiet stack, 60s timeout) because object_matches_label_selector (watch.rs:305-311) and parse_label_selector (generic.rs:233-283) do not implement the set-based 'in' and 'notin' operators. The conformance test opens watches with labelSelector='watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)'. This string contains no '=', '!=', or '!' prefix, so it falls to the bare-key Exists branch: labels.get("watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)") returns None, causing the function to return false and silently drop every matching ADDED event. The test then times out at exactly 60s. Confirmed via: (1) apiserver.log showing the exact URLs with 'in+%28' at 09:27:44; (2) sonobuoy e2e.txt showing FAILED at watch.go:409; (3) kubectl repro showing equality selectors work while in-selectors do not. Fix: add 'in (v1,v2)' and 'notin (v1,v2)' parsing in both watch.rs:object_matches_label_selector AND generic.rs:parse_label_selector+apply_label_selector. Blast radius: watch live event filter, sendInitialEvents snapshot filter, list handler filter. Add regression tests for both functions.
notes: ROOT CAUSE MAYOR-VERIFIED against source (2026-07-05). watch.rs:305-311 object_matches_label_selector: parse chain is !key → key!=v → key=v → BARE-KEY-EXISTS. A set-based selector 'watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)' has no !/!=/= → falls to line 305 as key='watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)' → labels.get(that) is None → return false → EVERY matching event dropped. Same gap in generic.rs:parse_label_selector (line 281 bare-key → LabelSelectorTerm::Exists) so LIST/snapshot with set-based selectors also matches nothing. Isolation repro (scout, lima-node-2): the Watchers configmap test FAILS in exactly 60.046s on a FRESH QUIET stack, single write, ring at rev~349/cap 1000 → REFUTES 'buffer eviction under burst' definitively. apiserver --verbose showed the 3 'in (...)' watch URLs + the configmap create, then ZERO 'emitting event' lines → event filtered out, never sent. This is why the 600s timeouts happen: test opens set-based-selector watch → apiserver silently drops all events → test waits its full ceiling. FIX: implement 'key in (v1,v2)' + 'key notin (v1,v2)' in BOTH watch.rs:object_matches_label_selector (live path) AND generic.rs:parse_label_selector+apply_label_selector (list path) + regression tests for each operator. Blast radius: apiserver-side filtering only (store broadcasts unfiltered; no store change). HIGH LEVERAGE — set-based selectors are used by many controllers/tests; this one bug likely explains a large fraction of the 123 failures AND the wall-clock regression.
close_reason: PR #687 opened; both Watchers conformance tests now PASS (was 60s timeout FAIL); in/notin selectors fixed in watch.rs + generic.rs; paren-safe term splitting; DELETED filtering; duplicate synthetic DELETED prevention; scope-reentry ADDED promotion

title: EPIC: pod probe lifecycle — liveness/readiness/startup probes not firing or miscounting
description: 9 conformance failures (sig-node Probing container). From conformance-failure-categorization-2026-07-05 (run 0705-1409). ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: probe handler dispatch broken across exec/HTTP/TCP/GRPC — probes fire before initialDelaySeconds, never execute, or results not propagated to pod status; restart count not incremented on probe-driven restart. EXAMPLES: 'with readiness probe should not be ready before initial delay and never restart'; 'should have monotonically increasing restart count'; 'should be restarted with a exec cat /tmp/health liveness probe'; 'should *not* be restarted with a GRPC liveness probe'. No existing bead. NOTE: this is kubelet/node-side behavior — confirm which component owns probes in u7s before scoping fixes. Next: --stack-only scout to reproduce one probe test + read where probe results flow into pod status.
notes:
SCOUT VERDICT + mayor-VERIFIED (2026-07-05): the 9 probe failures are NOT a probe bug and NOT an apiserver pod-status bug (my reframe DENIED with evidence — patch_pod_status returns 200 for every PATCH). ROOT: the KUBELET on the node was CRASH-LOOPING — re-registering (POST /nodes→409) every ~11s (VERIFIED in preserved apiserver.log: 00:52:57, :53:08, :53:20, :53:31... 27x in the probe window, ~11s apart = RestartSec=10 + init). No pod got past ContainerCreating (imageID:'' on all 9). So probe LOGIC is untested — the container never ran. IMPLICATION: a crash-looping kubelet poisons MANY node-side tests, not just these 9 (sig-node failure cluster is ~18) — fixing the crash could flip far more than 9, OR the crash is triggered by one test's config (hostPort at 19:55, or the InPlacePodVerticalScaling 1.36 feature gate 'Missing actuated pod level resource record' at kuberuntime_manager.go:1428) and is localized. CANNOT confirm the trigger without kubelet.log — sonobuoy didn't capture it. BLOCKED on 6el2.2 (capture kubelet.log) → then 6el2.1 (diagnose trigger). This is a NODE/kubelet issue, likely NOT u7s-apiserver code at all — possibly a feature-gate/config fix or an upstream-kubelet-version interaction.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND + mayor-verified (2026-07-05, salvaged kubelet.log from the crashed 2237 run). THE PANIC: "panic: non-positive interval for NewTicker" at kubelet prober/worker.go:169 (from prober_manager.go:227 AddPod) → the probe worker calls time.NewTicker with a 0 interval → Go panics → kubelet exits(2) → systemd restarts → next probe pod re-triggers → crash-loop (236 restarts, 159 panics in the salvaged journal). U7S BUG (NOT upstream, NOT sysctl — sysctl lead was wrong): u7s does not apply k8s PodSpec probe DEFAULTING. A probe with periodSeconds unset/0 (normal case; clients rely on server defaulting to 10) reaches the kubelet as 0. Evidence: core_gen_adapter.rs:274 only emits periodSeconds when non-zero, and no defaulting pass sets the upstream defaults. Poisons ~18-30 sig-node tests + drives wall-clock. The 2237 run failed to retrieve results because sonobuoy aggregator pod itself went Failed; #689 capture only runs on successful sonobuoy end → manual salvage was needed (consider: capture kubelet.log even on sonobuoy failure).

So the fix is verified against the targeted repro, NOT a full suite — a FULL conformance re-run is still needed to confirm the ~18-30 sig-node blast-radius flip. 6el2 remaining: 6el2.1 (the diagnosis task — now RESOLVED by this fix, close it) + 6el2.2 done. After a full re-run, re-check h24j (its 18 were likely partly this crash-loop collateral).

title: analyze: conformance run WALL-CLOCK REGRESSION (4.76h baseline → 11h+) after protobuf typegen EPIC
description:
REGRESSION CONFIRMED (timestamp-verified, 2026-07-05). Operator observes the current full conformance run making steady progress but running >11h and counting — vs a sub-5h baseline days earlier. Not wedged; genuinely slower.

## Baseline (ground truth, from e2e.txt)

## The correlation (NOT yet proven causation — analysis must establish it)
ALL 12 EPIC PRs (#673-#684) merged 2026-07-04→07-05, AFTER the 4.76h baseline. The EPIC routed every proto decode through generated structs + JSON-emission adapters (Adapter A). Prime suspects to investigate:
- Adapter allocation cost on the hot decode path (perf audit flagged: 440+ .to_string() on static keys [mayor-k8jt, closed as 'no cheap fix' — but at scale it may still matter], Map sizing [mayor-ihep, partially done]).

- The pu5i apiserver→kubelet log/proxy 500 window (mayor-pu5i) — retries/hangs could add wall-clock AND inflate failures.
- Something non-EPIC that also landed in the window (rule it out via git log).

## Analysis plan (DISPATCH AFTER THE RUN FINISHES — needs the completed results)
1. Correctness diff: current e2e.txt Passed/Failed vs baseline 303/141. Which tests newly fail (regressions) vs newly pass (EPIC fixes, e.g. the recovered fields)? Separate genuine failures from pu5i-spurious teardown-500s.
2. Perf attribution: WHERE did the wall-clock go — per-test timing deltas (ginkgo emits per-spec durations), or overall throughput? Is it decode latency (profile the adapter hot path), or more tests running, or retries/timeouts from pu5i?
3. Bisect suspicion: if decode latency, confirm against the EPIC by micro-benchmarking a hot decoder (Pod) old-hand vs new-gen path.
4. Verdict + fix beads.

Blocks nothing yet; P1 because a 2.3x conformance regression is a serious signal for a perf-sensitive apiserver.
notes:
RESOLVED — ROOT CAUSE IS HOST SLEEP, NOT A U7S BUG (2026-07-06, verified on BOTH ballooned runs). The ~8h wall-clock 'ballooning' is the Mac HOST SLEEPING during unattended overnight runs. PROOF: (1) apiserver.log has ~35 gaps of ~15-17min each where the apiserver logs NOTHING; (2) the SCHEDULER (host) and KUBELET node-lease (VM) go silent in the SAME windows — 3 independent processes freezing together; (3) kube-node-lease renewals (normally every 10s, unconditional heartbeat) STOP entirely during each gap then burst on resume = process frozen, not idle; (4) gaps are ~15-min periodic (= macOS DarkWake/PowerNap maintenance-wake cadence) and FILL THE ENTIRE NIGHT: run 0706-1152 gaps run continuously JST 23:18->08:35; run 0705-1409 gaps run from JST 01:08 onward; (5) ACTIVE (non-gap) time = 3.98h ~= ginkgo's reported 3.87h EXACTLY. Ginkgo's clock was CORRECT ALL ALONG — it measured the ~4h the host was awake. (6) The 0703 baseline (4h45m, wall-clock matched) ran during the DAY (attended); the ballooned runs ran OVERNIGHT. 

CONSEQUENCE: There is NO wall-clock ballooning bug. The proto EPIC is EXONERATED (spurious correlation — it landed right before we started running overnight). Ginkgo exec time ~3.9-4.9h vs 4.75h baseline = at most a MODEST ~1h real regression from the genuine slow-spec FAILURES (still worth fixing for conformance, but NOT an 8h emergency). FIX = disable host sleep during runs (caffeinate -dimsu ./scripts/... OR macOS Energy Saver 'prevent sleep'), and/or keep Lima VM awake. All the wall-clock 'category' analysis (gjy0/25ap/etc as WALL-CLOCK levers) is MOOT for the 8h — those beads remain valid as CORRECTNESS/conformance fixes only. Close this bead as root-caused: host sleep.

NOT a u7s bug, proto EPIC exonerated. Fix is operational (caffeinate/disable sleep), not code. title: fix(watch): CRD create does not deliver ADDED watch event to watchers — 5 FieldValidation tests + CRD-Watch spurious-DELETED (event lost between push_event and subscriber; needs live --verbose)
description:
CONFIRMED SYMPTOM (scout a9fa49a1 kubectl repro + mayor source verification). Creating a CustomResourceDefinition does NOT deliver an ADDED watch event to a client watching customresourcedefinitions, while creating a configmap DOES. This times out 5 [sig-api-machinery] FieldValidation conformance tests (all fail identically: 'cannot create crd gave up waiting for watch event', e2e.txt lines 564/7497/8089/14204/14519) because they create a CRD then wait for the ADDED before testing CR field validation. Related: CustomResourceDefinition Watch test gets 'Unexpected watch notification observed: {DELETED ...}' (e2e.txt:13856) — spurious DELETED, likely same root area (deletion_log tombstone replay).

kubectl repro (CONFIRMED by scout on live stack): 'kubectl get crds -w' + 'kubectl apply' a CRD → watch lists the CRD but emits NO ADDED event. Contrast: 'kubectl get configmaps -w' + create configmap → ADDED fires correctly.

WHAT THE MAYOR RULED OUT (read these before re-investigating — do NOT re-derive):
1. NOT a different write path: create_crd (crd.rs:358) uses the SAME state.store.put(&key, ..., Some(0)) as generic resources (resource.rs:307). Configmaps use the identical call and DO emit ADDED.
2. NOT an is_create bug: is_create is computed in put_sync (sqlite.rs:245) as stored.is_none(); the store.put path (sqlite.rs:844) uses it; internal_to_watch emits ADDED when is_create=true. A fresh CRD create has no prior row → is_create should be true. (Confirm on a live stack that it actually IS true for a CRD create — this is the FIRST thing to check with --verbose.)
3. NOT a key/prefix mismatch (the tidy hypothesis — FALSE): WRITE key = store_key(name) = '/registry/apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefinitions/<name>' (crd.rs:25). WATCH prefix = list_prefix() = '/registry/apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefinitions/' (crd.rs:29). The write key STARTS WITH the watch prefix, so the ring-buffer prefix filter (watch.rs:~921) would PASS the event. They align. Both use the same GROUP/PLURAL constants.

So: the write path, is_create logic, and prefix filter all look correct on static reading (scout AND mayor independently confirmed) — yet the ADDED never reaches the watcher. This requires RUNTIME OBSERVATION, not more static reading.

INVESTIGATION APPROACH (worker, LIVE stack, --verbose for RUST_LOG=debug): bring up the stack, start a CRD watch, create a CRD, and TRACE the event: (a) does put_sync log is_create=true for the CRD? (b) does push_event (sqlite.rs:99) actually broadcast the event, and with what key? (c) does the watch subscriber's ring-buffer filter (watch.rs:921) receive it and does the prefix comparison pass? (d) is there a race — e.g. the watch established at rv=N but the CRD event is at rv<N and skipped, or fetch_initial_events consumes it so the live stream never re-emits it? (e) the send_initial_events / initial_items path (crd.rs:231) — is the CRD delivered as an initial item (bookmark/list) INSTEAD OF as an ADDED watch event, so a client waiting specifically for ADDED never sees it? Hypothesis (e) is the STRONGEST given everything else checks out: the CRD may be showing up in the initial list snapshot but not as a discrete ADDED event. Also check the spurious-DELETED (deletion_log replay, sqlite.rs:146-149 evict-on-recreate).

Add debug logging as needed (via --verbose, NOT code changes for the investigation) or a targeted unit/integration test of watch_generic with a CRD create. Once the mechanism is pinned, fix + regression test + --focus gate on a FieldValidation test.

CONFIRMED symptom; root cause is PLAUSIBLE-narrowed (event lost between push_event and subscriber; hypothesis (e) initial-snapshot-vs-ADDED is the lead). Source anchors: crd.rs:231/358 (create + watch setup), sqlite.rs:99/245/844 (push_event/is_create/put), watch.rs:921 (ring filter) + fetch_initial_events.
acceptance_criteria: CRD create delivers an ADDED watch event to a watcher (kubectl get crds -w shows ADDED for a newly applied CRD, like configmaps do). The 5 FieldValidation tests + the CRD-Watch test pass under --focus (read e2e.txt). Regression test: a watch on customresourcedefinitions receives an ADDED event when a CRD is created. Spurious-DELETED resolved or confirmed separate.
notes: RESOLVED + MERGED as PR #672 (merge 93e05c15) on 2026-07-04. Final: CR version-key mismatch fix (writes now keyed by ctx.storage_version) + SSA-upsert-on-PATCH for CRs, YAML parsing via yaml-rust2 0.11.0 (pure-Rust, 0 unsafe, no unsafe-libyaml — replaced the worker's initial deprecated serde_yaml after operator YAML-crate decision). Yaml->serde_json::Value converter handles non-finite reals (400), non-string keys (coerce/skip), BadValue/Alias (400 not silent-null). 1868 tests pass, 17/17 CI green, --focus 'valid CR' 2/2 PASS. New transitive deps: arraydeque/encoding_rs/hashlink (all pure-Rust). Spurious-DELETED (CRD Watch test) status: verify whether the version-key fix also resolved it or if it's a separate residual — mayor to check on next full run. Follow-ups from this work: mayor-40cj (tolerations proto-drop), mayor-r5t4 (Unknown-array $patch:delete).

title: fix(patch): strategic-merge $patch:delete on metadata.ownerReferences stored literally (merge key 'uid' missing) — ReplicaSet/RC adopt-release panics conformance tests
description:
CONFIRMED root cause (scout + mayor read of patch.rs). The conformance test '[sig-apps] ReplicaSet should adopt matching pods on creation and release no longer matching pods' PANICS (test-client nil-deref at test/e2e/apps/replica_set.go:392 dereferencing *owner.Controller). ReplicationController has the analogous 'should release no longer matching pods' test.

MECHANISM: when a pod's label stops matching, KCM releases it by PATCHing (strategic merge) {"metadata":{"ownerReferences":[{"$patch":"delete","uid":"<rs-uid>"}]}} to remove the ownerReference. u7s stores the $patch:delete element LITERALLY instead of applying it, so the pod ends up with a garbage ownerReference {"$patch":"delete","uid":"..."} that has no 'controller'/'blockOwnerDeletion' fields. The test derefs *owner.Controller on it -> nil panic.

WHY (code CONFIRMED): $patch:delete is only honored inside strategic_merge_array (patch.rs:160-168, retains-by-merge-key), which is ONLY reached when merge_key_for_path returns MergeKeyKind::Key(...) (patch.rs:83). metadata.ownerReferences is NOT in the merge-key table (patch.rs:211-269 lists imagePullSecrets/hostAliases/volumeMounts/ports/conditions/podIPs/... but NOT ownerReferences), so it returns Unknown. The Unknown/Replace branch (patch.rs:89-98) only handles $patch:replace (has_replace_directive); a $patch:delete falls through to target_obj.insert(key, value.clone()) — stored verbatim.

kubectl evidence (scout, CONFIRMED): after adoption ownerReferences = full {apiVersion,blockOwnerDeletion:true,controller:true,kind,name,uid} (correct); after release ownerReferences = {"$patch":"delete","uid":"..."} (MALFORMED — the bug). KCM is CORRECT (sends the right $patch:delete directive); the defect is purely u7s not applying it.

FIX (surgical, matches upstream): add metadata.ownerReferences to merge_key_for_path with merge key 'uid' (upstream k8s treats ownerReferences as a strategic-merge list keyed by uid). This routes the delete through the working strategic_merge_array path, which correctly retains-by-uid (patch.rs:167). Add the path so both 'metadata.ownerReferences' and any '.metadata.ownerReferences' suffix resolve (match the existing suffix-pattern style, cf. .volumeMounts/.ports/.conditions).

SECONDARY (note, do NOT necessarily fix here): the Unknown-array branch silently mishandles $patch:delete for ANY unregistered array (stores it literally) — a latent hardening gap. Scope THIS bead to registering ownerReferences (the confirmed conformance failure); mention the broader Unknown-$patch:delete gap in the PR body for the mayor to decide on a follow-up.

Relate: this is the runtime.go:116 panic from the full run 0703 (ReplicaSet adopt). Distinct from proto-drop beads — this is strategic-merge directive handling, not a dropped proto field.
acceptance_criteria: metadata.ownerReferences (and .metadata.ownerReferences suffix) is in merge_key_for_path with merge key 'uid'. A $patch:delete on ownerReferences correctly REMOVES the matching element (not stored literally). Regression test: strategic-merge PATCH with {ownerReferences:[{$patch:delete,uid:X}]} on a pod owning [X,Y] leaves only Y, with no $patch key in the result. Live: the ReplicaSet adopt-release conformance test passes under --focus (read e2e.txt); kubectl before/after shows ownerReferences correctly cleared on release.
close_reason: PR #671 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/671

title: fix(openapi): /openapi/v2 proto Content-Type uses deprecated @v1.0 form, breaks kubectl validation (13 conformance tests: mime: unexpected content after media subtype)
description: First-ever full conformance run (0703-1822) surfaced 13 kubectl create/replace --validate failures with 'mime: unexpected content after media subtype'. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (root-cause scout + upstream-source verification + mayor read of both u7s source and kube-openapi source): u7s /openapi/v2 handler returns Content-Type: application/com.github.proto-openapi.spec.v2@v1.0+protobuf for a proto-only Accept. The @v1.0 embedded in the subtype is the DEPRECATED kube-openapi token (subTypeProtobufDeprecated) and is non-RFC-2045-compliant; Go's mime.ParseMediaType (in kubectl's validation path) rejects it. Upstream kube-openapi handler.go accepts BOTH the @ (deprecated) and . (current) forms as REQUEST Accept tokens, but ALWAYS responds with the dot form: application/com.github.proto-openapi.spec.v2.v1.0+protobuf (ReturnedContentType = 'application/' + subTypeProtobuf for both entries). u7s wrongly echoes the deprecated @ form in the RESPONSE Content-Type. FIX: change the constant at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs:1379 from @v1.0 to .v1.0 (body stays gnostic openapi_v2.Document proto — correct). The existing test openapi_v2_proto_only_accept_returns_200_proto at discovery.rs:3245 asserts ct.contains('protobuf') so it still passes, BUT its comment (lines 3235-3240) documents the wrong @ form — update the comment/expectation to the dot form so the test encodes the CORRECT upstream contract. This is a decision-resolved API-surface fix that matches upstream exactly. Findings: ai/findings/rc-mime-content-type-2026-07-03.md. Upstream refs: kube-openapi pkg/handler/handler.go subTypeProtobuf/subTypeProtobufDeprecated + the accepted table.
acceptance_criteria: discovery.rs:1379 constant emits the dot form; the openapi_v2 proto-only test asserts the correct dot-form contract; sonobuoy --focus over the affected Kubectl-client tests shows the mime error is gone and those tests PASS (read from e2e.txt).
close_reason: PR #668 opened: fix confirmed — mime error absent from sonobuoy runs, kubectl create/replace --validate succeeds

title: fix(apiserver): proto decode drops Deployment.status and ReplicaSet.status (new instances of proto-decode-drop pattern)
description:
Audit mayor-mil2 (quality) F-03, HIGH. New instances of the known proto-decode-drop class (see ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md). decode_deployment_proto (proto.rs:5437-5458) and decode_replicaset_proto (proto.rs:5535-5557) build JSON from ONLY metadata + spec and return — no status block. Their structural siblings decode_statefulset_proto (proto.rs:5343, status block ~5377-5432) and decode_daemonset_proto (proto.rs:5462) DO emit status. Any proto-encoded write of a Deployment/ReplicaSet carrying status silently drops it.

Fix: add status-emitting blocks to decode_deployment_proto and decode_replicaset_proto mirroring decode_statefulset_proto lines 5377-5432, using the correct upstream field numbers from k8s staging generated.proto for DeploymentStatus / ReplicaSetStatus.

Per dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check: add the field with the correct upstream field NUMBER, a proto-round-trip regression test, AND audit sibling fields in the same struct in the same pass.

Source: ai/findings/audit-2026-07-02/quality.md F-03. SOLO. proto.rs — disjoint from admission.rs workers.

title: fix(admission): CEL arithmetic uses unchecked i64 ops (mul/div/mod/add/neg) — VAP/MAP author can panic-DoS every admission request
description:
Audit mayor-37sk (security) Finding 1, HIGH. The hand-written CEL evaluator in admission.rs performs i64 arithmetic with plain Rust operators (l*r, l/r, l%r, ai+bi, -i) with no overflow checks. Rust panics on overflow in debug builds AND in release builds when overflow-checks=true (cargo's default for tests). Additionally i64::MIN / -1 panics (arithmetic overflow) and is NOT covered by the existing zero-divisor guard at admission.rs:1234.

A user who can create a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy submits a CEL expression like '9223372036854775807 * 2' or 'object.spec.replicas / -1'. The panic propagates up the async admission request thread → 500 or process abort on every subsequent admission-gated request. DoS.

Sites:
- admission.rs:1232 (multiply, apply_mul_op)
- admission.rs:1237 (divide)
- admission.rs:1243 (modulo)
- admission.rs:1177 (add, apply_add_op)
- admission.rs:1271 (unary negate)

Fix: replace with checked_mul/checked_div/checked_rem/checked_add/checked_neg, returning None (eval error) on overflow — exactly like the existing zero-divisor guard. ~5 line changes.

DISTINCT from mayor-kxht (that is a VAP namespace-context + status-persistence bug + a kubelet-side index panic; confirmed distinct by the auditor). This is purely the arithmetic ops in apply_mul_op/apply_add_op.

Source: ai/findings/audit-2026-07-02/security.md Finding 1. SOLO. Touches admission.rs — hot zone; do not run in parallel with other admission.rs workers.
Regression test: a VAP whose CEL does i64::MAX*2 (and i64::MIN/-1) must produce an eval error / deny, NOT panic the request thread.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #646: all 5 CEL i64 arithmetic ops (mul, div, mod, add, neg) replaced with checked variants. i64::MIN/-1 case covered by checked_div/checked_rem. 5 regression tests added.

title: fix(apiserver): PATCH subresource handlers use stored resourceVersion as CAS token instead of incoming — unconditional writes (scale/approval/status)
description:
Audit mayor-mil2 (quality) found a systemic copy-paste divergence: #643 fixed CAS on the PUT subresource handlers to honor the incoming body's resourceVersion, but the sibling PATCH handlers were MISSED and read the STORED object's resourceVersion (which always matches, since it was just fetched) — making them effectively unconditional writes that only catch true concurrent races, not stale-client writes.

Three affected PATCH handlers (each has a correct PUT sibling to mirror):
- scale.rs:436 scale_patch_impl uses obj.resource_version(); scale_put_impl:362 correctly uses scale.metadata.resource_version. HPA scales EXCLUSIVELY via PATCH, so a stale HPA scale silently wins over a concurrent write. HIGH.
- approval.rs:146 patch_approval uses current.resource_version(); put_approval:62 correctly uses incoming.resource_version(). A stale 'kubectl certificate approve' PATCH silently overwrites a concurrent approval/denial on a CSR. HIGH, security-sensitive (also flagged by mayor-37sk).
- status.rs:176 patch_resource_status and status.rs:323 patch_namespaced_resource_status use current.resource_version(); the PUT siblings (put_resource_status:114, put_namespaced_resource_status:249) correctly use incoming RV. Silent k8s semantic divergence. MED (controllers retry on 409 so low practical blast radius, but wrong).

Fix: in each PATCH handler, extract resourceVersion from the decoded patch body (patch["metadata"]["resourceVersion"]); use it as the CAS token when present, pass None (unconditional) when absent — matching upstream k8s PATCH semantics and the PUT sibling.

Source: ai/findings/audit-2026-07-02/quality.md F-01, F-02, F-04. Cluster HEAD.
Regression tests: for each handler, a PATCH with a stale resourceVersion must return 409; a PATCH with no resourceVersion must succeed unconditionally.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #647: scale_patch_impl, patch_approval, patch_resource_status, patch_namespaced_resource_status now use incoming patch body's metadata.resourceVersion as CAS token instead of stored object's RV; 6 regression tests.

title: apiserver proto decoder drops PodDisruptionBudget spec (selector + minAvailable) — breaks DisruptionController conformance
description:
## Summary

The u7s apiserver's protobuf decoder for PodDisruptionBudget DISCARDS spec entirely.
Proto-encoded PDB creates (what the e2e client / client-go send) are stored with no
spec.selector and no spec.minAvailable. Downstream, KCM's disruption controller cannot
match any pod to the (selector-less) PDB, computes expectedPods:0, and buildDisruptedPodMap
clears status.disruptedPods — failing the conformance spec.

Discovered diagnosing `[sig-apps] DisruptionController should update/patch
PodDisruptionBudget status` (test/e2e/apps/disruption.go:187).

## Root cause (crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs)

- proto.rs:2714 — `spec` captured as opaque bytes: `#[prost(bytes = "vec", tag = "2")] spec: Vec<u8>`.
  No `PodDisruptionBudgetSpec` message type exists.
- decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto (proto.rs:5896-5963) emits only apiVersion/kind/metadata/status.
  There is no `result["spec"] = ...` anywhere.

Confirmed flow: extract_body (util.rs:71-83) -> decode_proto_by_kind_and_version
(proto.rs:7918/7967) -> decoded JSON stored verbatim (resource.rs:1124->1232). GET/watch
serve stored JSON with NO proto re-encode (content_type.rs pass-through; resource.rs:1069).
apply_defaults only sets metadata.generation=1 (defaults.rs:84-94). So a spec-less stored
PDB is served spec-less. Fixing the DECODE is necessary AND sufficient.

## Evidence (0702-1607 run, 4 independent sources)

1. apiserver.log: decoded PDB create body has NO spec (only metadata+status).
2. KCM --v=4 log: "No matching PDB for pod" pod="disruption-3790/pod-0" on every pod event.
3. Every PDB reconcile logs expectedPods:0 (getPodsForPdb finds no pods).
4. buildDisruptedPodMap over empty pod list -> clears disruptedPods -> read-back FAILs.

## Why kubectl repros missed it

kubectl apply -f sends JSON (spec preserved) -> selector survives -> no failure. The bug
is specific to the PROTO create path the e2e client uses.

## Fix approach (typed, per project policy — no raw-bytes/map access for reasoned fields)

All in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs, reusing existing helpers:
1. Add typed `PodDisruptionBudgetSpec` prost struct (policy/v1 layout):
   f1 min_available: Option<IntOrString>, f2 selector: Option<AdmissionLabelSelector>,
   f3 max_unavailable: Option<IntOrString>, f4 unhealthy_pod_eviction_policy: String.
   Reuses IntOrString (proto.rs:305, .to_json()) and AdmissionLabelSelector (proto.rs:6227,
   rendered by label_selector_to_json at 6335).
2. Change PodDisruptionBudget.spec (proto.rs:2713-2715) from #[prost(bytes)] to
   #[prost(message, optional, tag = "2")] Option<PodDisruptionBudgetSpec>.
3. Emit spec JSON in decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto (conditional per sub-field, mirroring
   the status block style).
4. Amend existing test decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto_preserves_status_disrupted_pods
   (proto.rs:12730): spec: vec![] -> spec: None.
5. Add fail-on-revert regression test decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto_preserves_spec_selector:
   proto PDB with selector.matchLabels={foo:bar} + minAvailable=1; assert both survive.
   Assertion messages state WHY (without selector, KCM clears disruptedPods).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PodDisruptionBudgetSpec is a typed prost struct; spec field is #[prost(message)], not bytes.
- [ ] decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto emits spec.selector, spec.minAvailable,
      spec.maxUnavailable, spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy when present.
- [ ] Regression test asserts spec.selector.matchLabels + minAvailable survive proto decode;
      fails on revert of the decoder change.
- [ ] cargo test -p u7s-apiserver green (incl. amended status test + defaults PDB tests).
- [ ] E2E: decoded PDB create body includes spec; KCM matches pod-0 (no "No matching PDB");
      expectedPods becomes 1; DisruptionController conformance test PASSES.
- [ ] Temp debug logging removed; KCM --v threading decision (keep or revert) made.

## Relationship to other beads

MAY also resolve / supersede these, both filed today while chasing the same failing test:
- mayor-8phw (subresource PUT ignores incoming rv -> no 409). Real bug, tested fix, but
  VERIFIED not the cause of this conformance test (with that fix applied, the test still
  fails via this proto-spec-drop). Keep 8phw as an independent correctness fix.
- mayor-w8tj (KCM reconcile-race / disruptedPods cleared). This proto bug is the actual
  mechanism behind w8tj's symptom; w8tj's reconcile-race and global-bookmark theories were
  REFUTED. w8tj likely closes when this lands.
notes: PR #644 opened (branch fix/pdb-proto-spec-decode, commit 4ecd0fd4). VERIFIED end-to-end: (1) cargo test -p u7s-apiserver 1790 passed; regression test decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto_preserves_spec_selector fails-on-revert. (2) Focused conformance run 0702-1643 PASSES: 'Ran 1 of 7579 Specs -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed'. (3) apiserver debug log: decoded PDB now carries spec.selector={foo:bar}+minAvailable:1. (4) KCM --v=4 log (disruption-8286): 'addPod -> PDB'/'updatePod -> PDB' matches pod-0 to PDB foo, zero 'No matching PDB for pod' (was constant pre-fix). Awaiting PR review/merge before closing.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in #644 (commit a373f271). The apiserver proto decoder now decodes PodDisruptionBudgetSpec (typed struct: minAvailable, selector, maxUnavailable, unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy) instead of dropping spec as opaque bytes. Verified: cargo test green (regression test decode_poddisruptionbudget_proto_preserves_spec_selector fails-on-revert); the focused conformance run passes (Ran 1 of 7579 Specs -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed); apiserver log shows decoded PDB carries spec.selector; KCM --v=4 log shows the disruption controller now matches pod-0 to the PDB (addPod -> PDB) with zero 'No matching PDB for pod'. This was the true root cause of the DisruptionController conformance failure.

title: Subresource PUT handlers ignore incoming resourceVersion (no 409 on stale write) — clobbers status/scale, breaks PDB conformance
description:
## Summary

Subresource PUT handlers (`/status`, `/scale`) compute their optimistic-concurrency
compare-and-swap `resourceVersion` from the **stored** object they just read, NOT from
the **incoming client request body**. This makes the CAS unconditional: a PUT carrying a
**stale** `resourceVersion` is accepted (HTTP 200) instead of rejected (HTTP 409 Conflict).
Concurrent writers therefore silently clobber each other.

Discovered while diagnosing the consistently-failing conformance test
`[sig-apps] DisruptionController should update/patch PodDisruptionBudget status`
(test/e2e/apps/disruption.go:187).

## How it manifests (PDB conformance failure)

From apiserver debug logs (ns `disruption-5062`), two `PUT /status` calls 4ms apart:

1. Disruption controller GETs PDB at rv=1832 (no disruptedPods), builds its status update.
2. Test `UpdateStatus` PUT (body rv=1832, `status.disruptedPods={pod-0}`) -> stored rv=1845 (OK).
3. Controller status PUT (body built from stale rv=1832, NO disruptedPods).
   - Real k8s: **409 Conflict** (stored 1845 != 1832) -> controller retries from a fresh
     GET, sees pod-0 in disruptedPods, `buildDisruptedPodMap` preserves it, writes it back.
   - u7s bug: handler ignores the body's rv and uses the freshly-read stored rv (1845) as
     the CAS token -> stale write **succeeds** -> stored rv=1846, disruptedPods **wiped**.
4. Test GETs `/status` -> disruptedPods empty -> FAIL:
   `<map[string]v1.Time | len:0>: nil, expected key 'pod-0'`.

## Root cause

The correct pattern (main PUT, resource.rs:396):
    let expected_revision = parse_resource_version(obj.resource_version())?;  // INCOMING body

The buggy pattern (subresource PUTs):
    let expected_rv = parse_resource_version(current.resource_version())?;    // STORED object

## Affected handlers (all verified by reading source)

1. put_namespaced_resource_status  crates/apiserver/src/handlers/status.rs:256  (the PDB bug; all namespaced /status PUTs)
2. put_resource_status             crates/apiserver/src/handlers/status.rs:114  (cluster-scoped /status PUT)
3. put_cr_status                   crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:1765     (custom-resource /status PUT; Gateway API etc.)
4. put_namespace_status           crates/apiserver/src/handlers/namespaces.rs:601 (Namespace /status PUT)
5. scale_put_impl                  crates/apiserver/src/handlers/scale.rs:359   (/scale PUT; Deployment/RS/StatefulSet/RC).
   WORSE: does not even parse the incoming Scale's metadata.resourceVersion (only reads
   spec.replicas). HPA/kubectl safe-scale updates rely on this RV being honored.

## NOT affected (verified correct — already use incoming body RV)

- put_approval (approval.rs:62), replace_cr (cr.rs:853), replace_cr_namespaced (cr.rs:1420),
  replace_namespace (namespaces.rs:328), replace_pod (pods.rs:455), main resource.rs PUT paths.

## Correctly excluded from the fix

- All PATCH /status and PATCH /scale handlers: patches are latest-wins by design and clients
  do not send an RV in a merge/strategic/json patch. Do NOT change these.
- Soft-delete / evict internal writes (delete_pod, evict_pod, delete_namespace): they write
  the stored object with no client RV contract.

## Fix approach

For each of the 5 handlers, derive expected_rv from the INCOMING body instead of the stored
object, mirroring resource.rs:396:
    let expected_rv = parse_resource_version(incoming.resource_version())?;

For scale_put_impl, additionally read scale.metadata.resourceVersion (currently discarded).

Design note (important): an ABSENT resourceVersion in a subresource PUT body must remain an
UNCONDITIONAL write (None), matching upstream k8s. parse_resource_version already returns
Ok(None) for empty/absent, so the check only engages when the client actually sends an RV.
This avoids breaking clients that legitimately omit it.

## Repro (kubectl-only, deterministic)

temp/repro/stale-rv.sh — two hand-replayed writers share one snapshotted RV R0; W1 advances
the store to R1, then W2 PUTs /status with the stale R0. Asserts W2 must get 409.
Currently exits 1 (bug present); will exit 0 when fixed.
Supporting: temp/repro/pdb-status.yaml (ns + PDB minAvailable=1 selector foo=bar + pod-0).
(temp/repro/repro.sh is the naive single-writer version and PASSES — evidence the bug is a

title: Apiserver does not default ReplicationController spec.selector from template labels -> RC runaway
description: Conformance run 0701-1407 root cause. The upstream conformance test '[sig-apps] ReplicationController should serve a basic image on each replica' creates an RC with replicas=int32(1) (verified from k8s release-1.34 test/e2e/apps/rc.go). Our stack scheduled 599 DISTINCT pods for that exact RC (my-hostname-basic-a510c2de...) in a ~1-minute burst (903 schedule-events at 16:42 UTC in temp/u7s/scheduler.log), stopping only when the node saturated at 110/110 (OutOfpods). This single runaway is the source of the ~150 'saturation' failures in the run (collateral, NOT 150 bugs). SUSPECTED root cause: the recurring proto-decode field-drop pattern applied to ReplicationController.status -- if the apiserver drops status.replicas/readyReplicas/availableReplicas/fullyLabeledReplicas when KCM writes RC status over protobuf, KCM reads back '0 ready' and creates another replica forever. RC proto decoder was recently touched (#594). NEEDS: scout to confirm mechanism against the still-live apiserver (create 1-replica RC, watch .status convergence, dump RC-status proto round-trip), then a fix with a proto-round-trip regression test + audit of sibling RC status fields. See ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md proto-drop PATTERN section.
design: ROOT CAUSE PINNED + VERIFIED LIVE (2026-07-01, 6445 stack). The apiserver does NOT default an RC's spec.selector from spec.template.metadata.labels when selector is omitted. Upstream k8s defaults RC (and RS) selector from template labels at create; we don't. CHAIN (every link observed): (1) conformance newRC (test/e2e/apps/rc.go) creates the RC with spec.selector=nil, only template labels name=<x>; (2) our apiserver stores selector EMPTY -- verified: kubectl apply of a nil-selector RC then  returns empty; (3) KCM RC controller with empty selector cannot match the pods it creates -> always sees active=0 desired=1 -> creates pods forever (also 'Pod ...-xxxxx already exists' name-reuse collisions); (4) live: nil-selector RC -> 179 pods in 8s (runaway); an IDENTICAL RC WITH an explicit selector -> converges to 1 pod (1/1 Running). This is why a naive kubectl repro (which supplied a selector) did NOT reproduce, and why Deployment/RS-based suites pass (RS requires an explicit selector; different path). SUPERSEDES all prior theories on this bead (proto drop, host sleep, generic KCM race, scheduler-as-root). FIX: default spec.selector = template.metadata.labels for ReplicationController on create when selector is unset (match upstream RC defaulting). Likely in the apiserver's create/defaulting path for RC (types.rs/handlers). Also verify RS/other selector-bearing types default correctly (audit). Regression: create nil-selector RC, assert stored selector == template labels; and a convergence test (nil-selector RC settles at desired replicas, no runaway). The scheduler capacity-check gap is SEPARATE (mayor-bbxr) -- it only caps blast radius, it is NOT this root cause.
notes: RECONFIRMED + MECHANISM CORRECTED (2 fresh --reset --focus runs on 6445: 0701-1836 = 1141 pods FAIL, matching 0701-1757 = 1142 FAIL). The runaway is REAL and STABLE via the conformance/sonobuoy path. BUT a bare 'kubectl apply' of the IDENTICAL RC fixture on the SAME freshly-reset 6445 stack CONVERGED to 1 pod (1/1 Running, RC status ready=1) -- NO runaway. So the runaway is NOT unconditional; it is a RACE under load. Corrected mechanism: the RC's pods are slow to reach Ready under sonobuoy load/cold image cache; KCM's replica controller creates a 2nd/3rd/Nth pod BEFORE the 1st is Ready (apiserver.log: 2nd pod POSTed before 1st bound), racing ahead; created pods pile up, node fills at 110, remainder fail OutOfpods (which IsPodActive excludes), and KCM never converges -> ~1140 pods. Only a handful of pods ever reach Pulling/Started, and those start LATE (high-churn names) -- by the time any pod is Ready, hundreds exist. In the manual test the single pod reached Ready in ~2s (warm) so KCM saw ready=1 and stopped -> no race. TWO contributing bugs, both real: (1) SCHEDULER has no capacity check (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs pick_node, verified) -> lets the runaway grow unbounded instead of leaving pods Pending; (2) the deeper trigger is KCM over-creating during the create->Ready latency window, which in real k8s is bounded by slow-start/expectations -- need to determine why our stack doesn't bound it (is it our pod status/watch latency making KCM's informer see pods as not-yet-existing? does our apiserver ack pod creates in a way that resets KCM expectations?). ROOT CAUSE STILL NOT FULLY PINNED -- do NOT dispatch a fix yet. The scheduler capacity check is a real robustness fix but may only CAP the blast radius, not stop the race. Next: instrument why KCM creates N pods before the first is Ready on our stack specifically (pod create latency / status propagation / watch).
close_reason: Fixed by #634 (merged). RC spec.selector now defaults from template labels; runaway eliminated (live-verified 1142->1 pod). Remaining RC-serve-image conformance failure is separate pod-proxy bug mayor-rpcb.

title: P1: CRD sendInitialEvents watch returns bare 410 Gone → client informer hot-loops → apiserver self-saturates → conformance run death
description:
ROOT CAUSE (fully diagnosed 2026-06-30/07-01 from a crashed full conformance run; evidence in temp/research/crash-0630/). u7s returns a bare 410 Gone for watch requests with sendInitialEvents=true&resourceVersionMatch=NotOlderThan on CUSTOM RESOURCES (CRDs), while the SAME request returns 200 correctly for ~20 built-in types (services, nodes, endpointslices, configmaps, CSI, etc. — confirmed in the apiserver log). The client (the webhook conformance test's dynamic informer, k8s test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go) cannot recover from the bare 410 — a correct apiserver either streams the initial events + a bookmark, or returns a 410 carrying a resourceVersion the client can re-list from. Instead the informer HOT-LOOPS: it re-issues the watch, gets 410, retries immediately, ~6000 requests/SECOND. Over ~8+ min this generated 3.8M+ identical 410 responses, saturating the apiserver until it could not serve health checks — unreachable BOTH from the host (sonobuoy CLI: dial tcp 6443 i/o timeout) AND from inside the cluster (e2e worker: Get 10.96.0.1:443 ... failed). The conformance run died with ZERO results retrieved.

SEVERITY P1: this is a self-inflicted DoS that kills ANY conformance run exercising a CRD informer (webhook + CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI specs are standard non-disruptive-conformance). It also resisted recovery: apiserver restart (client reconnects), sonobuoy delete (couldn't land — apiserver saturated), even crictl-killing the e2e-job pod; only killing the apiserver fully stopped it. The bug is in the same family as the other CRD-watch-path gaps (cr.rs lacked apply_delete_policy etc.) — the CRD watch path doesn't implement sendInitialEvents correctly.

FIX DIRECTION (scout to confirm): make the CRD watch path handle sendInitialEvents=true the SAME way the built-in path does — stream the current CR objects as ADDED events followed by a bookmark (or, if rejecting, return a 410 with a usable resourceVersion). The asymmetry (built-in=200, CRD=410) is the tell: find where built-in watch handles sendInitialEvents (watch.rs / fetch_initial_events) vs the CRD watch path (cr.rs / the CR watch handler) and bring CRD to parity. SECONDARY: even on a deleted/absent CRD the apiserver should not emit a bare 410 that induces a hot-loop (defense-in-depth: a watch on a nonexistent resource should 404 or return a terminal error, not a retriable 410).
design:
ROOT CAUSE PINNED (scout a7303c59, mayor-verified at cr.rs:493-523). find_crd (cr.rs) checks a deleted-group TOMBSTONE and returns Status::gone (410) at cr.rs:295-298. This runs as the FIRST op in list_cr (cr.rs:493, err propagated :501) and list_cr_namespaced (:1005), BEFORE the 'if query.watch==Some(true)' branch (:523). So a tombstoned CRD group returns 410 for BOTH list AND watch — the sendInitialEvents/fetch_initial_events path (cr.rs:532) is never reached. TIMELINE (corrected): the webhook test's CRD was DELETED at cleanup (~11:19 UTC), writing a tombstone that persisted in SQLite for 3+h; the informer's watch on the now-tombstoned group 410s, its recovery re-LIST also 410s (no resumable resourceVersion in the 410 body) → permanent hot-loop ~6000/s. The tombstone 410 itself is CORRECT for non-watch requests (keep it + test deleted_crd_group_returns_410_gone_not_404 cr.rs:5977). Built-ins never hit this: list_resource→lookup() static registry, no tombstone check, always 200+bookmark for sendInitialEvents.

FIX (scout design, ~20 lines):
1. PRIMARY (cr.rs list_cr :493-502 + list_cr_namespaced :1005-1014): in the find_crd Err block, when err.0==GONE && query.watch==Some(true) && query.send_initial_events==Some(true), DON'T propagate 410 — instead serve watch_generic with initial_items=Some((vec![],0)) → HTTP 200 + empty sendInitialEvents snapshot + BOOKMARK, so the informer parks at a valid RV instead of hot-looping. (Consider: should watch=true WITHOUT sendInitialEvents on a tombstoned group also avoid the hot-loop? The scout kept 410 there — a plain watch on a deleted CRD 410 is arguably fine since the informer's LIST also 410s and it should stop; but VERIFY the client actually stops rather than loops. The fix worker must confirm the non-sendInitialEvents watch path doesn't ALSO hot-loop.)
2. SECONDARY (replace_crd, cr.rs:468-475): clear the tombstone after a successful PUT (mirror create_crd cr.rs:362-363) — guards CRD re-create via PUT leaving a stale tombstone.
3. DEFENSE (find_crd cr.rs:223-225): log a warning on tombstone-deserialization failure instead of silent skip.
REGRESSION TESTS: (a) live_crd_watch_sendinitialevents_never_returns_410 (after delete/tombstone, watch+sendInitialEvents → 200+BOOKMARK not 410); (b) deleted_crd_watch_no_sendinitialevents_returns_410 (watch без sendInitialEvents still 410); (c) keep deleted_crd_group_returns_410_gone_not_404 green (non-watch 410 preserved). Findings: ai/findings/0701-crd-sendinitialevents-410-scout.md.
notes: SCOUT a10b1f5b STALLED (watchdog, no doc written) but mayor-verified its conclusion in source. KEY FINDING (cr.rs): the 410 is INTENTIONAL for DELETED CRDs — cr.rs:286-296 returns Status::gone when a CRD tombstone exists, with comment (cr.rs:204-206) 'Without 410, informers treat the response as a transient 404 and retry; 410 makes informers stop retrying' + regression test deleted_crd_group_returns_410_gone_not_404 (cr.rs:5977). So a deleted-CRD 410 is upstream-correct. BUT: list_cr (cr.rs:478) DOES call fetch_initial_events (cr.rs:532) for sendInitialEvents — and the storm CRD (webhook-8340) was LIVE mid-test (webhook.go spec running at 14:57, storm at 14:58), NOT deleted. So the HYPOTHESIS to pin: the 410 (tombstone or resourceVersion/NotOlderThan path) is MISFIRING for a sendInitialEvents watch on a STILL-EXISTING CRD → informer re-lists (CRD present) → re-watches → 410 again → hot-loop ~6000/s. The fix is NOT 'add sendInitialEvents to CRDs' (it's there) — it's 'stop returning 410 on the sendInitialEvents/NotOlderThan path for a CRD that still exists' (and ensure the deleted-CRD 410 path doesn't get hit for live CRDs). EXACT misfire line NOT yet pinned (scout died first). Fix surface: cr.rs list_cr/list_cr_namespaced + fetch_initial_events interaction + the tombstone/Gone check ordering vs sendInitialEvents. NO w8tj code overlap (w8tj=resource.rs/status.rs/watch.rs status-write propagation; jiap=cr.rs CR-watch path). Scout worktree was a10b1f5b (stalled, no doc).
close_reason: PR #633 opened: watch+sendInitialEvents on tombstoned CRD group returns 200+BOOKMARK not 410; non-watch 410 preserved; 1765 tests pass; live-verified on lima-node-smoke

title: fix(apiserver): propagationPolicy=Orphan + make cascade Orphan-aware (GC correctness, builds on #617)
description: COMBINED GC-correctness fix (supersedes the cascade-then-orphan split). Builds ON PR #617's branch (worker/mayor-3dnc-cascade-delete) — keep #617's cascade code + 3 passing fail-on-revert tests, ADD the policy gate. WHY combined: #617's cascade runs UNCONDITIONALLY (it can't read propagationPolicy because the delete handlers take no body param). So it wrongly deletes pods on an Orphan delete — 3 GC orphan specs fail on the #617 binary. title: fix(apiserver): complete owner-ref cascade-delete chain (RS->pods, RC->pods, StatefulSet->pods) to stop 110-pod node saturation
description:
VERIFIED ROOT CAUSE (scout mayor-14bw, mayor-corroborated in source): the apiserver's cascade-delete is INCOMPLETE. On owner hard-delete, owned pods are left in the store and accumulate against the node's 110-pod cap, causing OutOfpods saturation (224x in 0627-1541 run) that manufactures ~24 fake test failures + likely the 6h timeout. Same class as mayor-plmu (which fixed Deployment->RS); these are the missing next rungs.

THREE missing cascade legs in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:
1. RS->pods: delete_replicasets_owned_by (line 2078) deletes each RS via state.store.delete(&rs_key, None) but NEVER calls the EXISTING helper delete_pods_owned_by (line 2028). Add delete_pods_owned_by(state, ns, &rs_uid, "ReplicaSet") after each RS delete. (NOTE: capture rs_uid from rs[metadata][uid] before deleting.)
2. RC->pods: MISSING ENTIRELY. This is the HIGHEST saturation-impact leg -- scout found namespace replication-controller-2022 with 385 pods created and ZERO individual pod deletes. Add an RC hard-delete cascade block calling delete_pods_owned_by(..., "ReplicationController").
3. StatefulSet->pods: MISSING. Add cascade block calling delete_pods_owned_by(..., "StatefulSet").

Pattern to follow: the existing DaemonSet->pods cascade in the hard-delete path (scout cites resource.rs ~1603-1650) and the delete_pods_owned_by call there. delete_pods_owned_by already filters by ownerReferences uid+kind, so pass the correct kind string per owner.

SCOPE: cascade legs ONLY. Do NOT touch propagationPolicy/DeleteOptions/body parsing -- that is a SEPARATE bead (Fix A, held). Do NOT change delete handler signatures.
notes: Scout findings: ai/findings/0627-node-saturation-scout.md (Defect B). Prior art: mayor-plmu (Deployment->RS cascade, resource.rs). Helper delete_pods_owned_by exists at resource.rs:2028. VERIFY: (a) cargo regression tests that FAIL on revert proving each of RS/RC/StatefulSet owned-pods are deleted on owner hard-delete; (b) sonobuoy --focus GC test on the assigned VM + that pods don't accumulate. title: fix(apiserver): watch DELETE tombstone lacks .spec -> KCM replication controller nil-panics on RC delete (kills whole KCM)
notes:
KCM CRASH (whole process) during the 2026-06-26 full conformance run. Crash at 20:15:52 (VM local) in /tmp/kcm.log. KCM restarted afterward (was ALIVE on re-check) but WILL crash again on the next RC delete — every conformance RC test is a landmine. This corrupts any controller-dependent test in each KCM-down window.

PANIC (from /tmp/kcm.log, exact stack):
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core/v1.Convert_v1_ReplicationControllerSpec_To_apps_ReplicaSetSpec (conversion.go:118)  <- nil deref
  <- Convert_v1_ReplicationController_To_apps_ReplicaSet (conversion.go:108)
  <- replication.convertRCtoRS (replication/conversion.go:312)
  <- replication.conversionEventHandler.OnDelete (replication/conversion.go:175)
  -> SIGSEGV nil pointer deref -> repanicked -> whole KCM dies (sync.WaitGroup.Go re-panic; see ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md 'KCM panic propagation').
Triggering object: a ReplicationController DELETE event (namespace replication-controller-4645 logged immediately before the panic).

ROOT CAUSE (high confidence): our watch DELETE path emits a METADATA-ONLY tombstone with no .spec. See crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:183 / :202 ('Fallback: reconstruct a minimal tombstone from the store key') and :617-637 (synthetic DELETED tombstone). The upstream KCM replication controller's OnDelete handler converts the deleted RC to an RS (convertRCtoRS) and dereferences RC.spec WITHOUT a nil guard for our spec-less tombstone — so a DELETED RC event carrying only metadata nil-panics the conversion, killing KCM.

WHY NOW: the replication controller was NEWLY ENABLED this session by the --controllers='*' change (commit 1a437ce9 / #613 lineage; before that replicationcontroller was not in the KCM allowlist). So this latent watch-DELETE-tombstone gap was newly exposed. Same risk class likely exists for OTHER controllers' OnDelete handlers that read .spec of a deleted object (deployment, RS, etc.) — investigate whether they tolerate a spec-less tombstone or also need the real last-known object.

LIKELY FIX (investigate; pick the upstream-faithful one):
- Real k8s watch DELETE events carry the LAST-KNOWN FULL object (not a metadata-only tombstone). Informers wrap a truly-unknown final state in cache.DeletedFinalStateUnknown, and well-behaved handlers unwrap it — but the conversion path here assumes a full RC. The robust fix is to serve the last-known full object in the DELETED watch event (we have it in the store at delete time / in the deletion log), instead of a minimal metadata tombstone. Check what the store has available at delete time (there is a bounded deletion_log per #591) and emit the full prior object on DELETE.
- If serving the full object isn't feasible everywhere, at minimum the RC (and similar) DELETE events must carry enough of .spec that the conversion doesn't nil-deref.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) kubectl repro on a worker VM — create an RC, delete it, watch the discovery/RC watch stream and confirm the DELETED event carries .spec (not metadata-only); AND confirm KCM does NOT panic (tail /tmp/kcm.log across the delete). title: fix(proto): add enableServiceLinks (field 26) to proto PodSpec — dropped on protobuf create path
notes:
RE-SCOPED after kubectl + code investigation (original "we never default it" framing was WRONG — we DO default it, and it works for JSON-created pods).

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE: the proto PodSpec decoder (crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs:866) does NOT include enableServiceLinks. Decoded fields are only tags 1,2,3,8,10,16,17,20,29. enableServiceLinks is upstream field 26 (optional bool). A pod created via the typed Go client (protobuf — what the conformance suite uses) has the field SILENTLY DROPPED on decode. Same proto-drop class as PR #596 (CSIDriver), #597 (Service status), #600 (runtimeClassName field 29).

VERIFIED via kubectl against a live stack (run 0626 on lima-node):
- kubectl run (JSON path): .spec.enableServiceLinks = true. JSON create + apply_pod_create_defaults works.
- proto PodSpec struct: grep shows NO enable_service_links field — dropped on the protobuf path.

TYPING GUIDELINE (operator directive): the apiserver REASONS about enableServiceLinks (defaulting; the kubelet needs it non-nil), so it MUST be properly typed end-to-end, NOT raw-json-map access. The typed PodSpec (types.rs:366) already has enable_service_links: bool with default_true — correct. The proto decoder must carry the field so it flows into that typed representation.

FIX:
1. Add the field to proto PodSpec (proto.rs:866) at tag 26, optional bool, and emit it from pod_spec_to_json when present (optional so an explicit false survives; absent stays absent so defaulting sets true). Follow the runtimeClassName tag-29 pattern added in #600.
2. IN SCOPE IF CLEAN (per typing guideline): the defaulting at pods.rs:2730 uses raw pod[spec][enableServiceLinks].is_null() map access. Prefer routing the default through the typed PodSpec rather than raw map access, consistent with the guideline. If that turns out to be a larger refactor than the bug warrants, do the proto fix and note the raw-access cleanup as a follow-on — do NOT sprawl.

CAVEAT (do NOT overclaim): the create-path defaulting (apply_pod_create_defaults, pods.rs:338) SHOULD still set enableServiceLinks=true even when proto drops it (dropped -> null -> defaulted). So the proto gap alone may NOT fully explain the single var-expansion nil-error in run 0625-2158. VERIFY by reproducing: create a pod via protobuf with enableServiceLinks unset AND with it explicitly false; confirm both round-trip correctly. If the var-expansion failure persists, there is a SECOND gap (e.g. a kubelet-facing read/watch proto ENCODER also missing the field) — report it, do not silently assume fixed.

ACCEPTANCE:
(a) unit test — proto PodSpec round-trips enableServiceLinks (both true and explicit false survive decode);
(b) kubectl repro against the worker VM — a protobuf-created pod shows the correct .spec.enableServiceLinks;
(c) if feasible, rerun the var-expansion conformance spec and report whether the pod now starts.
Surface: proto.rs (+ possibly pods.rs defaulting). Needs VM for (b)/(c).

Unit test enable_service_links_survives_proto_decode_so_kubelet_can_build_pod_env passes. kubectl repro: esl-false-test=false, esl-absent-test=true. pods.rs defaulting already uses typed access — no follow-on needed. notes:

The test (service.go:3269) does:

title: fix(apiserver): set pod.status.qosClass at admission time based on resource requests/limits
notes: Root cause: Pod.status.qosClass is never set by the apiserver. Kubernetes sets this field at admission time by inspecting container resource requests and limits. If all containers have matching requests==limits for both CPU and memory, class is 'Guaranteed'; if any request < limit, 'Burstable'; if no requests, 'BestEffort'. Representative failure: node/pods.go:200 expects 'Guaranteed', gets empty string. Fix: in the pod create/update handler in handlers/pods.rs, compute and set status.qosClass before persisting. Also investigate pod.metadata.generation starting at 2 not 1 (node/pods.go:530) — generation should start at 0 for pods (pods are not generation-tracked in the same way as deployments; the test expects 1 after create). Both are admission-time defaults in the same code path.

title: Job pod finalizer-removal never converges: apiserver rv mismatch on pod update → stuck Terminating, GC never completes
description:
Split from mayor-q161. q161's store get() 404 fix is necessary but NOT sufficient: with that fix applied (pod-GET false-404s dropped 105684->0, verified), the conformance test 'should delete a job' STILL fails 0/1 in 330s because of a SECOND independent bug. The kubelet sees a phantom pod spec/status diff on every reconcile and recreates the sandbox ~1/sec: 944 sandbox attempts for 2 pods in 5.5min, each ending 'Shutting down, got signal: Terminated', with ~28 PATCH /status per sec. This is the documented apply_status_patch phantom-array issue in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs (its own comment: 'Storing them literally causes the kubelet to detect phantom array changes on every reconcile and continuously recreate the pod sandbox'). The kubelet does a GET then PATCH /status each cycle; if the GET response body differs from what the kubelet last wrote (field reordering, empty-vs-null array, or a status array normalized differently on read), the kubelet believes the pod spec changed and recreates. REPRO (reliable, low-concurrency, ~5min): scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm --port

--kubelet-port --reset --focus '\[sig-apps\] Job .*should delete a job.*\[Conformance\]' — currently fails; will pass when phantom diff is gone. NEXT: run apiserver at RUST_LOG=debug, capture two consecutive kubelet GET pod response BODIES + the PATCH between them for one pod, diff to find the oscillating field. Suspects (per prior worker): containerStatuses ordering, empty-vs-null initContainerStatuses/ephemeralContainerStatuses, conditions ordering. Fix in handlers/pods.rs (apply_status_patch + the pod GET serialization / proto round-trip). Regression test must assert a pod status that round-trips through GET is byte/structure-stable vs what was PATCHed. Depends-on: mayor-q161 (the 404 fix PR).
notes:
2026-06-25T01:05Z ROOT CAUSE FOUND + kubectl-REPRODUCED (no sonobuoy). Read the REAL e2e.txt (podlogs/sonobuoy/.../logs/e2e.txt, not plugins/.../e2e.log): the test does NOT wait 5min for Running — it created the Job at 00:06:59 and DELETED it at 00:07:01 (2s later, pods reached Running fine). Failure is in the GC/delete phase (job.go:907): 'error while waiting for pods gone foo: there are 1 pods left, foo-e95ca'. Pods orphaned, never deleted.

KUBECTL REPRO on #583 worktree cluster: create the Job (parallelism2/completions4, pause), wait 5s (2/2 Running, ownerRefs->Job correct), then . Result: job deleted, BUT both pods survive indefinitely with deletionTimestamp set (01:04:22) — STUCK TERMINATING.

ROOT CAUSE (KCM /tmp/kcm.log): 'syncing orphan pod failed err=Pod foo-d4803 cannot be updated: resource version mismatch (expected 259, current 265)' and same for foo-e95ca (expected 266 current 269). The pods keep the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking FINALIZER. KCM job-controller must remove that finalizer via an optimistic-concurrency UPDATE/PATCH (If-Match rv), but the apiserver reports a DIFFERENT current rv than KCM read, so every update 409/conflicts; KCM re-reads, retries, conflicts again — FOREVER. Finalizer never removed -> pod never deletes -> GC never completes -> test fails. THIS IS the ~3,283 pod-main-resource PATCH loop seen earlier (finalizer-removal retries), unified with the stuck-pods + GC-failure into ONE bug.

CLASS: WAL stale-read / rv-consistency on the read-modify-write path (#574/#580 family) — but specifically the resourceVersion returned to a GET that precedes a conditional UPDATE is stale/ahead of what the next read sees, so optimistic concurrency never converges. NOT status churn, NOT sandbox churn, NOT proto template (that was #583, a real separate fix). 

NEXT (dispatchable, tight): make the apiserver's pod update path return/accept a consistent resourceVersion so an optimistic UPDATE following a GET converges. Where to look: store put() rv assignment + the conditional-update (expected_revision) path in handlers + the read rv the GET returns (must be the same rv the subsequent If-Match update expects). Repro is kubectl-only now: create job, delete --cascade=foreground, assert pods gone within 30s; regression-testable at the store/handler level (conditional update after read must not spuriously conflict). #583 should still merge (real proto fix); it is NOT this bug.
close_reason: PR #587 opened — fixes job pod GC via 5 bugs: patch_pod retry loop, hard-delete on patch, apply_status_patch protects finalizers, job delete cascade cleanup, and JobSpec template proto decode. 6th conformance run: 20 Passed | 0 Failed.

title: store get() returns 404 for existing pods under stale WAL read (phantom not-found)
description: Job focus run 0624-1813 (binary WITH #578+#579): 4 pass / 15 fail. #578 confirmed working (KCM /tmp/kcm.log has ZERO 'no labels' errors; pods ARE created + scheduled + bound). NEW failure mode, distinct from mayor-63rq: pods reach Running but DO NOT HOLD it under concurrent load. Evidence: temp/e2e/0624-1813-job-conformance/pod-logs/var/log/pods/job-6560_foo-88ad1*/ contains 454 separate container log files spanning 18:05:04-18:13:49 (~9 min), each a distinct sandbox attempt ending 'Shutting down, got signal: Terminated' — i.e. kubelet recreates the sandbox ~1/sec. apiserver.log shows 443 PATCH .../pods/foo-88ad1/status for the same pod (one per churn cycle). The existing apply_status_patch comment in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs already documents this exact class: 'Storing them literally causes the kubelet to detect phantom array changes on every reconcile and continuously recreate the pod sandbox.' Suspect a field that normalizes/serializes inconsistently under concurrent writes (podIPs, containerStatuses, conditions ordering, or empty-vs-absent array) OR a WAL stale-read returning an older status revision to the kubelet's GET-before-PATCH (related to #574 wal_autocheckpoint). notes: 2026-06-24T11:54Z SCOPE NARROWED to the store read-consistency 404 fix only. The sandbox-churn sub-symptom is SPLIT to mayor-okoy (kubelet phantom spec/status diff). Land this fix on its own merits (it eliminates a real read-consistency bug); okoy continues separately. list() does NOT need the same fix — it returns ListResponse with a revision (never None), guard already correct.

title: PATCH /status drops metadata changes (annotations/labels) for all resources
description: Focus run 0624-1415-job-conformance: '[sig-apps] CronJob should support CronJob API operations [Conformance]' fails in 0.06s (not a timeout — a real API bug). Test does PATCH /apis/batch/v1/namespaces/<ns>/cronjobs/<n>/status with metadata.annotations[patchedstatus]=true, then GETs and asserts the annotation is present. apiserver returns 200 for the PATCH (apiserver.log 05:04:41.469 PATCH .../cronjobs/test-api/status status=200) but the annotation never lands. Failure: 'patched object should have the applied annotation / Expected {updated,patched} to have {patchedstatus: true}'. Root cause hypothesis: the /status subresource PATCH handler merges only spec.status (or status) and discards metadata changes from the patch body. Upstream status-subresource semantics: PATCH /status MAY update metadata (labels/annotations) and status, and MUST ignore spec. Our handler appears to drop metadata.annotations. Where to look: the status subresource patch path in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/ (resource.rs / status patch / merge logic). Confirm against pod /status PATCH too (pods/.../status also used heavily in Job tests — check whether pod status patches preserve metadata). Fix: in /status PATCH, apply the patch to metadata + status, preserve spec from stored object. Regression test (Rule 14): PATCH /status with metadata.annotations[x]=y must result in stored object having that annotation, while spec is unchanged. NOTE: this is one of the 15 Job/CronJob conformance failures; the other 14 were the missing-Job-selector bug fixed in #578. This one is independent.
notes:
2026-06-24T06:47Z REPRODUCED from kubectl against live mayor cluster (server v1.36.0). Minimal repro:
1. kubectl -n NS patch cronjob X --subresource=status --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"patchedstatus":"true"}}}'  -> returns 'patched' (200)
2. kubectl -n NS get cronjob X -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.patchedstatus}'  -> EMPTY (annotation dropped)
CONTRAST: patching a status FIELD via --subresource=status DOES persist (set status.lastScheduleTime, read back present). So the /status handler applies 'status' but discards 'metadata'.
SCOPE BROADER THAN CRONJOB: same defect reproduced on a Pod — patch pod --subresource=status with metadata.annotations -> annotation dropped. This affects the status subresource for ALL resources, not just CronJob. Any controller/test that sets metadata via /status (annotations, labels, managedFields) loses it.
Upstream semantics: PATCH/PUT on /status updates status + metadata, ignores spec. Our handler updates status + (likely) preserves spec from stored object but does NOT merge the incoming metadata.
Fix location: the /status subresource write path in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/ (status update/patch + merge). Apply patch to metadata AND status; keep spec from stored object.
Regression test (Rule 14): /status PATCH with metadata.annotations[x]=y -> stored object has annotation x=y AND spec unchanged. Add for at least pod + a batch resource.
SIDE OBSERVATION: during repro the CronJob spawned Jobs (status.active populated with cj-repro-* jobs w/ uids) — confirms #578 Job selector generation works live (KCM now creates Job pods).
close_reason: PR #579 opened

title: apiserver: namespace sub-resource objects return 404 mid-test while namespace exists
description:
Objects within namespaces return 404 mid-test while the namespace itself still exists. The test framework interprets this as 'namespace already deleted' but apiserver logs show the namespace is intact — only the watchdog deletes it, at its scheduled time (~15min later).

Evidence from apiserver.log cross-referenced with e2e log and run.log:
- deployment-6664: test failed at 20:04:10 (ReplicaSet 'webserver-deployment-6488dd958c' not found). Namespace DELETE only at 20:19:06 by watchdog. Between 20:04:01 and 20:19:05 no DELETE of the namespace appears in apiserver log.
- var-expansion-2193: framework cleanup got 404 at 16:00:15 but watchdog only acted at 16:15:45. Namespace was missing from apiserver's perspective for 15 min with no DELETE logged.
- cronjob-5750, statefulset-7199, job-7985: watchdog and e2e cleanup simultaneous (~same second).

Root cause hypothesis: u7s apiserver returns 404 for namespace sub-resource queries (GET /api/v1/namespaces/<name>/pods, ReplicaSet lookups) on resources that still exist in the store. Possible causes: (1) stale read from SqliteStore returning miss despite object present, (2) namespace-scoped list/get filtering bug dropping results, (3) object deleted by KCM GC controller before test expects it.

The 'namespace termination hangs' framing was wrong — namespaces terminate normally. The real bug is objects disappearing from sub-resource listings mid-test. This is a correctness bug in namespace-scoped GET/LIST routing or store reads.
close_reason: no bug: audit confirms all 404s occur after watchdog DELETE, not before. The 15-minute window in the bead description was a UTC vs e2e-local-clock offset. Code paths (get_namespaced_resource, list_sync, delete_namespace_resources) are correct. See ai/findings/z5fo-namespace-subresource-404-audit-2026-06-24.md

title: apiserver: missing default_job/default_cronjob + shared pod template defaulting across workloads
description:
Root cause: apply_defaults has default_deployment/replicaset/statefulset/daemonset but NO default_job or default_cronjob. Jobs only get generation=1 from initialize_workload_generation. KCM job_controller merges job-name/job-uid labels into spec.template.metadata.labels — panics nil pointer at job_controller.go:1067 if that map is null. This kills the entire KCM process, so no default SAs are created in any subsequent test namespace — causing 168 cascading [BeforeEach] failures (confirmed by live KCM restart restoring SA provisioning).

Fix plan:
1. Extract a shared default_pod_template(template: &mut Value) function that defaults: metadata.labels to {}, metadata.annotations to {}, spec.enableServiceLinks to true, and any other pod template fields currently duplicated across default_deployment/replicaset/statefulset/daemonset.
2. Add default_job(obj) that calls default_pod_template(&mut obj[spec][template]) and defaults job-specific fields (spec.backoffLimit, spec.completions, spec.parallelism as appropriate per Kubernetes defaulting).
3. Add default_cronjob(obj) similarly for the inner jobTemplate.
4. Wire default_job and default_cronjob into apply_defaults.
5. Audit default_deployment/replicaset/statefulset/daemonset — replace any duplicated pod template defaulting with calls to default_pod_template.
6. The enableServiceLinks bug (mayor-cmtn) is likely also resolved by step 1 if default_pod_template sets it — verify and close mayor-cmtn if so.

Regression tests: job with nil template labels must not panic KCM (unit test: apply_defaults for batch/jobs produces labels={}); cronjob equivalent; pod template enableServiceLinks defaults to true via default_pod_template.
close_reason: default_job/default_cronjob added; shared default_pod_template extracts labels/annotations/{}/enableServiceLinks defaulting for all workload pod templates. Merged in #566.

title: apiserver: resource uid (metadata.uid) not populated on ServiceAccount create
description: KCM tokens_controller logs 'invalid serviceaccount key: uid empty' for every test namespace default SA. This means our apiserver returns SA objects with metadata.uid=="" — the UID is not being generated/assigned on SA create. Real Kubernetes assigns a UUID to metadata.uid on every resource create. This is likely a missing step in the SA-specific create handler or a gap in the generic object defaulting path. Check: does the SA create path call the same uid-generation logic as Pod/Namespace/etc create? A single fix here resolves 168 cascading [BeforeEach] failures.
close_reason: Invalid diagnosis. SA uid is correctly populated when KCM is running (confirmed live: b7c570c5-0f6c-4484-8608-4ad607282cb6). The empty-uid tokens_controller errors were KCM processing stale events from watchdog-deleted namespaces. The 168 cascade failures were caused by KCM being dead after the Job controller panic (mayor-md7t) — not by empty SA uids.

title: apiserver: default ServiceAccount not provisioned within 120s in test namespaces
description: 168 conformance tests fail in [BeforeEach] at framework.go:372 with 'wait for service account default in namespace X: timed out waiting for the condition'. Root cause identified from KCM logs: tokens_controller.go:255 logs 'invalid serviceaccount key: serviceaccount.serviceAccountQueueKey{namespace:X, name:default, uid:""}' for every test namespace SA. KCM rejects SA queue entries with empty uid — so it never creates the SA token secret. Our API server is returning ServiceAccount objects with metadata.uid=="" (empty string) instead of a real UUID on create. Fix: ensure metadata.uid is populated (via uuid generation) on SA create, same as other resources. Where to look: the SA create handler or the generic object defaulting path that assigns UIDs.
close_reason: Root cause identified as mayor-md7t: KCM job_controller panic kills entire KCM process, so no default SAs are created after the crash. SA provisioning itself works correctly when KCM is running (confirmed live). Closing in favour of mayor-md7t.

title: watch: context canceled cascade degrades all long-running conformance tests
description: Full conformance run (0622-1839): watch stream errors 'Watch failed err=context canceled' begin at ~06:35 UTC (2.5h into run) and become constant by 08:40.
