title: fix(apiserver): CR watch field selectors ignore CRD-declared selectableFields; CR watch never converts across versions
description:
DISCOVERED FROM mayor-lshow while verifying the live sonobuoy gate for CustomResourceFieldSelectors after fixing CR LIST field-selector plumbing.

STATUS AFTER mayor-lshow: the LIST portion of [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceFieldSelectors "MUST list and watch custom resources matching the field selector [Conformance]" now PASSES — all 4 LIST sub-assertions (v2 host=host1; v2 host=host1,port=80; v1 hostPort=host1:80; v1 hostPort=host1:8080, the last two requiring real webhook conversion) pass. The test now fails LATER, at crd_selectable_fields.go:251, the FIRST watch assertion:

  [FAILED] Timed out after 30.000s.
  Expected added: {cr-a, cr-b} (only host=host1 matches)
  Actual   added: {cr-a, cr-b, cr-c, <namespace-name>} (all 3 CRs plus a stray namespace-name event)

Evidence: temp/e2e/0716-1704-customresourcefieldselectors/podlogs/sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-c6276120564d4936/logs/e2e.txt (lines 17-113).

TWO DISTINCT ROOT CAUSES, both in the CR watch path (list_cr/list_cr_namespaced's `query.watch == Some(true)` branches, which call watch::watch_generic/fetch_initial_events):

1. FIELD-SELECTOR GENERICITY GAP: `object_matches_field_selector` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs) only recognizes 3 hardcoded fields — metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName. Any other field name (e.g. a CRD-declared `host`/`port`/`hostPort`) falls through the `_ => {}` catch-all and is silently IGNORED, meaning the term always passes — so a CR watch with `fieldSelector=host=host1` currently streams every CR regardless of its host value. Contrast with the NEW `cr_matches_field_selector` in cr.rs (added by mayor-lshow for LIST), which correctly consults the CRD's declared `selectableFields` and treats undeclared fields as absent — that function (or equivalent logic) needs to reach the watch path too, likely by threading CrContext (or just namespaced + selectable_fields) into WatchConfig and having watch.rs's per-event filtering call it for CR sources instead of (or in addition to) object_matches_field_selector.

2. NO CROSS-VERSION CONVERSION IN WATCH AT ALL: list_cr/list_cr_namespaced convert stored CR bytes to the requested version before serving LIST/GET (see convert_cr_list_items, object_needs_conversion — fixed for LIST by #829/#830). The watch path (fetch_initial_events + the live broadcast consumption in watch_generic) has NO equivalent — it streams raw stored bytes with only apiVersion/kind string fields overwritten, never calling the CRD's conversion webhook. In the conformance test, all 3 CRs are stored natively in v2 shape (created via the v2 client); a watch on v1 (`v1hostPortWatch`, selector hostPort=host1:80) would see raw v2-shaped bodies with no `hostPort` key at all, so even a perfect fix for (1) would still leave the v1-watch assertions (crd_selectable_fields.go:257-259, 299-301) failing. This is a substantial, separate feature (invoking an async webhook per historical+live watched event) — likely deserving its own design, not a small patch.

Fixing (1) alone will NOT turn the overall conformance test green (2) still blocks the v1-based watch assertions — but it's necessary and independently valuable (matches CR watches to same-version field selectors, which covers 2 of the 3 watch/informer assertion groups in this test). Consider splitting into two beads: one for (1), one for (2).

Verify with: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm <VM> --port <PORT> --kubelet-port <KUBELET_PORT> --focus "CustomResourceFieldSelectors"
notes:
PHASE-1 DESIGN COMPLETE + OPERATOR DECISION (2026-07-21). Root-cause-2 confirmed live: CR watch path never converts across versions. Two hook points in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs: (A) initial/backlog via fetch_initial_events (244-269), consumed 635-658 (restamp-only 651-654); (B) live events Added/Modified 712-744 + Deleted 803-804 via encode_watch_event (128-221, restamp-only). Convert-then-filter: LIST does it right (convert_cr_list_items cr.rs:1105 BEFORE cr_matches_field_selector retain cr.rs:1113-1117); both watch hooks currently filter the UNCONVERTED body — the bug.

FIX PLAN (Phase 3): reuse existing primitives, no reinvention. Hook A: in list_cr/list_cr_namespaced (cr.rs ~1027-1057, ~1669-1699) call convert_cr_list_items on initial_items.0 after fetch_initial_events returns, before building WatchConfig (zero watch.rs change for A). Hook B: CrFieldSelectorContext (watch.rs:476-479) gains conversion_webhook_client_config: Option<Value>; watch_generic_impl clones state into the stream (mirror _store_keepalive at line 585) and calls cr::call_conversion_webhook at both live sites when object apiVersion != target (mirror object_needs_conversion cr.rs:292-299). MUST convert BEFORE the #858 field-selector filter at both hooks. ~230-340 LoC, one helper, ONE PR.

OPERATOR DECISION: per-object/per-watcher conversion now (same-version short-circuits free), NO cache in this PR. The per-version-Cacher optimization (upstream architecture) is filed as follow-up mayor-zw0ou, to do as soon as conformance is green. This closes tv4ob root-cause-2; tv4ob can close when CustomResourceFieldSelectors passes fully.
PHASE 3 IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-21). Root-cause-2 (CR watch never converts across versions) is FIXED and verified: (1) unit/integration regression tests in cr.rs (3 new tests, each experimentally confirmed to fail when its specific mechanism is reverted); (2) live before/after repro on lima-node-3 — pre-fix binary: v1 watch+hostPort selector delivered NOTHING for a live-created v2 CR (confirmed via kubectl and apiserver.log showing zero conversion-webhook calls); post-fix binary: same repro delivers the CR converted to v1 (hostPort present), and a same-version v2 watch still works while making ZERO webhook calls (short-circuit confirmed); (3) focused conformance run: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --focus "CustomResourceFieldSelectors" now passes ALL LIST, WATCH, and informer field-selector assertions (crd_selectable_fields.go:229-267) instantly — this is the exact assertion set root-cause-2 blocked.

HOWEVER the overall CustomResourceFieldSelectors conformance test still FAILS, at a NEW, later, DISTINCT step: crd_selectable_fields.go:272, a DeleteCollection call with a field selector against the CRD-backed resource returns 404. Root cause: delete_collection_resource/delete_collection_namespaced_resource (resource.rs) have NO fallback to cr:: handling at all (unlike every other verb) and ignore field_selector even for built-in resources. This is root-cause-3, out of scope for this PR (different files, different mechanism, substantial standalone feature gap) — filed as mayor-qki6l (discovered-from this bead).

Per the bead's own instructions, NOT closing this bead since CustomResourceFieldSelectors does not fully pass yet — leaving that decision to the mayor once mayor-qki6l is also resolved. PR opened with full before/after evidence; quality gates green.
close_reason: CustomResourceFieldSelectors FULLY PASSES as of PR #866 (focused gate: 1 Passed). The hydra had 5 distinct root causes, all now fixed: #858 watch selectable-field filter, #861 conversion-webhook Accept header, #862 CR watch cross-version conversion, #863 DeleteCollection CR-fallback+field-selector, #866 watch synthetic-DELETE only-for-previously-matched. Verified via full-run 0721-1556 progression + per-head focused gates. Follow-up mayor-zw0ou (per-version conversion cache, Phase-5 perf) remains open by design.

title: fix(apiserver): CR LIST ignores field_selector — CustomResourceFieldSelectors conformance test fails
description:
Discovered live while verifying mayor-00kan's conversion-webhook self-call fix (sonobuoy --focus "CustomResourceConversionWebhook|CustomResourceFieldSelectors", 2026-07-16). 2 of 3 target tests now pass; this one still fails, but with a DIFFERENT root cause unrelated to conversion webhooks.

FAILING TEST: [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceFieldSelectors ... MUST list and watch custom resources matching the field selector [Conformance]

FAILURE (from junit, crd_selectable_fields.go:232):
  [FAILED] Expected <sets.Set[string] | len:3>: {selectable-field-cr64tkh, selectable-field-crlwlxd, selectable-field-crvf6ht}
  to equal <sets.Set[string] | len:2>: {selectable-field-crlwlxd, selectable-field-crvf6ht}

The test creates 3 CRs, then LISTs with a field selector (e.g. host=host1) matching a CRD-declared x-kubernetes-selectable-fields entry, and expects only 2 of the 3 back. u7s returns all 3 — the field selector is silently ignored on CR LIST.

ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs): list_cr (~line 984) and list_cr_namespaced (~line 1610) both hardcode

    ListOptions { field_selector: None, limit: query.limit, continue_key }

when calling state.store.list(...) for the non-watch LIST path — query.field_selector (the actual client-requested selector) is discarded. Contrast with the WATCH path in the same two functions, a few lines above, which DOES pass query.field_selector through to fetch_initial_events/WatchConfig correctly. So CR watches may filter by field selector but CR LIST never does.

Fixing this likely requires: (1) plumbing query.field_selector into the store list() call, and (2) resolving CRD-declared selectableFields (which reference arbitrary JSON paths like .spec.host, not just metadata.name/namespace) against each stored CR's JSON body, since the generic field-selector matcher used for built-in resources may only understand fixed metadata fields. Verify against the CRD's spec.versions[].selectableFields extraction (find_crd doesn't currently extract this at all — check).

Verify with: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm <VM> --port <PORT> --kubelet-port <KUBELET_PORT> --focus "CustomResourceFieldSelectors"
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #836): PASS -- with an important scope caveat. Fix is correct and well-tested. Worker found the real subtlety: selectableFields must be matched IN-MEMORY POST-conversion (the store cannot see version-converted CR shapes), and verified against upstream (crd_selectable_fields.go, customresource/strategy.go, fields/selector.go fetched to temp/research) that an undeclared field resolves to empty string, NOT a 400 -- correcting this bead's original assumption. Added the missing selectableFields extraction to crd.rs (parse_crd/patch_crd silently dropped it -- another latent gap). Extracted a shared json_path_equals matcher: I diffed the old inline sqlite.rs matcher vs the new fn and confirmed BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING (identical dot-walk, identical absent-field zero-value fallback that the scheduler's spec.nodeName= watch depends on, identical terminal String/Bool/Null/Number match) -- built-in field selectors are not affected. 3 fail-on-revert tests + 6 json_path_equals unit tests. SCOPE CAVEAT: this closes the LIST half of CustomResourceFieldSelectors (all 4 LIST sub-assertions now pass live, incl the 2 needing the real conversion webhook), but the WATCH half remains red -- CR watch's matcher only knows 3 hardcoded fields and does no cross-version conversion; correctly deferred as follow-on mayor-tv4ob (materially larger: needs cross-version conversion in the watch path). So the CustomResourceFieldSelectors conformance test is NOT fully green until tv4ob lands. Merging this on CI green regardless -- it is correct, additive, and closes real LIST-side functionality.
close_reason: PR #836 opened — CR LIST field-selector plumbing + selectableFields extraction/matching fixed and verified live (kubectl + sonobuoy: all 4 LIST sub-assertions in CustomResourceFieldSelectors now pass, including real-webhook-conversion cases). Overall conformance test still red on a separate, pre-existing watch-side gap, filed as mayor-tv4ob (discovered-from this bead).

title: fix(apiserver): namespace delete self-clears kubernetes finalizer synchronously — real KCM ns-controller never fires, NamespaceDeletionContentFailure condition never set
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: [sig-api-machinery] OrderedNamespaceDeletion 'namespace deletion should delete pod first' FAILS 'namespace ... has not been processed by namespace controller: context deadline exceeded' (namespace.go:579), after polling every 2s for 5min (302s). The test never even reaches its second assertion (pod-deleted-before-configmap ordering, namespace.go:581-610).

Reproduced live by Scout C on lima-node-4: created ns + pod (with finalizer) + configmap, then kubectl delete namespace -> spec.finalizers is ALREADY empty within ~1s (a control ns starts as ['kubernetes']); status.phase=Terminating. limactl shell grep of /tmp/kcm.log for the ns -> ZERO matches: the real upstream kube-controller-manager namespace controller (confirmed running: 'Starting namespace controller') NEVER touches this namespace. apiserver.log confirms no /finalize or ns /status PATCH ever occurs for it.

ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/namespaces.rs:988-1000, in delete_namespace): code comment states the design -- 'u7s has no namespace lifecycle controller, so we immediately remove the kubernetes finalizer (acting as the namespace controller)'. This synchronous self-clear happens INSIDE the DELETE handler, before the real KCM namespace-controller informer can ever observe deletionTimestamp != nil AND 'kubernetes' in spec.finalizers -- its only trigger. So the real (unmodified) namespace controller never runs its v1.34+ KEP-5080 ordered-content-deletion sequence and never PATCHes status.conditions with NamespaceDeletionContentFailure -- exactly what the test polls for, forever. u7s's own cascade (mayor-74j3.1) DOES soft-delete the finalizer-blocked pod and hard-delete the configmap (roughly pod-first in EFFECT), but the test can't observe it because the condition it gates on is permanently unreachable.

FIX DIRECTION (two candidates): (a) stop self-clearing spec.finalizers, let the real KCM namespace controller own it end-to-end (riskier -- must verify KCM reliably completes within conformance timeouts before removing the fast synchronous path); or (b) keep the self-managed cascade but have u7s itself emit the NamespaceDeletionContentFailure condition it is already simulating the rest of the controller's job for.

REGRESSION RISK: the existing cascade_delete_respects_object_finalizers test (namespaces.rs:3918) locks in the current fast-path behavior and must keep passing. mayor-cdqjc (setElementOrder patch leak) is confirmed UNRELATED (this flow issues no PATCH). Needs Lima VM verification. Child of mayor-74j3 (namespace deletion / GC cascade epic).
close_reason: PR #860 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/860 — delete_namespace no longer self-clears the kubernetes finalizer; real KCM namespace-controller now drives termination + sets status.conditions. Live-verified 3x (finalizer'd pod + KCM conditions, anti-wedge RC scenario, ordinary namespace) plus focused conformance run: SUCCESS 2 Passed 0 Failed. Follow-up filed as mayor-njkk1 for the cluster-scoped DeleteCollection twin bug.

title: fix(apiserver): pod/service proxy subresources don't parse scheme:name:port; pod proxy doesn't parse name:port at all
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: [sig-network] Proxy version v1 'should proxy through a service and a pod' FAILS (proxy.go:326, aggregated table-test). Reproduced live by Scout C on lima-node-4 -- exact match to every failure pattern:
  pods/proxy-test/proxy/                    -> 200 OK    (bare name works)
  pods/proxy-test:8080/proxy/               -> 404 'Pod "proxy-test:8080" not found'
  pods/http:proxy-test:8080/proxy/          -> 404 'Pod "http:proxy-test:8080" not found'
  services/proxy-test-svc:web/proxy/        -> 200 OK    (name:port works)
  services/http:proxy-test-svc:web/proxy/   -> 404 'Service "http:proxy-test-svc" not found'

ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs) -- two related gaps parsing k8s' scheme:name:port proxy addressing:
- Pods: resolve_pod_proxy_target (proxy.rs:1379-1413) does ZERO parsing -- literal store lookup on the raw path segment, port from the pod's own spec, ignoring the URL. ANY name:port or scheme:name:port pod-proxy URL 404s.
- Services: split_service_port (proxy.rs:1756-1761) does rsplit_once(':') -- correct for 2-part name:port (mayor-fgt2's fix) but for 3-part scheme:name:port it splits on the LAST colon, so bare_name='http:svcname' leaks the scheme into the name lookup -> 404.

Prior proxy fixes (mayor-fgt2 services, mayor-oj7t nodes) only handled the 2-part suffix form; pods never got equivalent handling and the 3-part scheme-prefixed form was never handled anywhere.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) give resolve_pod_proxy_target the same suffix-parsing split_service_port already does for services, using the URL-supplied port instead of always defaulting to the pod spec's first port; (2) make split_service_port (and the new pod equivalent) strip an optional leading http:/https: scheme token before the bare-name split.

Needs Lima VM verification. Regression tests: assert non-404 for all 3 wire forms (name, name:port, scheme:name:port) on BOTH pods and services.
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #837): PASS -- with a scope caveat like lshow. Parsing fix is correct and well-tested. split_scheme_name_port strips http:/https: only when a second colon confirms the genuine 3-part form -- so http:8080 parses as name=http port=8080 (NOT a bare-scheme misread) and a name merely starting with http is not mangled; both have explicit anti-overreach tests. Shared helper used by split_service_port (now a one-line delegate) and the new pod path (extend-don't-fork). resolve_pod_container_port mirrors the existing resolve_eps_port convention. Fail-on-revert verified empirically (reverted prod, all 6 tests failed with pre-fix symptoms, restored+checksum-verified). Single file, on-surface. Live: all 5 URL forms 404->200, zero 404s across 320 sonobuoy attempts. SCOPE CAVEAT: the parsing bug is fixed but the aggregated Proxy ginkgo spec stays RED for two DISTINCT pre-existing gaps that reproduce even on the never-broken bare-pod-name form -- HTML link rewriting (mayor-rmqrl) and https-scheme->TLS-backend (mayor-vkkma), correctly filed separately rather than absorbed. So the Proxy conformance test is NOT fully green until rmqrl+vkkma land too. Merging -- the parsing fix is correct, surgical, and closes its scope.
close_reason: PR #837 opened — fix verified live on lima-node-4 (kubectl before/after all 3 wire forms x pods/services, zero 404s across full Proxy conformance table-test). Two separate pre-existing gaps surfaced by the same test filed as mayor-rmqrl (HTML rewrite) and mayor-vkkma (https TLS backend).

title: fix(apiserver): AdmissionWebhook CONNECT/pods-attach deny not enforced against a REACHABLE backend on the POST/SPDY retry path (mayor-u6eb fix incomplete)
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook 'should be able to deny attaching pod' FAILS at webhook.go:1481 -- expected the attach to be denied with 'attaching to pod ... is not allowed', but instead got 'timed out waiting for command'. The attach was NEVER denied: it fully upgraded to an interactive session and hung.

Scout B (lima-node-3) proved the matching/invocation layer is SOUND today: a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration matching the exact e2e shape (pods/attach, CONNECT, namespaceSelector, failurePolicy:Fail) pointing at a DELIBERATELY UNREACHABLE service correctly denied via the WebSocket(GET) path ('unable to upgrade connection: admission webhook ... failed to respond'). NamespaceSelector, CONNECT-verb resource/subResource wire-split (unit-tested admission.rs:9342), and Fail-on-unreachable all verified sound.

The GAP is on the REACHABLE-backend deny path. Context: mayor-u6eb/PR #705 (2026-07-06) fixed the OLD symptom -- client-go's remotecommand executor dials WebSocket(GET) first, treats our correct 403 denial as an upgrade-failure and silently retries via POST(SPDY); the old POST route hit pod_attach's WebSocketUpgrade extractor which 405'd BEFORE admission re-ran, masking the denial. u6eb added pod_attach_post to re-run admission on POST. The CURRENT failure looks like that fix is INCOMPLETE: against a reachable backend that should DENY, the POST/SPDY path either doesn't enforce the denial or doesn't parse the webhook response -- the session upgrades and hangs instead of being denied.

FIX DIRECTION: trace pod_attach_post -- confirm it actually runs admission AND surfaces a webhook DENY (not just pod-lookup) on the SPDY-retry path against a reachable backend. Also check /exec (mayor-c7r3 filed the identical pattern for exec).

NEEDS a follow-up live session with a REAL webhook backend deployed (deploy agnhost webhook pod + the two-webhook VWC matching upstream webhook.go shape) -- Scout B only exercised the fail-closed path due to budget. This is the ONE failure in run 0715-2142 not conclusively root-caused; the repro recipe above is the next diagnostic step.

title: fix(apiserver): CR field-validation unknown-field wording must branch on request type (SSA Apply-patch vs Create/Update) — regressed by mayor-w1p59
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: TWO failures, both reproduced live by Scout B on lima-node-3:
- [sig-api-machinery] FieldValidation 'should create/apply an invalid CR with extra properties for CRD with validation schema' (field_validation.go:462, asserts response contains '.unknownField: field not declared in schema')
- [sig-api-machinery] FieldValidation 'should detect unknown metadata fields in both the root and embedded object of a CR' (field_validation.go:611, asserts '.metadata.unknownMeta: field not declared in schema' OR '.spec.template.metadata.unknownSubMeta: ...')

Both tests use rest.Patch(types.ApplyPatchType) with ?fieldValidation=Strict. u7s CORRECTLY detects+rejects the unknown fields (live repro: 'The request is invalid: strict decoding error: unknown field "unknownField"', all 3 unknown paths correctly identified). This is NOT a missing-feature gap -- it is a MESSAGE-WORDING mismatch for the SSA/Apply-patch request type.

ROOT CAUSE (RULE-7 CONFLICT -- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:786-813, apply_cr_field_validation): always emits 'strict decoding error: unknown field "<path>"'. mayor-w1p59/PR #773 (2026-07-14) DELIBERATELY changed the wording to this (from the dotted '.foo: field not declared in schema' SSA form) to fix 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI works for CRD with validation schema' -- a plain-CREATE test. That was correct FOR CREATE. But mayor-ago8/PR #722 had originally used the dotted SSA wording precisely because these two FieldValidation tests use ApplyPatchType, which upstream formats via structured-merge-diff (dotted), not plain strict-decoding. w1p59's global swap fixed one test and regressed these two. BOTH wordings are upstream-correct -- for DIFFERENT request types -- and u7s currently has no branch on request type.

FIX DIRECTION: DO NOT simply revert w1p59 (re-breaks CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI). Branch on whether the incoming request is SSA Apply-patch (dotted '.<path>: field not declared in schema') vs Create/Update (strict decoding error: unknown field "<path>").

Needs Lima VM verification: confirm BOTH the FieldValidation Apply-patch tests AND CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI (plain CREATE) pass simultaneously. Regression test both request-type wordings.
close_reason: PR #858 opened — branched CR field-validation wording on SSA (dotted) vs Create/Update (strict-decoding), both wordings confirmed live and both FieldValidation conformance specs pass in focused sonobuoy run

title: fix(scheduler): emit_scheduling_event has no request timeout — POST silently lost under concurrent load, no error surfaced
description:
Conformance run 0715-2142: [sig-scheduling] SchedulerPredicates 'validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching' FAILS 'context deadline exceeded' at predicates.go:1102 (the WaitForSchedulerAfterAction helper polls 2min for a FailedScheduling event).

Reproduced by Scout A live on lima-node-2 (isolated repro shows CORRECT behavior; failure only under full-suite load). The scheduler DECISION was correct: scheduler.log shows 'no node can fit the pending pod even after preempting lower-priority pods' for the restricted-pod, and no 'failed to emit event' error followed. But apiserver.log shows ZERO POST .../events for that namespace for the ENTIRE run -- and a plain re-list 2min later still shows 0 events (rules out a delivery-timing/watch race). The pod-creation POST and the test's watch (sendInitialEvents=true) were 2ms apart.

ROOT CAUSE: emit_scheduling_event (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:1630-1656) issues an HTTP POST to the apiserver with NO explicit timeout and NO failure logging/retry. Under the concurrent request load visible in apiserver.log at that exact timestamp, the call most likely hung indefinitely; the event never reached the apiserver and nothing was logged. The scheduler's event emission is fire-and-forget-and-hope.

FIX DIRECTION: add a request timeout + failure logging (and a bounded retry) around the scheduler's apiserver HTTP calls, starting with emit_scheduling_event. Consider auditing other scheduler->apiserver calls for the same no-timeout pattern.

Needs Lima VM verification UNDER LOAD (did NOT reproduce in a quiet single-test kubectl repro) -- e.g. sonobuoy --focus on the full SchedulerPredicates set, or a concurrent-create stress repro.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-07-17 (conformance run 0716-2043). PR #833s request timeout landed, but Scout B found SchedulerPredicates validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching STILL fails under full --e2e-parallel load: scheduler.log:131 shows the CORRECT decision (scheduling error for sched-pred-2291/restricted-pod: no node can fit even after preempting at 09:53:14.598Z) but apiserver.log has ZERO POST .../sched-pred-2291/events for the whole run, and main.rs:378 error did NOT fire. So the timeout alone did not close this under load -- the event is still lost.

CAVEAT TO CONFIRM BEFORE FIXING (mayor, Rule 12): sched-pred-2291 is a SchedulerPredicates namespace in the SAME run where the sibling SchedulerPredicates test validates resource limits was classified ENVIRONMENTAL (timed out at upstream WaitForStableCluster, never created its pod, downstream victim of the namespace-Terminating hang mayor-74j3.6). Must verify live whether this NodeSelector test genuinely reached the emit-event path and the event was lost, vs. it too was starved earlier. A scout/worker should reproduce UNDER LOAD (sonobuoy --focus on the full SchedulerPredicates set, or a concurrent-create stress) on a stack that ALSO has the 74j3.6 namespace fix, so environmental starvation is ruled out. DO NOT dispatch a fix until this is disambiguated -- it may resolve for free once 74j3.6 (namespace hang) and mayor-ouuo5 (preemption) land. Cross-ref mayor-et5o / mayor-7lrp watch-latency umbrella. Held (not dispatched) pending ouuo5 + 74j3.6 landing and a fresh full re-run.

title: strategic-merge-patch $setElementOrder/<field> directives leak into stored objects as literal garbage keys outside Pod status
description:
Discovered live on lima-node-4 while VM-verifying mayor-iwyrd's ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks fix (itself resolving mayor-t4opz).

Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs's generic strategic_merge_patch_at has no handling at all for `$setElementOrder/<field>` directives. Real kubectl (client-side three-way apply, via client-go's strategicpatch package) emits `$setElementOrder/<field>` alongside ANY diff to a registered merge-key list, to communicate the field's full desired ordering -- this is normal, expected, extremely common kubectl traffic, not an edge case. The ONLY place this codebase strips/interprets `$setElementOrder/*` is a bespoke, Pod/PodStatus-specific handler in handlers/pods.rs (conditions, podIPs, containers) -- the shared strategic_merge_patch path used by every OTHER resource type (Service, ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, ServiceAccount, CSINode, Node, etc.) has no equivalent, so the directive key falls through generic object-key handling and gets inserted as a literal sibling field.

Reproduced live (lima-node-4, --stack-only) for TWO independent, unrelated resource kinds to confirm this is pre-existing and cross-cutting, not specific to any one field:

1. Service.spec.ports (merge key "port" was already registered well before mayor-iwyrd): kubectl apply create a Service with one port, kubectl apply again changing only targetPort -> `kubectl get -o json` shows `.spec` containing a literal `"$setElementOrder/ports"` key alongside `ports`.
2. ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks (mayor-iwyrd's new fix): same second-apply pattern -> top-level literal `"$setElementOrder/webhooks"` key persisted alongside `webhooks`.

Impact: every resource type with a merge-keyed list field, patched via a real kubectl apply that changes anything in that list, gets a permanent garbage `$setElementOrder/*` key written into its stored JSON. Real kube-apiserver consumes this hint during patch application and never persists it. Risks: breaks fieldValidation=Strict for clients that don't expect it, pollutes kubectl's own last-applied-configuration 3-way diff on the NEXT apply (the annotation itself now differs from a clean object), and could break strict-shape assertions in conformance tests or other consumers.

Not blocking mayor-iwyrd or mayor-t4opz: t4opz's actual reported impact (clientConfig/failurePolicy/admissionReviewVersions/sideEffects silently dropped) is fully fixed and verified live; this is a distinct, adjacent, pre-existing defect found incidentally during that verification.

Suggested fix direction: generalize the existing $setElementOrder/<field> stripping+reordering logic already implemented ad hoc in handlers/pods.rs (see its conditions/podIPs/containers handling) into the shared strategic_merge_patch_at path in patch.rs, so every merge-keyed field benefits instead of just Pod/PodStatus.

description:

in the JSON (see collect_leaf_paths/has_field/assert_fields_present helpers, currently duplicated
per-file rather than factored out — matches established precedent, but worth flagging to the
mayor as a candidate for a shared test-utility module if the duplication keeps growing).

If a completeness test flags deletionTimestamp/deletionGracePeriodSeconds/managedFields as

notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #831): PASS. 7 files, all on the assigned surface (4 target adapters + sentinel + sentinel-derive + recursion test); no leak. Recursion guard reviewed in detail: sentinel_guard uses a thread-local TypeId stack -- returns T::default only when T is ALREADY mid-construction on the call stack, else push/build/pop. Genuine no-op for the 550+ non-cyclic types (never re-enter own TypeId); handles indirect/mutual cycles (JsonSchemaProps to JsonSchemaPropsOrArray to JsonSchemaProps) since the stack tracks all in-flight types. Derive change is a clean one-line wrap requiring T:Default (every prost message has it). Minor non-blocking note: push/build/pop is not panic-safe (a panic in build leaves the TypeId on the stack) but sentinel is test-only code building simple structs and a panic fails the test anyway -- not worth a Drop guard. 17 real dropped fields found+fixed, all additive Option/non-empty-gated and proven by the completeness test that found each. title: kubectl apply (strategic merge patch) on ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks[] drops sibling fields on second apply
description:
Discovered while doing live VM verification for mayor-7a6x8 (webhook rule
scope enforcement) — unrelated to that bead's fix, filing separately.

Repro on lima-node-smoke (--stack-only):
1. kubectl create a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration with one webhooks[] entry
   containing clientConfig, failurePolicy, admissionReviewVersions,
   sideEffects, and rules (all fields populated).
2. kubectl apply -f - the SAME object with only rules[].resources changed
   (everything else identical in the submitted YAML).
3. kubectl get -o yaml the object afterward: the stored webhooks[] entry has
   lost clientConfig, failurePolicy, admissionReviewVersions, and
   sideEffects — only name and rules survive. The response also showed a
   top-level '$setElementOrder/webhooks' key, suggesting the strategic
   merge patch logic for this list-of-objects field is only applying a
   partial diff instead of merging/replacing the full keyed list element.

Impact: a second `kubectl apply` of a webhook config (e.g. to update just
the rules, matchConditions, or timeout) silently corrupts the webhook,
leaving it registered but non-functional for dispatch (missing
clientConfig means invoke_mutating_webhook/run_validating_webhooks can't
resolve a target). Likely affects any built-in type with a list-of-objects
field patched via strategic merge (not confirmed beyond
ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks[]).

Workaround used during verification: delete + recreate instead of apply
over an existing object.

Not investigated further — this is patch.rs/SSA territory (adjacent to
concurrent work on the Sentinel macro / patch.rs at time of discovery), not
the admission.rs surface mayor-7a6x8 covers.
close_reason: Resolved by PR #825 (mayor-iwyrd gap #8 fix: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks merge-key entry, real JSON key lowercase 'webhooks' not proto's 'Webhooks'). Verified live on lima-node-4 against this bead's exact repro: create ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, apply again changing only rules[].resources -- clientConfig/failurePolicy/admissionReviewVersions/sideEffects all confirmed to survive post-fix.

comments.author: Erdos Balint
comments.text: Root cause identified via mayor-iwyrd (found independently by the patch.rs completeness-check audit): ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks[] has no merge-key entry in merge_key_for_path because the .proto token is capitalized 'Webhooks' but the real JSON key this codebase emits is lowercase 'webhooks' (admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs:352) -- a naive entry keyed on the .proto spelling would never match real traffic, which is exactly why this fell through to whole-object-replace-ish behavior on re-apply. Dispatching mayor-iwyrd (which already documents this as gap #8 with precise evidence) instead of fixing here separately -- close this as duplicate/subsumed once iwyrd lands, don't fix twice.

title: audit gen_object_meta_to_json for deletionTimestamp/deletionGracePeriodSeconds/managedFields handling
description:
While building the Sentinel completeness-test mechanism (mayor-3s9hf, PR #818), core_gen_adapter.rs's gen_object_meta_to_json was found to never emit deletionTimestamp, deletionGracePeriodSeconds, or managedFields (selfLink is also missing but that one's unambiguous: real Kubernetes removed the concept, safe to leave out).

decode_pod_proto_gen (and the other decode_X_proto_gen functions using gen_object_meta_to_json) is only ever used to decode INBOUND client request bodies (see extract_body in util.rs) — never to round-trip stored objects. deletionTimestamp is otherwise set server-side by directly mutating the stored JSON (handlers/pods.rs, handlers/generic.rs), not via this decode path.

Open question this bead did not resolve: is dropping these 3 fields on decode harmless (because a client-submitted deletionTimestamp/managedFields is never honored anyway, e.g. server-authoritative fields get overwritten downstream regardless of what the request body says), or is it a live bug for the narrow case of a controller PUT/update that echoes back an object it previously GET'd while deletionTimestamp was set (e.g. finalizer removal during graceful deletion) — which would silently un-terminate the object if the update handler trusts the decoded body's metadata wholesale?

Needs someone to trace the actual update/replace/patch handler's metadata-merge logic (does it preserve server-owned metadata fields regardless of the decoded body, or does it trust the decoded body's metadata as authoritative?) before deciding whether to add handling, or to allow-list these fields with a confident justification once the update path's behavior is understood.

description:
Follow-up to mayor-3s9hf (PR #818), which built the u7s-sentinel/u7s-sentinel-derive proc-macro + leaf-key-path completeness test mechanism as a proof of concept on core_gen_adapter.rs (gen_pod_spec_to_json, gen_container_to_json) only. Roll out the same completeness-test pattern to the other 9 *_gen_adapter.rs files (apps_gen_adapter.rs, admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs, apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs, apiregistration_gen_adapter.rs, rbac_gen_adapter.rs, coord_gen_adapter.rs, net_disc_cert_policy_events_gen_adapter.rs, storage_node_flow_gen_adapter.rs, batch_gen_adapter.rs).

2. 8 of the 10 *_gen_adapter.rs files have their own near-duplicate gen_object_meta_to_json (only apps_gen_adapter.rs and batch_gen_adapter.rs delegate to core_gen_adapter's copy) — each needs its own completeness check since they've already drifted independently.
3. Decide per-file whether the target decode_X_proto_gen functions are decode-inbound-only (client request bodies) or also used for stored-object round-trips — this changes what belongs on the intentional-omissions allow-list vs. what's a live bug. title: kubectl explain <built-in resource> completely broken via OpenAPI v3 path (openapi_v3() never lists built-in groups)
description:
Discovered while investigating mayor-zejxr (CRD shortname explain flake). handlers::discovery::openapi_v3() (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs) only ever populates paths[] with CRD-backed group/versions read from the CRD store; it never adds entries for the core group ("api/v1") or any static built-in group ("apis/apps/v1", etc). kubectl 1.28+ defaults kubectl explain to the OpenAPIv3 renderer (kubectl/pkg/explain/v2), which looks up paths[resourcePath] (e.g. "api/v1" for pods) in this exact document and errors with "couldn't find resource for ..." if absent — it does NOT fall back to the v2/swagger renderer just because paths is empty or incomplete (that fallback only triggers if the /openapi/v3 fetch itself errors, confirmed by reading kubectl/pkg/cmd/explain/explain.go @ release-1.36).

Live repro on a --stack-only u7s (lima-node-2, port 6445), latest main (321cd492):
  kubectl get --raw /openapi/v3   -> {"paths":{}}   (no CRDs registered)
  kubectl explain pods            -> error: couldn't find resource for "/v1, Resource=pods"
  kubectl explain pods.spec       -> same error
  kubectl explain deployments     -> (expected to fail the same way; same missing "apis/apps/v1" path)

This means kubectl explain for ANY built-in resource is currently broken by default (non-flaky, 100% reproducible, no caching involved) — verified with a fresh --cache-dir to rule out client-side caching. CRD-backed explain works fine because openapi_v3() does add the CRD's own group/version to paths.

Not fixed as part of mayor-zejxr because: (a) it's orthogonal to that bead's actual failure (a different, upstream-acknowledged kubectl client-cache flake, confirmed via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/65517), (b) none of the 29 CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI specs explain a built-in resource so it doesn't block that gate, and (c) a correct fix is architecturally bigger than a surgical bug fix: it needs a real (or at least path-complete) OpenAPI v3 document — with a components.schemas entry and a paths entry per Kind — for every static built-in group (core v1, apps/v1, batch/v1, ...), mirroring what already exists for /openapi/v2. That's a substantial, cross-cutting feature, not a one-line patch.

Suggested follow-on scope: add paths["api/v1"] and paths["apis/<group>/<version>"] entries for every STATIC_GROUPS entry (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs) to openapi_v3(), and implement (or reuse an adapted form of) the /openapi/v2 -> v3 schema conversion for the corresponding openapi_v3_group()-equivalent per built-in group, so kubectl explain <builtin> works via the default v3 renderer instead of only working by accidental v2 fallback (which itself doesn't currently trigger, per this finding).

title: fix(scheduler): concurrent preemption attempts race on the same victim (409 Conflict)
description: Found running '[sig-scheduling] SchedulerPreemption validates various priority Pods preempt expectedly with the async preemption' (non-conformance, gated behind SchedulerAsyncPreemption feature u7s does not implement -- out of scope for mayor-rsei's 4-test conformance gate, which passed). With 10 concurrent pending medium-priority pods each independently calling find_preemption_plan/delete_pod against overlapping sets of low-priority victims, two scheduler goroutines can pick the SAME victim pod; the second DELETE races the first's earlier mutation and gets HTTP 409 (resource version mismatch), which main.rs currently propagates as a hard error via '?' -- that pending pod's whole scheduling attempt fails (FailedScheduling event) instead of retrying against a re-fetched victim list or treating a 409-during-eviction as 'someone else is already handling this pod, try a different victim'. Likely fix: in the preemption loop in main.rs, treat a 409 from delete_pod as non-fatal and retry find_preemption_plan once (the watch will also redeliver the pod on the next relist/backoff, so this may already self-heal via the outer watch loop -- verify whether that happens in practice before adding retry logic). Not required for mayor-rsei's conformance gate (all 4 target tests are effectively single-preemptor scenarios); only matters for high-concurrency preemption storms.
notes:
RESCOPE + ELEVATE P3->P2 2026-07-16 (conformance run 0715-2142, Scout A verified live 2x on lima-node-2): this bead is the home for FOUR of the run's failures -- all SchedulerPreemption tests (basic preemption predicates.go:1041; lower-priority-by-critical preemption.go:309; pod-disruption-condition preemption.go:538; PreemptionExecutionPath preemption.go:896). ROOT CAUSE is broader than this bead's original title: delete_pod (scheduler lib.rs:1703-1717) issues TWO unconditional DELETEs (soft then force, per commit b224bf9f); the 2nd races the 1st's RV bump -> 409 Conflict -> check_delete_response (lib.rs:1511, only tolerates 2xx/404) rejects -> main.rs:224 ? aborts the ENTIRE scheduling cycle -> preemptor stuck Pending, only recovers on a passive watch reconnect ~3.5min later (past test timeout). CRITICAL: this fires even in a SINGLE-preemptor scenario with ZERO concurrency -- NOT just 'concurrent preemption attempts race on the same victim' as the title says. Rescope title/scope accordingly. FIX: tolerate 409 like 404 in check_delete_response (or make the force-delete conditional/retry-on-409); verify the whole preemption cycle no longer aborts. RECONCILIATION with mayor-rsei (CLOSED, #816/4892cc40 merged 08:54Z, IS in this run's binary): rsei fixed a DIFFERENT layer (extended-resource accounting -- before it, find_preemption_plan never ran at all). The 409 is the downstream eviction now failing. rsei stays correctly CLOSED; its close-reason 'all 4 pass' was true via --focus at merge but is now stale (full-suite exposed the 409). Sequential layers, not a contradiction. Needs Lima VM verification (preemption path).
MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #832): PASS. Single-file, single-line logic change: check_delete_response tolerates 409 like the existing 404 arm, with a thorough doc comment. Scope verified SAFE: check_delete_response has ONE caller (delete_pod, the preemption eviction path); a 409 there can only be an optimistic-concurrency conflict on the soft-delete PUT (victim concurrently modified by kubelet status-sync or another preemptor) -- in all cases the pod is moving toward deletion, which is what preemption wants, and delete_pod issues DELETE twice by design to drive it gone, so the first attempt losing a race is benign. Genuine failures still abort: the existing check_delete_response_err_on_failure test (500/RBAC-403) is unchanged and the 409 addition does not weaken it. Regression test check_delete_response_ok_on_409_conflict is a pure-function fail-on-revert with a WHY message. Worker READ the apiserver DELETE handler (pods.rs) to confirm root cause rather than assuming, and reproduced the race LIVE (two concurrent preemptors -> 409 on the wire -> stuck Pending pre-fix; identical 409 but clean evict+bind post-fix). Sonobuoy: all 4 SchedulerPreemption target tests PASS (24/25; the 1 failure is SchedulerAsyncPreemption, a feature gate u7s does not implement -- genuinely out of scope). Closes 4 of the run's 17 failures. Merging on CI green.
close_reason: PR #832 opened — tolerate 409 in check_delete_response, live-verified on lima-node-5 (before/after 409 abort vs clean eviction+bind), all 4 target SchedulerPreemption conformance tests pass

title: extract patch.rs merge-key completeness check from .proto +patchMergeKey comments; fix the 6 known-missing entries
description:
Operator-approved (2026-07-15) follow-through on the schema-mapping-completeness audit's recommendation. Companion to the Sentinel-macro bead (same audit, different mechanism -- this one targets patch.rs's merge-key table specifically, not the gen_*_to_json family).

FINDING: the vendored .proto files already carry the exact patchMergeKey/patchStrategy metadata as machine-parseable `//` comments, verbatim from upstream's Go struct tags, e.g. crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto:808-812:
  // +patchMergeKey=mountPath
  // +patchStrategy=merge
  repeated VolumeMount volumeMounts = 9;

MECHANISM: write a parser (build-time script or test-time helper -- your call which is more appropriate given the codebase's existing conventions) that extracts every (message, field) -> patchMergeKey pair from the vendored .proto comments, and a completeness TEST asserting every schema-declared patchMergeKey field has SOME matching entry (exact-path OR one of the existing generic suffix arms like `.conditions`/`.ownerReferences`/`.podIPs`) in patch.rs's merge_key_for_path (patch.rs:330-419). 

IMPORTANT DESIGN CONSTRAINT: do NOT auto-generate the whole table and replace the hand-written one. The existing table's generic suffix arms (e.g. `.conditions` covering 7+ distinct `*Status.conditions` fields with one rule) are a deliberate, working generalization -- preserve that design. The goal is a completeness CHECK that catches gaps against the existing table structure, not a wholesale regeneration.

KNOWN CONFLICT TO HANDLE, NOT RESOLVE: batch/v1/generated.proto:367-369's JobStatus.conditions carries BOTH +patchMergeKey=type+patchStrategy=merge AND +listType=atomic simultaneously. Also see mayor-lm71q (separate, unresolved investigation) for containerStatuses's exact-opposite case (+listType=atomic with NO patchMergeKey, but patch.rs currently merges by "name" anyway). Your completeness check must not force a resolution of these conflicts -- if a field has ambiguous/conflicting annotations, the check can flag it for manual review rather than asserting a specific answer. Do not touch containerStatuses's existing behavior in this bead; that's mayor-lm71q's job once evidence exists.

CONCRETE FIX INCLUDED IN THIS BEAD: mayor-m8k75 already identified 6 fields with unambiguous +patchMergeKey annotations and NO existing table entry (exact or suffix) -- fix all 6 as part of proving the completeness check works (each becomes a real regression-test case, same pattern as mayor-yhg35's fixes):
1. Container.volumeDevices / EphemeralContainerCommon.volumeDevices -> devicePath
2. ContainerStatus.allocatedResourcesStatus -> name
3. NodeStatus.addresses -> type
4. PodStatus.hostIPs -> ip
5. PodStatus.resourceClaimStatuses -> name
6. ServiceAccount.secrets -> name
(exact .proto line numbers are in mayor-m8k75's description)

This bead effectively closes mayor-m8k75 as part of its work -- reference it, don't duplicate the investigation.

Full audit context (may no longer exist on disk, was gitignored/worker-local -- this description is self-contained with the load-bearing facts): ai/findings/schema-mapping-completeness-audit-2026-07-15.md, Section 1b/3.

PodStatus.hostIPs deliberately excluded (same patchMergeKey+listType=atomic conflict as JobStatus.conditions / mayor-lm71q, not force-resolved). Scan of all vendored protos found 9 more real gaps, filed as mayor-iwyrd (discovered-from this bead) rather than bundled in — 2 need the real JSON wire key not the proto token, 1 needs exact-path scoping to avoid a cross-message collision.

title: build in-house Sentinel derive macro for gen_*_to_json field-completeness testing (proof-of-concept on core_gen_adapter.rs)
description:
Operator-approved (2026-07-15) follow-through on the schema-mapping-completeness audit's recommendation. Goal: prevent the recurring "protobuf field silently dropped from gen_*_to_json" bug class (most recent live instance: mayor-jdv5a, matchExpressions dropped entirely) via a completeness TEST, not full codegen (full codegen was investigated and ruled out -- wire-identical fields need opposite emission policies not derivable from the schema alone, e.g. PodSpec.host_network needs Some(true)-only emission while host_users/set_hostname_as_fqdn need any-Some, both are `optional bool` in the .proto).

MECHANISM (verified feasible by the audit, cite exact evidence when implementing):
- A small in-house derive macro (NOT a third-party crate) generating `fn sentinel() -> Self` for every prost-generated message type: populate every scalar field with a distinguishable non-default value, every Vec/HashMap with one synthetic element, recurse into embedded message fields (which also derive the same macro).
- Apply via `prost_build::Config::type_attribute(".", "#[derive(u7s_sentinel::Sentinel)]")` in crates/apiserver/build.rs (currently a single `compile_protos()` call, ~line 9-104). VERIFIED this hook exists and supports the global "." pattern for blanket application -- prost-build's own crate docs use exactly this pattern (`config.type_attribute(".", "#[derive(Eq)]")`), confirmed by reading prost-build-0.14.4/src/config.rs directly.
- VERIFIED no `oneof` unions exist in any of the 20 vendored .proto files -- the macro only needs to handle plain struct fields, no enum-variant case analysis needed.
- Write a generic "collect every leaf key path in a serde_json::Value tree" test helper (~30-50 LOC).
- For a completeness test: build a sentinel instance of the target message type, encode to protobuf, decode via the real `decode_X_proto_gen` entry point, assert the JSON output's leaf-key-path set is a superset of expected keys, MINUS a small explicit per-type "known intentional omissions" allow-list (fields deliberately not exposed in JSON, if any exist -- check first, may be zero for most types).

SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD (proof-of-concept, not full rollout): build the macro crate, wire the build.rs hook, write the test helper, and apply the completeness test to core_gen_adapter.rs ONLY (the largest, most central adapter file -- ~5528 lines, contains gen_pod_spec_to_json and friends). Prove the test actually catches a real regression: temporarily re-introduce one of this session's already-fixed decode-drop bugs (e.g. comment out the hostUsers handling added in mayor-05sxm/PR #800) and confirm the new completeness test fails with a clear message naming the missing field; then restore the fix and confirm it passes.

Do NOT roll out to the other 9 *_gen_adapter.rs files in this bead -- if the proof-of-concept works cleanly, file a follow-up bead (or beads) for the rollout, sized based on what this bead learns about effort-per-file.

Full audit context (may no longer exist on disk, was gitignored/worker-local -- this description is self-contained with the load-bearing facts): ai/findings/schema-mapping-completeness-audit-2026-07-15.md, Section 4.

Found and fixed 7 silently-dropped fields (schedulingGroup, workingDir, stdin, stdinOnce, tty, volumeDevices, restartPolicyRules) while building it. Regression-catching proof done via hostUsers revert/restore. gen_object_meta_to_json and the other 9 *_gen_adapter.rs files intentionally left for follow-up (documented in PR).

1. Container.volumeDevices / EphemeralContainerCommon.volumeDevices -> devicePath (core/v1/generated.proto:815-820, :1604-1609)
2. ContainerStatus.allocatedResourcesStatus -> name (core/v1/generated.proto:1161-1165)
3. NodeStatus.addresses -> type (core/v1/generated.proto:2966-2970)
4. PodStatus.hostIPs -> ip (core/v1/generated.proto:4884-4886)
5. PodStatus.resourceClaimStatuses -> name (core/v1/generated.proto:4962-4968)
6. ServiceAccount.secrets -> name (core/v1/generated.proto:6116-6120)

Not yet reproduced at runtime (audit was read-only, static cross-reference only) -- verify each via kubectl strategic-merge-patch before fixing, same pattern as mayor-yhg35's regression tests (construct, patch to add one entry, assert existing entries survive; fails on revert).

Fix each the same way as the existing 11 entries in this file: add the (path, key) pair to merge_key_for_path, add a regression test per field.
