title: 04-start-kcm.sh restart-kill pkill pattern never matches, so KCM 'restart' silently no-ops (same process persists across runs)
description:
## Discovered by
mayor-s8s3s scout (2026-07-13), incidentally, while doing an A/B KCM content-type comparison.

## Bug
`scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh` tries to kill a stale KCM before starting a new one:
```bash
limactl shell "$VM_NAME" bash -c \
  "if pgrep -f '^kube-controller-manager' >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... pkill -f '^kube-controller-manager' ...; fi"
```
The actual process is launched via an absolute cached-binary path:
```
/home/lima.guest/.cache/u7s/kcm/kube-controller-manager-1.36.2-linux-arm64 --kubeconfig=... ...
```
`pgrep -f '^kube-controller-manager'` anchors the regex to the START of the full command line, which is `/home/lima.guest/...`, NOT `kube-controller-manager` — so the pattern never matches and the "kill stale process" branch never fires. Every subsequent (non-`--reset`) `run-all.sh --focus ...` invocation's `04-start-kcm.sh` therefore:
1. Fails to detect/kill the existing KCM (silently — the `if` is just false, no warning).
2. Attempts to start a NEW instance, which immediately dies (`serving.go:411` self-signed cert generated, then `run.go:72 "command failed" err="failed to create listener: ... 127.0.0.1:10257: bind: address already in use"` — because the OLD instance still holds the healthz/metrics port).
3. The heredoc's `> "$KCM_LOG" 2>&1 &` still TRUNCATES `/tmp/kcm.log` via shell redirection even though the new process dies instantly — losing all prior log history from the still-running old instance (observed as literal NUL-byte gaps / garbled lines in captured `host-logs/kcm.log` where the old process's fd offset resumed past the truncation point).
4. The script prints `"kube-controller-manager running (PID $!, ...)"` unconditionally — a fabricated success message; the reported PID is the dead process's.

Net effect: **KCM is never actually restarted by any `run-all.sh` invocation that omits `--reset`** — the same KCM process (and its in-memory informer caches / config, e.g. a content-type flag set on an earlier run) silently persists across every subsequent "restart" in the same VM lifetime. Confirmed via `pgrep -af kube-controller-manager` showing the SAME PID across 3 consecutive `--focus` runs in one session, and via `host-logs/kcm.log` in sonobuoy run archives showing the "address already in use" failure + truncation artifact.

## Impact
- Any scout/worker relying on "run `--focus` again to pick up a changed KCM flag/version without `--reset`" is silently testing the OLD KCM, not the new one. (mayor-s8s3s worked around this by always using `--reset` before measurement, per its own dispatch instructions, so its A/B results are NOT affected — but this is a trap for future ad-hoc iteration.)
- Log evacuation for non-`--reset` focus runs is unreliable (truncation artifacts), which can hide real KCM errors from earlier in the run.

## Fix sketch
Match on the actual binary name, not an anchored full-path prefix, e.g. `pkill -f 'kube-controller-manager-[0-9.]+-linux-'` or `pgrep -f 'kube-controller-manager' | ...` (drop the `^` anchor, or match the basename). Verify the OLD process's port is actually free (or the new one binds successfully) before printing the "running" success message — currently that message is unconditional.

## Not in scope for mayor-s8s3s
Pure harness-script bug, unrelated to apiserver correctness; filing separately per mayor-s8s3s's scope (measure protobuf blast radius only, no harness changes).
close_reason: PR #763 opened — matched real KCM argv (versioned binary basename) instead of the never-matching anchored prefix; verified across 4 restarts on 2 boots that pkill+restart actually replaces the PID

title: scout: flip KCM to protobuf (--kube-api-content-type) on one VM — measure blast radius before harness change
notes:
SCOUT COMPLETE (2026-07-13, lima-node-2). Findings doc: ai/findings/protobuf-kcm-blast-radius-2026-07-13.md (worktree-local, gitignored — not pushed).

A/B result: JSON baseline (ReplicaSet PASS, Job PASS, Services/Endpoints FAIL pre-existing/unrelated to protobuf — context deadline exceeded at service.go:775, matches known watch-latency family) vs protobuf KCM. Full 3-test re-run under protobuf was not completed because within ~30s of every protobuf-KCM fresh boot, the bootstrap kube-system/coredns Deployment enters an UNBOUNDED hash-collision retry storm (collisionCount 907+, 500+ ReplicaSets, resourceVersion climbing continuously, still unresolved after 5+ min) that starves the whole controller-manager (a hand-created unrelated Deployment got 0 pods for 2+ min). Confirmed via A/B on two separate fresh --reset boots (JSON: 0 collisions, 1 RS, stable; protobuf: storm) that this is protobuf-triggered, not incidental flakiness.

Apiserver does NOT reject protobuf request bodies (no 415s; util.rs::extract_body decodes unconditionally, already unit-tested via #757). content_type.rs never re-encodes responses as protobuf (always JSON + Accept fallback, same as kubelet/kubectl). Root cause is KCM's deployment-controller collision-avoidance never observing its own recent writes via its informer before retrying — likely SAME root-cause family as mayor-sjlw1 (P1, watch wedge under heavy write load) / mayor-et5o / mayor-7lrp.1 (watch/bookmark latency), possibly a much cheaper repro path for those (10s stack boot vs needing a live sonobuoy run).

Filed: mayor-tkp2f (P1, the collision storm, related to sjlw1/et5o/7lrp.1) and mayor-ogukf (P2, incidental find: 04-start-kcm.sh's pkill pattern is anchored to the wrong string and never matches the absolute binary path, so KCM "restart" between non-reset runs is a silent no-op — did not affect this scout's results since --reset was used before each measurement).

RECOMMENDATION: (c) keep JSON in the harness. Do not flip to protobuf until mayor-tkp2f is fixed. 04-start-kcm.sh left reverted to application/json in this worktree (no harness change pushed, per dispatch MERGE GATE — this was a read-only diagnostic, no PR).
close_reason: Scout complete: protobuf KCM triggers an unbounded Deployment/RS collision storm (mayor-tkp2f, P1) — recommend keeping JSON until fixed. Secondary find mayor-ogukf (P2) filed. Findings: ai/findings/protobuf-kcm-blast-radius-2026-07-13.md. No harness change pushed (read-only diagnostic).

title: fix(apiserver): node/pod/service proxy handlers drop response headers (Content-Type) when forwarding to kubelet/pod
description:
All four proxy dispatch sites in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs build the outgoing
Response with only `.status(...)` and a body, never copying any headers (Content-Type in
particular) from the upstream (kubelet or pod) response:

  - node_proxy() (~line 1272-1314): GET /api/v1/nodes/{name}/proxy/{*path}
  - pod_proxy_dispatch() (~line 1515-1609), both the konnectivity-tunnel branch and the
    direct-connection branch, used by pod_proxy() and pod_proxy_root()
  - service_proxy_dispatch() (reuses pod_proxy_dispatch's forwarding pattern)

Confirmed via raw curl against a live --stack-only cluster (2026-07-13, mayor-3z4pr re-scout):

  curl --cacert ... --cert ... --key ... \
    -H "Accept: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf, application/json" \
    https://127.0.0.1:6444/api/v1/nodes/lima-node-2/proxy/pods

  -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
     transfer-encoding: chunked
     (no content-type header at all)
     body: {"kind":"PodList","apiVersion":"v1",...}  (plain JSON, not protobuf)

Per client-go's Request.transformResponse (k8s.io/client-go/rest/request.go), when the
response Content-Type header is empty, the client falls back to its OWN configured
default content type -- which is application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf for any standard
typed clientset (kubernetes.Clientset). The client then feeds real JSON bytes to the
protobuf decoder and fails with exactly:

  "provided data does not appear to be a protobuf message, expected prefix [107 56 115 0]"

This is precisely the error seen 44x in the 0712-2356 conformance run's failure-dump
helper (sonobuoy/e2e framework's kubelet-pods-via-node-proxy dump, called from dump.go
after a test already failed) -- see mayor-3z4pr notes. It is a real, narrowly-scoped
correctness bug for ANY protobuf-preferring client hitting node/pod/service proxy
subresources, separate from (and not the root cause of) mayor-3z4pr's DaemonSet delete
hang -- normal pod/list GET already returns correct Content-Type: application/json
(verified unaffected via the same probe against /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/<name>).

Fix: propagate at least the upstream Content-Type header (ideally all safe-to-forward
headers) from kubelet_resp / pod_resp onto the Response::builder() in all four sites.
Regression test: FixedService-style unit test asserting the proxied response's
Content-Type matches the upstream's, for at least node_proxy and pod_proxy_dispatch.
close_reason: PR #754 opened: proxy handlers now forward upstream Content-Type via shared proxied_response/forward_proxied_headers helpers; verified via live curl on lima-node-2 (before/after) and red-on-revert unit tests

title: chore(scripts): scheduler/KCM restart-collision guard breaks across worktrees with relative --workdir
description:
Discovered while investigating mayor-3z4pr. scripts/conformance/05-start-scheduler.sh (and likely 04-start-kcm.sh, reset.sh -- same pattern) scope their "already running, kill and restart" guard via `pgrep -f "u7s-scheduler.*${WORKDIR}/kubeconfig"`. WORKDIR defaults to `$PWD/temp/u7s` (absolute) but every documented worker invocation (ai/prompts/vm-operations.md) passes `--workdir ./temp/u7s` (relative). Two parallel workers in DIFFERENT worktrees, both following the documented relative-path invocation, produce IDENTICAL process command-line strings (`u7s-scheduler --kubeconfig ./temp/u7s/kubeconfig`) since the relative path carries no worktree-distinguishing prefix. pgrep -f cannot tell them apart: when worker B restarts its stack, its collision-avoidance pkill matches and kills worker A's scheduler too, silently breaking worker A's cluster (all new pods stay Pending forever, no crash/log trace).

Reproduced firsthand: lost my own u7s-scheduler (lima-node-2, port 6444) mid-investigation when the parallel mayor-m5mu7 worker (lima-node-smoke, port 6445) restarted its own stack with the same relative --workdir convention.

Fix direction (not investigated in depth): resolve WORKDIR to an absolute path before constructing the pgrep pattern (e.g. `WORKDIR="$(cd "$WORKDIR" && pwd)"` after parsing --workdir), in 05-start-scheduler.sh and any sibling script with the same pattern (04-start-kcm.sh, reset.sh).
close_reason: PR #749 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/749

title: fix(apiserver): CRD defaulting cannot-create-intermediate-key STILL fails after #730/kc9m4
description: REOPEN of mayor-kc9m4 (closed 2026-07-07, Close reason: PR #730 opened). Run 0712-2356: [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceDefinition resources custom resource defaulting for requests and from storage works [Conformance] still fails (custom_resource_definition.go:315) with an error CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER IDENTICAL to the pre-fix symptom kc9m4 quoted: setting default for a to "A" in schema: cannot create intermediate key '0' in non-object (HTTP 422 Invalid). PR #730 (CRD defaulting walker handles array/indexed paths) either doesn't cover this exact code path or the fix regressed. This is not an unverified-fix case -- the error text match is exact. FIX: re-examine the CRD defaulting walker (grep default + openAPIV3Schema in the CRD/CR handler crates) for the array/indexed-path case #730 targeted; add a regression test asserting this exact schema shape (an array default requiring an intermediate object key) round-trips correctly, since #730 apparently shipped without one that caught this. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'custom resource defaulting for requests and from storage' passes. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #7).
notes: Priority bumped P3→P2 by mayor: this is a fixed-then-broke-again (PR #730 shipped a fix that demonstrably does not hold — error is character-identical to pre-fix), which is higher-signal than a never-worked P3. A regressed shipped fix means #730 lacked a regression test that would have caught this (Rule 14). Fix must add that test.
close_reason: PR #747 opened — fixed json_navigate_one_or_create (json_patch.rs), the actual code path the conformance test hits (JSON-Patch RFC6902 'add' on the CRD itself through an existing array index), not the cr.rs walker #730 touched. Added regression tests, verified sonobuoy --focus PASS.

title: investigate(watch): DaemonSet Failed-pod delete hang — load-gated watch-latency symptom (clean cluster passes in 3s); under et5o/7lrp.1/sjlw1 umbrella
description:
Run 0712-2356: [sig-apps] Daemon set [Serial] should retry creating failed daemon pods [Conformance] fails intermittently -- NOT a regression from #729/#733/#735 or any PR merged since the 0707-2254 baseline (investigated and cleared; see notes for full mechanism + evidence). This is a PRE-EXISTING race between the real kubelet's independent status-manager correction and kube-controller-manager's DaemonSet controller never issuing a targeted pod DELETE for the test's injected Failed status -- proven present already in the 0707-2254 "passing" baseline (same pod-level fingerprint found retroactively). Whether the test PASSES or FAILS is decided by an unrelated coin-flip: the project's own 5-minute namespace watchdog (scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh) racing the test's own 5-minute poll timeout (dsRetryTimeout, upstream ginkgo constant) to force-cleanup the stuck namespace first. Confirmed via 2 mandatory --focus gate reruns: #1 FAILED, #2 "PASSED" (but only because the watchdog won the race -- verified via matching apiserver.log/watchdog-log timestamps; kube-controller-manager never issued a DELETE for the pod in EITHER run). Real fix requires KCM's DaemonSet controller to reliably react before the kubelet's correction -- a watch/informer-notification-latency problem, related to the open mayor-et5o / mayor-7lrp.1 watch-latency work (relates_to linked; caveat in notes that the exact mechanism may not be identical, re-verify before assuming). Keeping open as known-flaky per investigation mandate rather than closing. Cross-ref mayor-n3yk (distinct, adjacent).

Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #14); full mechanism + per-run log citations in notes below.
notes: RE-SCOUT VERDICT (2026-07-13, lima-node-2 clean --stack-only, 2 live iterations): on an UNCONTENDED cluster the full delete chain works perfectly in ~3s: PUT status=Failed → soft DELETE 200 → hard DELETE 200 → GET 404 (timestamped in apiserver.log). kcm.log shows the informer saw Failed within ~1.5ms (daemon_controller.go:887 'Found failed daemon pod...will try to kill it' + SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate). So: B (watch-delivery) RULED OUT — informer saw it; A (delete-never-completes) RULED OUT as a deterministic bug — soft→hard two-phase delete in pods.rs:638-724 worked, pod reached NotFound cleanly. A' (protobuf) is REAL but NARROW, not systemic: normal pod GET with Accept:protobuf correctly returns JSON+Content-Type (client decodes fine); only the kubelet-PROXY path /api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/pods returns a body with NO Content-Type header, so client-go falls back to its default (protobuf) and hits the 44x 'expected prefix [107 56 115 0]' — but that path is ONLY hit by the e2e failure-DUMP helper AFTER the test already failed, so it is NOT the cause of the DaemonSet failure. Filed mayor-bzhgk for the proxy header-drop bug. CONCLUSION: the original 0712 5-minute hang is NOT deterministic — a fresh cluster is too clean to reproduce it. It likely requires LOAD/CONTENTION (accumulated objects/watchers from a long full run) to manifest, pointing at et5o/7lrp.1 (watch latency under load). NEXT REPRO: inject load (many objects/watchers) BEFORE failing the pod, not a fresh cluster. Re-scope 3z4pr as a load-dependent watch-latency symptom under the et5o/7lrp.1 umbrella; it is NOT an independent deterministic delete/serialization bug. BONUS: lima-node-2's konnectivity tunnel was HEALTHY (node-proxy call returned 200; zero ECDSA errors in apiserver.log) — evidence that ij0es is likely lima-node-smoke-specific, not systemic (pending the ij0es scout's fresh-VM lima-node-3 scope test for confirmation).

title: Deployment controller never scales down old ReplicaSet after a full-object PUT replace
description:
Reproduced live on lima-node-smoke while investigating mayor-yv5p (deployment lifecycle test).

After: create Deployment (RS-A, 2 replicas) -> strategic-merge patch (spec change, creates RS-B) -> full-object PUT/replace via dynamic client (spec change again, creates RS-C) -- RS-B (the previous "new" RS, e.g. test-deployment-565b7c7547) is left permanently at desired=1 and never scaled to 0, even minutes after RS-C is fully available. Pods on RS-B keep running forever (a leak).

Also: deployment.status.replicas only reflects the newest RS's replica count (2), not the sum across all owned ReplicaSets (should be 3 while RS-B lingers) -- suggesting the deployment controller's list of ReplicaSets it considers "owned" by the Deployment is incomplete/stale after a PUT-driven rollout, which is likely also why cleanup/scale-down never fires for the orphaned RS.

Does NOT block '[sig-apps] Deployment should run the lifecycle of a Deployment' (mayor-yv5p) -- none of that test's watch assertions check status.replicas or RS counts, only readyReplicas/updatedReplicas/unavailableReplicas which are unaffected. But it is a real correctness bug: kubectl get deploy REPLICAS column and rollout history would show wrong counts, and it wastes cluster resources (leaked pods never get cleaned up).

Repro: manual kubectl steps mimicking the lifecycle test's create -> patch -> patch-image-fix -> full PUT/replace sequence against a live u7s-apiserver + real kube-controller-manager on lima-node-smoke; `kubectl get rs -n <ns>` shows 2 non-zero-desired ReplicaSets indefinitely after the PUT-driven rollout completes.
close_reason:
Confirmed FIXED by mayor-h0lte (PR #793, commit 541e3279) — closing as duplicate-of/fixed-by.

Hypothesis confirmed: mayor-drjdh was filed before h0lte's fix landed. h0lte's fix
(replace_namespaced_resource restores metadata.uid from the stored object whenever a PUT
body omits it) is NOT EndpointSlice-specific — it applies to any resource whose
`needs_stored_read` is true, which includes every resource with has_status_subresource=true
(Deployment is registered with has_status_subresource: true in state.rs build_registry()).
So the Deployment's own UID was corrupted (blanked) by exactly the same blind-PUT gap, for
exactly the same reason: kube_client-go's dynamic client Update() call in the upstream e2e
lifecycle test (test/e2e/apps/deployment.go:339-352, cached at
temp/research/deployment_e2e.go) builds `testDeploymentUpdate := testDeployment` from the
pre-Create() local struct — never a live Get() — so ObjectMeta.UID/ResourceVersion are
zero-value and get omitted (`omitempty`) by ToUnstructured(). Pre-fix, this blanked the
Deployment's own stored uid on the PUT. A blanked *Deployment* uid (not just EndpointSlice)
explains the full symptom: KCM's ReplicaSetControllerRefManager claims/ignores RS's by
comparing each RS's ownerRef.UID against the Deployment's own live UID
(metav1.GetControllerOf(rs).UID == deployment.UID). Once the Deployment's own UID goes
blank, every existing RS (RS-A, RS-B — both stamped with the real, non-blank UID) stops
matching and gets silently ignored (not adopted, not released — "owned by someone else" per
upstream's ControllerRefManager.ClaimObject), so the controller loses ALL visibility into
them (hence RS-B never scales down, pods leak) while any *new* RS created after the
corruption (RS-C) is stamped with the deployment's now-blank UID and self-matches, so it's
the only one ever reconciled — and status.replicas is summed only over that "owned" set,
so it only reflects RS-C's count. Root cause is identical in kind to the EndpointSlice bug
h0lte fixed, just observed through the Deployment/ReplicaSet ownership path instead of
EndpointSliceTracker.

LIVE VERIFICATION on lima-node-smoke (post-h0lte HEAD, commit b1bba42e + h0lte's 30c8e20a
ancestor), exact repro from the bead description, reproduced twice in independent
namespaces (drjdh-repro, drjdh-repro2):

1. Create Deployment test-deployment, 2 replicas, image pause:3.10 -> RS-A
   (test-deployment-5c9cb95778), rollout completes 2/2. uid=f411bafc-91c6-48ae-96dd-531344a38d5f
   captured (repro2).
2. `kubectl patch --type=strategic` (spec.replicas=1, new image pause:3.9,
   terminationGracePeriodSeconds=2) -> creates RS-B (test-deployment-8696fcf57f). RS-A
   correctly scales to 0/0/0. Deployment uid unchanged, generation 1->2.
3. Blind full-object PUT via `kubectl replace --raw=".../deployments/test-deployment" -f
   body.json`, where body.json has NO metadata.uid and NO metadata.resourceVersion (byte-
   identical in structure to what client-go's dynamic client sends for
   ToUnstructured(never-fetched local struct)) — spec.replicas=2, new image pause:3.8 ->
   should create RS-C.

RESULT (metadata.uid preservation): PUT response AND a subsequent fresh GET both show
metadata.uid == f411bafc-91c6-48ae-96dd-531344a38d5f (unchanged from step 1), even though
the PUT body omitted it entirely. generation correctly incremented 2->3. UID preservation
confirmed working correctly.

RESULT (RS-B leak — GONE): tight 1s-interval poll immediately after the PUT:
  t+1s: status.replicas=3 (RS-C 1/1/0 + RS-A 0/0/0 + RS-B 2/2/1 = 3) -- CORRECT transient
        sum across all owned ReplicaSets, refuting the bug's second complaint directly.
  t+2s: status.replicas=3 (RS-C 2/2/1 + RS-B 1/1/1)
  t+3s: status.replicas=2, RS-B already at 0/0/0, RS-C fully 2/2/2 -- converged within 3s.
Re-checked ~90s later (bug reported "even minutes after RS-C is fully available" RS-B stayed
non-zero): RS-B and RS-A both stable at 0/0/0 in BOTH repro namespaces;
generation(3)==observedGeneration(3); status.replicas=2 matching only RS-C.
`kubectl get pods`: only 2 pods exist, both owned by RS-C, both Running -- zero leaked pods.

Noise ruled out: kcm.log shows the expected, already-tracked, self-healing
"read version N is not as new as written version M" transient errors (mayor-7lrp family,
closed separately as a documented WAL-lag/watch-propagation issue) during this repro --
these retry and do not block convergence; unrelated to this bug and not reintroduced by
this verification.

No code changes required -- h0lte's fix already resolves this. No PR opened per the
dispatch's duplicate-closure instructions. Cleanup: deleted the two repro namespaces on
lima-node-smoke; no source files touched (git status clean throughout).

title: fix(cr): CRD enum validation error message doesn't match kubectl's 'Unsupported value' format
description:
[sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI 'works for CRD with validation schema' fails on the enum-rejection sub-step (crd_publish_openapi.go:97-101), even after the OpenAPI schema-content gap (mayor-uam0) is fixed.

Repro: create a CRD whose schema has an enum field (e.g. `feeling: enum [Great, Down]`), then `kubectl create` a CR with an out-of-enum value.

Actual (from crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs, boon jsonschema validator):
  "CR schema validation failed: jsonschema validation failed with file:///.../schema.json#
   - at '/spec/bars/0/feeling': value must be one of 'Great', 'Down'"

Expected (upstream test asserts err.Error() contains):
  `Unsupported value: "NonExistentValue"`

Fix: reformat the boon/jsonschema enum-violation error in cr.rs to surface a message containing `Unsupported value: "<value>"` (matching the k8s field.ErrorList Unsupported() convention), while still being generically compatible with both client-side and server-side CRD validation per the upstream TODO comment in the test.

Discovered live during mayor-uam0 verification (sonobuoy --focus CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI, run 0708-0748): 28/29 passed, this is the sole remaining failure and is unrelated to OpenAPI schema publishing — scoped to crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs admission validation error formatting.

title: SECURITY(apiserver): merge/strategic-patch to /status can still change non-protected metadata (follow-on to #733)
description: Residual flagged by PR #733 (mayor-t4zd3 worker). #733 fixed the JSON-Patch path so /status subresource patches can't write /spec or /metadata. BUT merge_incoming_metadata — used by the merge-patch and strategic-merge-patch content types when patching /status — still allows changes to non-protected metadata fields on the /status endpoint. So a caller with only <resource>/status rights could still mutate some metadata via a MERGE patch (not JSON-Patch). For Namespace, verify whether this re-opens the PSA-label bypass via merge-patch (the JSON-Patch vector is now closed). FIX: apply the same /status path restriction to the merge/strategic-merge patch paths on status subresources — a /status patch (any content-type) must only touch /status. Extend the guard beyond JSON-Patch to cover merge_incoming_metadata on the status handlers (patch_namespace_status, patch_crd_status, and the generic status.rs patch handlers). GATE: a MERGE patch to .../status setting metadata.labels (incl pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce on a Namespace) or spec → rejected/ignored; a legit /status merge patch works. Test WHY: closing only the JSON-Patch vector leaves the merge-patch vector open — same authz-boundary/PSA-bypass class as #733, different content-type. Cross-ref #733, v2hu6/t4zd3.
close_reason: PR #735 opened - added labels to merge_incoming_metadata's protected fields, closing merge/strategic-merge-patch PSA-label bypass on /status; regression tests + live kubectl + sonobuoy (Namespace status + CRD status conformance) verified

title: test(apiserver): add decoder tests for apiextensions + storage_node_flow gen adapters (zero coverage)
description: Code-quality audit 0708 (scout a1f99), HIGH-value test gap (feeds z6qx, whose 2026-07-04 snapshot is stale). Two gen-adapters have ZERO #[test]s while others now have 2-11 each: apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs (744 lines, CRD decoder) and storage_node_flow_gen_adapter.rs (897 lines, 10 decoders: CSINode/CSIDriver/CSIStorageCapacity/VolumeAttachment/StorageClass/VolumeAttributesClass/RuntimeClass/PriorityClass/FlowSchema/PriorityLevelConfiguration). Given the content-type-decode-drop bug class this session (securityContext/status/immutable/dnsConfig all silently dropped on protobuf → conformance failures), untested decoders are a latent-bug reservoir. FIX: add by-construction protobuf-decode tests for each decoder in these 2 files — encode a wire-format object with all significant fields (incl status/optional fields) via the hand-rolled proto structs (test-only encoders), decode via the real *_gen_adapter fn, assert every field survives INTO json AND that absent fields do NOT leak spurious json (field-omission assertions — see #3). GATE: each decoder in both files has a field-survival + field-omission test; a deliberately-dropped field fails its test. Test WHY: these decoders serve CRD/CSI/storage/scheduling/flow-control objects to typed clients over protobuf; a silent field-drop (the pattern that caused ~11 conformance failures this session) would be invisible without these. Cross-ref z6qx (update its stale snapshot), memory content-type-determines-decode-path + adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation.
close_reason: PR #739 opened

title: perf(apiserver): admission config cache deep-clones Vec<Value> on every write — return Arc
description: Perf audit 0708 (scout ad381), NEW HIGH. The admission config cache (added by PR #666 / mayor-al9a to close the cef5 SQLite-LIST-per-request issue) reads RwLock<Option<Arc<Vec<serde_json::Value>>>> but does cached.as_ref().clone() at admission.rs:653,676,1100,2504 — this DEEP-CLONES the entire Vec<Value> (all mutating+validating webhook configs + VAP/MAP policies, including webhook CA-bundle strings) on EVERY write, unconditionally, BEFORE any rule-matching filter, at the top of run_mutating_webhooks/run_validating_webhooks. Called from nearly every write path (resource.rs, pods.rs, namespaces.rs, cr.rs, crd.rs, csr.rs, proxy.rs). NET: #666 eliminated the SQLite round-trips but replaced them with an equivalent-order in-memory deep clone — a regression baked into the fix. FIX: the cache read helpers should return Arc<Vec<Value>> (clone the Arc, O(1)) and callers iterate the shared Arc, not a deep copy. Only deep-clone if a caller must mutate (it doesn't — rule matching is read-only). GATE: a unit/bench asserting the cache read is O(1) Arc-clone not O(configs) deep-clone (e.g. the helper returns Arc and no serde_json::Value clone of the vec happens per call); confirm run_mutating/validating_webhooks no longer deep-clone. Test WHY: admission runs on every write; a per-write deep clone of all webhook configs scales cost with (#webhooks × config-size × write-rate), inflating write latency + allocation churn cluster-wide. Cross-ref #666/al9a/cef5.
close_reason: PR #732 opened

title: fix(apiserver): Job pod-failure-policy ignore DisruptionTarget still fails after #718
description: Run 0707-2254: [sig-apps] Job 'should allow to use a pod failure policy to ignore failure matching on DisruptionTarget condition' STILL FAILS despite #718 (PDB eviction + DisruptionTarget condition) merged. The DisruptionTarget condition is now set on eviction, but this Job test still fails — likely the pods are not being DELETED (0454 symptom: 'failed to await for all pods to be deleted, 300s') OR the pod-failure-policy matching on the condition isn't wired end-to-end. Re-investigate live: does an evicted pod get DisruptionTarget AND does the Job controller then ignore-and-not-recreate per the policy? May be a Job-controller/KCM interaction needing an apiserver field. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'pod failure policy to ignore failure matching on DisruptionTarget' passes.
close_reason: Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs strategic_merge_patch_at had no handling for the $deleteFromPrimitiveList/<field> SMP directive, which KCM's Job controller uses to remove the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking finalizer from evicted pods. The directive was stored as a literal garbage metadata key instead of removing the finalizer, so evicted pods stayed Terminating forever and the test timed out waiting for pod deletion. This is distinct from #718 (PDB eviction+DisruptionTarget, confirmed still working) and from #767 (watch/broadcast ordering, unrelated). Fixed + regression test in PR #774. Verified: sonobuoy --focus 'pod failure policy to ignore failure matching on DisruptionTarget' -> SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 7578 Skipped (e2e.txt). cargo test --workspace (2158+ tests) and clippy -D warnings both clean.

title: cluster-scoped core/v1 resources (e.g. persistentvolumes) return 405 on DeleteCollection
description:
Conformance: [sig-storage] PersistentVolumes CSI Conformance "should run through the lifecycle of a PV and a PVC" — live-reproduced on lima-node-2 (0707-1912 focus run, e2e.txt persistent_volumes.go:660). The test successfully creates, patches, and deletes individual PV/PVC objects (delete+confirm both succeed quickly now that mayor-f4uv's finalizer-drain fix landed), then calls DeleteCollection on persistentvolumes and gets:

  the server does not allow this method on the requested resource (delete persistentvolumes)
  reason: MethodNotAllowed, code: 405

ROOT CAUSE: crates/apiserver/src/main.rs's route for cluster-scoped core/v1 resource collections,
  .route("/api/v1/{resource}", get(core_list_resource).post(core_create_resource))
has no `.delete(...)`. The namespaced counterpart (/api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/{resource}) already
wires `.delete(core_delete_collection_namespaced_resource)` — the cluster-scoped route needs the
equivalent (e.g. a new core_delete_collection_resource handler, mirroring
handlers::resource::delete_collection_resource which already exists for non-core groups at
main.rs:719 but is not reachable for the empty-group/core route).

FIX: add `.delete(handlers::core::core_delete_collection_resource)` (new handler, mirroring
core_delete_collection_namespaced_resource) to the /api/v1/{resource} route.

GATE: DELETE /api/v1/persistentvolumes (collection, no name) must return 200 Status with the
matching PVs actually removed, not 405. Regression test: DeleteCollection on a cluster-scoped
core resource (persistentvolumes) must succeed.
close_reason: PR #727 opened

title: fix(apiserver): PUT/replace handlers miss finalizer-drain hard-delete (PVC/VAC stuck deleting)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aba09, live-reproduced on lima-node-2 with request trace): [sig-storage] PersistentVolumes CSI 'lifecycle of a PV and a PVC' (PVC never deletes) AND VolumeAttributesClass 'lifecycle' (VAC never deletes) — SHARED root cause. Upstream KCM protection controllers add/REMOVE kubernetes.io/{pvc,vac}-protection finalizers via PUT. When KCM PUTs the object with finalizers now empty AND deletionTimestamp already set, the apiserver must COMPLETE the delete (hard-delete). That check exists ONLY in do_patch (resource.rs:795-822, PATCH path); replace_resource (resource.rs:350) and replace_namespaced_resource (resource.rs:1431) do a literal store.put with no finalizer-drain completion check. So KCM removes the finalizer via PUT, u7s stores the object (still present), and the delete never completes. FIX: extract the finalizer-drain hard-delete check from do_patch into a shared helper and call it from replace_resource + replace_namespaced_resource (and do_patch) — after any update, if deletionTimestamp is set and finalizers is empty, hard-delete. GATE: create a PVC/VAC with a finalizer + deletionTimestamp, PUT with finalizers=[] → object is hard-deleted (GET 404); the CSI/VAC lifecycle tests confirm deletion. Test WHY: finalizer removal via PUT (KCM's mechanism) must complete the delete; without it every finalizer-protected object (PVC, VAC, and any protection-finalizer resource) stays stuck Terminating forever.
close_reason: PR #725 opened — shared finalizer-drain hard-delete helper wired into replace_resource/replace_namespaced_resource; VAC lifecycle conformance test now PASSES, PVC lifecycle progresses past the finalizer-drain hang (blocked by unrelated mayor-yssp DeleteCollection 405 bug, filed separately)

title: fix(apiserver): decode_configmap_proto_gen/decode_secret_proto_gen drop the immutable field
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aba09): [sig-storage] ConfigMap 'should be immutable if immutable field is set' AND Secrets 'should be immutable if immutable field is set' — mutating an immutable CM/Secret is wrongly ALLOWED. ROOT CAUSE: the immutability CHECKS are correct (resource.rs:743-749 PATCH, resource.rs:1507-1527 PUT) but decode_configmap_proto_gen (core_gen_adapter.rs:1080) and decode_secret_proto_gen (core_gen_adapter.rs:1299) NEVER copy the prost-generated immutable: Option<bool> into JSON output. client-go typed Update() sends protobuf → immutable:true silently dropped on decode → stored object never has immutable:true → the checks never fire. FIX: emit 'immutable' in both decode adapters. GATE: decode a protobuf ConfigMap/Secret with immutable:true → served JSON carries immutable:true; then a mutating update is rejected 422. Test WHY: immutable CM/Secret is a data-integrity guarantee; dropping the field on decode silently disables it for all protobuf clients. Cross-ref memory content-type-determines-decode-path (another whole-field drop on the protobuf path).
close_reason: PR #726 opened

title: fix(apiserver): replace_pod PUT has no pod-spec immutability guard (resources rewritable outside /resize)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aba09): [sig-api-machinery] ResourceQuota 'capture the life of a pod' (resource_quota.go:312) — NOT a quota bug (quota admission works, wired at pods.rs:450/resource.rs:1271). Real failure: the test asserts 'a pod cannot update its resource requirements' via generic PUT, but replace_pod (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:496-569) has ZERO pod-spec-immutability validation — clients can freely rewrite containers[].resources (and other immutable pod-spec fields) via PUT, outside the /resize subresource. FIX: add pod-spec immutability validation to replace_pod (and patch path if applicable) — reject changes to immutable spec fields (containers[].resources except via /resize, and the other k8s pod-spec-immutable fields: most of spec except activeDeadlineSeconds, tolerations additions, image, and the resize-allowed resources). Mirror upstream pod update validation (ValidatePodUpdate). GATE: a PUT that changes containers[].resources on a running pod (not via /resize) is rejected; an allowed change (e.g. image) succeeds. Test WHY: pod spec is largely immutable post-create; allowing arbitrary resource rewrites via PUT bypasses the resize QoS rules and quota accounting.
close_reason: PR #723 opened

title: fix(apiserver): unify core/v1 and events.k8s.io/v1 Event storage keyspace
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout af9a8): [sig-instrumentation] Events API 'event can be fetched, patched, deleted, and listed' — 'expected single event, got []'. ROOT CAUSE: keys.rs:27-54 derives DIFFERENT storage keys for group='' vs group='events.k8s.io' events (/registry/events/<ns>/<name> vs /registry/events.k8s.io/events/<ns>/<name>), so an event created via one API group is invisible via the other — the test creates via events.k8s.io and lists/gets, or vice versa. SECONDARY: event_matches_field_selector (handlers/pods.rs:131) doesn't support source/reportingController field selectors. FIX: map both core/v1 Event and events.k8s.io/v1 Event to ONE keyspace (they are the same underlying object, dual-grouped in k8s), and add source/reportingController to the event field-selector. GATE: an Event created via events.k8s.io is GET/LIST-able via core/v1 and vice versa; field-selector on source works. Test WHY: k8s exposes Events under two groups backed by one store; splitting the keyspace makes events created via one group invisible to clients using the other.
notes: PR #720 (worker ae393) unifies the STORAGE KEYSPACE (both groups → one key) + adds source/reportingController field selectors. CAVEAT flagged by worker: the two Event API representations differ in FIELD NAMES (core involvedObject/source vs events.k8s.io regarding/reportingController). #720 does NOT translate field shapes between representations. If [sig-instrumentation] Events API test STILL fails after #720 merges (reads back via the other group's field shape), file a follow-on for Event field-shape translation between core/v1 and events.k8s.io/v1. Confirm on the next conformance run.
close_reason: PR #720 opened

title: fix(apiserver): PodSpec proto decode missing hostNetwork/hostAliases/dnsConfig/ephemeralContainers/automountServiceAccountToken + enableServiceLinks mis-tagged (26→30)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout af9a8, mayor-verified proto.rs:856-902): the PodSpec proto struct is missing multiple fields, so they are silently dropped on protobuf Pod decode (default wire format for typed/e2e clients). Missing: hostNetwork (tag 11), hostAliases (tag 23), dnsConfig (tag 26), ephemeralContainers (tag 34), automountServiceAccountToken (tag 21). CRITICAL MIS-TAG: proto.rs:895 binds enable_service_links to tag 26 — but tag 26 is dnsConfig upstream; enableServiceLinks is tag 30. So enable_service_links currently mis-decodes dnsConfig bytes. FIXING dnsConfig REQUIRES fixing the enableServiceLinks tag simultaneously (they collide on 26). FIXES conformance: [sig-network] DNS 'configurable pod DNS nameservers' (dnsConfig); [sig-node] Ephemeral Containers 'should update ephemeral containers' (ephemeralContainers — merge logic pods.rs:2239 is correct but never sees the field); [sig-node] Kubelet hostAliases '/etc/hosts entries' (hostAliases); [sig-node] KubeletManagedEtcHosts (hostNetwork — dropped per existing comment proto.rs:2336-2342); [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts 'opting out of API token automount' (automountServiceAccountToken pod-level override of SA default — NOT fixed by #713). FIX: add all 5 fields to PodSpec with correct tags + move enable_service_links to tag 30 + add tag 26 dnsConfig, then emit each in gen_pod_spec_to_json. GATE: unit test decoding a protobuf Pod with each field set → served JSON carries it; enableServiceLinks and dnsConfig both round-trip (no tag collision). Test WHY: these pod fields are silently dropped for all protobuf clients; the tag-26 collision actively corrupts dnsConfig<->enableServiceLinks. Cross-ref memory content-type-determines-decode-path, adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation. CLUSTER with cfp7 (pod securityContext tag 14) + hdwo (container securityContext tag 15) — all proto.rs PodSpec/Container struct completions → ONE proto.rs+adapter PR.
close_reason: PR #726 opened

title: test(apiserver): sonobuoy re-verify invalid-sysctl rejection via protobuf after securityContext decode fix

Scout aa0d2 (run 0707-0454) found #711's sysctl-name validation is CORRECT but was never exercised via protobuf because gen_pod_spec_to_json strips sysctls before validate_pod_sysctls runs. Once the pod.spec.securityContext protobuf-decode bead lands, the [sig-node] Sysctls 'should reject invalid sysctls' conformance test must be RE-VERIFIED via sonobuoy --focus (it may still fail or silently mis-pass until decode is fixed). No separate re-verify bead needed.

title: fix(apiserver): IPAddress/ServiceCIDR protobuf decode missing → POST returns 400
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout a0ae5, apiserver.log:84664 verified POST .../ipaddresses status=400 at failure timestamp — it's the Create, not the Get the test error string implies): [sig-network] ServiceCIDR and IPAddress API 'should support IPAddress API operations'. ROOT CAUSE: proto.rs:1242 dispatch table has no 'IPAddress'/'ServiceCIDR' arm, so util.rs:55-96 extract_body can't decode client-go's protobuf-encoded body, falls through to raw bytes → serde_json fails 'expected value at line 1 column 1' → 400. title: fix(apiserver): CSR spec.request is base64(PEM) but decoded as DER (ASN.1 tag 0x2d)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout a0ae5): [sig-auth] Certificates API 'should support CSR API operations' — 'spec.request does not contain a valid DER-encoded PKCS#10: unknown/unsupported ASN.1 DER tag: 0x2d'. 0x2d = '-' = the '-----BEGIN' PEM armor. ROOT CAUSE: csr.rs:72-82 base64-decodes spec.request then calls CertReq::from_der directly — but spec.request is base64(PEM), so it DER-parses the literal PEM armor. FIX: enable the 'pem' feature on x509-cert (Cargo.toml:39) and use CertReq::from_pem (after base64-decode); update csr.rs:276-359 test fixtures to base64(PEM). GATE: a CSR create with a valid base64(PEM) spec.request is accepted (was 422); the CSR API operations test passes. Test WHY: kubectl/client-go submit CSRs as base64(PEM); rejecting valid CSRs breaks all certificate issuance.
close_reason: PR #719 opened

title: fix(apiserver): custom resources bypass fieldValidation (unknown fields + unknown metadata not rejected)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout a0ae5, static): [sig-api-machinery] FieldValidation 'should create/apply an invalid CR with extra properties for CRD with validation schema' AND 'should detect unknown metadata fields in both the root and embedded object of a CR' — SHARED root cause. resource.rs:238-251,917-930 route any CR to handlers/cr.rs BEFORE apply_field_validation (resource.rs:257-263) runs; cr.rs never calls it and never even parses ?fieldValidation=. So CRs get ZERO fieldValidation. FIX: implement CRD structural-schema strict-field detection — walk the CRD openAPIV3Schema honoring x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields and x-kubernetes-embedded-resource — and wire it into create_cr/patch_cr + namespaced variants (cr.rs), parsing ?fieldValidation=Strict/Warn/Ignore. GATE: create a CR with an unknown top-level property under fieldValidation=Strict → 422 listing the unknown field; unknown metadata field (root + embedded) rejected. Test WHY: fieldValidation=Strict is how clients catch typo'd/unknown fields; CRs silently accepting them means schema drift goes undetected. Biggest of the api-machinery static beads.
close_reason: PR #722 opened

title: fix(apiserver): decode_deployment_proto_gen drops spec.strategy/progressDeadlineSeconds/revisionHistoryLimit
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aaf96, live-verified): [sig-apps] Deployment RecreateDeployment ('does not use a Recreate strategy: RollingUpdate') AND 'should delete old replica sets' (cleanup half) — SAME root cause. decode_deployment_proto_gen (crates/apiserver/src/apps_gen_adapter.rs:159-218) DROPS spec.strategy, spec.progressDeadlineSeconds, spec.revisionHistoryLimit when decoding protobuf-encoded request bodies (the default wire format for typed clientsets — e2e framework AND KCM both use protobuf). Once dropped, defaults.rs fills RollingUpdate/10, CLOBBERING the user's Recreate/0. FIX: decode all three fields in decode_deployment_proto_gen from the generated proto struct (strategy incl type + rollingUpdate maxSurge/maxUnavailable; progressDeadlineSeconds; revisionHistoryLimit). ALSO FIX the vacuous test apps_gen_adapter.rs:478 'generated_deployment_struct_emits_rolling_update_strategy_by_construction' — it never asserts the strategy VALUE so it passes despite the bug. GATE: unit test decoding a protobuf Deployment with strategy.type=Recreate → JSON carries Recreate (not defaulted to RollingUpdate); revisionHistoryLimit=0 survives. Test WHY: a Recreate deployment silently becoming RollingUpdate changes rollout semantics (all-pods-down vs surge); dropping it on decode makes strategy/history uncontrollable via protobuf clients. Cross-ref memory adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation. NOTE: proportional-scaling failure may be secondary to this — re-test after.
close_reason: PR #716 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/716

title: fix(apiserver): pods/eviction subresource ignores PodDisruptionBudget and never sets DisruptionTarget condition
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aaf96, live-verified: eviction of a pod with disruptionsAllowed:0 returned HTTP 201 instead of 429): [sig-apps] DisruptionController 'should block an eviction until the PDB is updated to allow it' ('Expected an error, got nil') AND [sig-apps] Job 'pod failure policy to ignore failure matching on DisruptionTarget condition' — SAME root cause. evict_pod (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:827-873) has ZERO PDB awareness and never sets pod conditions. FIX: (a) on /pods/{name}/eviction, look up matching PodDisruptionBudgets; if the pod is covered and status.disruptionsAllowed<=0, reject with 429 TooManyRequests (matching upstream eviction REST). (b) when an eviction/preemption/disruption proceeds, set the pod's DisruptionTarget condition (status.conditions) so pod-failure-policy consumers (Job controller) can match it. GATE: (1) unit/integration — eviction of a pod covered by a PDB with disruptionsAllowed:0 returns 429; (2) an evicted/disrupted pod gets a DisruptionTarget condition. Test WHY: PDBs are the primary safety mechanism against voluntary disruption; ignoring them lets evictions violate availability guarantees, and a missing DisruptionTarget condition breaks Job pod-failure-policy matching. Touches PDB status too (disruptionsAllowed must be computed) — check that PDB status is populated by KCM's disruption controller and readable.
close_reason: PR #718 opened: PDB-aware eviction (429 + DisruptionBudget cause) + DisruptionTarget condition

title: fix(apiserver): status subresource PUT/PATCH never injects TypeMeta (Deployment lifecycle)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aaf96, live-verified): [sig-apps] Deployment 'should run the lifecycle of a Deployment' STILL fails post-#710. #710 fixed inject_type_meta on the MAIN resource PUT/PATCH (resource.rs) but the STATUS subresource handlers were missed. ROOT CAUSE: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/status.rs — put_resource_status (:80), patch_resource_status (:125), put_namespaced_resource_status (:197), patch_namespaced_resource_status (:260) never call inject_type_meta. UpdateStatus() responses lack kind/apiVersion → dynamic/typed client missingKindErr. FIX: add inject_type_meta before the success response in all 4 status handlers, mirroring the resource.rs PUT/PATCH idiom (#710, resource.rs:2997 defines it). GATE: unit test — a status PUT/PATCH whose body omits kind/apiVersion returns an object with non-empty kind; must fail if the call is removed. Test WHY: UpdateStatus() from typed/dynamic clients requires TypeMeta on the response to decode; without it Deployment (and any) status update fails with 'Object Kind is missing'. Same bug CLASS as #710 h0ab, different handler family (status subresource).
close_reason: PR #717 opened

title: fix(apiserver): TokenReview response missing authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name extra info for bound SA tokens
description:
Live-verified on run 0707-0613 (worker mayor-owhv/mayor-s9u0 session): after the ServiceAccount admission fixes (default serviceAccountName + auto-mount token volume), the token/ca.crt/namespace files ARE correctly present in every pod (verified via kubectl exec: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/{token,ca.crt,namespace} all populated, kube-api-access-* volume+mount injected). Two conformance tests still fail for a DIFFERENT, deeper reason:

1. [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts 'should mount an API token into pods' fails at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/auth/service_accounts.go:151 with: 'expected single authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name extra info item matching <pod>, got []'. This test calls TokenReview on the pod's bound SA token and expects the response's status.user.extra to include authentication.kubernetes.io/{pod-name,pod-uid,service-account-uid} — u7s's token authenticator/TokenReview handler does not populate these extra fields for bound (projected) service-account tokens.

2. [sig-api-machinery] Aggregator 'Should be able to support the 1.17 Sample API Server' — sample-apiserver-deployment's sample-apiserver container CrashLoopBackOffs with only 'Shutting down, got signal: Terminated' surviving in the rotated container log (root cause not visible; happens before any request reaches u7s per apiserver.log — no GET to kube-system/configmaps/extension-apiserver-authentication, no 401/403 in the failure window, so this crashes before or during its own startup/client-auth setup). May share root cause with (1) since sample-apiserver's own SA token must also validate/authenticate correctly, or may be an unrelated startup issue (TLS cert secret, flags). Needs a from-scratch repro (kubectl run + inspect pod logs directly, not via sonobuoy) to pin down.

NOT caused by missing SA-name-default or missing token-volume injection — both proven correct via direct kubectl exec verification before this bead was filed. This is a separate authentication-layer gap.
notes: RE-CHECK AFTER the proto.rs securityContext decode cluster (mayor-cfp7/hdwo) lands. pl0h has two parts: (a) TokenReview response missing authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name extra for bound SA tokens; (b) sample-apiserver crash-loops before reaching u7s. Part (b) may be DOWNSTREAM of the securityContext protobuf-decode P1 bug (extension apiserver pods may have been mis-configured/failing due to dropped securityContext or SA-token mount). Re-verify (b) on a fresh stack once the proto cluster merges — it may already be resolved. Part (a) is a distinct TokenReview extra-info gap regardless. Do not dispatch until proto cluster lands + a re-check.
close_reason: PR #768 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/768 — implemented pod-name/pod-uid/node-name/node-uid TokenReview extra info for bound SA tokens (release-1.36 upstream check showed the third+fourth missing fields are node-name/node-uid, not service-account-uid as the bead paraphrased). Live-verified via kubectl TokenReview on lima-node-4 (v1.36.2): all extra fields present and matching actual pod/node UIDs. cargo test (2157 apiserver tests) + clippy clean. Flagged for operator signoff per auth-surface stance; not merged.

title: feat(apiserver): ServiceAccount admission auto-mount of default token volume into pods
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout ae178, live-reproduced x2): [sig-api-machinery] Aggregator sample-apiserver deployment ReadyReplicas:0 (crash-loops 'failed to get delegated authentication kubeconfig: ... no such file or directory'), and bare pods have no /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount. ROOT CAUSE: no ServiceAccount admission plugin — u7s never auto-injects the default kube-api-access-* projected token volume + volumeMount into every container (upstream ServiceAccount admission controller does this). FIX: implement ServiceAccount admission on pod create: inject a projected volume (serviceAccountToken + configmap ca.crt + downwardAPI namespace) named kube-api-access-XXXXX and mount it at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount in each container (unless automountServiceAccountToken=false). This is the LARGER of the SA beads — likely a new admission module. GATE: create a pod → it gets the kube-api-access volume + mount in every container; with automountServiceAccountToken=false it does NOT. Test WHY: in-cluster clients (incl extension apiservers, the sample-apiserver) read the token/ca from that path; without auto-mount they cannot authenticate and crash-loop → extension-apiserver/webhook deployments never become Ready. UNBLOCKS the Aggregator test and likely reduces contention on webhook-deployment tests. Depends on serviceAccountName defaulting (mayor-<B1>). Cross-ref [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts opting-out-of-automount + mount-API-token tests (may share this).
close_reason: PR #713 opened

title: fix(apiserver): default spec.serviceAccountName to "default" when omitted
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout ae178, live-reproduced): [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts 'should mount projected service account token' — pod never Succeeded. ROOT CAUSE: handlers/defaults.rs apply_defaults has NO Pod case, so spec.serviceAccountName is never defaulted to 'default'. Live repro: kubelet log 'failed to fetch token: resource name may not be empty' (client-go rejects empty resource name). FIX: add a Pod defaulting branch in apply_defaults that sets spec.serviceAccountName='default' when absent (and spec.deprecatedServiceAccount for compat if the codebase surfaces it — check). Mirror the existing default_service idiom. GATE: unit test — a Pod created without serviceAccountName gets 'default' after defaulting. Test WHY: kubelet/token machinery requires a non-empty SA name to fetch the projected token; an empty name fails token fetch and the pod never runs. Related: the auto-mount bead (token volume injection) is separate.
close_reason: PR #713 opened

title: fix(apiserver): emit optional field for ConfigMap/Secret volume and projected sources
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout ae178, live-reproduced): 4 failures — [sig-storage] ConfigMap optional updates reflected in volume, Projected configMap optional updates, Projected secret optional updates, Secrets optional updates — all pods never become running+ready (300s) because the kubelet gets FailedMount 'not found' for an OPTIONAL configmap/secret that should be tolerated. ROOT CAUSE: crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs gen_pod_spec_to_json (lines ~638-659, ~683-708) and gen_projected_volume_source_to_json (~135-166) — the 'optional' bool (proto field 4) on ConfigMap/Secret volume sources and projections is decoded by the generated prost struct but NEVER emitted into JSON. So the kubelet sees a required mount, blocks pod start on a missing optional source. Confirmed via the archived run's captured Pod object (no 'optional' key) + matching kubelet FailedMount event. FIX: emit 'optional': <bool> in those blocks (only when set, matching k8s omitempty semantics — verify how other optional bools are emitted in the same file). GATE: unit test — decode a pod with a ConfigMap volume source optional=true → JSON carries optional:true; same for secret + projected. Test WHY: an optional configmap/secret volume must not block pod startup when the source is absent; dropping 'optional' makes every optional mount behave as required. Cross-ref memory adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation.
close_reason: PR #715 opened — emits optional bool for ConfigMap/Secret volume + projected sources; live-verified pod with optional-absent CM/secret volumes reaches Running; sonobuoy focus 5/5 passed

title: fix(apiserver): decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen never decodes status (phase/message/reason)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aee89): [sig-storage] PersistentVolumes CSI Conformance 'should apply changes to a pv/pvc status' fails — updated status comes back empty. Scout notes PV/PVC decoders look broadly incomplete (dead-code warnings on PersistentVolumeClaim* structs — see also mayor-imn3). FIX: decode PV status.phase/message/reason. title: fix(apiserver): decode_ingress_proto_gen never decodes status.loadBalancer

title: fix(apiserver): MicroTime decode drops pre-1970 acquireTime/renewTime on Lease
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aee89): [sig-node] Lease 'lease API should be available' fails — AcquireTime/RenewTime come back nil (should be set). ROOT CAUSE: gen_microtime_fields_to_rfc3339 (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:9-14) does 'if secs <= 0 { return None }', silently dropping the field. The conformance test deliberately uses pre-1970 timestamps (time.Time{}.Add(2s)) which are negative/near-zero as Unix seconds. FIX: secs_to_rfc3339 (and the MicroTime helper) must accept i64/negative values and emit the correct pre-1970 RFC3339 — do NOT just remove the guard (must handle negative seconds correctly). GATE: decode a MicroTime with negative Unix seconds -> correct pre-1970 RFC3339 string, not None. Test WHY: Lease acquire/renew times can legitimately be any instant; dropping non-positive times makes leader-election/heartbeat leases look never-acquired. This helper is shared, so the fix also unblocks the Job/CronJob condition-time beads. Cross-ref memory adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation.

title: fix(apiserver): replace_resource/replace_namespaced_resource omit kind/apiVersion on PUT response
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aee89, mayor-verified): [sig-apps] Deployment 'should run the lifecycle of a Deployment' fails 'failed to update the DeploymentStatus: Object Kind is missing'. MISGROUPED as a /status bug — it is actually a general PUT-response bug on the MAIN resource (test uses a dynamic/unstructured client Update). ROOT CAUSE: replace_resource (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:350) and replace_namespaced_resource (:1429) NEVER call inject_type_meta before responding, unlike GET (225,1145), POST (299,1273), and PATCH (342,867,900,1312) in the same file. Mayor-verified via grep: those two fn bodies are absent from the inject_type_meta call sites. A PUT with kind/apiVersion omitted echoes the omission back -> unstructured-client decode fails (runtime.NewMissingKindErr). FIX: add inject_type_meta(&mut obj.body, &group, &version, &meta.kind) before the final response in BOTH replace_resource and replace_namespaced_resource, mirroring the existing PATCH-path calls. GATE: an existing test idiom exists (resource.rs:5798, 9776, 9851 assert inject_type_meta presence on GET/PATCH) — add the equivalent for PUT: a PUT whose body omits kind/apiVersion must return an object with non-empty Kind; removing the new inject_type_meta call must fail the test. Test WHY: unstructured/dynamic clients require TypeMeta on Update responses to decode; without it every dynamic-client PUT breaks. HIGH VALUE — affects all PUT, not just Deployment.

title: fix(apiserver): add dedicated CRD status subresource route (apiextensions .../customresourcedefinitions/{name}/status)

title: fix(apiserver): register trailing-slash discovery routes for /api/, /apis/, /apis/{group}/
description: Conformance (2 failures, run 0707-0454, scout aa225): [sig-api-machinery] Discovery should validate PreferredVersion for each APIGroup ('Failed to find /apis/: server could not find the requested resource') and [sig-cli] Kubectl proxy --port 0 ('Expected at least one supported apiversion, got'). title: apiserver: no validation of securityContext.sysctls[].name format at pod admission (should reject invalid sysctls test)
description: VERIFIED live (h24j scout a18244, 2026-07-07). Conformance 'should reject invalid sysctls' expects the APISERVER to reject malformed sysctl NAMES at pod create (422, message with Invalid value: 'foo-' and Invalid value: 'bar..' — syntactic name validation, independent of allow/deny-listing). u7s ACCEPTS the pod (created, exit 0) and persists the malformed names; the pod is later killed by the KUBELET with 'SysctlForbidden: forbidden sysctl foo- not allowlisted' — WRONG layer + WRONG message (that's the allowlist check for valid-but-unsafe sysctls, a different mechanism). u7s has NO apiserver-side sysctl-name-format validation. FIX: add structural validation of securityContext.sysctls[].name on the pod create/update admission path (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs, near other securityContext validation — scout couldn't locate an existing sysctl validator; may need a new fn). Validate the k8s sysctl name format (segments matching the sysctl naming rules); reject malformed at 422. GATE: create a pod with sysctls [{name:'foo-'},{name:'kernel.shmmax',value:'100000000'},{name:'safe-and-unsafe',value:'100000000'},{name:'bar..',value:'42'}] → REJECTED at create with 422 containing Invalid value: 'foo-' and 'bar..', and must NOT reject/mention kernel.shmmax or safe-and-unsafe (syntactically valid). Split from EPIC h24j.

title: apiserver: pod resize validation conflates 'key absent from patch' with 'key removed' → false-positive QoS/removal rejections (2 InPlaceResize conformance tests)
description: VERIFIED with 2 live repros (h24j scout a18244, 2026-07-07). Both failing InPlaceResize conformance tests ('3 containers various operations', '6 containers various operations') build their resize PATCH via strategicpatch.CreateTwoWayMergePatch, which OMITS unchanged resource keys (a cpu-only change produces a patch section with no memory key — meaning 'memory unchanged', NOT 'remove memory'). u7s misinterprets absent-key as removal. ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs): (1) merge_resize_for_qos (~2055) REPLACES stored_container['resources'][section] WHOLESALE with incoming[section] instead of merging key-by-key → a cpu-only patch drops the existing memory key before QoS is recomputed → false 'QOS class may not change' rejection. (2) validate_resize_patch Rule 3 (~2000) reads incoming['limits'/'requests'][resource] via serde index → Value::Null for BOTH absent (unchanged→preserve) AND explicit null (real removal) → can't distinguish → false 'resource requests cannot be removed'. REPRO A: Guaranteed 3-container pod, PATCH only c1 cpu (memory omitted) → 'QOS Class may not change ... Guaranteed→Burstable' (should be accepted). REPRO B: Burstable pod (requests only), PATCH only requests.memory (cpu omitted) → 'resources.requests.cpu: resource requests cannot be removed' (should be accepted). FIX: merge_resize_for_qos merge per-key (not replace section); Rule 3 use .get() to distinguish None(absent→preserve stored) from Some(Null)(explicit removal); KEEP wholly-absent/null section = 'remove all in section' (the existing passing 'remove cpu&memory limits' test needs that — don't regress). GATE (2 unit tests, reject→accept): (a) Guaranteed 3-ctr, patch touching only c1 cpu → Ok; (b) Burstable requests-only, patch only requests.memory → Ok. HIGHEST-VALUE h24j fix: deterministic, one root cause, both failing tests. Split from EPIC h24j.

title: pods/exec CONNECT webhook denial likely masked the same way as pods/attach (mayor-u6eb)
description:
Same class of bug as mayor-u6eb (fixed via PR #705), NOT yet fixed here.

/exec has the identical get(pod_exec).post(pod_exec) routing (crates/apiserver/src/main.rs), where pod_exec's last extractor is also axum's WebSocketUpgrade. kubectl exec uses the same k8s.io/client-go/tools/remotecommand fallback executor as attach: it dials WebSocket (GET) first, and treats any non-101 handshake response (including a correct admission-webhook 403 denial) as an upgrade failure, silently retrying via POST (SPDY) — discarding the original GET attempt's error/message. Since pod_exec's POST leg hits the same WebSocketUpgrade extractor, it 405s with axum's generic 'Request method must be `GET`' before resolve_exec_target/admission ever runs on the retry — masking a webhook's denial exactly like pods/attach did before mayor-u6eb.

Not verified live — flagged during mayor-u6eb's investigation as the same pattern by inspection, not confirmed with a real kubectl exec + deny-webhook repro. portforward may or may not share this (kubectl port-forward historically defaults to SPDY-first rather than WebSocket-first; needs its own check before assuming the same fix applies).

Suggested fix: mirror mayor-u6eb's approach — a pod_exec_post handler that calls resolve_exec_target (running admission) and returns its Result, falling back to 501 if all checks pass.
close_reason: Merged PR #707 (51c4c1a7). Found more than expected (Rule 8): resolve_exec_target had ZERO admission integration — pods/exec webhooks were never invoked on EITHER GET or POST. Fix: (1) added run_validating_webhooks to resolve_exec_target (resource=pods/exec, operation=CONNECT, mirroring attach); (2) added pod_exec_post (no WS extractor) reusing resolve_exec_target, propagating Status, 501 if all pass; (3) /exec route get(pod_exec).post(pod_exec_post). Live-verified: exec denial now surfaces the webhook message on both GET+POST legs (403 each); webhook received both CONNECT requests. 2 fail-on-revert tests. Completes the attach/exec webhook-denial pair (u6eb #705 = attach).

comments.author: Erdos Balint
comments.text: PR #707 opened (branch worker/agent-aa5c1b31296960f3e): mirrors mayor-u6eb/#705 for pods/exec. Fix has two parts: (1) resolve_exec_target had NO admission check at all (unlike resolve_attach_target) -- added run_validating_webhooks for resource pods/exec op CONNECT; (2) added pod_exec_post handler (no WebSocketUpgrade extractor) reusing resolve_exec_target, POST route repointed. Live-verified on lima-node-smoke:6444 with webhook-scout test double: kubectl exec now surfaces the webhook's actual denial message instead of a generic 405; apiserver.log shows both GET and POST legs returning 403. Regression tests added, fail-on-revert proven manually. Not merged, bead left open per instructions -- mayor to merge/close.

title: admission webhooks skipped on deletecollection (delete_collection_resource / delete_collection_namespaced_resource)
description: Follow-up to mayor-w354: single-object DELETE handlers (delete_resource, delete_namespaced_resource, delete_pod, delete_cr(_namespaced), delete_crd, delete_namespace) now run the validating admission webhook chain before deleting. delete_collection_resource and delete_collection_namespaced_resource (DELETE on the collection endpoint, e.g. 'kubectl delete cm --all') were intentionally left out of that fix to keep the change scoped: they loop over every matching object in a single request and none of them extract the caller's UserInfo today. Upstream kube-apiserver's DeleteCollection calls admission per object being deleted. FIX: thread Extension<UserInfo> into both handlers and call run_validating_webhooks per object (with operation=DELETE) inside the deletion loop in resource.rs, matching the per-object semantics of the single-delete handlers; skip/continue objects a Fail-policy webhook denies rather than aborting the whole collection (match upstream: partial failure, not all-or-nothing) — needs a design decision on the aggregate response shape when some objects are denied.
acceptance_criteria: kubectl delete <resource> --all against a namespace/cluster with a Fail-policy validating webhook denies the matching objects (and only those); cargo test -p u7s-apiserver passes; cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean.
notes: PR #704 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/704 — awaiting review/merge. Deny semantics deviated from the bead's proposed skip/continue design: used fail-fast (propagate first denial, abort request) to match the existing non-NotFound-store-error handling already in this loop; see PR body for rationale. Live-verified on lima-node-smoke:6444 via raw DELETE to the collection endpoint (kubectl's own --all resolves client-side to per-object deletes, so it doesn't exercise this path).
close_reason: Merged PR #704 (028769fc). Per-object validating admission (operation=DELETE) added to delete_collection_resource + delete_collection_namespaced_resource, mirroring #700's single-delete pattern; UserInfo threaded through core.rs collection handler + 2 router test fixups. Fail-fast deny semantics (task instruction over bead's skip/continue — flagged Rule 7). 2 fail-on-revert tests. Live-verified via raw collection DELETE endpoint (both namespaced+cluster-scoped): Fail-policy VWC -> 500, objects survive; removed -> 200, deleted. Completes the deletecollection half of webhook DELETE admission (w354 did single delete).

title: admission webhook matchConditions not evaluated at invocation (CEL only checked syntactically at registration)
description: VERIFIED live (scout aa9f7278, 2026-07-06): a webhook with matchCondition 'object.metadata.name != "skip-me"' mutated BOTH skip-me AND a normal configmap identically — matchConditions are never evaluated at invocation. WebhookEntry (admission.rs L108-126) has NO match_conditions field. They ARE validated syntactically at config write time (validate_webhook_match_conditions_cel L2047) but ignored at runtime. FIX: add match_conditions to WebhookEntry, and in run_*_webhooks skip a webhook when any matchCondition CEL-evaluates false — reuse the existing CEL evaluator (already used for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy). Breaks conformance 'should mutate everything except skip-me configmaps'. SMALL. GATE: webhook w/ matchCondition excluding name=skip-me -> skip-me NOT mutated, others mutated.
notes: PR #701 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/701 (feat(apiserver): evaluate admission webhook matchConditions at invocation). Not merged/closed per task instructions — mayor will merge and resolve any overlap with mayor-w354 (also touching admission.rs).

title: PodTemplate missing from /api/v1 discovery resource list — kubectl get/apply podtemplates fails with 'server doesn't have a resource type'
description:
Found while live-verifying mayor-tw11 (fieldValidation=Strict top-level field fix).

crates/apiserver/src/types.rs V1_RESOURCES (the static list backing GET /api/v1,
served by handlers/discovery.rs::api_v1_resources) has no entry for "podtemplates",
even though:
  - state.rs::build_registry registers ("", "v1", "podtemplates") — the resource IS
    served (POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/podtemplates returns 201).
  - main.rs wires generic core routes for it via the {resource} catch-all.

Live repro against a freshly built worktree stack (port 6445):
  $ kubectl get podtemplates -n default
  error: the server doesn't have a resource type "podtemplates"
  $ kubectl get endpoints -n default   # contrast: endpoints IS in V1_RESOURCES
  No resources found in default namespace.

Because kubectl resolves Kind -> resource name via discovery (RESTMapper) before
issuing any request, this means `kubectl apply -f <podtemplate.yaml>` and
`kubectl get podtemplates` never reach the apiserver's create/list handlers at
all — they fail locally in kubectl with "no matches for kind". A direct REST
POST (bypassing kubectl's discovery) works fine and correctly enforces
fieldValidation=Strict (see mayor-tw11).

Fix: add a "podtemplates" ApiResource entry to V1_RESOURCES in types.rs
(name, singular_name: "podtemplate", namespaced: true, kind: "PodTemplate",
verbs: CORE_VERBS, short_names: None) — mirroring the existing entries for
endpoints/events immediately above/below it alphabetically. Add a regression
test following the existing discovery.rs table-driven pattern
(names.contains(&"podtemplates")) so this can't silently regress again.
notes: MAYOR-VERIFIED LIVE (2026-07-06, HEAD 638da558): GET /api/v1 discovery does NOT list 'podtemplates' (confirmed: configmaps/endpoints/events/secrets/etc ARE listed, podtemplates is NOT). So kubectl get/apply/describe podtemplates fails client-side ('the server doesn't have a resource type') before reaching the apiserver — even though a direct curl POST to /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/podtemplates works (201). FIX: add the podtemplates entry to V1_RESOURCES in crates/apiserver/src/types.rs (name=podtemplates, singularName=podtemplate, namespaced=true, kind=PodTemplate, verbs=[create,delete,deletecollection,get,list,patch,update,watch]). Match the existing entries' shape. Trivial. GATE: kubectl get podtemplates -> no discovery error (empty list ok). Pairs with tw11 (#697) which fixes the fieldValidation side; both needed for PodTemplate to be fully usable via kubectl. Likely contributes to a fast-fail conformance failure that touches podtemplates (e.g. the chunking test creates podtemplates). Small, clean, dispatch-ready.
close_reason: Merged PR #698 (42924220). Added podtemplates entry to V1_RESOURCES (types.rs); regression test podtemplates_advertised_in_v1_discovery fail-on-revert; live gate kubectl get/apply/describe podtemplates all work (no 'server doesn't have a resource type'). Pairs with tw11 (#697) fieldValidation fix — PodTemplate now fully usable via kubectl.

title: fieldValidation=Strict falsely rejects non-spec top-level fields on PodTemplate, core/events.k8s.io Event, and CSIStorageCapacity
description:
Follow-up from the known_top_level_fields audit done for mayor-i5x4 (ValidatingWebhookConfiguration/MutatingWebhookConfiguration fix). Same root cause, different resource types: known_top_level_fields (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs) falls back to the default ["apiVersion","kind","metadata","spec","status"] set for any (group, plural) without an explicit arm. Several REGISTERED (state.rs build_registry) and SERVED types have top-level fields that are neither "spec" nor "status", so fieldValidation=Strict (kubectl's default) falsely 422s "unknown field" for every real field on these types. Verified against the vendored upstream proto (crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/.../generated.proto):

- core/v1 PodTemplate ("", "podtemplates"): real top-level field is `template` (PodTemplateSpec), not `spec`.
- core/v1 Endpoints ("", "endpoints") — NOT EndpointSlice, already fixed separately: real top-level field is `subsets`.
- core/v1 Event ("", "events"): top-level fields are involvedObject, reason, message, source, firstTimestamp, lastTimestamp, count, type, eventTime, series, action, related, reportingComponent, reportingInstance (verify full list against k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto — old-style Event schema, NOT spec/status shaped at all).
- events.k8s.io/v1 Event ("events.k8s.io", "events"): different schema from core Event — eventTime, series, reportingController, reportingInstance, action, reason, regarding, related, note, type, deprecatedSource, deprecatedFirstTimestamp, deprecatedLastTimestamp, deprecatedCount (see crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/events/v1/generated.proto).
- storage.k8s.io/v1 CSIStorageCapacity ("storage.k8s.io", "csistoragecapacities"): top-level fields are nodeTopology, storageClassName, capacity, maximumVolumeSize (see crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/storage/v1/generated.proto:387+).

Confirmed all five (group, plural) pairs are present in state.rs::build_registry and therefore reachable via the generic create_resource handler (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs), which calls apply_field_validation unconditionally per POST — so they are live, reachable 422 false-positives under fieldValidation=Strict, not speculative.

NOT included in mayor-i5x4's fix: that PR is scoped narrowly to the admissionregistration.k8s.io webhook config types per its title/deliverable. This bead tracks the additional gaps found during that bead's required audit step, deliberately kept out of that PR's diff to keep it surgical.

Fix: add match arms to known_top_level_fields for each (group, plural) pair above, verified field-for-field against the vendored proto (do not guess). Add regression tests following the existing endpointslice_top_level_fields_are_not_unknown / webhook_configuration_webhooks_field_is_not_unknown pattern in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs.

GATE: for each type, curl POST with ?fieldValidation=Strict&dryRun=All using a body containing only its real top-level fields -> assert 2xx (not 422).
notes: MAYOR-VERIFIED LIVE (2026-07-06, HEAD 24027ca6): all reproduce as 422 under fieldValidation=Strict&dryRun=All — PodTemplate(template)->422, Endpoints(subsets)->422, CSIStorageCapacity->422.
