title: apiserver does not resolve priorityClassName → spec.priority on pod create (blocks scheduler preemption)
description: VERIFIED live (mayor + rsei worker, 2026-07-06): creating a Pod with only spec.priorityClassName set leaves spec.priority NULL/absent after create (priorityClassName is preserved, but not resolved). Setting spec.priority explicitly survives (osuq's wire-decode works). No admission logic resolves priorityClassName -> PriorityClass.value -> spec.priority anywhere (admission.rs, handlers/defaults.rs, handlers/pods.rs all checked, zero hits). GAP: on pod create (and the PriorityClass admission plugin's job upstream), if spec.priorityClassName is set and spec.priority is absent, look up the PriorityClass object by name and copy .value into spec.priority (also handle globalDefault PriorityClass when no className given; and the two built-in system-cluster-critical/system-node-critical classes). BLOCKS preemption: the scheduler's new preemption logic (PR #695, mayor-rsei) keys off spec.priority which is always 0 without this. This is the HIGHEST-LEVERAGE next step to make '[sig-scheduling] SchedulerPreemption validates basic preemption works' reachable. GATE: kubectl create a PriorityClass (value N) + a pod with priorityClassName=it, GET pod -> assert spec.priority == N. Likely small (a create-path defaulting step). Discovered building rsei.
notes: PR #699 REVIEWED + APPROVED (mayor, pending green CI). Resolution in async create_pod handler (store GET of scheduling.k8s.io/priorityclasses) delegating to pure resolve_pod_priority_class(pod, stored_class) — correct semantics: early-return on no/empty className + on explicit priority (preserves osuq's wire value); system-cluster-critical(2000000000)/system-node-critical(2000001000) matched by name BEFORE store (work without seeded objects, verified live); not-found -> Err -> 403 Forbidden (matches upstream + the file's RuntimeClass convention); preemptionPolicy copied only if pod didn't set one. globalDefault deferred (MVP, not needed by preemption tests). Single file +480 (11 tests: 8 pure + 3 integration), clippy clean. Live gate: PriorityClass(12345)+pod -> priority=12345; nonexistent className -> 403; system-cluster-critical -> 2000000000 unseeded. WILL MERGE on green. UNBLOCKS mayor-rsei — after this, the shipped preemption (#695) can see real priorities; SchedulerPreemption basic test becomes reachable (still needs kg2s extended-resource accounting for the specific tests). Survived a port collision (mayor dispatched it + kc54 scout on same :6445 — 2u9x's final gate still ran clean).
close_reason: Merged PR #699 (19ed8bc4). resolve_pod_priority_class in create_pod handler: priorityClassName→spec.priority via store GET, system-cluster/node-critical hardcoded, 403 on not-found, explicit priority preserved; 11 tests, live-verified. UNBLOCKS rsei.

title: proto decode drops Namespace status (decode_namespace_proto_gen ignored ns.status → phase+conditions lost for protobuf clients)
description: VERIFIED (worker a897, PR #694): crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs decode_namespace_proto_gen never read ns.status — any protobuf-encoded Namespace write silently loses status.phase AND status.conditions. Classic proto-decode-drop class (cf dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check). Fix mirrors the existing Service status.conditions decode pattern in the same file + a prost encode->decode round-trip test (namespace_status_put_preserves_phase...). This fix is GOOD and should land — it rode into PR #694 (ftkl) but is UNRELATED to the ftkl panic (that stack uses JSON, not protobuf, for ns writes, so this drop never fired there). Carve it out of #694 (or keep it in #694 but relabel — mayor decides). Gate: prost-encode a Namespace with status.phase=Active + a condition, decode via decode_namespace_proto_gen, assert both survive. Discovered while reviewing ftkl; the worker was right to fix it but flag the disconnect.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-07-07, ftkl PANIC-1 worker a5bd2f2f): my earlier note calling this 'unrelated to the ftkl panic' was WRONG. decode_namespace_proto_gen decoding ns.status (this fix, #694/a1902a96) IS the fix for ftkl PANIC-1. WHY I got it wrong: the e2e client sends UpdateStatus as application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf (e2e framework defaults typed clients to protobuf; 06-run-sonobuoy.sh doesn't override), so the namespace-status PUT goes through the PROTO decoder — which dropped status until this fix. My probe used JSON (+ the mayor's :6443 was cert-drifted anyway), so I saw JSON-path working and wrongly concluded proto-decode was unrelated. The two-client distinction (KCM uses --kube-api-content-type=application/json; e2e uses protobuf) is the crux. So oww6 (#694) and ftkl PANIC-1 are the SAME fix. LESSON: content-type determines the decode path; test the path the FAILING CLIENT uses (protobuf), not the convenient one (JSON).
close_reason: Merged in PR #694 (c92d9d6a). decode_namespace_proto_gen now decodes ns.status (phase+conditions), mirroring the Service pattern; round-trip regression test proven fail-on-revert. Proto-decode-drop class fix.

title: wrap long conformance runs in caffeinate to prevent host-sleep wall-clock inflation
description:
Unattended overnight full-conformance runs on macOS accumulate ~8h of dead wall-clock because the host sleeps (~15min DarkWake cycles freeze apiserver+scheduler+Lima-kubelet together). VERIFIED root cause of the '12h vs ginkgo-4h' discrepancy on runs 0705-1409 + 0706-1152 (see bead d13f, closed). Ginkgo's exec clock is correct (~4-5h); the excess is pure host-sleep.

FIX: prevent sleep for the duration of a run. Options: (a) document + require operators run 'caffeinate -dimsu scripts/conformance/run-all.sh ...' for full runs; (b) have run-all.sh self-wrap in caffeinate when it detects a full (non---focus, non---stack-only) run — spawn 'caffeinate -w $$' as a child so it dies with the script; (c) macOS Energy Saver 'prevent automatic sleeping'. Prefer (b) — automatic, no operator memory required — but keep it macOS-guarded (Linux CI doesn't need it). ACCEPTANCE: a full overnight run's apiserver.log shows NO synchronized multi-minute gaps across apiserver/scheduler/kubelet-lease; wall-clock ~= ginkgo 'Ran in'. Low effort, high value (unblocks trustworthy overnight baselining). Note: keeping the host awake for ~5h is fine; this is local Mac dev only.

title: Server-Side Apply not supported — apply-patch+yaml content-type returns 400 (blocks ApplyStatus + kubectl apply --server-side, multiple conformance failures)
description:
VERIFIED live (apiserver :6443, HEAD 1fb9c258, 2026-07-06): u7s does NOT support Server-Side Apply. A PATCH with Content-Type 'application/apply-patch+yaml' returns 400 'invalid patch JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' on BOTH a status subresource (namespaces/X/status) AND a plain resource (default/configmaps/Y) — u7s is parsing the YAML apply body as JSON and failing. So the apply-patch content-type isn't handled at all.

IMPACT: SSA is used pervasively — every e2e ApplyStatus() call, kubectl apply --server-side, and many conformance tests that build objects via Apply configurations. Surfaced via the ftkl panic cluster (Namespaces 'apply changes to a namespace status' panics because ApplyStatus 400s then the client indexes an empty slice), but the blast radius is far wider. Likely one of the highest-leverage single correctness levers.

REPRO / GATE (fast, kubectl+curl, no VM): 
curl -sk --cert <c> --key <k> -X PATCH -H 'Content-Type: application/apply-patch+yaml' --data-binary '<yaml manifest>' '<server>/api/v1/namespaces/default/configmaps/ssa-test?fieldManager=test'
BUG = 400 'invalid patch JSON'. FIXED = 200/201 with the object, and a second apply with a different fieldManager merges/conflicts per SSA semantics.

SCOPE NOTE (pre-alpha): full SSA (managedFields tracking, field ownership, conflict detection, apply-patch+json too) is large. A scout should size it: minimum viable = parse apply-patch+yaml/json, treat apply as upsert (create-or-merge), populate managedFields enough that ApplyStatus round-trips and clients don't panic. Determine whether a reduced SSA satisfies the conformance tests or whether field-ownership/conflict is required. Flag as an EPIC candidate. ARCHITECTURE/API-SURFACE — flag for operator before large build. Root-caused under mayor-ftkl.
notes:
SIZING COMPLETE (scout a54a, 2026-07-06) + MAYOR-VERIFIED. REFRAME: this is a SMALL MVP parser bug, NOT a high-leverage conformance lever, NOT P1 (downgraded to P2). KEY FINDINGS:
1. ROOT CAUSE is precise: ~8 built-in PATCH handlers detect Content-Type application/apply-patch+yaml but parse the body with serde_json::from_slice / Object::from_bytes (JSON-only) -> real multi-line YAML 400s with 'invalid patch JSON'. A YAML-tolerant parser (cr.rs:469 ssa_body_to_json, using yaml_rust2 already a dep) EXISTS and WORKS but is wired into only 2 call sites (CR-create path, fixed by mayor-4xgf/PR#672). MVP = generalize it to the other ~8 sites: resource.rs:639/676/735 (do_patch), status.rs:146/293 (+ these lack ANY is_ssa handling), namespaces.rs:640, pods.rs:646, approval.rs:101, cr.rs update-path 1656/1791. Move ssa_body_to_json to a shared home (json_patch.rs). Size ~= mayor-4xgf (single small PR, no new deps). crates/store needs NO changes.
2. CONFORMANCE BLAST RADIUS ~= 0 (contradicts this bead's original 'highest-leverage' framing). The real SSA-semantics tests (test/e2e/apimachinery/apply.go: conflict/force/field-removal/managedFields) use ginkgo.It NOT framework.ConformanceIt -> they do NOT run under u7s's --mode=non-disruptive-conformance suite. The conformance-tagged CR-apply tests (field_validation.go) hit the already-fixed CR-create path (#672, 21/21 passed). So MVP fixes a real bug for 'kubectl apply --server-side' + Argo CD (real repo goals) but is NOT a conformance-failure lever.
3. FULL SSA (managedFields persistence, structured-merge-diff conflict/409/force) = EPIC, multi-week, NO Rust crate exists (verified crates.io: structured-merge=0, fieldsv1=0 results). DEFER; needs operator ARCHITECTURE sign-off (esp. whether to persist managedFields in stored JSON — a visible GET/LIST behavior change). Decide AFTER an MVP + fresh sonobuoy shows real residual count. Full doc was in the scout return.
ACTION: keep kz1m as the MVP parser-fix bead (P2, dispatchable, gate: curl apply-patch+yaml on a configmap -> 2xx). File a SEPARATE P3 EPIC bead for full-SSA (deferred, operator-gated).
close_reason: PR #799 opened — generalized ssa_body_to_json to all 8 remaining SSA call sites (resource.rs do_patch x3, status.rs x2, namespaces.rs, pods.rs, approval.rs, cr.rs update-path x2); moved shared parser to json_patch.rs; live curl+kubectl gate confirms 400->2xx on genuine multi-line YAML across all sites

title: apiserver returns malformed/missing responses → 5 conformance tests PANIC (namespace status conditions, strict fieldValidation, GC, statefulset)
description:
Run 0706-1152: 5 [PANICKED!] conformance specs. The panic is in the Go e2e CLIENT (runtime/panic.go) — the apiserver did NOT crash (run completed) — but each is a real apiserver correctness bug: the apiserver returns a structurally-wrong or missing response that the client immediately nil-derefs / indexes out of range. Fast panics (0.03-2s) confirm it's a bad RESPONSE, not a hang. All are kubectl-reproducible (good before/after gates). Source pinned release-1.36.

PANIC 1 (CLEAN REPRO) — Namespaces 'should apply changes to a namespace status', namespace.go:365, 'index out of range [-1]'. Test does PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{name}/status then reads patchedStatus.Status.Conditions[len-1]. u7s returns 0 conditions -> len-1 = -1 -> panic. REPRO: kubectl patch ns <n> --subresource=status --type=merge -p '{"status":{"conditions":[{...}]}}' and GET; assert .status.conditions is present & non-empty. ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: u7s namespace /status subresource doesn't persist/return status.conditions.

PANIC 2 (CLEAN REPRO) — FieldValidation 'should detect unknown and duplicate fields of a typed object', field_validation.go:104, nil deref on err.Error(). Test does POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/{ns}/deployments?fieldValidation=Strict with a body containing unknown+duplicate fields, expects a 400 'strict decoding error: unknown field'. u7s returns err==nil (ACCEPTS the invalid body) -> test calls nil.Error() -> panic. REPRO: POST a deployment with a bogus top-level field + ?fieldValidation=Strict; assert HTTP 400 + 'strict decoding error'. ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: u7s does not implement fieldValidation=Strict (unknown/duplicate field rejection).

PANIC 3 — Namespaces 'should ensure that all pods are removed when a namespace is deleted', namespace.go:247, nil deref. Pod Create response deref'd for Spec fields. Investigate whether Create returns an incomplete Pod.

PANIC 4 — Garbage collector 'should not delete dependents that have both valid owner and owner waiting for dependents', garbage_collector.go:722 (120s then panic). Likely ownerReferences/GC finalizer response shape.

PANIC 5 — StatefulSet 'Burst scaling should run to completion even with unhealthy pods', statefulset.go:836 (70s then panic). Likely related to qrip (statefulset rollout) — may dedupe.

ACCEPTANCE: a scout reproduces PANIC 1 + PANIC 2 via kubectl (highest-confidence, cleanest), confirms the missing behavior (ns status.conditions; strict fieldValidation), and files/rescopes fix beads. PANIC 3/4/5 need the test source read (namespace.go:247, garbage_collector.go:722, statefulset.go:836) to confirm the exact response gap. Split into fix beads by root cause. These are P1 because a malformed apiserver response that panics a well-behaved client is a correctness red flag beyond the specific test.
notes:
PANIC-1 test coverage MERGED PR #708 (7eae86f5): put_namespace_status_persists_conditions_from_protobuf_content_type regression test (fail-on-revert proven) + corrected the misleading oww6/proto comments. PANIC-1 fully closed (fix was #694, now test-covered on the protobuf path). ftkl remains OPEN for PANIC-3 (ns ensure-pods-removed nil-deref), PANIC-4 (GC dependents), PANIC-5 (statefulset burst-scaling) — need root-causing on a clean stack.
RESCOPE 2026-07-16 (conformance run 0715-2142 reconciliation): PANIC-4 (GC multi-owner dependents) is now split out to its own bead mayor-jdh73 (P1) -- root-caused live to delete_pods_owned_by ignoring co-ownership; reuse strip_owner_from_resources. ftkl is now scoped to PANIC-3 (namespace.go:247 nil-deref, ns ensure-pods-removed) + PANIC-5 (statefulset.go:836 burst-scaling) ONLY. Neither PANIC-3 nor PANIC-5 appeared as a FAILURE in run 0715-2142's 17-failure set -- they may be masked by an earlier skip/precondition or already resolved; a scout should confirm whether they still reproduce on the current stack before further work, or this bead may be closeable. Downgraded P1->P2 since the P1-signature piece (PANIC-4) moved to jdh73.
close_reason: Re-confirmed BOTH remaining PANICs RESOLVED on current main via kubectl repro + sonobuoy --focus gates on lima-node-4 (findings: ai/findings/ftkl-panic3-panic5-reconfirm-2026-07-23.md, not committed). PANIC-3 (namespace.go:247, ensurePodsAreRemovedWhenNamespaceIsDeleted deref of pod.Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds at line 132): fixed by 76be4f86 (mayor-y2p53, 2026-07-13) which defaults spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30 on pod create. kubectl repro confirms non-nil field + full create-ns/pod/delete-ns/recreate-ns/verify-pod-gone sequence works; sonobuoy --focus 'should ensure that all pods are removed when a namespace is deleted' -> Ran 1 of 7579 Specs, SUCCESS 1 Passed 0 Failed. PANIC-5 (statefulset.go:836, Burst scaling): no single fixing commit identified, but manually reproduced the full test sequence (Parallel podManagementPolicy StatefulSet, break/restore readiness via exec, burst scale-up 1->3 while unhealthy, burst scale-down 3->0 while unhealthy) live -- all steps behave correctly, no nil derefs; sonobuoy --focus 'Burst scaling should run to completion even with unhealthy pods' -> Ran 1 of 7579 Specs, SUCCESS 1 Passed 0 Failed. No follow-on beads needed.

title: investigate: workload pods never reach awaited status → deployment/job/var-expansion tests hang (~1h wall-clock combined)
description:
Cluster of test-hangs in run 0705-2315 sharing one signature: object exists (GET 200) but never reaches the status the e2e framework polls for, so the test hangs until watchdog reap. Verified from apiserver.log:
- deployment-8597 (331s): polls GET pods/webserver-deployment-… + GET replicasets/… — Deployment rollout never reaches Available (pods PATCHed but rollout not satisfied).
- job-9079 (671s): 1031 PATCH …/pods/fail-once-local-*/status — the Job backoff/'fail once then succeed' test; pods churn status but Job completion never observed.
- var-expansion-7371 (974s): polls GET pods/var-expansion-… every 2s — pod phase transition (env-var substitution / subpath expansion) never completes.
SHARED HYPOTHESIS: a pod-readiness/phase or workload-controller-status gap (KCM writes status but the awaited condition — Available/Complete/Succeeded/Ready — never flips). title: API list chunking/pagination (?limit + ?continue) — sig-api-machinery chunking tests hang (~31m wall-clock, 2 ns)
description: Two chunking namespaces (chunking-8870 1873s… actually 929s, chunking-4661 944s) hung ~31m combined in run 0705-2315, watchdog-reaped. Verified from apiserver.log: the test creates many podtemplates (POST …/podtemplates ×N) then polls GET …/podtemplates?limit=40 — it was still on the FIRST page (limit=40) and never advanced, indicating the ?continue pagination token isn't honored (either not emitted in the list response's metadata.continue, or a follow-up ?limit=&continue=<token> isn't served correctly). sig-api-machinery '[Chunking] should return chunks of results for list calls' / 'should support continue listing…'. ACCEPTANCE: LIST with ?limit=N returns metadata.continue when more items exist; a follow-up LIST with that continue token returns the next page; the chunking --focus passes. Root-cause with a kubectl-driven repro (create 50 podtemplates, GET ?limit=10, follow continue) before fixing. Wall-clock cost ranked in d13f. No existing bead.
notes: (2026-07-06, adding to prior note) basic ?limit+continue works. The chunking conformance failures may ALSO be partly host-sleep (the '[Slow]' inconsistent-continue test polls). Re-probe the full multi-page + compacted-away continue flow with adequate waits before dispatch. Likely lower-value than first thought.
close_reason: PR #775 opened (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/775). Root cause: pagination itself (limit/continue/HMAC tokens/remainingItemCount) was already correctly implemented; the bug was that every page reported the store's LIVE global resourceVersion instead of one pinned to the pagination pass, so it drifted upward whenever unrelated resources were written between page fetches -- failing chunking.go's assertion that all pages of one listing share the same resourceVersion. Fix: continue tokens now embed the resourceVersion pinned at page 1 (generic.rs encode_continue/decode_continue), and resource.rs/core.rs/csr.rs list handlers report that pinned rv on every page instead of resp.revision; a fresh rv is only minted on token expiry (matching the inconsistent-list-restart test). New regression test list_namespaced_resource_paginates_all_items_once_with_stable_resource_version (resource.rs) creates 25 objects, pages with interleaved concurrent writes, and asserts all items returned once in order with one shared resourceVersion -- verified it fails on revert. Gate: sonobuoy --focus 'Servers.*API chunking|should return chunks of results for list calls|should support continue listing' -> 'Ran 2 of 7579 Specs in 98.586 seconds; SUCCESS! -- 2 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 7577 Skipped'. cargo test --workspace (2159 tests) and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings both clean.

title: fix(proxy): Service proxy must parse <name>:<port> suffix (named-port proxy syntax)
description:
DETERMINISTIC apiserver bug (NOT environmental/reachability — proven). Follow-on from cyrd.1 (Service proxy route, #686), found by re-running the proxy conformance test tighter (run 0705-2024).

## Symptom
'[sig-network] Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' FAILS. The test requests `/api/v1/namespaces/proxy-1014/services/proxy-service-84b98:portname1/proxy/` and gets **404 in ~1-3ms**: `Service "proxy-service-84b98:portname1" not found`.

## Why it's NOT reachability/setup (operator's worry, ruled out)
The 404 returns in ~1ms — nothing was dialed. It's an immediate name-lookup rejection, not a connection timeout / context-deadline / unreachable-pod. The apiserver never tried to reach a pod IP.

## Root cause (mayor-verified)
`resolve_service_proxy_target` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:1435-1447) does `object_key("services", ns, svc_name)` with the RAW svc_name including the `:portname1` suffix → Service lookup 404s because the stored Service is named `proxy-service-84b98`, not `proxy-service-84b98:portname1`. k8s proxy URL syntax allows `services/<name>:<port-or-portName>/proxy/` to target a specific service port; cyrd.1 didn't parse the suffix.

## Fix (mirror the EXISTING node-proxy pattern)
proxy.rs ALREADY has `strip_node_port` (line 1000-1009, `rsplit_once(':')`) for exactly this on node proxy. Service names are DNS-1123 (no colons) so the same rsplit is safe. Steps:
1. In resolve_service_proxy_target: split svc_name into (bare_name, Option<port_or_portName>) via rsplit_once(':'); look up the Service by bare_name.
2. USE the parsed port: resolve it to the target endpoint port. The suffix may be a numeric port OR a named port — map a named port through the Service's spec.ports[].name → targetPort, and match the EndpointSlice port by name. (The failing test uses ':portname1' — a NAMED port.)
3. If no suffix, keep current behavior (first ready endpoint + its port).
Add regression tests: services/<name>:<numericPort>/proxy and services/<name>:<portName>/proxy both resolve; bare services/<name>/proxy still works.

## Verify
--focus 'Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' → PASS (was 404-loop → 122s timeout). VM.

## Pattern note
Same class as cyrd.6 (label-selector) — an incompletely-parsed k8s URL form failing fast. Cross-ref cyrd.1 (#686), cyrd (epic).
close_reason: PR #688 opened — Service proxy named-port parsing fixed; bare name used for store lookup, port spec resolved via EndpointSlice ports[].name; 2103 tests pass; kubectl repro shows 404→502 (forward attempted, not parse error); conformance run ongoing

title: fix(store): per-prefix bookmark RV — retarget to EnsureReady() RS/DS/SS false-positive retries (not ES tracker)
description:
Scout findings clarify that the per-prefix bookmark fix (cyrd.3) was described as fixing 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' but that error comes from endpointSliceTracker.Has() (object cache generation check), NOT from ConsistencyStore.EnsureReady() which uses LastStoreSyncResourceVersion/bookmarks.

The per-prefix bookmark fix IS valuable, but for a different failure: when a cross-resource global bookmark (e.g. from a Pod write) advances a StatefulSet informer's LastStoreSyncResourceVersion past the most recent StatefulSet write RV, EnsureReady() passes prematurely. This was observed as: 'read version: 391 is not as new as written version: 392 for group resource statefulsets.apps' in kcm.log.

This bead should be closed or retargeted. The per-prefix bookmark work should target:
1. Prevent cross-prefix global bookmarks from advancing LastStoreSyncResourceVersion past the per-prefix write RV
2. Test: StatefulSet write at rv=N; StatefulSet informer bookmark arrives at rv>=N without a Pod write at rv=N driving it

The EndpointSlice tracker convergence issue should be addressed by mayor-cyrd.4 (ring/broadcast capacity) instead.

title: fix(apiserver): investigate namespace termination latency (~8h conformance gap driver)
description: The ~8h wall-clock regression in conformance run 0705-1409 is caused by namespace termination latency (10 large inter-spec gaps totaling 9.13h), NOT the WAL-read-lag controller retry churn. d13f and the 7lrp scout both confirm this. The EndpointSlice->Sysctls gap alone is 163 minutes. Root cause appears to be slow namespace GC/finalizer processing in u7s apiserver. This is a distinct bug from the WAL-lag retry churn (7lrp). Needs separate investigation: profile namespace deletion in apiserver, check finalizer processing loops, GC cascade for EndpointSlice/Service/Pod, and why the 0703-1822 baseline run did NOT show this (~4.76h total elapsed).
notes:
REFRAMED (2026-07-06, from live run 0705-2315 terminal watchdog log + apiserver.log). The title 'namespace termination latency' is MISLEADING — namespace TERMINATION is NOT slow. Proof: the watchdog's own force-delete DELETE completes in seconds (DELETE 200 -> DELETE 404 within ~1-9s for every reaped ns; e.g. cronjob-2149 14:35:17.44 DELETE 200 -> next-second gone). The ~4.5h 'gap' is NOT teardown cost.

REAL MECHANISM: conformance tests HANG mid-execution polling a condition u7s never satisfies, so the test never reaches its AfterEach cleanup DELETE. There is NO test-issued namespace DELETE in apiserver.log for ANY stuck ns before the watchdog's — the tests go silent while polling. The watchdog (06-run-sonobuoy.sh) reaps each at a 5-min-Active / 10-min-Terminating threshold. So each hang costs [test-specific poll time] + [up to 5 min watchdog threshold], serialized against suite progress.

Examples (apiserver.log, verified): cronjob-2149 polled GET cronjobs/suspended every 2s returning 200 until reaped (= 0rc4); statefulset-6615 polled pods?labelSelector=baz= waiting for pods that never appear (= qrip). Each stuck ns maps to a DISTINCT correctness bug, NOT a shared teardown bug.

CONSEQUENCE: the wall-clock regression and the correctness FAILURES ARE THE SAME LIST. Fixing the per-area correctness bugs (gjy0 proxy, 0rc4 cronjob, qrip statefulset, kxht webhook, uam0 crd-openapi, rsei preempt + NEW: chunking/services/var-expansion) buys back the wall-clock directly. This bead (7lrp.2) is therefore largely a DUPLICATE lens on d13f + those beads — recommend CLOSE as superseded by d13f's per-area breakdown, keeping only any residual genuine ns-termination-latency finding (none observed). Wall-clock cost ranking by area is in d13f.
close_reason: Superseded by d13f's per-area breakdown: the 'termination latency' framing was wrong (teardown itself is fast, seconds). Real mechanism is per-area tests hanging mid-poll on conditions u7s never satisfies, then reaped by the watchdog threshold — same list as the correctness bugs already tracked individually (gjy0/0rc4/qrip/kxht/uam0/rsei/25ap). No residual latency finding beyond those. Closing to stop double-tracking.

title: Per-prefix bookmark RV to fix informer cache consistency (endpointslice hot-loop factor B)
description: Global bookmark events advance endpointslice informer RV past last write on that prefix, causing KCM consistency check to fail. Track last-write rv per key prefix in push_event. Emit heartbeat bookmark at max(prefix_last_rv, current_revision()). Test: EndpointSlice write at rv=N; watcher BOOKMARK arrives at rv=N within 60s; no premature cross-prefix bookmark.
notes: SHARPENED DIAGNOSIS (mayor, 2026-07-05) — the '600s timeout' mechanism + a correction to the buffer-eviction theory. The massive durations are NOT slow relists: they are conformance tests' own 'wait for watch notification / wait for condition' loops hitting their HARD ceiling (300s/600s) because an awaited event NEVER ARRIVES. Concrete proof (ConfigMap watch test, watch-8063, all @19:22:23 UTC in host-logs/apiserver.log): label-selector watch opened (GET .../configmaps?labelSelector=watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)&watch=true → 200), ConfigMap created (POST → 201) with matching label watch-this-configmap=multiple-watchers-A, but the ADDED event never delivered → test '[FAILED] Timed out waiting for expected watch notification: {ADDED ...configmap-a...}' (e2e.txt:573), namespace idle until 19:39 (~16min later). KEY CORRECTION to the scout's 'buffer eviction under burst' theory: this ConfigMap test is a SINGLE create on a QUIET namespace — NO burst — yet the event still didn't arrive. So buffer capacity (cyrd.4) is NOT the whole story. There appears to be a LABEL-SELECTOR WATCH DELIVERY bug: matching events aren't delivered to label-filtered watch streams on the LIVE path (filtering may only be applied to the initial snapshot — cf core.rs:528 comment + super::watch::object_matches_label_selector). A fix-scout must check: does the live watch-broadcast path apply label-selector matching and deliver matching events? This likely underlies BOTH the ConfigMap watch failures AND EndpointSlice non-convergence (KCM's endpointslice informer uses watches too). Buffer bump (cyrd.4) may help under-load cases but will NOT fix the quiet-namespace label-watch drop. RE-SCOPE cyrd.3 around live label-selector watch delivery.
close_reason: Scout complete: cyrd.3 was misdirected. 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' comes from endpointSliceTracker.Has() (object cache generation check), NOT ConsistencyStore.EnsureReady() (which uses LastStoreSyncResourceVersion). Per-prefix bookmark fix does not address this error. Follow-on: mayor-cyrd.4 (ring/broadcast capacity increase) is the correct fix for ES tracker lag; mayor-cyrd.5 retargets the per-prefix bookmark work to RS/DS/SS EnsureReady() false positives. Findings: ai/findings/cyrd3-7lrp3-watch-endpointslice-scout-2026-07-05.md

title: Reduce SQLite WAL read lag (endpointslice hot-loop factor A)
description: EndpointSlice hot-loop is exacerbated by SQLite WAL read lag: after writing rv=N on write connection, read connection sees rv=N-1. Tune wal_autocheckpoint from 100 pages to ~10. Add PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) after write batch in sqlite.rs. Test: write-then-read verifies revision is visible without lag.
notes: MAYOR CORRECTION (2026-07-05): the cyrd scout attributed the EndpointSlice hot-loop to WAL read lag ('is not as new as written') — but log counts show these are DISTINCT loops: 'EndpointSlice for Service X not found' occurs only 44-46× and ALL for ONE service (endpointslice-6289, the single EndpointSlice conformance test) — localized, not run-wide. The 'is not as new as written' WAL-lag signature occurs 204× across replicasets(121)/statefulsets(72)/daemonsets(11) — ZERO for endpointslices. So cyrd.2's WAL-lag work is really about the 7lrp class (workload-controller consistency), NOT the endpointslice loop. RE-SCOPE: cyrd.2 should likely be MERGED INTO / reopened as 7lrp (WAL read lag), not kept as a cyrd child. The endpointslice-6289 loop is a separate localized issue (part of the EndpointSlice sync failure, cyrd's actual scope). Recommend: move cyrd.2 under the 7lrp umbrella; keep cyrd.1 (proxy route) + cyrd.3 (bookmark RV) as cyrd.
close_reason: AUDIT 2026-07-14 (ai/findings/cyrd-service-discovery-audit-2026-07-14.md): already reparented under mayor-7lrp (closed) per its own prior notes; superseded by 7lrp's conclusion that the root cause is watch-event TCP-propagation lag, not WAL read-connection lag — cyrd.2's proposed fix (wal_autocheckpoint tuning + PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)) targets a mechanism 7lrp's own deeper investigation moved away from. The actual recommended fix (TCP_NODELAY) is tracked at mayor-7lrp.1 (open, P3, possibly already landed via #759/tkp2f pending remeasurement). This audit re-confirmed the 'read version N not as new as written N+1' symptom still reproduces live (transient/self-healing, replicasets.apps) but attributes it to the 7lrp/7lrp.1 mechanism, not WAL tuning. title: investigate: CronJob 'suspended' disappears after create (GET 200→404) — sig-apps 'should not schedule jobs when suspended' fails
description:
Surfaced by the 0705 conformance diff (mayor-d13f), but MIS-ATTRIBUTED there to protobuf codegen — it is NOT a proto deser bug. Needs a scout to confirm root cause + whether it's pre-existing (NOT proven EPIC-caused; the test was not in the 0703 baseline run set).

## Symptom
[sig-apps] CronJob 'should not schedule jobs when suspended [Slow] [Conformance]' FAILS with: 'Unexpected final error while getting *v1.CronJob: CronJob "suspended" not found'.

## Evidence (preserved host log)
temp/e2e/0705-1409-conformance/host-logs/apiserver.log:
- POST/create of cronjob-3176/cronjobs/suspended succeeds; subsequent GET /apis/batch/v1/namespaces/cronjob-3176/cronjobs/suspended returns 200 at 16:08:48, 16:24:18, 16:24:20 ... then 404 at 2026-07-05T16:24:22.646741Z. The object VANISHED between 16:24:20 and 16:24:22.
So the CronJob was created and readable, then disappeared ~15min later while the test still expected it. Candidate causes: (a) an over-eager GC/orphan sweep deleting the suspended CronJob; (b) a TTL/finalizer bug; (c) namespace/ownership cascade. NOT the proto decode path (create+GET returned valid 200s before the 404).

## NOT the k8s\0 protobuf error
The '[107 56 115 0]' error in the same test's output is a SEPARATE pu5i artifact (dump.go diagnostic hitting the kubelet-proxy) — see mayor-pu5i. Do not conflate.

## Scope for a scout (--stack-only, when a VM is free)
Reproduce: create a suspended CronJob, watch whether it persists or gets deleted (kubectl get -w + apiserver log + kcm.log). Determine what deletes it. Confirm whether baseline (pre-EPIC) had the same behavior (was this test even run/passing before?). Then decide severity + whether it's EPIC-related (unlikely) or a pre-existing CronJob lifecycle bug.

## Cross-ref
mayor-d13f (conformance diff), mayor-pu5i (the proto-prefix red herring).
notes: RE-ROOT-CAUSED LIVE (mayor, 2026-07-06) — NON-BUG on current main (c92d9d6a). Created a suspended CronJob (schedule '* * * * *'), waited 70s past a tick: 0 jobs spawned, suspend honored correctly. The 239s hang of '[sig-apps] CronJob should not schedule jobs when suspended [Slow]' in the ballooned run was a HOST-SLEEP artifact (the test polls for ~1min to confirm no jobs appear; a Power Nap gap during that poll inflated it to 239s and may have tripped a timeout). RECOMMEND: close/park until a CAFFEINATED full run confirms — this likely PASSES clean without host-sleep. Not worth a fix dispatch. Cross-ref tier2-conformance-beads-stale-symptom-framed, conformance-wallclock-ginkgo-vs-realtime.

Live-confirmed pre-fix (watchdog fired on a same-age namespace at 468s; real test missed the same tick by ~10-15s and passed by luck) and post-fix (test ran its full 300s window cleanly, no watchdog interference). title: apiserver: Export and unify MicroTime timestamp helper across adapters
description:
MicroTime fields are handled correctly in coord_gen_adapter, net_disc_cert_policy_events_gen_adapter, and core_gen_adapter (Event.series), but there's no exported helper.

Each adapter that needs microsecond-precision timestamp formatting imports crate::util::secs_nanos_to_rfc3339_micro directly. Risk: if util function changes, all adapters must be reviewed.

Low priority but indicative of per-adapter reimplementation pattern.

See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #5.

title: apiserver: Standardize PodTemplateSpec empty-object handling across adapters
description:
core_gen_adapter.rs:905-914 emits { metadata: <json>, spec: <json> } unconditionally, even if both are empty objects.

batch_gen_adapter.rs:245-255 wraps the result with conditional logic that produces { template: {} } if empty.

This inconsistency means a Pod and a Job with the same template can have different JSON representations.

Fix: Decide on behavior (emit always or omit if empty) and standardize across core and batch. If omitting: update gen_pod_template_spec_to_json to return Option, then unwrap_or emit empty.

See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #4.
close_reason: Non-issue on inspection: core gen_pod_template_spec_to_json and batch gen_job_spec_to_json both emit {} for empty PodTemplateSpec. The conditional wrapper in batch is logically equivalent — both paths produce {}. No code change needed.

title: apiserver: Add test coverage for all adapter decoders + field-omission assertions
description:
Test coverage gaps: only core_gen_adapter (3 tests) and batch_gen_adapter (3 tests) have tests. 7 adapters untested: coord, rbac, admissionreg, apiextensions, net_disc_cert_policy_events, storage_node_flow, apps.

Existing tests are construction-based (verify data survives roundtrip) but not correctness-based (verify JSON is null-free and omits zero/empty fields).

Example: if condition type is None, tests don't catch that JSON emits "type": null instead of omitting the field.

Fix: 
1. Add roundtrip tests for each untested adapter
2. Add explicit field-omission assertions (verify optional fields produce null JSON value, not omitted from dict or serialized as empty)
3. Test with all-defaults proto to verify only required fields are emitted

See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #3.
notes:
Audit 2026-07-13 (mayor-z6qx protobuf status-decode audit): filed mayor-v58bk (Node, HIGH) and mayor-wbu24 (ResourceQuota, HIGH) — both proto decoders drop .status, same bug shape as #755/Pod. All other 7 status-subresource types checked (Deployment/RS/SS/DS, Job/CronJob, CRD, PVC, PDB, Ingress, ServiceCIDR, CSR, VolumeAttachment, FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy) already decode .status correctly — no further HIGH/MED status-decode gaps found. Field-omission assertions remain uneven: coord_gen_adapter.rs, admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs, batch_gen_adapter.rs (and rbac_gen_adapter.rs, weakly) have zero is_null()/is_none() regression assertions — no live bug found by manual read, but the omit-vs-null guarantee is untested there. Leaving z6qx OPEN as the umbrella for this remaining field-omission-coverage work (not closing). Findings doc: ai/findings/adapter-status-decode-audit-2026-07-13.md
PR #757 (test-only): added 27 decode_*_proto_gen correctness tests across core/apps/batch/admissionreg/net_disc_cert_policy_events/rbac gen_adapter files. All 56 decode_*_proto_gen entry points now have >=1 populated round-trip test (was ~29); every status-subresource type in every adapter now has a dedicated status round-trip assertion (added: Service, PersistentVolumeClaim, Deployment, StatefulSet full-status, Job counts, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, CertificateSigningRequest, PodDisruptionBudget). No decoder bugs found (all new tests pass, none needed #[ignore]) -- confirms the 2026-07-13 manual audit's conclusion that no further status-decode gaps exist beyond the already-fixed Node/RQ/Pod. storage_node_flow/apiextensions/coord were already fully covered, verified not changed. Remaining for a follow-on: field-omission (is_null/is_none) spot-checks are still uneven in coord_gen_adapter.rs, admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs, batch_gen_adapter.rs, rbac_gen_adapter.rs (priority-3, not attempted here). Leaving z6qx OPEN per instructions.

title: apiserver: Fix condition type/status null-safety in apps and batch adapters
description:
apps_gen_adapter.rs:145-146 and batch_gen_adapter.rs:163-164 directly serialize condition type/status fields without null-checking:
  
  apps_gen_adapter line 145-146:
    "type": c.r#type,
    "status": c.status,

  This serializes Option<String> directly. If Some(None), produces JSON null, violating K8s spec (conditions require non-null type).

  core_gen_adapter correctly uses unwrap_or_default() to convert None to empty string.

  Fix: Change both adapters to use unwrap_or_default(). Add test verifying condition with None type produces type: "", not type: null.

  See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #2.
close_reason: PR #684: Fixed unwrap_or_default() on condition type/status in apps macro and batch inline code. Two regression tests added that fail on revert.

title: apiserver: Consolidate gen_object_meta_to_json — delegate from 5 adapters to core_gen_adapter
description:
rbac_gen_adapter (line 10), admissionreg_gen_adapter (line 6), apiextensions_gen_adapter (line 6), net_disc_cert_policy_events_gen_adapter (line 10), storage_node_flow_gen_adapter (line 9) all reimplement gen_object_meta_to_json locally. Drift risk: any bugfix to core_gen_adapter::gen_object_meta_to_json won't propagate.

Fix: Replace local fn gen_object_meta_to_json with delegation to crate::core_gen_adapter::gen_object_meta_to_json. See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #1.
notes: MERGED #684 (7fed8731). BONUS CORRECTNESS BUG found during consolidation (not in original scope): admissionreg_gen_adapter + apiextensions_gen_adapter were MISSING the owner_references emission block entirely → silent data loss for GC-owned webhooks/CRDs (a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration or CRD with an ownerReference would lose it on decode→JSON). Both now match core. rbac/net_disc/storage_node_flow/coord were already correct. KEY FINDING: function-level ObjectMeta delegation is architecturally IMPOSSIBLE — each adapter's ObjectMeta is a distinct Rust type from its own proto-generated module (prost generates per-package types); the 'consolidation' is keeping the copies byte-identical + correct, not sharing one fn. Future adapter authors: copy core's gen_object_meta_to_json EXACTLY incl owner_references.
close_reason: PR #684: admissionreg and apiextensions owner_references fix (was missing block). Function delegation infeasible due to distinct Rust types per proto module.

title: fix(apiserver): Pod spec update does not bump metadata.generation (is_workload_resource excludes pods)
description:
Split from mayor-40cj (whose proto-drop half was fixed by #675). This is the REMAINING half of the pod-generation conformance failure — a generation-tracking gap, NOT a proto issue.

## Symptom
Conformance test `[sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) pod generation should start at 1 and increment per update` FAILS: 3 Passed | 1 Failed. e2e.txt (verified 2026-07-04 on merged main ec8b0a0f, VM lima-node-2): `[FAILED] Expected <int64>: 1 to be equivalent to <int64>: 5 at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/node/pods.go:530`. The test does 4 spec updates and asserts metadata.generation reaches 5 (starts at 1, +1 per update); it stays at 1.

## Root cause (verified against code)
`is_workload_resource` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs:84-95) lists apps deployments/replicasets/statefulsets/daemonsets, batch jobs/cronjobs, policy poddisruptionbudgets — but NOT ("", "pods"). The generation machinery is gated on this predicate at:
- defaults.rs:44 (set generation=1 on create)
- resource.rs:729 (spec_before_patch for PATCH generation tracking)
- resource.rs:1460/1496 (spec_before_replace for PUT) → because is_workload_resource is false for pods, spec_before_replace=None, so the increment at resource.rs:1544 (increment_workload_generation_if_spec_changed) never runs for Pods.
The proto-decode of the updated field (tolerations) is already correct post-#675 — the PUT succeeds and carries the new spec; only the generation bump is missing.

## Fix (needs care — Pods are not like workload controllers)
Adding ("", "pods") to is_workload_resource is the obvious first step, BUT verify upstream Pod generation semantics before doing so blindly:
- Upstream (PodObservedGenerationTracking, GA) increments metadata.generation on Pod SPEC updates. Pods are largely immutable post-create — only a specific mutable subset (e.g. activeDeadlineSeconds, tolerations additions, spec.containers[*].image for in-place resize, etc.) can change. Confirm the generation bump fires for exactly the mutable-spec updates the test performs and does not misfire on status-only or metadata-only updates.
- Confirm create-time generation=1 is correct for Pods (it is, upstream).
- Ensure the spec-diff used by increment_workload_generation_if_spec_changed compares the right subtree for Pods (spec, excluding status).

## Verification (MANDATORY — sonobuoy, this is the pods.go:530 test)
Inject Lima VM protocol. Gate: `--focus 'sig-node\] Pods Extended \(pod generation\)'` must go 4/4 (the other 3 already pass). Read e2e.txt (not e2e.log). Read the test source (temp/research/ or WebFetch pods.go from the pinned upstream branch) to confirm the exact update sequence before fixing.

## Regression test
Extract the generation-bump decision into/against a pure function and assert: a Pod spec update bumps generation; a status-only update does not. Must fail on revert.

## Cross-ref
- Proto half: mayor-40cj (closed, fixed by #675).
- BLOCKS mayor-osuq (held pending this + a Pod e2e that exercises priorityClassName end-to-end).
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-04, VM lima-node-smoke/6444/kubelet10251 (needs sonobuoy: pods.go:530). Disjoint from EPIC proto.rs work (touches defaults.rs is_workload_resource:84 + resource.rs generation paths). Parallel-safe with wave-2c.
close_reason: MERGED as PR #681 (8b7119ac, 2026-07-04). Root cause diverged from the is_workload_resource hypothesis (that path is dead for pods — they route through dedicated pods.rs handlers): the real bug was replace_pod/patch_pod accepting a client-supplied lower metadata.generation and downgrading it. Fix (pods.rs only): stamp stored_generation into the incoming body before increment_pod_generation_if_spec_changed. Sonobuoy: [sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) now 4/4 (was 3/1); kubectl before/after verified all 8 cases incl client-gen-ignored. 2 regression tests fail on revert. Dead is_workload_resource pods-addition removed pre-merge (mayor review, Rule 2). Unblocks osuq.

title: fix(proto): PodSpec proto decode drops tolerations (field 22) — client-go PUT loses tolerations; pod-generation conformance test still fails
description:
New instance of the proto-decode-drop bug class (see dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check). Surfaced 2026-07-03 by the pod-generation fix worker (PR #670, mayor-h4xw): the conformance test '[sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) pod generation should start at 1 and increment per update' does an update that ADDS a toleration and asserts generation bumps. It still FAILS after #670 (latest --focus run: 3 Passed | 1 Failed) because client-go sends the PUT body as protobuf, and u7s proto.rs PodSpec has NO tolerations field (upstream metav1 PodSpec tolerations = field 22). So extract_body silently drops tolerations before the generation compare ever runs — the toleration add looks like a no-op, generation doesn't bump, test fails.

CONFIRMED by the worker: the fix's own unit test client_go_toleration_update_bumps_generation passes at the JSON level, proving the generation logic is correct; the failure is purely the proto decoder not carrying tolerations into the typed spec.

FIX: add tolerations (field 22, repeated Toleration message) to the PodSpec prost struct in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs with the correct upstream field number, decode it in the pod proto decode path, add a proto-round-trip regression test (encode a pod with tolerations → decode → assert tolerations survive), AND audit sibling PodSpec fields in the same pass for other drops (per dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check — the recurring pattern). This is likely SUBSUMED by the proto EPIC mayor-xmu4 (P2 tkyb migrates core-group structs to generated code, which would carry tolerations by construction) — decide whether to fix discretely now or fold into the EPIC. Filing discretely so it is not lost.

Once fixed, the pod-generation --focus should go 4/4 (the other 3 already pass via #670).

Related: mayor-h4xw (the merged partial fix), mayor-xmu4 (proto EPIC), mayor-osuq (sibling PodSpec proto drop: priorityClassName/priority).
acceptance_criteria: proto.rs PodSpec decodes tolerations (field 22); a proto-round-trip test asserts tolerations survive; the pod-generation --focus conformance run goes 4/4 (the toleration-add-bumps-generation case passes). Sibling PodSpec fields audited for other drops in the same pass.
notes: VERIFICATION on merged main (#675, ec8b0a0f) — 2026-07-04T04:15Z, VM lima-node-2. Result: STILL FAILS, 3 Passed | 1 Failed (UNCHANGED from pre-fix). e2e.txt: temp/e2e/0704-1312-.../logs/e2e.txt line 78-82: '[FAILED] Expected <int64>: 1 to be equivalent to <int64>: 5 at pods.go:530'. ROOT CAUSE SPLIT (verified against code): (1) proto-decode-drop of tolerations = FIXED by #675 (decode_pod_proto_gen emits tolerations, the update PUT returns 200). (2) SEPARATE, still-broken: metadata.generation never increments on Pod spec updates because is_workload_resource (defaults.rs:84-95) does NOT include ('','pods') — so spec_before_replace=None (resource.rs:1496) and the increment at resource.rs:1544 never runs for Pods. The test asserts generation reaches 5 after 4 updates; stays 1. This generation-bump gap is a DISTINCT bug the proto fix merely unmasked — NOT a proto-typing issue. NEEDS OPERATOR DECISION on scope (see below). The proto half is genuinely done; do not re-attempt the proto decode.
close_reason: PROTO HALF FIXED by #675 (protobuf typegen wave-2a, ec8b0a0f). The filed bug — PodSpec proto decode drops tolerations (field 22) — is resolved: decode_pod_proto_gen now emits tolerations via generated core_v1::PodSpec (verified: update PUT returns 200, tolerations survive). The conformance test [sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) at pods.go:530 STILL fails (3P|1F) but for a DISTINCT, non-proto reason: Pod spec updates don't increment metadata.generation because is_workload_resource (defaults.rs:84-95) excludes ('','pods'). That is split into a new bead (see below). Closing 40cj as the proto-drop it was filed for is fixed; the generation gap is separate work. title: investigate: transient ~30-60s apiserver read/kubelet-proxy failure during namespace force-delete under load (full run 0703, 08:55 UTC)
description:
Operator observed during the first full conformance run (0703-1822), ~08:55:17 UTC (17:55 JST). While manually dumping the sonobuoy e2e pod logs a few times/hour, kubectl failed transiently for ~30-60s then self-recovered. The run itself COMPLETED; transient glitch to root-cause, not a run-blocker.

TEMPORAL CORRELATION (strong, not proof): terminal.log:980 shows '[watchdog] 2026-07-03T08:55:17Z force-deleting namespace crd-webhook-9918 (Active for 302s)' — EXACT match to operator's last-good ts. Watchdog force-deleted 9 namespaces across the run; only this one is known to coincide with an observed failure. Verify, don't assume causation.

EXACT SYMPTOMS (operator report — PRIMARY evidence; apiserver.log for 08:55 UTC is GONE, rotated to a later restart 10:48+ UTC):
PRIMARY failure (~12x): 'Error from server (InternalError): kubelet request failed: error sending request for url (https://127.0.0.1:10250/containerLogs/sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-.../e2e)'. CODE CONFIRMED: this is proxy.rs:209 — the reqwest .send() to the kubelet log endpoint failing, surfaced as 500 InternalError. IMPORTANT (operator corrected mayor's initial misread): the apiserver KNEW the pod throughout — the log handler (proxy.rs:100-127) successfully reads the pod + node from the store BEFORE the kubelet call at line 205, and 'Defaulted container e2e out of: e2e, sonobuoy-worker' proves kubectl fetched the pod spec fine. So this is the apiserver->kubelet ROUND-TRIP failing, NOT the pod disappearing from the apiserver's store. (Mayor's earlier 'pod flickered in/out of the apiserver view' framing was WRONG.)
SECONDARY anomaly (2x, mechanism UNKNOWN): a plain 'kubectl get pods sonobuoy-e2e-job-...' returned 'Error from server (NotFound): the server could not find the requested resource'. This is a plain store read (NOT the kubelet path), so it's a DISTINCT, smaller symptom. Could be a transient store/watch-cache/routing hiccup during the ns-drain, or unrelated. Do NOT over-weight it — it's 2 occurrences and unverifiable without the lost log. kubectl get pods showed the correct list otherwise (operator checked).

FOCUS THE INVESTIGATION on the PRIMARY (kubelet-proxy round-trip failing during a namespace force-delete). Note the failing target (sonobuoy-e2e-job pod, in 'sonobuoy' ns) is UNRELATED to the force-deleted ns (crd-webhook-9918).

HYPOTHESES for the PRIMARY (verify/refute): (a) konnectivity tunnel churn — the apiserver->kubelet 10250 path goes via konnectivity; a namespace force-delete cascade (heavy watch/delete churn) could transiently starve or reset the konnectivity connection, making reqwest .send() fail for ~30-60s. (operator wondered about konnectivity cert renewal ~4h in — lima-start.sh:289 generates a konnectivity-agent client cert; CHECK its TTL, though a cert expiry would more likely be a hard failure than a 30-60s blip). (b) node-IP / kubelet reachability transiently lost during the churn. (c) resource starvation in the apiserver (the ns-drain saturates a runtime/threadpool, delaying/failing the outbound kubelet request). For the SECONDARY get-pods-NotFound: only if time permits — could relate to mayor-7lrp (WAL stale read under load) but the evidence is too thin to assume.

APPROACH (read-only scout, --stack-only, reproduce): bring up the stack; create a namespace with many objects / a stuck finalizer; force-delete it (repeatedly, or several at once to mimic the churn) while in a tight loop hammering 'kubectl logs <pod>' AND 'kubectl get pods <pod>' on a pod in a DIFFERENT namespace; watch for the kubelet-proxy 500 (primary) and any plain-read NotFound (secondary). Correlate with apiserver.log + konnectivity-server.log + /tmp/kcm.log. If reproduced, pin the mechanism + file:line. Check the konnectivity cert TTL. Relate to mayor-7lrp only if the secondary reproduces.

ACCEPTANCE (investigation): reproduce the kubelet-proxy transient failure under a namespace force-delete + concurrent log requests, OR rule it out with evidence (e.g. konnectivity reconnect is expected/benign). Pin the mechanism (file:line if u7s; or 'expected konnectivity behavior'; or environmental). Report on the secondary get-pods-NotFound only as far as evidence allows. Findings doc, NO fix (mayor decides fix scope after).
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the transient failure under a namespace force-delete + concurrent reads, OR rule it out with evidence. Root cause pinned to a mechanism (file:line if u7s) or identified as benign/environmental. Relationship to mayor-7lrp established.
notes:
Repro attempt 2 (worker a5c7cbd4, 2026-07-04) — DONE RIGHT (isolated worktree, kubeconfig on correct port 6445, node Ready confirmed BEFORE churn → the port-confusion flaw of attempt 1 is closed). RESULT: NOT-REPRODUCED. 8 namespace-churn cycles (light + heavy, incl. force-deleting namespaces with running pods) concurrent with tight log-fetch loops: 182 apiserver->kubelet log-proxy requests, 182x status=200, ZERO 500s, ZERO 'kubelet request failed'. konnectivity-server: 1 connection, ZERO reconnects/disconnects across all churn → hypothesis (a) 'connection churn from the drain' NOT supported at this load. No apiserver ERROR/500; no threadpool-starvation evidence (hyp b); kubelet stayed responsive (hyp c).

MOST-LIKELY EXPLANATION (unproven, best-evidenced): the original 08:55Z failure happened ~4h into a FULL sonobuoy run — dozens of concurrent test namespaces + webhooks + full KCM GC/SA loop, FAR heavier watch fan-out than a 5-namespace sequential churn. A transient konnectivity tunnel stall under that specific load, or a single brief reconnect coinciding with in-flight log requests, fits the 30-60s self-recovering window. NOT deterministically reproducible in isolation.

REAL CONFIG FACTS surfaced (IMPORTANT attribution: these are the KONNECTIVITY-SERVER's OWN LOGGED DEFAULTS, NOT u7s config — grep found no konnectivity keepalive/channel config in scripts/ or crates/): konnectivity keepalive = 1h (a stale tunnel isn't detected for up to an hour) and XfrChannelSize = 10 (could back up under heavy watch fan-out). If we want to mitigate, that likely means passing flags to the konnectivity-server binary (in scripts/conformance/*), not a u7s code change — verify how konnectivity-server is launched first.

POSSIBLE MITIGATIONS (deferred, only if it recurs): (1) retry-once on connection-error (not 4xx/5xx) at proxy.rs:~209 .send() to ride out a reconnect window; (2) lower konnectivity keepalive (~30s) via a server flag so stale tunnels are detected fast; (3) bump XfrChannelSize. All speculative until the failure is actually observed again.

DISPOSITION: DEFER. Transient, self-recovered, run completed, NOT reproducible under recreatable load. Revisit IF it recurs on a future full run (watch for 'kubelet request failed' 500s in apiserver.log correlated with a konnectivity reconnect) — capture apiserver.log + konnectivity-server.log at the moment THEN. The operator's original symptom evidence + both repro attempts are preserved here.
RECURRENCE (2026-07-21/22, worker agent-afd993abcf8f1a649, mayor-pgm5q.6 2-node verification session):
Hit the identical symptom on lima-node-2 (primary, 2-node cluster) — 'Error from server
(BadGateway): kubelet request failed: error sending request for url
(https://127.0.0.1:10251/containerLogs/<ns>/<pod>/<container>)'. Unlike the original
30-60s transient report, this one did NOT self-recover: persisted across 2 separate
kubectl logs attempts ~immediately after a fresh apiserver restart, AND recurred
identically ~15 minutes later after a second apiserver/kubelet restart cycle (a
different run-all.sh --focus invocation). Reproduced against TWO different target pods
(sonobuoy aggregator AND konnectivity-agent), both on the primary node, ruling out a
pod-specific cause. Also seen from INSIDE the e2e test binary itself (test framework's
post-failure dump.go: 'Unable to retrieve kubelet pods for node lima-node-2: kubelet
unreachable: error sending request for url (https://127.0.0.1:10251/pods)') and inside
sonobuoy's own results bundle (the 'podlogs/' directory that sonobuoy normally populates
via the same apiserver->kubelet log path was entirely absent from the retrieved tarball —
consistent with sonobuoy's own pod-log gathering also hitting this failure).
Ruled OUT as cert/trust related: kubelet-serving.crt verifies OK against ca.pem
(openssl verify), SANs correct (127.0.0.1, VM IP), not expired; /etc/kubelet-ca.crt on
the VM is byte-identical to the host's ca.pem; a plain `curl -k` to the same
127.0.0.1:<kubelet-port> completes the TLS handshake and gets a normal 401 (kubelet
alive and serving). Did not get further (out of scope for that verification session) —
did not confirm whether this is 2-node-specific or would also reproduce single-node;
worth checking if it correlates with an apiserver restart specifically (both hits here
followed a run-all.sh-triggered apiserver kill+restart, which the original 0703 report
did not involve as far as documented).

title: fix(apiserver): delete_collection swallows non-NotFound store errors → silent partial delete + quota drift
description:
From the 2026-07-02 quality audit (mayor-mil2 F-05), promoted from tracker mayor-cef5. Correctness bug.

PROBLEM: both bulk-delete loops use 'let _ = state.store.delete(&obj.key, None).await' which discards ALL errors, not just NotFound races:
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs ~2010 (cluster-scoped delete_collection_resource)
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs ~2018 (namespaced delete_collection_namespaced_resource)
A NotFound (concurrent delete) is fine to ignore. But a StoreError::Internal (disk full, DB error) is SILENTLY swallowed → some objects survive, the handler returns 200 Success, the client thinks everything was deleted. This breaks quota accounting consistency and hides real failures.

FIX: match on the delete result — continue silently ONLY on StoreError::NotFound; for any other error, propagate it (fail the collection-delete with the appropriate status) OR at minimum tracing::error! it and surface a partial-failure. Prefer propagating a real error (upstream returns an error status if a collection delete genuinely fails). Read how StoreError variants are matched elsewhere + how delete_collection builds its response to return the right status. Apply to BOTH sites.

VERIFY: cargo test (Rule 14, fails-on-revert): a delete_collection where one store.delete returns a non-NotFound error must NOT return 200-success-with-silent-loss — it must propagate/surface the error; a NotFound must still be tolerated. This is unit-testable if you can inject a failing store, or extract the loop's error-handling into a testable helper. Live VM optional (collection delete is exercised by namespace teardown / the sonobuoy delete path — a --focus isn't strictly needed if the unit test proves the error-handling; note if you rely on cargo-only).

ACCEPTANCE: non-NotFound store errors during collection delete are propagated/surfaced (not swallowed); NotFound still tolerated; both sites fixed; fails-on-revert test.

LABELS: apiserver, correctness
close_reason: PR #665 opened — both delete_collection sites fixed, 3 fails-on-revert tests, all 1848 tests pass

title: perf(apiserver): cache admission configs in AppState instead of 5 SQLite LISTs per write
description:
From the 2026-07-02 perf audit (mayor-m9u4 F1), promoted from tracker mayor-cef5. HIGH-value perf, biggest write-latency lever in the codebase, no correctness change IF cache invalidation is correct.

PROBLEM: every admission-gated write (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE on any resource) does FIVE separate store.list() calls to fetch admission config objects that almost never change: MutatingWebhookConfigurations (admission.rs:535), ValidatingWebhookConfigurations (:550), MutatingAdmissionPolicies (:952), ValidatingAdmissionPolicies, and ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBindings (the VAP fetch sites ~2239-2269 / run_validating_admission_policies). Each is spawn_blocking + Mutex<Connection> + BEGIN DEFERRED. Under conformance write bursts this is the dominant latency source.

FIX: cache these 5 config sets in AppState (mirror the existing Arc<RbacIndex> / token_map pattern in state.rs:88+). Use RwLock<...> or arc-swap (arc-swap is NOT currently a dep — prefer std RwLock<Arc<...>> unless there's a strong reason; do NOT add a crate without flagging). The cache MUST be refreshed when any of these config objects change — the natural mechanism is the store's watch (these objects already flow through push_event/watch). On a write to any of the 5 config types, update the cache. On admission, read from the cache (zero store round-trips on hit).

CRITICAL CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT: a newly-created/updated/deleted webhook or admission policy MUST take effect promptly (the cache cannot go stale). This is the whole risk of caching — if the refresh is wrong, webhooks silently stop working. Live-verify: create a webhook, confirm it fires on the next matching request; delete it, confirm it stops. If a clean watch-refresh is too complex, an acceptable fallback is a short-TTL cache (e.g. re-list only if >N ms since last list) — but prefer watch-driven. Document the invalidation approach.

VERIFY: cargo tests + LIVE (this is the admission hot path — cargo alone insufficient). --stack-only + kubectl: (a) create a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, confirm a matching create is intercepted; (b) delete it, confirm interception stops; (c) confirm normal writes still work. A --focus on an AdmissionWebhook conformance test as the gate. Measure: confirm the 5-LIST-per-write is gone (apiserver --verbose log should not show the config LISTs on every write).

ACCEPTANCE: admission reads configs from an AppState cache, not per-write LISTs; cache stays correct on config create/update/delete (live-verified); no admission-behavior regression; the AdmissionWebhook --focus test still passes.

LABELS: apiserver, performance, admission
close_reason: PR #666 opened: cache admission configs in AppState (5 SQLite LISTs → 0 per write). Write-through invalidation via refresh_admission_config inline after each store write. 1849 tests pass, clippy clean. VM: create-fires ✓, delete-stops ✓, LISTs-gone ✓, mutate focus 5/5 PASS.

title: fix(apiserver): PodSpec proto decode drops priorityClassName (field 24) + priority (field 25)
description:
Proto partial-drop (rsei scout 2026-07-03, mayor-verified against proto.rs + upstream). The PodSpec prost struct (crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs, struct starting ~line 942) declares tags 1,2,3,5,8,10,16,17,20,26,29 but NOT priorityClassName or priority. When a pod is created with spec.priorityClassName, the prost decoder ignores those wire tags → stored pod JSON lacks spec.priority + spec.priorityClassName → the scheduler (and anything priority-aware) cannot see pod priority.

CORRECT upstream field numbers (verified in crates/apiserver/proto/api-core-v1-generated.proto lines 4615/4623 — NOTE the rsei scout's report TRANSPOSED these; use these):
  optional string priorityClassName = 24;
  optional int32 priority = 25;

FIX: add priorityClassName (field 24, Option<String>) + priority (field 25, Option<i32>) to the PodSpec prost struct + emit in pod_spec_to_json. Audit sibling PodSpec fields in the same pass (many still missing — PodSpec has 41 upstream fields, we decode ~11). Round-trip regression test (fails on revert). 

RELATIONSHIP: this is an instance of the class the proto-typing EPIC mayor-xmu4 fixes structurally (complete codegen would include these automatically). It's ALSO a prerequisite for scheduler preemption (mayor-rsei) — the scheduler can't compare priority without it. Decide: fix standalone now (small, unblocks priority-awareness) OR let mayor-xmu4 sweep it up. Either way, record here so it's tracked + the numbers are right.

title: prost-typing P1: wire prost-build for ONE group + prove decode+JSON-emission adapter pattern (GATE)
description: Phase 1 of EPIC mayor-xmu4 (prost-build migration). Establish the pattern before fan-out. Pick ONE group (recommend coordination/v1 — small, and Lease already has a byte-verified Direction-A-vs-B PoC at ai/findings/proto-spike-poc/). Add a build.rs + prost-build dep; generate the group's structs from its .proto; then solve the HARD part: proto.rs's decode fns COMBINE proto-decode + serde_json emission — design the adapter so generated structs feed a JSON-emission layer (generated or hand). Prove end-to-end: proto bytes → generated struct → JSON identical-or-better than the current hand decode, with a previously-complete type (Lease) AND ideally one partial type to show a previously-dropped field now appears. Document the adapter pattern for phases 2-4. This is a GATE — do not fan out until the pattern is proven and reviewed. cargo-only verification is fine here; the runtime path is exercised later. Basis: ai/findings/proto-source-of-truth-spike-2026-07-03.md.
notes:
Operator decision (2026-07-04): the PoC gate must build the Lease JSON-emission adapter BOTH ways — (A) hand-written struct→serde_json::Value mirroring today's manual omit-empty logic, and (B) serde-derive on prost-generated structs (via prost-build type_attributes) — then diff both outputs byte-for-byte against the current decode_lease_proto() and recommend which pattern to adopt for phases 2-4 (~200 decoders). The recommendation + its cost projection is the real deliverable of the gate. Naming: call this 'protobuf typegen', NOT 'prost-typing'/'proto-typing' (avoids confusion with 'prototype').

Adapter B (serde-derive) fails k8s wire fidelity on 4 axes (snake_case names, MicroTime={seconds,nanos} not RFC3339, Some(0) not omitted, missing creationTimestamp:null); fixing all 4 erases its LoC win + adds fragility. title: EPIC: migrate proto decode to prost-build codegen (complete typing, kill the silent-field-drop bug class)
description:
## Problem
Nearly every conformance bug this past week was the SAME class: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs (17.6k lines of HAND-WRITTEN PARTIAL prost structs — 224 of 643 upstream message types) silently drops fields on decode. Instances fixed this week: enableServiceLinks, PDB spec, Deployment/RS status, Job spec/successPolicy/podFailurePolicy, Lease MicroTime nanos + renewTime, Volume defaultMode, generic PATCH TypeMeta, PodSpec activeDeadlineSeconds, ResourceQuota scopeSelector. Every '// skipped' field in proto.rs is a latent conformance bug.

## Decision (operator, 2026-07-03): DIRECTION A — prost-build codegen
Generate COMPLETE Rust structs FROM upstream generated.proto via prost-build. Completeness becomes STRUCTURAL — a field cannot be silently omitted (you get all fields or the code doesn't generate). This directly and permanently eliminates the bug class.

Rejected alternatives (evidence in ai/findings/):
- STATUS QUO (hand-maintain proto.rs): a worsening treadmill; ~28 field additions/release + multiple silent-drop bug PRs/week. Not viable.
- DIRECTION B (our types = source of truth, derive proto + compat-check): the operator's initial lean, mirroring upstream Go (structs are truth; proto/OpenAPI derived via go-to-protobuf). REJECTED because: (1) NO Rust 'types→proto' tool exists (spike surveyed 7 crates — all go proto→Rust); Direction B in Rust = hand-author complete structs + custom checker = 'proto.rs but complete', ~2x cost (5-10d + 1.5-2d checker); (2) its compat-checker catches WRONG tags but NOT omissions — so it does NOT structurally kill the bug class it's meant to fix; (3) field numbers stay upstream-pinned either way. Direction B's only real win (rich per-field doc comments) is separable and can be layered onto A later.

## Basis (READ before planning implementation)
- ai/findings/k8s-proto-schema-churn-1.34-1.36-2026-07-03.md — upstream churn: 55 field additions, 0 breaking changes across 1.34→1.36; our .proto FILES already complete/current at v1.36; bloat of full codegen ~225KB (negligible). Per-release upkeep ~2-4h.
- ai/findings/proto-source-of-truth-spike-2026-07-03.md — the A-vs-B toolchain evaluation + byte-level-verified Lease PoC (ai/findings/proto-spike-poc/lease-direction-b/).

## Scope / cost
~3-5 days one-time. Key work: wire up prost-build (new build-dep) for all proto files; the HARD part is that proto.rs's decode functions COMBINE proto-decode + JSON-emission (~200 fns) — these must be split into generated-decode + a hand/gen JSON-emission adapter layer. 10 GA groups currently have NO proto file (admission, autoscaling v1/v2, certificates, discovery, events, networking, policy, resource/DRA, scheduling) — add them. Field numbers come from upstream (structural, no hand-pinning).

## Downstream
Complete typing is a NECESSARY-not-sufficient prereq for OpenAPI-v2 (mayor-52wo, currently deferred — note that bead embeds a STATIC upstream blob, a different approach; the typing EPIC could later enable GENERATED OpenAPI instead). Link, don't merge.

## Phasing (filed as child beads blocked by this EPIC)
1. SPIKE→REAL: wire prost-build for ONE group (coordination/v1 or core/v1), prove generated-decode + JSON-emission adapter end-to-end, establish the pattern + the adapter design. Gate before fan-out.
2. Migrate remaining existing-proto groups to generated structs + adapters.
3. Add the 10 missing GA groups.
4. Delete the dead hand-written proto.rs structs; regression-test the JSON-emission adapter for representative types (round-trip incl. previously-dropped fields).

## Acceptance
- proto decode is generated (prost-build) for all built-in GA groups; no hand-written partial structs remain for typed resources.
- A previously-dropped field (e.g. pick 3 from the fixed-this-week list) is proven present by construction + round-trip test.
- No conformance regression; binary size delta < ~500KB.

LABELS: apiserver, proto, epic, architecture
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE (operator sign-off 2026-07-05). All proto decode migrated to prost-build generated structs + Adapter A: 12 PRs #673-#685, proto.rs 17,667→11,002 (-38%), silent-field-drop bug class eliminated for every GA group with a .proto. Conformance-verified: +18 correctness (321P|123F vs 303P|141F), ~0 perf cost (4.97h vs 4.76h exec). Also fixed 2 silent field CORRUPTIONS (Ingress ingressClassName, CSR signerName wrong field #s) + 2 cleanup bugs (condition null-safety, owner_references loss). Children: dqwf/tkyb/0vl5/2bfd all closed; Tier B (huy9) detached as independent optional work (net-new HPA/DRA nothing decodes today). Adapter test coverage z6qx (P2) open independently. Full history in the merged PR bodies + ai/findings/ wave docs.

title: feat(conformance): add --stack-only flag to run-all.sh (bring stack up without running sonobuoy)
description:
run-all.sh ALWAYS runs step 6 (sonobuoy). A bare invocation with no --focus runs the FULL conformance suite, which at our current state runs until the 6h timeout. There is no way to bring the stack up for kubectl/sqlite3 investigation without triggering a sonobuoy run. This burned a scout's time (2026-07-02): dispatched to investigate the WAL stale-read via kubectl/direct-DB queries, it ran a bare run-all.sh and kicked off a full run.

FIX: add a --stack-only flag that runs steps 1-5 (build, apiserver, lima VM, kcm, scheduler) and SKIPS step 6 (sonobuoy). The stack is left running so the caller can use kubectl (KUBECONFIG is printed at step 2) and query the DB directly.

Concrete change (scripts/conformance/run-all.sh, structure confirmed by reading it):
- Add STACK_ONLY=0 near the other flag vars (~line 57).
- Add case: '--stack-only) STACK_ONLY=1; shift ;;' in the arg loop (~line 62).
- Add a doc line in the Usage header block describing it.
- Gate step 6 (lines 146-150): 'if [ "$STACK_ONLY" -eq 1 ]; then banner "Step 6/6: Run sonobuoy (skipped — --stack-only)"; else <existing step-6 body> fi'.
- Guard: --stack-only + --focus together is contradictory; either ignore --focus with a warning, or error. Prefer a one-line warning to stderr and proceed stack-only.

title: fix(admission): matches_rule ignores the namespace parameter — namespace-scoped webhook rules are not enforced
description:

Fix: implement the namespace match using the discarded parameter (namespaceSelector against the target namespace's labels, per MutatingWebhookConfiguration/ValidatingWebhookConfiguration semantics). Confirm whether the caller passes the namespace's labels or just its name — may require threading the namespace object's labels into the call.

title: fix(apiserver): JSON Patch on /status subresource is not path-restricted — patch <res>/status can write /spec
description:
Audit mayor-37sk (security) Finding 2. The status subresource PATCH handlers apply a JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json) to the FULL object document without restricting operation paths to /status/*. A client with 'patch' on <resource>/status can send [{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":100}] and it writes to spec — privilege escalation from status-only rights to spec writes.

Sites:
- status.rs:150-153 (cluster-scoped patch_resource_status, PatchType::Json branch)
- status.rs:298-300 (namespaced patch_namespaced_resource_status, PatchType::Json branch)

The merge-patch and strategic-merge-patch paths are ALREADY correctly restricted (they only apply the 'status' field from the patch body). Only the PatchType::Json branch is unguarded.

Fix: before apply_json_patch on a status-subresource request, validate that every op 'path' starts with /status/ or /metadata/ (return 422 otherwise), OR snapshot current.body['spec'] before the patch and restore it after. Prefer the 422-validation approach (matches upstream strategy-layer rejection).

Source: ai/findings/audit-2026-07-02/security.md Finding 2. Same surface as mayor-egmm (status.rs) — fold into that cluster PR.
Regression test: a JSON Patch to /status with an op targeting /spec/* must be rejected 422 (or leave spec unchanged); an op targeting /status/* must succeed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #647: validate_status_json_patch_paths() added to patch_resource_status and patch_namespaced_resource_status in status.rs; 4 regression tests.
