title: proxy: https: scheme prefix in pod/service proxy URLs should connect to the backend over TLS
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-caskz (scheme:name:port proxy parsing) via the [sig-network] "Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod" conformance test on lima-node-4 (run 0716-1715). Upstream k8s's scheme:name:port proxy addressing (`net.SplitSchemeNamePort` / `net.JoinSchemeNamePort`) uses the scheme not just to disambiguate the name/port split but to select the wire protocol used for the apiserver-to-backend connection: an `https:<name>:<port>` proxy URL must connect to the pod/endpoint IP with TLS (skipping cert verification, since arbitrary workload pods have no known CA), not plain HTTP.

mayor-caskz's fix (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs: split_scheme_name_port) correctly parses and strips the scheme for the name/port lookup, matching that bead's explicit scope ("strip an optional leading http:/https: scheme token"). It intentionally does not thread the scheme into the backend connection. pod_proxy_dispatch/service_proxy_dispatch always build `http://{ip}:{port}/...` regardless of the requested scheme.

Effect: an `https:`-prefixed proxy request to a pod/service port that is actually a TLS listener gets a plaintext HTTP request, and the TLS server correctly rejects it — observed as a 400 "Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server" instead of the proxied TLS response.

Repro (from e2e.txt, run 0716-1715): all 5 https-scheme table-test cases (services tlsportname1/tlsportname2, pods 443/460/462) get this 400 instead of the expected proxied body ("tls baz" / "tls qux" / rewritten HTML). Confirmed unrelated to name/port parsing: zero 404s in the same run; these are pure protocol-selection failures.

Fix direction: resolve_pod_proxy_target / resolve_service_proxy_target need to return the parsed scheme (or a bool) alongside (ip, port, proxy_addr); pod_proxy_dispatch / service_proxy_dispatch need an https branch that connects with a TLS client that skips backend cert verification (matching upstream's InsecureSkipVerify behavior for pod-target TLS, since pod TLS certs are self-signed/unknown to the cluster CA).
close_reason: PR #859 opened — https-scheme pod/service proxy now connects to the backend over TLS (direct branch: reqwest danger_accept_invalid_certs; konnectivity tunnel branch: second inner TLS session to the pod). Verified live on lima-node-4: kubectl repro against an agnhost TLS backend returns 200 (no more 400 'HTTP request to HTTPS server'); focused conformance run for 'Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' passes (1 Passed, 0 Failed). Companion fix mayor-rmqrl (HTML link rewrite) landed in the same PR — both were required for the aggregated Proxy conformance spec to go green.

title: proxy: pod/service proxy does not rewrite relative HTML links to include the proxy path prefix
description: Discovered while verifying mayor-caskz (scheme:name:port proxy parsing) via the [sig-network] "Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod" conformance test on lima-node-4 (run 0716-1715). That test's aggregated table includes cases where the proxied backend (agnhost porter) returns HTML containing a relative link, e.g. `test`. Upstream kube-apiserver's proxy rewrites such relative hrefs to be prefixed with the full proxy subresource path (so the link still resolves through the proxy when followed), e.g. expected `test`. u7s's pod_proxy_dispatch / service_proxy_dispatch (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs) stream the backend response body through unmodified (`Body::from_stream(...)` / `Body::from(body)`) — there is no HTML content rewriting anywhere in proxy.rs (confirmed: zero matches for "rewrite"/"text/html" in the file). This is NOT related to mayor-caskz's scheme:name:port name/port parsing fix (which is verified correct: all 320 proxy attempts in the same run had zero 404s). It reproduces even on the plain bare pod-proxy-root form (`pods//proxy/`), which never had a parsing bug. Repro (from e2e.txt, run 0716-1715): path .../pods//proxy/: wanted `test`, got `test` 3 of the 16 table-test cases fail on this (pod bare root, pod :1080, pod http:...:1080 — all serving the SERVE_PORT_80/1080 env body). Fix direction: kube-apiserver's UpgradeAwareProxy wraps text/html responses with a Transport that rewrites href/src attributes referencing absolute-path URLs to be relative to the proxy request's own path. u7s would need an equivalent rewrite step in pod_proxy_dispatch/service_proxy_dispatch when the upstream Content-Type is text/html.
close_reason: PR #859 opened — pod/service proxy now rewrites root-relative href/src links in text/html responses to include the proxy path prefix, matching upstream's proxy Transport. Verified live on lima-node-4: kubectl repro against an agnhost HTML backend returns the correctly-rewritten <a href=".../proxy/rewriteme"> link for both pod-proxy and service-proxy forms; focused conformance run for 'Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' passes (1 Passed, 0 Failed). Companion fix mayor-vkkma (https TLS backend) landed in the same PR — both were required for the aggregated Proxy conformance spec to go green.

title: fix(scheduler): find_preemption_plan conflates 'no viable preemption target' with 'GET nodes failed' — same typed-error gap as pick_node
description:
Follow-on from mayor-zf07r (pick_node's typed PickNodeError fix).

find_preemption_plan (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs) issues its own live GET
/api/v1/nodes and `bail!`s with an untyped anyhow::Error on a GET/parse
failure, exactly like pick_node used to. It has the same latent gap:
main.rs's preemption arm does `find_preemption_plan(...).await?`, so a
transient GET failure there is indistinguishable from "no node can fit the
pod even after preempting every eligible lower-priority pod" — both surface
as the outer Err, which main.rs turns into a FailedScheduling event.

Why this wasn't folded into mayor-zf07r: fixing pick_node only needed one
early-return guard ahead of the existing 2-arm match (first_pick captured
once, `should_retry_without_preempting` gates a bare `return;` from the
tokio::spawn body before the `outcome` async block is even entered).
find_preemption_plan's call sits one level deeper, INSIDE that `outcome:
anyhow::Result<String>` async block, after victims may already have been
evicted. A bare early-return doesn't type-check there (the block's declared
type is anyhow::Result<String>, not unit), so a correct fix needs the
`outcome` slot itself to gain a third "skip, no event" state (e.g.
`Option<anyhow::Result<String>>`) threaded through both the Ok/Preempt arms
and the final reason/message/event_type derivation — a materially bigger,
still-worth-doing change, not a one-match-arm tweak.

Suggested shape: either reuse PickNodeError (rename NoCapacity if needed to
cover "no viable preemption plan" too) or add a small analogous
FindPreemptionPlanError{NoViablePlan, ApiError(anyhow::Error)}; thread a
skip-vs-fail distinction through main.rs's outcome computation for the
preemption arm specifically. Blast radius: one pod's scheduling attempt
transiently marked FailedScheduling instead of retried, same P3 class as
the parent bead.

title: feat(scheduler): request allowWatchBookmarks on the pod watch so the 5-min idle timeout never fires spuriously on an idle cluster
description: Follow-up from mayor-4pctj/PR #833 (watch idle timeout). PR #833 added a 5-minute per-frame idle timeout to watch_stream in crates/kubeconfig/src/lib.rs -- correct and necessary (a half-open watch previously hung the entire scheduler). But the scheduler's own pod watch in crates/scheduler/src/main.rs does NOT request allowWatchBookmarks=true, so on a genuinely idle cluster (no pod changes for 5 min) the idle timeout fires and forces a reconnect. This is a HARMLESS no-op (main.rs already reconnects on any disconnect with a fresh watch, no resourceVersion), NOT a bug -- a periodic reconnect on an idle cluster is strictly better than the previous infinite-hang risk. This bead just eliminates the spurious reconnect: add allowWatchBookmarks=true to the scheduler's watch request URL so the apiserver's 60s bookmark heartbeat keeps the idle timeout from ever tripping on a healthy-but-quiet watch. Low priority -- purely an efficiency/cleanliness improvement, no correctness impact. Verify: on an idle single-node cluster, the scheduler watch stays connected past 5 min (no reconnect log) once bookmarks are requested.

title: refactor(apiserver): factor the duplicated Sentinel completeness-test helpers into a shared test-util module
description: The Sentinel protobuf-decode completeness-test helpers (collect_leaf_paths / has_field / assert_fields_present, ~35 lines each) are now duplicated across all 9 *_gen_adapter.rs test modules after mayor-8agr1 completed the rollout (PR #831). Each adapter re-implements the identical traversal+assertion helpers. Factor them into one shared test-util module (e.g. a #[cfg(test)] mod or a small internal test-support crate) and have all 9 adapters use it. Low priority / do opportunistically next time this area is touched -- flagged by the 8agr1 worker. No behavior change; pure test-code dedup. Verify all 9 adapters' completeness tests still pass after the refactor.
close_reason: PR #843 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/843

title: fix(scheduler): pick_node's Err conflates 'no capacity' with 'GET nodes failed' — transient API error triggers spurious preemption/FailedScheduling
description:
Found by the scheduler->apiserver glue audit (2026-07-16, finding CS8).

ROOT CAUSE: crates/scheduler/src/main.rs:178,190 -- pick_node returns the SAME Err whether the cause is 'no node has room' (should try preemption) or 'the GET /api/v1/nodes call itself failed' (transient infra hiccup -- lib.rs:1273-1276 bail, or a body-parse error). The match arm binds it as _no_capacity, baking in the wrong assumption.

CONSEQUENCE: a transient apiserver hiccup makes the scheduler treat a normal pod exactly like a preemption candidate -- it issues a second redundant GET /api/v1/nodes inside find_preemption_plan lib.rs:1341, and if that also fails transiently the pod is marked FailedScheduling (user-visible, disruptive) instead of simply retried on the next watch tick. Worst case: if the first GET failure was transient but a later call inside find_preemption_plan happens to succeed, the scheduler could evict real lower-priority pods to solve a problem that was never actually 'no capacity'.

FIX DIRECTION: give pick_node a typed error enum PickNodeError with NoCapacity vs ApiError variants so main.rs can retry ApiError with backoff instead of always falling through to preemption. Small contained change -- one function's return type + one match arm -- but touches the public signature, so its own bead not a drive-by. Regression test: pick_node returning an ApiError must NOT trigger preemption; a genuine NoCapacity must. P3: real correctness risk but requires the transient-failure window to hit, and blast radius is one pod.
notes: MAYOR REVIEW 2026-07-16 (PR #835): PASS. PickNodeError enum via thiserror matches the existing PatchError/StoreError idiom (transparent + from anyhow::Error). pick_node returns Result<String,PickNodeError>: GET-failure -> ApiError, select_node_with_capacity failure -> NoCapacity. should_retry_without_preempting is a trivially-correct pure predicate with 2 fail-on-revert tests (verified by hardcoding to false). main.rs captures first_pick once, and on ApiError logs + RELEASES the in_flight key + bare return (skips both preemption AND FailedScheduling) so the pod stays Pending for watch redelivery -- correctly also addresses the audit's CS9 in_flight-orphan concern for this path. NoCapacity/Ok arm untouched. find_preemption_plan has the same untyped-bail issue but fixing it needs a third skip-no-event state through the outcome block -- correctly deferred as follow-on mayor-7xr09 rather than a messy partial. CI CLEAN. Closes the scheduler hardening cluster. Merging.
close_reason: PR #835 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/835 — pick_node now returns typed PickNodeError{NoCapacity,ApiError}; main.rs retries on ApiError instead of preempting/FailedScheduling. Follow-on mayor-7xr09 filed for find_preemption_plan's analogous gap.

title: Extend built-in OpenAPI v3 schemas beyond curated Pod/Service/ConfigMap/Secret/Namespace/Deployment set
description:
mayor-fut44 fixed kubectl explain <builtin> being 100% broken (empty /openapi/v3 paths + no per-group v3 document for static built-in groups). The fix added a generic mechanism in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs: static_group_v3_document() builds paths+components.schemas for ANY static group/version from its existing APIResourceList data (static_group_resources()/api_v1_resource_list_value()), enriched by two curated lookup tables (curated_kind_description, curated_top_level_properties) for a handful of Kinds: Pod, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, Namespace, Deployment. Every OTHER built-in Kind (ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob, Node, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, Endpoints, Event, ServiceAccount, ResourceQuota, LimitRange, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, ClusterRole/Role, StorageClass, Lease, HorizontalPodAutoscaler, PodDisruptionBudget, CustomResourceDefinition, APIService, all of admissionregistration/authentication/authorization/certificates/coordination/discovery.k8s.io/flowcontrol/gateway.networking/node.k8s.io/policy/rbac/resource/scheduling/storage) now gets a CORRECT but MINIMAL schema (apiVersion/kind/metadata only, no spec/status breakdown) -- kubectl explain <kind> succeeds and shows a real description, but the FIELDS list is incomplete for these.

Follow-up scope: add more Kinds to curated_kind_description/curated_top_level_properties (same mechanism, just more data -- transcribe real field names/descriptions from k8s.io/api types.go, release-1.36, the same way mayor-fut44 did for the initial 6). Prioritize by real usage signal if available (conformance explain calls, common kubectl usage) rather than guessing. Also consider (separate decision, flag before doing it): whether kubectl explain <kind>.spec (recursing one level into spec/status internals, e.g. Pod.spec.containers) is worth the much larger transcription effort for the highest-traffic Kinds (Pod, Deployment) -- out of scope for mayor-fut44, which only covers the top-level 'kubectl explain <kind>' case.
acceptance_criteria: kubectl explain <kind> for additional prioritized built-in Kinds (beyond Pod/Service/ConfigMap/Secret/Namespace/Deployment) shows real top-level field names/types instead of just apiVersion/kind/metadata. No regression to the generic static_group_v3_document mechanism or existing curated Kinds.

title: patch.rs merge_key_for_path: 9 more confirmed +patchMergeKey gaps found by the new completeness check (2 need special JSON-key handling)
description:
Found by mayor-izlrz's new merge_key_for_path completeness test (crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs, test merge_key_for_path_covers_every_schema_declared_patch_merge_key), which parses every +patchMergeKey annotation out of ALL vendored .proto files (not just core/v1, apps/v1, batch/v1) and cross-references it against merge_key_for_path.

Beyond the 6 fields mayor-izlrz fixed (closing mayor-m8k75), the broader scan surfaced 9 more schema-declared +patchMergeKey fields with no matching entry (exact-path or suffix arm) in merge_key_for_path. They are deliberately NOT fixed by mayor-izlrz (kept in a known_missing_tracked_separately allowlist in the test, with the same evidence below) because each needs individual collision/JSON-key verification, same as NodeStatus.addresses did in that change.

Straightforward (field name unique or consistent across all declaring messages, key value consistent, likely a safe suffix arm — but NOT verified against a live cluster/kubectl repro, do that before fixing, same evidence discipline as mayor-izlrz):
1. CSINodeSpec.drivers -> name (storage/v1/generated.proto:346-350)
2. MutatingWebhook.matchConditions -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:466-471)
3. MutatingAdmissionPolicySpec.matchConditions -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:1065-1070)
4. ValidatingWebhook.matchConditions -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:647-651)
5. ValidatingAdmissionPolicySpec.matchConditions -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:1247-1252)

Needs an exact-path entry, NOT a generic suffix arm (same shape as NodeStatus.addresses vs EndpointSubset.addresses):
6. ValidatingAdmissionPolicySpec.variables -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:1079-1084). MutatingAdmissionPolicySpec.variables (same file, line 425) shares the field name "variables" but declares +listType=atomic with NO patchMergeKey at all -- a generic ".variables" suffix arm would incorrectly start merging MutatingAdmissionPolicySpec.variables by "name" too, even though upstream declares it replace-only. Needs a literal "spec.variables" (or whatever the real call-site path turns out to be) entry scoped to ValidatingAdmissionPolicySpec only, verified against real usage the way addresses was.

Needs the REAL JSON key, not the literal .proto token (verified via this repo's own JSON adapters, not guessed):
7. MutatingWebhookConfiguration.Webhooks -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:660-666). The .proto field is literally spelled "Webhooks" (capitalized), but crates/apiserver/src/admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs:336 constructs the real JSON as "webhooks" (lowercase). A merge_key_for_path entry keyed on ".Webhooks" as extracted from the .proto would never match real traffic; it must be ".webhooks" (or "webhooks" bare, whichever path shape a real strategic-merge-patch against this resource actually produces -- verify, don't guess).
8. ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.Webhooks -> name (admissionregistration/v1/generated.proto:1261-1267). Same capitalization mismatch, same adapter file confirms lowercase "webhooks" (crates/apiserver/src/admissionreg_gen_adapter.rs:352).
9. JSONSchemaProps.xKubernetesValidations -> rule (apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/v1/generated.proto:587-592). The .proto field is "xKubernetesValidations" (camelCase), but crates/apiserver/src/apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs:425 constructs the real JSON key as "x-kubernetes-validations" (hyphenated, per OpenAPI/JSONSchema vendor-extension convention). Also nested inside a recursive JSONSchemaProps structure (properties/items/allOf/oneOf/anyOf/not can all nest this field arbitrarily deep) with no fixed parent path -- lower priority given how rarely a CRD's OpenAPI schema is strategic-merge-patched in practice, but worth a suffix-arm entry once the correct JSON key is confirmed.

Fix each the same way as mayor-izlrz's 6: verify the gap reproduces (falls through to MergeKeyKind::Unknown) via a failing unit test first, then add the (path, key) entry to merge_key_for_path plus a regression test (construct parent object, strategic-merge-patch to add one array entry, assert existing entries survive). Once fixed, remove the corresponding entry from known_missing_tracked_separately in patch.rs's completeness test so the check stays honest.
close_reason: PR #825 opened — fixed 7/9 gaps (CSINodeSpec.drivers, 4x matchConditions, both WebhookConfiguration.webhooks); deferred ValidatingAdmissionPolicySpec.variables (real cross-kind path collision, needs resource-kind context threaded into merge_key_for_path — architecture decision, not guessed) and JSONSchemaProps.xKubernetesValidations (unreachable via SMP today since CRD spec.versions has no merge key upstream either)

title: fix(apiserver): core_gen_adapter drops explicit spec.priority=0 on protobuf decode
description: core_gen_adapter.rs's gen_pod_spec_to_json (~line 1401, in the generated-protobuf-to-JSON adapter used when a client PUTs/POSTs a protobuf-encoded pod) does: if let Some(p) = spec.priority.filter(|&v| v != 0) { ...insert into json... } — this treats an explicitly-set spec.priority of 0 the same as absent/never-set, silently dropping it. Found as a byproduct of mayor-rsei (scheduler preemption) investigation while auditing priority handling; not exercised by the SchedulerPreemption conformance tests themselves (none of those pods have priority exactly 0), so left unfixed there to keep that change surgical. Likely fix: track presence via the prost Option<i32> directly (Some(0) vs None) rather than filtering by value, mirroring how hostNetwork/other tri-state-vs-bool fields are handled elsewhere in the same file. Needs a round-trip regression test: protobuf-encoded pod with priority explicitly 0 must decode to spec.priority: 0, not omit the field.
close_reason: PR #822 opened: fixed gen_pod_spec_to_json to track spec.priority presence via Some/None instead of filtering by value, added regression tests for Some(0) and None cases

title: webhook rules: RuleWithOperations has no scope field, so scope: Namespaced/Cluster is silently ignored
description:
Discovered while implementing mayor-0c3db (admission webhook typed-cache perf fix).

crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs's RuleWithOperations struct (the typed shape
MutatingWebhookConfiguration/ValidatingWebhookConfiguration webhooks[].rules[]
entries are deserialized into) has only api_groups/api_versions/resources/operations
- no scope field. Upstream's Rule.Scope (*ScopeType: "Namespaced"/"Cluster"/"*")
is silently dropped by serde during deserialization (no deny_unknown_fields).

matches_rule (the Value-based rule matcher, still used for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
matchConstraints/matchResources) DOES implement scope matching and has passing unit
tests for it - but those tests construct raw serde_json::Value rules directly, never
through the real WebhookConfig/WebhookEntry/RuleWithOperations deserialization path.
For actual MutatingWebhookConfiguration/ValidatingWebhookConfiguration objects, a
user-specified `scope: Namespaced` (or Cluster) on a rule has never been enforced:
the field is dropped at parse time, so the webhook fires regardless of whether the
target resource is namespaced or cluster-scoped.

mayor-0c3db intentionally preserved this exact (buggy) behavior rather than fixing
it - the bead required identical before/after behavior for the perf-only cache
change, and matches_rule_typed (the new typed fast path) explicitly does not
filter by scope, matching what matches_rule effectively did for the webhook path
(scope always defaulted to "*" since the key was never present after the
to_value(RuleWithOperations) round trip either).

Fix would be: add `#[serde(default)] scope: Option<String>` to RuleWithOperations,
and add scope matching to matches_rule_typed (mirroring matches_rule's
"Namespaced"=>namespace.is_some(), "Cluster"=>namespace.is_none(), _=>true logic).
Needs a real behavior-change test (a webhook with scope: Namespaced must not fire
on a cluster-scoped resource create) - the existing matches_rule scope tests do NOT
cover this because they bypass the real deserialization path.

LABELS: apiserver, bug, admission
close_reason: PR #817 opened

title: investigate: containerStatuses merge key 'name' vs schema's +listType=atomic (replace-whole-array) declaration
description:
Found by the schema-mapping-completeness audit (2026-07-15), flagged as an inconsistency to investigate, NOT a confirmed bug.

patch.rs:405-413 registers containerStatuses/initContainerStatuses/ephemeralContainerStatuses with merge key "name" -- but the vendored schema marks all three +listType=atomic (core/v1/generated.proto:4918,4930,4948) and carries NO +patchMergeKey/+patchStrategy=merge annotation for any of them (unlike every other entry in this file, this block has no justifying comment).

+listType=atomic is upstream's declaration that the array should be replaced wholesale, not merged by key -- the opposite of what patch.rs currently does here.

Two possibilities, neither confirmed:
(a) patch.rs's entry is stale/wrong and should be removed (let these fall through to whole-array-replace, matching the schema).
(b) real kubelet wire behavior still expects name-keyed merging regardless of the schema's atomic declaration (plausible -- +listType=atomic is a newer structural-schema/SSA-era annotation and may not reflect legacy strategic-merge-patch client expectations, e.g. kubelet's own status-patch construction).

Contrast: batch/v1/generated.proto:367-369's JobStatus.conditions carries BOTH +patchMergeKey=type+patchStrategy=merge AND +listType=atomic simultaneously -- the two annotation systems are not mutually exclusive in the schema itself, so "prefer whichever tag exists" is not a safe general rule.

Needs either reading kubelet's actual patch-construction source, or a live e2e run showing which behavior real clients expect, before deciding. Do not change patch.rs's existing behavior without that evidence -- it may be intentionally compensating for real client behavior, not a leftover mistake.
notes: Second instance of this exact question found while working mayor-izlrz: PodStatus.hostIPs (core/v1/generated.proto:4882-4886) ALSO declares patchStrategy=merge/patchMergeKey=ip simultaneously with +listType=atomic -- the identical annotation shape as JobStatus.conditions above, not just containerStatuses' opposite case. mayor-izlrz's new patch.rs completeness test (merge_key_for_path_covers_every_schema_declared_patch_merge_key) deliberately does NOT register a hostIPs merge-key entry, tracking it in a known_ambiguous allowlist alongside JobStatus.conditions pending whichever evidence resolves this bead. If/when this is resolved, hostIPs's known_ambiguous entry in patch.rs should be revisited too (either add the ip merge-key entry, or explicitly confirm it should stay Unknown/whole-replace).

title: fix(apiserver): kubectl explain fails for CRD name colliding with unrelated resource-type lookup ("server doesnt have a resource type")
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-7qqrd (CRD OpenAPI standard-field injection). After
that fix, sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI' on lima-node-5 (run
temp/e2e/0715-1644-customresourcepublishopenapi) is 28/29 passing; the one remaining
failure is a DIFFERENT, unrelated It block in the same Describe container:

  [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI [Privileged:ClusterAdmin] [It]
  [Flaky] kubectl explain works for CR with the same resource name as built-in object.
  (test/e2e/apimachinery/crd_publish_openapi.go:490-509)

This test creates a CRD (kind "Waldo", random plural like "ksvc-1784101416" chosen to
alias-collide with a built-in-ish short name) and then runs
`kubectl explain <plural>.spec`, expecting it to succeed. u7s currently returns:

  stderr: the server doesn't have a resource type "ksvc-1784101416"
  error: exit status 1

Note this It is marked `[Flaky]` by upstream itself (not a hard conformance
requirement), so it may not be a certification blocker, but it indicates a real gap:
kubectl's REST-mapping/discovery resolution for a freshly-created CRD's plural name
sometimes fails to resolve to the CRD's own resource type. Not yet root-caused — needs
investigation into whether this is a discovery-cache timing issue (CRD created
immediately before explain, discovery not yet refreshed) or a genuine resource-type
resolution bug. Root cause file:line not yet identified; start from
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs (API discovery endpoints) and
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs (CRD create path) — check whether the CRD's
resource is immediately visible via /apis/<group>/v1/... discovery right after create,
since kubectl's RESTMapper build depends on that.

GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI' -> "kubectl explain works for CR
with the same resource name as built-in object" passes (or is confirmed to be an
upstream-flaky test unrelated to u7s and safe to leave as a known gap — flag back to
mayor if so).
close_reason: Investigated, no code fix: root cause is a confirmed upstream kubectl client-side discovery-cache staleness bug (k8s.io/kubernetes#65517), not a u7s server defect. The test's OWN title is misleading — the 'colliding' identifier is ksvc-<timestamp>, a CRD ShortName alias (not the plural, which is deliberately 'services' to collide with the built-in); kubectl resolves it via restmapper.shortcutExpander.expandResourceShortcut(), which snapshots discovery via the SAME on-disk ~/.kube/cache used by the whole e2e binary run and does not retry/refresh on a stale miss (only the wrapped DeferredDiscoveryRESTMapper retries, and only AFTER expansion already failed). Verified server-side is correct and immediate: CRD Established:True synchronously; GET /apis/<group>/<version> and /apis both include the new group+shortName right after create (no propagation delay). Live repro on --stack-only (lima-node-2:6445, latest main @321cd492): identical CRD+shortName explain FAILS with kubectl's normal (reused) cache dir, SUCCEEDS instantly with a fresh --cache-dir -- proves the failure is 100% a function of client cache state, not server state. Gate: sonobuoy --focus CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI run twice on current main (no code changes) -- run 1: target test 'kubectl explain works for CR with the same resource name as built-in object' PASSED (status=passed, junit_01.xml), 28/29 overall (1 unrelated transient i/o timeout dialing 10.96.0.1:443, gone on rerun); run 2 (settled stack): 29/29 PASSED including target test. cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -D warnings both clean (no changes made). Follow-on: found and filed a separate, real, much bigger defect during investigation -- mayor-fut44 (openapi_v3() never lists built-in groups in its paths index, breaking kubectl explain <any built-in> via the default v3 renderer) -- correctly out of scope here per dispatch instructions (orthogonal to this suite, needs a cross-cutting OpenAPI v3 build-out, not a surgical fix).

title: kubectl get <custom-resource> <name> ignores Accept:Table (cr.rs get_cr/get_cr_namespaced)
description:
Discovered incidentally while implementing mayor-ssnyd (single-object GET Table fix for
built-in/registry resources). Custom resources (CRD-backed) share the same bug that
mayor-ssnyd fixed for registry resources, but in a different file that bead's root-cause
list didn't cover.

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs get_cr (~line 1048) and get_cr_namespaced (~line 1666)
both take only (State, Path) — no HeaderMap param at all — and unconditionally return
Json(obj). resource.rs's get_resource/get_namespaced_resource forward to these two
functions for any group/plural not in the static registry (i.e. every CRD-backed type), so
`kubectl get <cr-kind> <name>` for a custom resource still falls back to NAME/AGE-only
output post mayor-ssnyd, same "Unable to decode server response into a Table" symptom.

Fix shape: same pattern as mayor-ssnyd — add `headers: HeaderMap`, check
super::table::wants_table(accept), and call super::table::build_table(&group, &plural,
vec![obj]) for a single-row Table. list_cr (LIST) already has a wants_table check
(cr.rs ~860) as a reference for the Accept-parsing/406 pattern to mirror.

Not fixed as part of mayor-ssnyd to keep that PR's diff scoped to the exact files/functions
named in its root-cause list (pods.rs, resource.rs) and avoid touching cr.rs while another
worker (mayor-auzv5) was active on the adjacent crd.rs SSA-parsing surface this session.
close_reason: PR #812 opened

title: kubectl get pods -A ignores Accept:Table — falls back to NAME/AGE (core_list_resource cross-ns pods branch)
description:
Discovered incidentally while VM-verifying mayor-ssnyd (single-object GET Table fix). The
bead mayor-ssnyd claimed "LIST requests (kubectl get pods, kubectl get pods -A) DO honor
Table correctly" but that is only true for the namespaced list_pods path.

Repro on a live stack:
  kubectl get pods -n kube-system        # full READY/STATUS/RESTARTS/AGE columns (correct)
  kubectl get pods -A                    # NAME/AGE only (bug)
  kubectl get pods -A -v=8 2>&1 | grep 'Unable to decode'
  # matches: table_printer.go:45 Unable to decode server response into a Table

Root cause: core_list_resource's special-cased cross-namespace "pods" branch
(crates/apiserver/src/handlers/core.rs:45-153, GET /api/v1/pods) builds the PodList body
directly via build_list_response (core.rs:143) and never checks
super::table::wants_table(accept) / calls super::table::build_table, unlike the namespaced
list_pods (pods.rs) which already does this correctly. kubectl sends the same
Accept: application/json;as=Table;... header either way; only this one cross-namespace
code path ignores it.

Fix shape: mirror list_pods's wants_table check + super::table::build_table("", "pods",
items) call in this branch of core_list_resource, same pattern as list_pods/list_resource.

Out of scope for mayor-ssnyd (that bead is single-object GET only); filing separately so
the incidental LIST-side finding isn't lost.
close_reason: PR #811 opened

title: perf(apiserver): parallelize/cap per-backend discovery fetches in aggregated discovery
description:
Follow-up from PR #801 review (mayor-vl391 API aggregation proxying).

discovery.rs's build_aggregated_discovery (~lines 305-345) awaits each
APIService backend's live discovery fetch (discovery_resources_for_apiservice)
SEQUENTIALLY, once per group/version in a for loop. Each fetch has its own
10s connect+request timeout (build_backend_client in aggregation.rs). One
slow/down aggregated backend stalls the WHOLE aggregated-discovery response
(used by /discovery/v2 and any client that negotiates the aggregated Accept
header, including modern kubectl) by up to that backend's own timeout, and
this compounds ADDITIVELY: N unresponsive backends -> up to N * 10s added to
every /apis and /discovery/v2 call, cluster-wide, for every caller, until
those backends are fixed or removed.

Fix direction: run the per-group discovery fetches concurrently (e.g.
futures::future::join_all or a bounded join set) instead of sequentially
inside the for loop, and/or cap the TOTAL time spent on APIService discovery
fetches for one /apis response (e.g. a shorter per-fetch timeout specifically
for the discovery path, separate from the request-proxy path's 10s, since a
stale discovery listing is far less harmful than a slow read that blocks
every kubectl user).

Not a correctness bug for the currently-passing aggregator conformance test
(single well-behaved backend) -- a robustness/scalability concern once
multiple APIServices are registered, one of which is unhealthy.
close_reason: PR #806 opened

title: perf(apiserver): cache registered APIService group/versions instead of a store lookup per request
description:
Follow-up from PR #801 review (mayor-vl391 API aggregation proxying).

find_apiservice (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/aggregation.rs:72-81) does a real
store lookup on EVERY /apis/{group}/{version}/* request via proxy_middleware,
even when zero APIServices are registered -- adding latency/lock contention to
ALL non-core traffic (every request that isn't a literal built-in route match,
which given axum's routing is effectively every /apis/... request, since the
middleware runs before route matching).

api_group_list_inner's extra list_apiservice_groups call (called on every plain
GET /apis) has the same shape: a full store list scan even when there are no
APIServices at all.

Fix direction: an in-memory cache of registered APIService group/versions
(name -> parsed spec, or just the set of "{version}.{group}" keys), invalidated
on APIService create/update/delete -- similar to the existing
AdmissionConfigCache pattern in state.rs (write-through invalidation, RwLock,
warmed at startup). Given APIService writes are rare (cluster-admin-only,
infrequent) and reads are on every non-core request, this is a clear
read-heavy/write-rare cache candidate.

Not a correctness bug -- purely a latency/scalability concern. Do not fix
without measuring the actual overhead first; the store lookup may already be
fast enough (SQLite, single lookup by key) that this isn't worth the added
cache-invalidation complexity for a pre-alpha project. Investigate before
implementing.
close_reason: PR #807 opened

title: crd.rs patch_crd/patch_crd_status have the same apply-patch+yaml JSON-only parsing bug as mayor-kz1m
description:
Found while implementing mayor-kz1m (SSA YAML-tolerant parser generalization). crd.rs's patch_crd (~line 634) and patch_crd_status (~line 778) both call detect_patch_type() which accepts application/apply-patch+yaml as StrategicMerge, but then parse the body unconditionally with serde_json::from_slice — identical shape to the bug fixed in mayor-kz1m's other 8 call sites. A genuine multi-line YAML apply-patch+yaml body against an existing CRD or its /status subresource will 400 with 'invalid patch JSON'.

NOT fixed in mayor-kz1m because the scout's sizing pass explicitly enumerated 8 call sites (resource.rs, status.rs, namespaces.rs, pods.rs, approval.rs, cr.rs) and crd.rs was not among them — kept mayor-kz1m surgical to its assigned scope rather than expanding it.

Fix should mirror mayor-kz1m exactly: detect is_ssa via content_type(&headers).contains("apply-patch+yaml"), branch to crate::handlers::json_patch::ssa_body_to_json(&body) when true. json_patch.rs already exports ssa_body_to_json as pub(crate) after mayor-kz1m, so this is a small follow-up (no new shared-helper work needed).
close_reason: PR #805 opened

title: fix(apiserver): single-resource GET ignores Accept:Table — kubectl get <res> <name> always falls back to NAME/AGE
description:
kubectl 'get <resource> <name>' (single-object GET, any resource type) never honors 'Accept: application/json;as=Table;...' — the handler unconditionally returns the raw object with Content-Type: application/json, so kubectl logs 'table_printer.go:45 Unable to decode server response into a Table. Falling back to hardcoded types' and prints only NAME/AGE instead of the normal READY/STATUS/RESTARTS/etc columns. LIST requests (kubectl get pods, kubectl get pods -A) DO honor Table correctly (list_pods calls table::build_table at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:324-325) — only the single-name GET path is missing it.

ROOT CAUSE (file:line): crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:499-519 get_pod<S> — always returns 'stored.value' raw bytes with a hardcoded 'application/json' content type, never inspects the Accept header. Same pattern in the generic single-resource handler crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:209-234 get_resource<S> — always does Json(obj), never checks for as=Table. (get_namespaced_resource at resource.rs:1341 likely shares the same gap — not yet checked.)

REPRO (kubectl -v=8 shows the raw response is kind:Pod, not kind:Table):
  kubectl get pod <any-pod-name>          # prints only NAME/AGE columns
  kubectl get pod <any-pod-name> -v=8 2>&1 | grep 'Unable to decode'
  # I0715 ... table_printer.go:45 Unable to decode server response into a Table ...
Confirmed on plain pods with no special fields (e.g. coredns pod) and on pods with duplicate volumeMounts/subPathExpr — the trigger is purely 'single GET vs LIST', not any particular pod spec shape (ruled out: subPathExpr, duplicate volumeMounts-same-name, terminated container state all render fine via LIST).

IMPACT: kubectl UX only — the Go e2e test framework polls objects via typed client-go Get() (plain JSON, no Table Accept), so this does NOT explain any of the mayor-25ap status-hang cases (confirmed while scouting that bead). But any conformance test that runs literal 'kubectl get <resource> <name>' and asserts on column output (some [sig-cli] Kubectl client tests do) would be affected.

FIX SHAPE (not yet implemented): thread the Accept header into get_pod/get_resource/get_namespaced_resource the same way list_pods already does, and call table::build_table with a single-item list when Table is requested.
close_reason: PR #808 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/808

title: protobuf PodSpec decode also drops hostUsers/setHostnameAsFQDN/resources/hostnameOverride
description:
While completing mayor-w5eoy (which fixed schedulerName, hostPID/hostIPC/shareProcessNamespace,
imagePullSecrets, preemptionPolicy, topologySpreadConstraints, readinessGates, overhead, os,
resourceClaims, and the deprecated serviceAccount alias in
crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs::gen_pod_spec_to_json), found 4 more PodSpec fields
that function still never reads off the generated prost struct:

  - hostUsers (field 37) — host user-namespace toggle, default true; k8s:conversion-gen=false
  - setHostnameAsFQDN (field 35) — bool, changes kernel hostname format
  - resources (field 40) — pod-level ResourceRequirements, alpha PodLevelResources feature gate
  - hostnameOverride (field 41) — string, alpha HostnameOverride feature gate

These were deliberately left out of mayor-w5eoy's scope (that bead's field list was already
enumerated). Same fix pattern applies: add the read-from-prost-struct + JSON-insert-if-present
logic in gen_pod_spec_to_json, plus a regression test per field following the pattern
established in core_gen_adapter.rs (construct a core_v1::Pod, encode, decode_pod_proto_gen,
assert the field survives).

Lower priority than mayor-w5eoy's fields: hostUsers/setHostnameAsFQDN have narrower blast
radius (no scheduler-correctness impact like schedulingGates did), and resources/
hostnameOverride are both still-alpha upstream feature gates unlikely to be exercised by
conformance today.
close_reason: PR #800 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/800

title: replace_resource (cluster-scoped PUT) has the same missing metadata.uid restoration gap as replace_namespaced_resource
description: mayor-h0lte (PR #793) fixed replace_namespaced_resource to restore metadata.uid from the stored object when a client's PUT body omits it, matching real kube-apiserver's rest.BeforeUpdate (unconditional for every resource, every Update). replace_resource (the cluster-scoped PUT handler in the same file, crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs) has the identical gap: it never restores uid either. No cluster-scoped resource has a CONFIRMED live failure from this today (unlike EndpointSlice, which is namespaced), so it was left out of the surgical mayor-h0lte fix. Worth auditing cluster-scoped controllers (e.g. Node, PersistentVolume, ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding, StorageClass, PriorityClass) for any that PUT with a blank uid, and applying the same restoration (reusing the existing conditional stored-object reads already done for status-subresource/PriorityClass-immutability checks, to avoid adding a new unconditional read).
close_reason: PR #796 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/796) opened. Consolidated replace_resource's two conditional stored-object reads (PriorityClass immutability, status-subresource) into one, extended to also fire when incoming body's uid is blank, and restore metadata.uid from the stored object in that case (mirrors replace_namespaced_resource's mayor-h0lte fix). Regression test replace_resource_restores_uid_when_put_body_omits_it (StorageClass, a type hitting neither pre-existing conditional read) added and confirmed to fail on revert. cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2225 apiserver tests + all other crates green. cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean. Live kubectl verification on lima-node-smoke (--reset --stack-only): StorageClass blind-put-verify (uid 52c3241b-d2d2-4f33-96ec-4c45e7b6ce30) and ClusterRole blind-put-verify-cr (uid 3f8c23ec-f158-4dce-95fc-a3a129dd8fd3) both PUT with metadata.uid stripped from body via kubectl replace -f -; both retained original uid after, resourceVersion advanced normally.

title: perf(apiserver): cache typed webhook/policy structs — avoid per-request Value clone+reparse and per-rule to_value
description:
Follow-on from perf audit mayor-pnnak (ai/findings/session-perf-audit-2026-07-14.md,
item 5), spot-checking mayor-cef5's deferred F2 finding against current main.

F2 (per-rule serde_json::to_value(rule) inside the webhook rule-matching loop) is
CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT, unchanged: admission.rs:964 (mutating) and :2892 (validating)
— every rule of every configured webhook is re-serialized from its typed
RuleWithOperations struct into a serde_json::Value on every admission-gated request,
purely so matches_rule can index into it.

NEW related finding in the same hot path (not previously called out at this exact
line): run_mutating_webhooks/run_validating_webhooks (admission.rs:2483,2883) do
`serde_json::from_value::<WebhookConfig>(config.clone())` — cloning each cached config
Value before parsing it into a typed struct, on EVERY admission-gated write (not just
writes to webhook-config objects themselves). mayor-al9a (PR #666) and mayor-4qm5x
(PR #732) already fixed the CACHE-READ side of this (fetch_mutating_configs /
fetch_validating_configs etc. return Arc::clone, O(1), no deep-clone of the Vec) — but
the CALLERS still clone+reparse each individual Value out of that Arc'd Vec on every
single request, which is a distinct, still-open cost sitting right next to F2.

Both F2 and this clone-then-parse cost share the same root cause: the admission cache
stores raw serde_json::Value configs, not their parsed typed form, so every request
pays a Value->struct (config) and then a struct->Value (each rule, for matching) round
trip.

FIX SHAPE: extend AdmissionConfigCache (or a sibling cache) to store the ALREADY-PARSED
typed form (e.g. Arc<Vec<WebhookEntry>> instead of Arc<Vec<serde_json::Value>>),
re-parsed only on write-through refresh (same invalidation strategy as today — see
AppState::refresh_admission_config), not on every read. Change matches_rule (or add a
typed variant) to accept &RuleWithOperations directly instead of &serde_json::Value,
eliminating the per-rule to_value call. This removes both the per-request Value clone
and the per-rule reserialization in one change, on a path that runs on every
admission-gated write in the cluster.

GATE: a unit/bench asserting run_mutating_webhooks/run_validating_webhooks no longer
clone or serde_json::to_value any config/rule data per call when the cache is warm;
existing admission.rs webhook/VAP test suite (cargo test -p u7s-apiserver) stays green.
close_reason: PR #810 opened - cached typed WebhookEntry list (both F2 and clone-then-parse fixed together)

title: perf(store): deletion_log O(n) eviction now runs inside the global write lock
description:
Follow-on from perf audit mayor-pnnak (ai/findings/session-perf-audit-2026-07-14.md,
item 3), auditing mayor-sjlw1's broadcast-ordering fix (PR #767).

crates/store/src/sqlite.rs's push_event_locked's deletion_log eviction path (roughly
lines 182-197) does a linear `.iter().min_by_key(|(_, e)| e.revision)` scan over up to
2*RING_CAPACITY (2000) entries when the deletion-log cap is exceeded — this is the
pre-existing mayor-cef5 F12 finding ("O(N) deletion_log eviction, sqlite.rs:137"),
unchanged in absolute cost.

What changed this session: mayor-sjlw1 (PR #767) correctly moved push_event_locked's
call site to run INSIDE the spawn_blocking closure while still holding write_conn's
blocking_lock guard (previously it ran after releasing the guard, which caused a real
broadcast-ordering race and silently-dropped DELETE events under load — that fix was
necessary and is not in question). Side effect: the ~1-in-2000 O(n) linear-scan eviction
now runs while blocking EVERY OTHER WRITER IN THE CLUSTER (global write_conn mutex),
where before it only delayed that one writer's own post-lock continuation. The absolute
cost is still small (in-memory HashMap scan, likely low-microseconds even at n=2000),
so this is not an urgent regression, but the blast radius changed from "one writer" to
"every concurrent writer," which makes the pre-existing F12 finding worth fixing now
rather than continuing to defer it.

FIX SHAPE: replace the linear min-scan with an O(log n) structure, e.g. maintain a
BTreeMap<u64 revision, String key> alongside the existing
HashMap<String, Arc<InternalEvent>> deletion_log, so eviction is a
`pop_first()`-equivalent instead of a full scan. Must preserve existing semantics:
evict-on-recreate (remove tombstone when a PUT arrives for a tombstoned key) and
cap-at-2xRING_CAPACITY (evict lowest-revision entry when over cap).

GATE: existing sqlite.rs deletion_log/eviction unit tests continue to pass; add a test
asserting eviction remains correct (evicts lowest revision, not scan order) with the
new structure; no change in observable watch/tombstone-replay behavior.
close_reason: PR #844 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/844

title: audit newer PodSpec fields for protobuf-decode + strategic-merge-key registration gaps
description:
mayor-pwf4g's schedulingGates fix hit TWO pre-existing infra gaps, both for the
same reason: a relatively new PodSpec field (spec.schedulingGates, added
1.27+) was present in the vendored .proto schema and decoded fine via JSON,
but was invisible via two other paths real clients use:

1. crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs's gen_pod_spec_to_json (the
   protobuf Pod-decode path client-go/kube-controller-manager use by default)
   never read obj.scheduling_gates into the output JSON — silently dropped on
   any protobuf-encoded pod create (e.g. every pod a controller creates from a
   template), even though prost correctly generates the field from the .proto.

2. crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs's merge_key_for_path table didn't register
   spec.schedulingGates (merge key "name", matching upstream's
   patchStrategy:"merge" patchMergeKey:"name" tag) — so a strategic-merge-patch
   $patch:delete on this field returned 400 instead of removing the named gate.

Both gaps were invisible to a plain `kubectl apply`/JSON-based manual test
(only surfaced via a real ReplicaSet-controller-created + gate-removal e2e
flow), which is exactly why they weren't caught by earlier ad-hoc kubectl
verification. Worth an audit of other fields added to the vendored
proto/*.proto schemas within the last few k8s minor versions (schedulingGates,
resizePolicy, os, hostUsers, schedulingGroup, etc.) against both
core_gen_adapter.rs's per-kind decoders and patch.rs's merge-key table, to find
any other silently-dropped-via-protobuf or rejected-$patch:delete fields
before they show up as conformance failures.
notes: Follow-up bead filed: mayor-5x99r (patch.rs merge_key_for_path unreachable for CronJob's 3-level jobTemplate nesting — architectural, not fixed in this dispatch). Direct fixes applied in this dispatch (patch.rs merge_key_for_path): registered spec.topologySpreadConstraints/spec.template.spec.topologySpreadConstraints (key=topologyKey), spec.template.spec.hostAliases (key=ip, bare spec.hostAliases was already registered), spec.resourceClaims/spec.template.spec.resourceClaims (key=name). core_gen_adapter.rs gen_pod_spec_to_json audited field-by-field against upstream 1.36 PodSpec (41 live fields) — no actionable gaps found (all already fixed this session); schedulingGroup (proto tag 43, alpha GenericWorkload feature) is unread but is an unimplemented feature everywhere (not JSON-decodable either), not a regression, so no bead filed for it — flagged as informational only. Findings doc: ai/findings/yhg35-podspec-audit-2026-07-15.md (gitignored, worker-local).
close_reason: PR #804 opened — audit complete, 3 patch.rs merge-key gaps fixed directly (hostAliases template path, topologySpreadConstraints, resourceClaims), 1 follow-up bead filed (mayor-5x99r, CronJob nesting-depth architectural gap), 1 informational item flagged (schedulingGroup — unimplemented alpha feature, not a regression). core_gen_adapter.rs protobuf-decode path audited field-by-field, no gaps found (already complete). Findings doc: ai/findings/yhg35-podspec-audit-2026-07-15.md (gitignored, worker-local).

title: scheduler must set PodScheduled=False/Reason=SchedulingGated status condition on gated pods
description:
Follow-on to mayor-vkobg: needs_scheduling now correctly keeps a pod with
non-empty spec.schedulingGates out of the scheduling cycle entirely (verified:
gated pods stay Pending with spec.nodeName empty, both via direct kubectl
reproduction and via sonobuoy). However, "validates Pods with non-empty
schedulingGates are blocked on scheduling" STILL fails (predicates.go:831,
WaitForPodsSchedulingGated times out) for a reason DISTINCT from "does the pod
get scheduled".

Root cause CONFIRMED by reading the actual upstream helper this test calls
(k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/pod/wait.go:475-486,
WaitForPodsSchedulingGated): it does NOT just check that the pod is
unscheduled -- it polls each pod's status.conditions for a
`PodScheduled: False, Reason: SchedulingGated` condition, which upstream's
REAL kube-scheduler explicitly PATCHes onto a gated pod's status the moment it
sees the gates (kubescheduler.pkg/scheduler's schedulingQueue does this so
`kubectl describe pod` / clients can distinguish "not ready yet" from a
predicate failure). u7s's scheduler never patches ANY status condition for a
gated pod -- it just silently ignores it (never enters the scheduling cycle at
all, so no code path ever runs for it), so status.conditions stays at whatever
the apiserver's admission left it (no PodScheduled condition at all).

Fix: when needs_scheduling detects non-empty schedulingGates, PATCH the pod's
status.conditions to add {type: PodScheduled, status: False, reason:
SchedulingGated} (mirroring upstream's exact condition shape -- see
v1.PodReasonSchedulingGated). This needs new pod-status-PATCH plumbing in
crates/scheduler/ (there is currently zero pod-status write capability in this
crate -- only Binding POST and pod DELETE). Must be idempotent (gates can be
removed one at a time per predicates.go:833-846, and the condition should be
removed/updated once gates clear) and should not fight with any future
kubelet-written PodScheduled=True condition once the pod actually gets bound.
close_reason:
PR #791: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/791

Fix: crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs adds scheduling_gate_status_patch (sets
PodScheduled=False/reason=SchedulingGated when gates non-empty) and
scheduling_gate_status_reset (clears the stale reason once all gates clear,
deliberately omitting "status" so it can't race bind_pod's True flip), plus
patch_pod_status/http_patch_status PATCH .../status plumbing. Wired into
crates/scheduler/src/main.rs's watch loop. crates/kubeconfig/src/lib.rs gets
HyperApiClient::request_with_content_type (additive) since the status-PATCH
endpoint requires application/strategic-merge-patch+json, not the
application/json request() always sent.

Two pre-existing gaps also blocked this end-to-end for a real ReplicaSet
(found via kubectl-first diagnosis after the scheduler fix alone still
failed sonobuoy): core_gen_adapter.rs's protobuf Pod decoder never read
spec.schedulingGates (kube-controller-manager's RS controller creates pods
via protobuf, silently dropping gates on decode), and patch.rs's
strategic-merge-patch table didn't register spec.schedulingGates (merge key
"name"), so removing one gate via $patch:delete returned 400. Both fixed
in this PR with regression tests. Filed mayor-yhg35 to audit other newer
PodSpec fields for the same two gap categories.

Verification:
- cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2181 passed, 0 failed
- cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean
- sonobuoy --focus 'validates Pods with non-empty schedulingGates are
  blocked on scheduling' PASS (podlogs/sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-cf62ffb3317c436a/logs/e2e.txt):
  "Ran 1 of 7579 Specs in 4.814 seconds / SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed |
  0 Pending | 7578 Skipped / Test Suite Passed"

title: fix(apiserver): kubectl explain on CRD doesn't document standard fields (apiVersion/kind/metadata)
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-uhp54 (CR required-field validation error wording). After
that fix, the upstream conformance test [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI
"works for CRD with validation schema" (test/e2e/apimachinery/crd_publish_openapi.go)
progresses past the required-field-message assertion (line 118-123, now fixed) and fails
at a NEW, later, previously-masked assertion at line 125-127:

  verifyKubectlExplain(..., crd.Crd.Spec.Names.Plural,
    `(?s)DESCRIPTION:.*Foo CRD for Testing.*FIELDS:.*apiVersion.*<string>.*APIVersion defines.*spec.*<Object>.*Specification of Foo`)

Live repro (sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI', lima-node-5, run
temp/e2e/0714-1832-customresourcepublishopenapi):

  kubectl explain <crd-plural> currently returns:

    DESCRIPTION:
        Foo CRD for Testing

    FIELDS:
      spec	<Object>
        Specification of Foo

      status	<Object>
        Status of Foo

  It is missing the standard TypeMeta/ObjectMeta fields (apiVersion, kind, metadata) that
  upstream always injects into a CRD's published OpenAPI schema/explain output, regardless
  of what the CRD author declared in openAPIV3Schema. The e2e assertion requires
  `apiVersion.*<string>.*APIVersion defines` to appear before `spec.*<Object>`.

Root cause is presumably in the CRD-schema-to-explain/discovery-doc rendering path
(crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs and/or discovery.rs — NOT cr.rs, which only handles
CR object validation, not schema publishing for kubectl explain). Not yet root-caused to
a specific line; needs investigation into where the "explain" fields/openapi doc is built
from the CRD's openAPIV3Schema and where standard object metadata should be injected.

Not a regression from mayor-uhp54's fix — cr.rs's validate_cr_schema/error-message-rendering
was the only change in that PR; this is a distinct, pre-existing bug in a different
subsystem (schema publishing, not CR validation) that mayor-uhp54's fix simply unmasked by
letting the test progress further (same "onion" pattern as mayor-bypo8 -> mayor-w1p59 ->
mayor-uhp54).

GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI' -> "works for CRD with validation
schema" passes the full It block end-to-end (all sub-assertions, not just this one).
close_reason: PR #809 opened — kubectl explain <crd> and <crd>.metadata now show apiVersion/kind/metadata via injected TypeMeta/ObjectMeta schema; sonobuoy --focus CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI target test passes (28/29, unrelated flaky failure filed as mayor-zejxr)

title: investigate(apiserver/scheduler): PVC node-affinity test fails at WaitForPodNotPending (predicates.go:929) — pod never leaves Pending
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates shows
"when PVC has node-affinity to non-existent/illegal nodes, the pod should be scheduled
normally if suitable nodes exist" failing at predicates.go:929
(e2epod.WaitForPodNotPending), NOT at the Event-wait line (predicates.go:1102) — this
test doesn't use observeEventAfterAction at all, so it is unrelated to mayor-lafgk's
Event-emission fix.

The test creates a PersistentVolume with node affinity listing the real node PLUS two
non-existent node names (v1.NodeSelectorOpIn with 3 values), a matching PVC, and a pod
mounting that PVC — expecting the pod to still schedule normally onto the one real,
matching node. It then waits up to 5 minutes for the pod to leave Pending; it never
does.

Not yet root-caused in this scout — candidates: (a) the scheduler has no PV/PVC
volume-binding awareness at all (needs_scheduling/pick_node only look at
nodeSelector/priority, never resolve a pod's volumes to a PV's node affinity), so a pod
using a PVC bound to a PV with ANY node affinity might never get scheduled regardless of
whether the affinity is satisfiable; or (b) a kubelet-side volume-mount stall unrelated
to scheduling. Needs its own scout: reproduce with kubectl (create the PV/PVC/pod
manually per predicates.go's e2epv.CreatePVPVC + bindPvPod set-up) and check whether the
scheduler binds the pod at all before investigating kubelet volume mounting.

title: chore(apiserver): CRD/CR LIST ignores ?limit/?continue pagination
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs's CRD/CustomResource LIST handler ignores ?limit/?continue entirely, unlike the built-in resource LIST path (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs + resource.rs/core.rs/csr.rs), which correctly implements signed-continue-token pagination with a pinned resourceVersion per pass (fixed in mayor-l3wu / PR #775). No known failing conformance test currently exercises CR pagination specifically, but any client (kubectl get --chunk-size, or a controller doing paginated CR listing) would silently get the full unpaginated list instead of a real page. Follow the mayor-l3wu pattern (encode_continue/decode_continue in generic.rs) when implementing this for CRs. Discovered while fixing mayor-l3wu; flagged in PR #775 description as a follow-up, not fixed there (different handler file, out of scope for that bead).
close_reason: PR #783 opened (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/783). Wired encode_continue/decode_continue + pinned-resourceVersion machinery from generic.rs into list_cr and list_cr_namespaced (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs), mirroring list_namespaced_resource. Added regression test list_cr_namespaced_paginates_all_items_once_with_stable_resource_version; verified it fails when the fix is reverted. cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2171+81+17+14+70+11 passed, 0 failed. cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings: clean.

title: fix(apiserver): CR required-field validation error message doesn't match upstream wording
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-w1p59 (CRD unknown-field pruning). After that fix, the upstream
conformance test [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI "works for CRD with
validation schema" (test/e2e/apimachinery/crd_publish_openapi.go) progresses past its
line-108/109 unknown-field-pruning assertion (now fixed) and fails at a NEW, later,
previously-masked assertion at line 118-119:

  noRequireCR := `{...,"spec":{"bars":[{"age":"10"}]}}`  // missing required "name"
  if _, err := RunKubectlInput(..., "create", "-f", "-"); err == nil ||
    (!strings.Contains(err.Error(), `missing required field "name"`) &&
     !strings.Contains(err.Error(), `spec.bars[0].name: Required value`)) {
    Failf("unexpected no error when creating CR without required field: %v", err)
  }

Live repro (u7s --stack-only, lima-node-5):
  kubectl create -f - with a CRD requiring `spec.bars[].name`, submitting an item missing
  `name`, currently returns:

    The request is invalid: error when creating "STDIN": CR schema validation failed:
    jsonschema validation failed with file:///.../schema.json#
    - at '/spec/bars/0': missing properties 'name'

  This IS a rejection (422), but the wording doesn't match either upstream substring
  (`missing required field "name"` or `spec.bars[0].name: Required value`), so kubectl's
  error message match fails the conformance assertion even though the CR is correctly
  rejected.

Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs `validate_cr_schema` (~line 441-462) renders
boon's JSON-schema validation errors as raw boon text (`{path}: {boon message}`) rather than
translating the `required` keyword violation into upstream's `field.Path`-style
"<path>: Required value" wording (mirrors what `enum_violation_message` already does for the
`enum` keyword in the same function — a similar depth-first search over the boon error tree
is needed for `ErrorKind::Required`/whatever boon calls it, translating to
"spec.bars[0].name: Required value" or an equivalent "missing required field" phrasing).

Not a regression from mayor-w1p59's PR — validate_cr_schema was untouched by that fix; this
is a distinct, pre-existing bug that mayor-w1p59's fix simply unmasked by letting the test
progress further (same "onion" pattern as mayor-bypo8/PR #738 unmasking mayor-w1p59 itself).

GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI' -> "works for CRD with validation
schema" passes the full It block end-to-end (all sub-assertions, not just this one).
close_reason:
PR #778 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/778

Fix: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs — added required_violation_message() +
instance_location_as_field_path(), mirroring enum_violation_message's DFS pattern over
boon's error tree, translating ErrorKind::Required into "<path>.<field>: Required value".
Wired into validate_cr_schema's error dispatch alongside the existing enum handling.

Verified: cargo test --workspace --quiet -> 2169 passed, 0 failed (all workspace crates
green, including the new regression test
schema_required_violation_in_array_item_uses_upstream_required_value_phrasing which fails
on revert). cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings -> clean.

sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI' (lima-node-5, run
temp/e2e/0714-1832-customresourcepublishopenapi): e2e.txt confirms the
"kubectl validation (kubectl create and apply) rejects request without required
properties" STEP (crd_publish_openapi.go:118-123) now completes without [FAILED] for both
create and apply (previously failed on message wording) -- this bead's exact target
assertion is fixed and verified live.

The It block as a whole is NOT fully green: it progresses to a new, later, unrelated
failure at crd_publish_openapi.go:127 (kubectl explain output missing standard apiVersion
field docs) -- a distinct pre-existing bug in CRD schema/explain publishing
(crd.rs/discovery.rs, not cr.rs), out of scope for this bead's root cause. Filed as
mayor-7qqrd (same onion pattern as mayor-bypo8 -> mayor-w1p59 -> mayor-uhp54 ->
mayor-7qqrd).

title: SchedulerPredicates: scheduler doesn't emit expected scheduling-failure Events (predicates.go:1102 context deadline exceeded)
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-35zvy's fix (namespace-delete cascade race). Once the
"wait for stable cluster" precondition timeout was eliminated, a sonobuoy --focus
"SchedulerPredicates" run (temp/e2e/0714-1724-schedulerpredicates) shows 8 of 13 tests in
this group now reach their real assertion (previously masked entirely by the 10-minute
precondition timeout) and fail there with a NEW, distinct symptom:

  Unexpected error: context deadline exceeded
  In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:1102

predicates.go:1102 is inside WaitForSchedulerAfterAction -> observeEventAfterAction: the
test performs an action expected to fail scheduling (unsatisfiable resource request,
non-matching NodeSelector/NodeAffinity, taints-tolerations mismatch, non-empty
schedulingGates) and then watches for a specific Kubernetes Event (e.g. a FailedScheduling
event) that never arrives within the watch deadline. Affected tests (same run):

  - validates resource limits of pods that are allowed to run [Conformance]
  - validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching [Conformance]
  - validates that NodeAffinity is respected if not matching
  - validates that taints-tolerations is respected if not matching
  - validates local ephemeral storage resource limits of pods that are allowed to run
  - validates Pods with non-empty schedulingGates are blocked on scheduling
  - validates pod overhead is considered along with resource limits ([BeforeEach])
  - when PVC has node-affinity to non-existent/illegal nodes (different failure, predicates.go:929)

Leading hypothesis: our scheduler either does not emit an Event object when it fails to
bind a pod (no FailedScheduling event created), or the event's reason/message string
doesn't match what observeEventAfterAction's predicate expects, or the e2e client's watch
on Events never delivers it (possible overlap with the watch-reliability-under-load
hypothesis being investigated elsewhere, though this reproduced in a short focused run with
no real contention, which argues against pure load-based flakiness).

This is a NEW visibility, not necessarily a new regression -- these tests never reached
this assertion before because they were always blocked by the stable-cluster precondition
timeout (see mayor-35zvy). Needs a scout: reproduce with kubectl (create an unschedulable
pod, `kubectl get events` for a FailedScheduling event), check crates/scheduler for event
emission on bind failure, and confirm whether it's a missing-Event bug vs a watch-delivery
bug before fixing.
close_reason:
PR #777 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/777

Root cause CONFIRMED: crates/scheduler/ never created a Kubernetes Event object on bind
success or failure at all (grepped whole codebase for POST /events or "kind: Event"
creation -- none existed outside generic resource plumbing). Fixed by adding
scheduling_event_payload/scheduling_event_name/events_path/emit_scheduling_event in
crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs and wiring them into main.rs's bind spawn loop: POST
"Scheduled" (Normal) on successful bind, "FailedScheduling" (Warning) when no node fits
even after preemption -- matching upstream's scheduleFailureEvent/scheduleSuccessEvent
predicate shape (test/e2e/scheduling/events.go): name prefixed by pod name, exact
reason/type.

Verified live on a fresh --stack-only stack (lima-node-4): kubectl-created unschedulable
pod -> FailedScheduling (Warning) event now appears; schedulable pod -> Scheduled
(Normal) event with the exact "Successfully assigned ns/pod to node" message upstream's
predicate does strings.Contains on. Before the fix, no event ever appeared for either
case.

cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2168+ tests pass, 0 failed (11 new unit tests added).
cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean.

GATE (honest, partial): sonobuoy --focus 'SchedulerPredicates'
(temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates): 32 ran / 24 passed / 8 failed. The same 8
tests from the bead's original list still fail -- but for reasons CONFIRMED DISTINCT
from the Event-emission gap this PR fixes. Each is a genuine, pre-existing scheduler/
apiserver predicate gap that mayor-35zvy's namespace-delete-race fix simply unmasked
(these tests used to time out earlier on the stale "wait for stable cluster"
precondition, before ever reaching the assertion). Filed follow-on beads per root cause:

- NodeAffinity not enforced at all -> mayor-oei5x
- taints/tolerations not enforced at all -> mayor-2ksh8
- non-empty schedulingGates not respected -> mayor-vkobg
- NodeResourcesFit only checks pod count, not cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage requests
  (kubelet rejects with OutOfcpu/OutOfephemeral-storage instead of the scheduler ever
  seeing it) -> mayor-7duz2 (covers both "resource limits [Conformance]" and "local
  ephemeral storage" tests)
- pod overhead [BeforeEach] fails on an unrelated 409 "Node already exists" patching a
  fake extended resource onto the node -- not a scheduling/event issue -> mayor-wxsrr
- PVC node-affinity to non-existent nodes fails at WaitForPodNotPending
  (predicates.go:929), doesn't even use observeEventAfterAction -> mayor-twn1a
- NodeSelector-not-matching is the one genuinely surprising case: node_selector_matches
  is correct and verified via a clean manual repro right after stack bring-up, but ~10min
  into the real e2e run (after prior tests + a 10-pod resource-saturation burst) the
  identical scenario got bound anyway (scheduler.log shows bind ~2.5ms after detection,
  no preemption fallback logged -- pick_node believed the selector matched on the first
  try). Not root-caused this session; likely a watch-parsing race under sustained load,
  distinct from the already-fixed mayor-sjlw1 and from mayor-et5o -> mayor-qvvba

None of the 8 originally-listed tests fully pass yet -- this PR fixes the Event-emission
mechanism (necessary and confirmed correct in isolation) but is not sufficient on its own
because each of those 8 tests also exercises a separate, still-missing scheduler
predicate. Scope of this scout bead (confirm missing-Event vs wrong-message vs
watch-delivery) is fully discharged: missing-Event was confirmed and fixed; the
remaining failures are out of scope and now tracked individually.

title: NEW(controller): ReplicationController never sets failure condition when pod creation blocked by quota
description:
Run 0714-1535: [sig-apps] ReplicationController "should surface a failure condition on a common issue like exceeded quota" fails (e2e.txt:11567, rc.go:594). Not present in the 0712-2356 baseline's 38 failures — genuinely new to this run, no matching bead found (searched bd for replicationcontroller/failure condition/rc manager keywords).

Test creates a ResourceQuota allowing only 2 pods, then creates an RC asking for more pods than the quota permits, and expects the RC controller to set a failure `ReplicationControllerCondition` on rc.status.conditions describing the quota problem. Error:

  rc manager never added the failure condition for rc "condition-test": []v1.ReplicationControllerCondition(nil)

status.conditions stays nil/empty — our RC controller does not implement this conditions-reporting behavior at all (distinct from mayor-74j3.2, which covers ResourceQuota's OWN status.used field, not RC's condition reporting).

ACCEPTANCE: read test/e2e/apps/rc.go around line 550-594 to confirm the exact condition type/reason/message expected. Implement RC controller logic to set the failure condition when repeated pod-create attempts are rejected by quota (mirrors upstream's ReplicationController "ReplicaFailure" condition). GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should surface a failure condition on a common issue like exceeded quota' passes.

Evidence: ai/findings/0714-1535-run-triage.md (failure #18).
close_reason: PR #776 opened — apiserver bug found+fixed: ResourceQuota admission was check-then-act with no lock spanning the check+write, so concurrent creates (KCM's RC controller batch-creates replicas) raced past the quota. Fixed with a per-namespace Semaphore(1) in AppState held across quota check + store put. sonobuoy --focus PASS: 2 Passed | 0 Failed.

title: core_gen_adapter: protobuf decode emits unrequested hostNetwork: false
description:
Secondary finding from mayor-wx3mn (terminationGracePeriodSeconds storm fix). At crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:1128 (gen_pod_spec_to_json), `if let Some(hn) = spec.host_network { spec_map.insert("hostNetwork", ...) }` emits an explicit "hostNetwork": false in decoded protobuf output even when the source object (e.g. a Deployment created via kubectl apply/JSON) never set hostNetwork at all.

Live evidence (from mayor-wx3mn repro): KCM's own protobuf-encoded ReplicaSet POST decodes to spec.template.spec containing "hostNetwork": false, while the source Deployment's JSON-decoded template has no hostNetwork key at all.

Hypothesis (unverified — needs upstream k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go inspection, not vendored in this repo): PodSpec.HostNetwork is a plain (non-pointer) bool in Go (unlike EnableServiceLinks/AutomountServiceAccountToken which are genuine *bool for tri-state semantics). If so, client-go's protobuf marshaler (gogoproto nullable=false generated code) has no way to represent "unset" and always writes the field, while JSON marshal uses `omitempty` and drops the zero value — meaning "false" and "absent" are indistinguishable at the API-intent level for this specific field, and our decoder should mirror JSON's omit-when-false behavior (like the existing `priority.filter(|&v| v != 0)` and `active_deadline_seconds` `ads > 0` patterns nearby) rather than always emitting Some(false).

Likely NOT a storm driver on its own: HostNetwork is a plain bool (not pointer) on the Go side, so Deployment controller's apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual comparison sees `false == false` regardless of JSON key presence — no nil-vs-pointer mismatch like terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Did not independently reproduce a storm in isolation from the terminationGracePeriodSeconds bug.

Fix candidate (needs confirmation before applying): change line 1128's unconditional Some(hn) emission to filter out `false`, e.g. `spec.host_network.filter(|&v| v)`, so only explicit `true` survives decode — matching upstream JSON's own omitempty semantics for this field.

Cross-ref: mayor-wx3mn (the primary storm bug this was found alongside).
close_reason:
PR #795: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/795

Hypothesis CONFIRMED. HostNetwork is a plain (non-pointer) bool upstream, unlike the
genuine tri-state *bool fields (automountServiceAccountToken, enableServiceLinks).

Verified via:
1. Vendored k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto: proto2 syntax, go-to-protobuf-generated.
   In proto2 every singular scalar field MUST carry an optional/required label, so the
   proto's "optional bool hostNetwork" tells us nothing about upstream Go pointer-ness —
   confirmed by checking the prost-generated Rust struct directly: host_network,
   automount_service_account_token, and enable_service_links are all identically typed
   Option<bool>. The Rust type system cannot distinguish these fields; only behavior can.
2. Doc-comment convention: hostNetwork's proto comment says "Default to false." (fixed
   zero-value default => plain Go bool), while automountServiceAccountToken/
   enableServiceLinks carry no such phrasing (tri-state/inherit semantics) — same
   distinction this file already draws between terminationGracePeriodSeconds (genuine
   *int64, 0 is real intent) and activeDeadlineSeconds (filtered at 0).
3. Live evidence already in hand (from mayor-wx3mn's repro): KCM's protobuf-encoded
   ReplicaSet POST decoded spec.template.spec to "hostNetwork": false even though the
   source Deployment's JSON template had no such key — only explainable if gogoproto's
   marshaler for this non-nullable field unconditionally writes the zero value, i.e.
   Some(false) is indistinguishable from unset at the wire for every real client-go sender.

Fix applied at crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs (gen_pod_spec_to_json,
hostNetwork block): changed `if let Some(hn) = spec.host_network { insert(Bool(hn)) }` to
`if let Some(true) = spec.host_network { insert(Bool(true)) }`, matching the file's own
established idiom (11 other Some(true)-only sites) and upstream JSON's omitempty behavior.
Scoped to this one field only — automountServiceAccountToken/enableServiceLinks untouched.

Added regression test generated_pod_spec_omits_host_network_when_wire_carries_the_zero_value:
encodes host_network=Some(false) -> asserts no hostNetwork key; encodes Some(true) ->
asserts hostNetwork:true. Verified it FAILS on revert (reproduced the panic with the old
Some(hn) code before reapplying the fix).

cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2225 apiserver tests + full workspace, 0 failed.
cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean.

Live Lima VM verification skipped per task guidance (unit test is primary gate for this
