title: investigate: SchedulerPredicates x2 fail stable-cluster precondition -- leftover pods in unrelated namespaces never schedule
description: Run 0712-2356, two conformance failures share an identical symptom: [sig-scheduling] SchedulerPredicates [Serial] validates resource limits of pods that are allowed to run [Conformance] (framework.go:51 / predicates.go:333, 600.7s) and validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching [Conformance] (framework.go:51 / predicates.go:445, 601.2s) BOTH fail with: Timed out after 10m0s waiting for stable cluster, blocked on the SAME list of leftover, never-scheduled pods from UNRELATED namespaces: deployment-1634/test-new-deployment-..., replication-controller-4972/e2e-rc-w2pqx-..., replication-controller-5367/pod-adoption-..., services-1336/externalname-service-.... This is the upstream e2e framework's pre-test wait-for-a-clean-cluster precondition timing out -- neither test ever reaches its actual resource-limits or nodeSelector assertion. The 0707-2254 baseline triage doc grouped SchedulerPredicates with SchedulerPreemption under mayor-kg2s/mayor-rsei, but kg2s and rsei are BOTH scoped narrowly and explicitly to extended-resource (scheduling.k8s.io/foo) preemption accounting -- neither bead's description mentions stable-cluster preconditions or leftover pods from other test namespaces. Treating this as already covered by kg2s/rsei risks it silently never being addressed (their acceptance criteria don't cover it), so filing distinctly. ACCEPTANCE (scout): determine why pods from OTHER test namespaces (deployment/RC/service, not scheduling-preemption related) are still unscheduled/pending by the time these Serial tests run 10+ minutes later -- candidates: general scheduler throughput/backlog under sustained conformance-suite load, a stuck-namespace-cleanup issue, or overlap with mayor-sjlw1's watch-reliability-under-load hypothesis. Rule out simple resource contention on the single-node dev VM before assuming a code bug. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failures #33 and #34).
close_reason: Root cause confirmed: a check-then-act race in namespace-delete cascade (cascade_delete_namespace_resources takes one LIST snapshot before hard-deleting the namespace; a pod created by a concurrent controller after that snapshot but before create_namespaced_resource's Terminating-check would reject it is invisible to the cascade and orphaned forever once the namespace hard-deletes). Fixed with cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable (retry+re-list until stable) in PR #769. Verified via sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates: 'wait for stable cluster' timeout no longer reproduces (temp/e2e/0714-1724-schedulerpredicates). Follow-up filed as mayor-lafgk for a newly-exposed, unrelated scheduler event-emission gap.

title: investigate: ReplicaSet Replace-and-Patch never scales to 3 -- reconcile against stale not-a-bug verdict
description: Run 0712-2356: [sig-apps] ReplicaSet Replace and Patch tests [Conformance] fails (replica_set.go:560, 305.077s). Error: failed to see replicas of test-rs in namespace replicaset-5121 scale to requested amount of 3: timed out waiting for the condition. The ONLY record of prior investigation is a single line in ai/findings/0707-2254-run-triage.md: 'scout aaf96 verdict: NOT-a-bug (upstream-matching patch + test fixture); re-confirm, likely stays'. Searched exhaustively for the reasoning behind that verdict: no bead named aaf96 or mayor-aaf96 exists (bd show returns 'no issue found'), no ai/findings/*.md file mentions aaf96 anywhere else, and bd memories has no matching entry. The verdict is effectively unrecoverable/undocumented. Taken at face value, the CURRENT failure text describes a concrete functional defect (a ReplicaSet never reaching its desired replica count after a replace+patch sequence, timing out after 5 minutes) which is hard to reconcile with a 'not a bug' conclusion. ACCEPTANCE (scout): read test/e2e/apps/replica_set.go's 'Replace and Patch tests' spec to understand exactly what it does (likely: create RS, replace/PUT it, then PATCH replica count to 3), reproduce live, and determine whether this is genuinely a test-fixture/upstream-semantics mismatch (in which case document why and close as wontfix, replacing the lost aaf96 reasoning with a durable one) or a real reconcile bug (in which case rescope as a fix bead). Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #19).
close_reason:
VERDICT: (a) NOT a u7s bug -- upstream test-fixture defect that reproduces identically on real Kubernetes, superseding the lost aaf96 note (new durable reasoning recorded, see bd memory 'replicaset-replace-and-patch-not-a-bug').

Mechanism: testRSLifeCycle (test/e2e/apps/replica_set.go:467-560, release-1.36) creates the RS with its container named "agnhost" (AgnhostImageName), then strategic-merge PATCHes containers with {"name": rsName /* "test-rs" */, "image": rsPatchImage} -- a container-name that does NOT match the existing container. Container lists use patchMergeKey="name", so the mismatched patch item is APPENDED as a second container rather than merged into the first. containers[0] stays "agnhost" with the OLD image forever; containers[1]="test-rs" gets the patched pause image. The test's watch condition requires Containers[0].Image == rsPatchImage, which is permanently unsatisfiable -- hence the 305s timeout at replica_set.go:560, regardless of apiserver implementation.

Live evidence (lima-node-5, u7s stack, kubectl before/after): reproduced create(replicas=1, container "agnhost") -> PUT-replace(replicas=2) -> strategic-merge PATCH(name="test-rs", image=pause:3.10.2, replicas=3) exactly as the test does. `kubectl get rs -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers}'` showed TWO containers post-patch: [{"name":"agnhost","image":".../agnhost:2.53"}, {"name":"test-rs","image":".../pause:3.10.2"}] -- containers[0].image never changed. All 3 pods reached Running/Ready within seconds and status.{replicas,readyReplicas,availableReplicas}=3 converged correctly, proving the u7s RS controller/patch handling itself is correct; only the upstream test assertion is unsatisfiable. Confirmed against the actual conformance run archive too (temp/e2e/0714-1535-conformance e2e.txt:10874): ReadyReplicas=3/AvailableReplicas=3 observed ~2s after the patch, but `found=false` (image mismatch) for the rest of the 305s window.

Overlap note: the same test's log block is full of 'retrywatcher.go:169 Watch failed err=context canceled' spam (also present across ~30 other conformance failures in that run). This is a KNOWN, separately-diagnosed artifact (mayor-7lrp.4): purely client-side noise from watchtools.Until's retry loop after its wait-context is torn down, never reaches the apiserver. Not evidence of a watch-stability bug for this test; no relation to mayor-drjdh's Deployment PUT-replace scale-down bug (that bug is about the KCM's owned-ReplicaSet bookkeeping going stale after a PUT-replace; this test's failure has nothing to do with reconciliation staleness -- it is a pure client-payload/mergeKey mismatch).

No code changed, no PR.

title: fix(apiserver): PodStatus patch-count tracking returns 0 instead of 2 (sig-node Pods lifecycle)
description: Run 0712-2356: [sig-node] Pods should run through the lifecycle of Pods and PodStatus [Conformance] fails (pods.go:1044, 0.78s -- fast, clean assertion mismatch). Error: failed to update PodStatus - field patch count doesn't match the total. Expected <int>: 0 to equal <int>: 2. The test patches pod status and then checks that some patch-count/field-manager-style bookkeeping reflects 2 applied patches; our apiserver reports 0. Possibly related to managedFields/field-manager tracking on the status subresource, or a literal patch-application no-op. FIX: read test/e2e/common/node/pods.go around line 1044 to identify exactly what 'field patch count' checks (likely managedFields entries or a status field), then verify the status PATCH handler actually persists/tracks it. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should run through the lifecycle of Pods and PodStatus' passes. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #32).
close_reason: PR #755 opened - fixed decode_pod_proto_gen dropping .status entirely, root cause of the PodStatus patch-count conformance failure

title: fix(apiserver): Pod response has nil deletionGracePeriodSeconds where int64 expected (sig-node submitted-and-removed)
description: Run 0712-2356: [sig-node] Pods should be submitted and removed [NodeConformance] [Conformance] fails (pods.go:334, 3.6s). Error: Expected <*int64 | 0x0>: nil not to be zero-valued -- a *int64 field the test expects to be populated (non-nil) comes back nil. Given the test name/flow (submit a pod, then delete it), the field is most likely DeletionGracePeriodSeconds on either the delete response or a subsequent GET during termination. FIX: read test/e2e/common/node/pods.go around line 230-334 to confirm exactly which field/response is being asserted, then check the corresponding decode/encode path in the apiserver pod handler for a dropped or never-set pointer field. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should be submitted and removed' passes. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #31).
close_reason: PR #753 opened — root cause was spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds never defaulted (not metadata.deletionGracePeriodSeconds as hypothesized); confirmed against upstream pods.go:334 and fixed in apply_pod_spec_defaults; sonobuoy focus run confirms target conformance test now passes

title: chore(conformance): single-node lima cluster permanently fails 2-node conformance preconditions
description: Run 0712-2356, two conformance failures are explicit, self-evident single-node-topology preconditions, not code bugs: (1) [sig-architecture] Conformance Tests should have at least two untainted nodes [Conformance] (architecture/conformance.go:45, 0.02s): Conformance requires at least two nodes. (2) [sig-apps] Daemon set should rollback without unnecessary restarts [Conformance] (daemon_set.go:451, 0.02s): Conformance test suite needs a cluster with at least 2 nodes. Expected <int>: 1 to be > <int>: 1. Both are immediate, explicit skip-style checks against node count -- the lima-node test cluster genuinely has exactly one node. This matches the 0707-conformance-triage.md (92-failure baseline) CAT-INFRA conclusion ('unfixable on a 1-node lima cluster... exclude from the fixable count') but no bd bead currently documents this decision, so filing one purely for visibility/decision-tracking (not a code fix). ACCEPTANCE: a decision -- either (a) accept these 2 tests as a permanent, documented conformance gap (WONTFIX-ENV), or (b) if there's appetite, add a second lima node to the test topology (infra/tooling change outside crates/apiserver|kubelet|controller-manager, would need its own scoping). No apiserver/kubelet/controller-manager code change is implied by this bead as filed. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failures #15 and #21).
notes: RECONFIRMED 2026-07-16 (conformance run 0715-2142): both documented example failures still present, unchanged, 10 days after this bead was filed -- (1) [sig-architecture] Conformance Tests 'should have at least two untainted nodes' (conformance.go:45, 'Conformance requires at least two nodes', fails in 0.036s); (2) [sig-apps] Daemon set 'should rollback without unnecessary restarts' (daemon_set.go:451, 'Expected 1 to be > 1', fails in 0.048s before any DaemonSet is created). Both are pure single-node-lima topology preconditions -- NOT u7s bugs -- confirmed via live node count on lima-node-4 (exactly 1 node). The daemonset one is DISTINCT from mayor-3z4pr (that is a different DS test, 'should retry creating failed daemon pods', a watch-latency/load race). These 2 are the ONLY infra-gated failures in the run's 17; they cannot pass without adding a 2nd VM node to the lima cluster (WONTFIX-ENV unless multi-node lima is stood up).

title: fix(apiserver): CRD/CR unknown-field pruning inconsistent -- over-rejects and under-prunes
description: Run 0712-2356, two distinct conformance failures both pointing at inconsistent structural-schema pruning of unknown/undeclared fields: (1) [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook should mutate custom resource with pruning [Conformance] (webhook.go:2222, 3.2s): mutating webhook chain runs both stages correctly (mutation-stage-1 and mutation-stage-2 both applied), but an intermediate field that should be pruned by the CRD structural schema survives -- expected map only containing mutation-stage-1+mutation-start, got map also containing mutation-stage-2. (2) [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI works for CRD with validation schema [Conformance] (crd_publish_openapi.go:109, 0.7s): creating a CR with a genuinely unknown field (.spec.foo, not declared in schema) is REJECTED with a strict-decoding error (HTTP 422/exit 1), when the test expects it to succeed via silent pruning of the unknown field. NOTE: this is NOT the enum-format bug that mayor-bypo8/#738 already fixed -- bypo8 was scoped to crd_publish_openapi.go:97-101 (enum rejection message format); this failure is at line 109, a different sub-step (unknown-field pruning), and #738's fix holds (test now progresses further into the same It block and hits this new, previously-masked failure). Opposite-looking symptoms (under-prune in case 1, over-reject in case 2) but both are consistent with a single hypothesis: CRD/CR admission pruning of unknown fields (per structural-schema x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields / pruning semantics) is not applied consistently -- possibly pruning happens before mutating webhooks run instead of being re-applied after (case 1), and/or strict-decode is applied even without ?fieldValidation=Strict on plain create (case 2). Scope as one investigation; may split into 2 fix beads once root-caused. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI|AdmissionWebhook' relevant sub-tests pass. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failures #3 and #9).
close_reason:
PR #773 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/773

Root cause (single, shared): crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs never actually pruned CR
data against the CRD's structural schema -- apply_cr_field_validation only DETECTED unknown
fields for ?fieldValidation= reporting, never removed them. Fix: prune_cr_unknown_fields
(rewritten from walk_cr_unknown_fields) now mutates in place (matching upstream
structuralpruning.PruneWithOptions), applied once at decode (feeding Strict/Warn
detection) and again via prune_cr_for_storage() after mutating+validating webhooks at all
8 CR write paths -- plus corrected the Strict-mode error wording to upstream's exact
`unknown field "<path>"` (was invented ".foo: field not declared in schema").

GATE evidence:

  with pruning' -> isolated re-run: "Ran 1 of 7579 Specs ... SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed"

  targeted CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI "works for CRD with validation schema" sub-test
  progressed from failing at crd_publish_openapi.go:108-109 (unknown-field rejection wording,

  pre-existing, unrelated code path validate_cr_schema) -- filed as mayor-uhp54. Remaining
  failures in this broad-area focus run are pre-existing infra flakiness (dial tcp
  10.96.0.1:443 i/o timeout under parallel load) and a pre-existing [Flaky]-tagged test, none
  are regressions from this change.
- Live kubectl verification on --stack-only lima-node-5: unknown CR field silently pruned
  under fieldValidation=Ignore (previously survived forever); rejected under Strict with
  exact upstream wording `unknown field "spec.foo"`.

title: fix(apiserver): CR PATCH via non-stored CRD version 404s (AdmissionWebhook mutate different-stored-version)
description: Run 0712-2356: [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook should mutate custom resource with different stored version [Conformance] fails (webhook.go:2275, 3.2s -- fast fail, webhook infra is up). Error: failed to patch custom resource cr-instance-1 in namespace webhook-4618: e2e-test-webhook-4618-9194-crd "cr-instance-1" not found (HTTP 404 NotFound). Test creates a CRD with multiple versions (one stored, one not) and a CR, then patches it via a non-stored version, relying on conversion. The 404 suggests our apiserver fails to locate an existing CR when accessed through a non-stored version -- likely a distinct bug from the conversion-webhook-connectivity cluster (mayor-n3yk covers CRDConversionWebhook + FieldSelectors + Aggregator, all of which show 'error sending request' / Deployment-not-Available symptoms, NOT 404s), though thematically both are CRD multi-version handling gaps. FIX: read webhook.go's 'different stored version' test flow and reproduce the PATCH against a non-stored-version CR route; determine whether the storage-version lookup or the conversion path is dropping the object. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should mutate custom resource with different stored version' passes. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #2).
close_reason: PR #750 opened. Root cause confirmed: cr_store_key embedded the CRD's live storage_version into the CR's physical key, so an object written under one storage version became unreachable through any version once the CRD's storage pointer moved. Fixed by making the CR storage key version-independent (group/resource/namespace/name only), matching upstream. Verified via a new regression test (proven red-on-revert against pre-fix code, reproduces the exact reported 404) and a live kubectl repro of the full conformance flow (create via v1, flip CRD storage to v2, patch via v2 -> succeeds, both directions readable post-flip). cargo test --workspace and clippy -D warnings both clean. Could NOT get a sonobuoy --focus PASS line: blocked by a confirmed, deterministic, pre-existing infra defect (konnectivity-agent TLS handshake failure against u7s-ca, reproduced across 2 full VM resets, unrelated to this diff, absent from the 0712-2356 baseline logs) -- filed separately as mayor-ij0es and cross-referenced on mayor-n3yk since it may be n3yk's true root cause.

title: fix(apiserver): AdmissionReview encodes subresource requests as resource=pods/attach instead of resource=pods+subResource=attach
description: Run 0712-2356: [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook should be able to deny attaching pod [Conformance] fails (webhook.go:1481, 5.25s -- fast fail, webhook infra is up and responding). Error: unexpected kubectl attach error message. expected to contain "attaching to pod 'to-be-attached-pod' is not allowed", got "...admission webhook 'deny-attaching-pod.k8s.io' denied the request: expect resource to be {v1 pods}, got {v1 pods/attach}...". The test's webhook asserts AdmissionReview.request.resource == {group:"", version:"v1", resource:"pods"} with the subresource conveyed SEPARATELY via AdmissionReview.request.subResource == "attach", per the upstream admission API contract. Our apiserver appears to combine resource+subresource into a single 'pods/attach' string in the resource field instead of population resource=pods plus a distinct subResource field. This is NOT a Deployment/webhook-availability issue (contradicts the speculative '#1-3 AdmissionWebhook -> n3yk/pod-readiness' grouping in the 0707-2254 triage note -- the webhook clearly received and answered the request). FIX: find where AdmissionReview requests are constructed for subresource operations (attach/exec/proxy/log/etc, likely in the admission webhook dispatch path) and ensure resource is set to the base resource with subResource set separately, matching k8s.io/api/admission/v1 AdmissionRequest semantics. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should be able to deny attaching pod' passes. Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #1).

title: SECURITY(apiserver): pods.rs apply_status_patch has separate metadata-merge not covered by #735 labels-protection
description: Flagged by PR #735 worker (mayor-76w5y). #733+#735 closed the /status metadata-write vector for the generic status handlers + namespace/CRD by protecting labels/spec in merge_incoming_metadata (JSON-Patch + merge/strategic). BUT pods.rs apply_status_patch has its OWN separate, DUPLICATED metadata-merge logic that does NOT call merge_incoming_metadata — so a Pod /status merge-patch may still allow changing metadata.labels (and possibly spec) that the shared guard now blocks elsewhere. VERIFY: can a caller with only pods/status rights change a pod's metadata.labels via a merge-patch to pods/{name}/status? If yes, same authz-boundary class as #733/#735. FIX: route pods.rs apply_status_patch through the shared merge_incoming_metadata guard (dedup — Rule 2), or apply the same labels/spec protection. GATE: a Pod /status merge-patch setting metadata.labels or spec → rejected/ignored; legit pod /status patch works. Test WHY: pods are the highest-volume object; a status-only grant must not mutate pod labels/spec (label changes affect selector/scheduling/service membership). Cross-ref #733/#735, v2hu6/t4zd3/76w5y.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #780 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/780). Before: apply_status_patch in pods.rs had its own metadata-merge that did not protect labels, so a Pod /status merge-patch with metadata.labels landed the change (confirmed via unit test apply_status_patch_does_not_change_labels and HTTP-handler test patch_pod_status_does_not_persist_smuggled_labels, both failed pre-fix with labels={app:evil,escalated:true} persisted). After: routed pods.rs through the shared merge_incoming_metadata guard (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:1897) instead of the duplicated protected-field list; both tests now pass (labels unchanged, legit status.phase update still applies). cargo test --workspace (2171 passed) and cargo clippy -D warnings clean. description: Run 0707-2254 (NEW failure vs baseline 0707-0454): [sig-network] HostPort 'validates that there is no conflict between pods with same hostPort but different hostIP and protocol' — 'Failed to connect to exposed host ports' (hostport.go:164). close_reason: Real, reproducible failure (2/2 sonobuoy --focus runs), but root cause is NOT hostPort/dataplane routing. CRI-O's own nftables hostports implementation correctly disambiguates by (hostIP,protocol,port) and manual repro of the actual hostPort connectivity (127.0.0.1 vs node-IP, TCP vs UDP, same port 54323) succeeds every time. The test's own hostNetwork:true e2e-host-exec pod (used only to exec curl/nc from) hits a PRE-EXISTING u7s apiserver bug — kubelet logs continuous 'Sandbox for pod has changed. Need to start a new one' for any hostNetwork pod, killing/recreating the container ~1/sec forever, so the test's ExecWithOptions calls race a dying/starting container. This matches the already-documented workaround comment in scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh (podIPs strategic-merge-patch accumulation causing kubelet sandbox churn on hostNetwork pods) — it is broader than HostPort (affects any e2e test using a hostNetwork exec pod) and not narrow/self-contained enough to fix within this bead. title: investigate: pods/attach CONNECT webhook denial not surfaced to client (generic upgrade error instead of webhook message)
description: VERIFIED live (scout aa9f7278, 2026-07-06): the pods/attach CONNECT path DOES invoke the validating webhook and it DOES deny (webhook server logged the request) — but kubectl attach shows a generic 'unable to upgrade connection: Request method must be GET' instead of the webhook's denial Status/message. The StatusError from run_validating_webhooks isn't surfaced through the attach handler's WebSocket/SPDY-upgrade response path the way it is for plain REST create/update. Breaks conformance 'deny attaching pod' (asserts the webhook message text). SCOUT to trace proxy.rs attach handler (L339-349 admission call) -> where the StatusError gets swallowed by the upgrade path. MEDIUM. Not a missing-invocation bug (invocation+deny work); it's error-propagation through the connection-upgrade response.
notes:
Root cause pinned + fix implemented, PR opened per mayor instructions (do NOT merge, do NOT close): https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/705

Root cause: client-go's remotecommand executor dials WebSocket(GET) first; treats ANY non-101 response (incl. our correct 403 admission denial) as an upgrade-failure and silently retries via POST(SPDY), discarding the GET attempt's error/message. /attach routed POST to the same pod_attach handler, whose WebSocketUpgrade extractor 405s non-GET methods before admission runs a second time -- so the retry's generic 405 'Request method must be `GET`' masked the webhook's denial. Live-verified before/after on lima-node-2:6445.
close_reason: Merged PR #705 (0e2beabf). Root cause: client-go remotecommand executor dials WebSocket(GET) first; on any non-101 (incl our correct 403 admission denial) it silently retries via POST(SPDY), discarding the GET error — and u7s's /attach POST route mapped to pod_attach whose WebSocketUpgrade extractor rejects POST with a hardcoded 405 BEFORE admission re-runs, so kubectl only saw the generic 405. Fix: new pod_attach_post handler (no WS extractor) reusing resolve_attach_target to run pod-lookup+admission, propagating the Status (501 only if all checks pass); POST route repointed. Live before/after verified: generic 405 -> the webhook's actual denial message. Regression test fail-on-revert. Follow-up: /exec has the identical pattern -> mayor-c7r3 (P2, filed).

title: scheduler has no extended-resource accounting (SchedulerPreemption tests exhaust a fake resource, not pod-count)
description: Found by rsei worker (2026-07-06) reading test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go release-1.36: both target tests ('validates basic preemption works', 'lower priority pod preemption by critical pod') add a FAKE extended resource (scheduling.k8s.io/foo) to the node and create pods REQUESTING it to fill the node — they do NOT rely on pod-count exhaustion. u7s's scheduler (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs) only does pod-COUNT capacity (select_node_with_capacity), zero extended-resource (or CPU/mem) accounting. title: GC orphan race: nil-policy RC delete races with KCM GC informer cache
description: Root-cause: nil-policy RC delete calls orphan_owned_resources (resource.rs:2184) to strip pod ownerRefs, but KCM GC processes pods from its stale informer cache (with old ownerRef) immediately when RC deletion event arrives — before MODIFIED watch events from the strip propagate. Result: GC deletes pods that should survive. Fix: either remove u7s ownerRef-stripping and trust the KCM GC, or ensure stripping happens before the RC delete event is visible (atomic in store). See findings: ai/findings/74j3-namespace-gc-scout-2026-07-05.md
close_reason: Confirmed real, still-live bug via repeated live repro (not fixed by PR #767's watch-ordering fix): KCM's GC controller can cascade-delete a pod within single-digit ms of an orphan RC-delete becoming visible, before its pod-informer catches up on the ownerRef-strip. A post-strip delay mitigation was tried and reverted after live repro showed it makes things WORSE (0/N survival) — keeping the RC alive during the delay lets its own controller spawn a genuine replacement pod that then gets legitimately reaped. Correct fix requires the real k8s finalizer-based orphan protocol; filed as follow-up mayor-74j3.5 (P2) since it is a larger, riskier change than fits this dispatch. No code shipped from this bead — repo left unchanged (reverted to main).

title: close(investigation): Watch failed context canceled is downstream of cyrd EndpointSlice convergence failure
description:
Scout investigation (cyrd3-7lrp3-watch-endpointslice-scout-2026-07-05.md) confirms:

'Watch failed: context canceled' (12762 occurrences in 0705 vs 4950 in 0703) is entirely client-side:
1. e2e binary creates a RetryWatcher to wait for EndpointSlice appearance
2. The watch NEVER reaches the apiserver (zero watch=true requests for namespaced endpointslices confirmed in apiserver.log)
3. Client rate limiter returns context.Canceled because the watch context expires (after wait condition resolves, the context is canceled for cleanup; retries then fail immediately)
4. This cascades for the full test duration (until rate limiter returns context deadline exceeded)

Root cause of test failures: the tests time out because KCM cannot converge EndpointSlice state (mayor-cyrd.4 issue — ring buffer eviction under burst writes). If cyrd.4 is fixed, EndpointSlice reconciliation is faster, tests complete before context deadline, and the retrywatcher errors stop.

No server-side fix needed for 7lrp.3 itself. This bead can be closed when mayor-cyrd.4 is merged and a conformance re-run shows reduced failure count.
notes: CROSS-REF 2026-07-14 (cyrd audit, ai/findings/cyrd-service-discovery-audit-2026-07-14.md): this bead's hypothesis (context-canceled is downstream of the EndpointSlice convergence failure) is now substantiated — mayor-h0lte documents a live-reproduced, PERMANENT EndpointSlice-tracker wedge (not just buffer eviction) that would fully explain a client watch waiting past its deadline. Zero 'context canceled' occurrences observed in kcm.log this session, so this specific symptom string was not independently re-verified server-side; recommend closing 7lrp.4 once mayor-h0lte lands and a conformance re-run confirms this symptom is gone too.
close_reason: Closing condition met: h0lte (PR #793, merged 2026-07-15) fixed the permanent EndpointSlice-tracker wedge this bead's context-canceled noise was downstream of. Two full conformance re-runs since then (0723-1535-conformance and 0723-2104-conformance, both this session) show ZERO EndpointSlice-convergence-timeout failures -- the only appearance of the watch-context-canceled string was as unrelated background noise inside the 0723-2104 GRPC-liveness-probe failure, which mayor-rqyit separately root-caused to an unrelated cause (confirmed flake, no kubelet crate in this codebase) and explicitly ruled out this noise as causal. No evidence of the wedge recurring post-h0lte.

title: fix(store): increase ring/broadcast buffer capacity to reduce EndpointSlice informer lag
description:
Scout findings (cyrd3-7lrp3-watch-endpointslice-scout-2026-07-05.md) show that RING_CAPACITY=1000 and BROADCAST_CAPACITY=2048 are too small under concurrent RS/DS/SS write bursts. When the ring fills faster than KCM's informer receiver drains, EndpointSlice MODIFIED events get evicted from the ring before delivery, forcing a Compacted fallback → full relist → seconds of additional delay → endpointSliceTracker.Has() sees stale cache → 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' (450 occurrences in 0705 run).

Fix: increase RING_CAPACITY from 1000 to 4000 and BROADCAST_CAPACITY from 2048 to 4096 in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs. This is a surgical change to two compile-time constants.

Evidence: 0705 kcm.log shows 450 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date'. apiserver.log:377 shows PUT at 16:03:04, kcm.log shows error at 16:03:05 — 1s after write, before watch event delivered. Lag source traced to broadcast ring eviction under concurrent writes from RS/SS/DS controllers all retrying simultaneously.

Done-when: cargo test --workspace passes; 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' occurrences reduce significantly in a conformance re-run.

Files to change: crates/store/src/sqlite.rs lines 9-10 (RING_CAPACITY and BROADCAST_CAPACITY constants).
notes:
MECHANISM VERIFIED by mayor against source (2026-07-05). Two capacity limits in series in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs: BROADCAST_CAPACITY=2048 (tokio broadcast, line 10) + RING_CAPACITY=1000 (replay ring, line 9). Chain: burst write → slow KCM informer receiver → broadcast RecvError::Lagged drops msgs (line 1022) → watcher re-subscribes → asks for dropped events → ring can't replay (Compacted, line 937, horizon past them) → KCM full relist → seconds lag → endpointSliceTracker.Has() sees stale cache → 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' (450×). CODE ALREADY DOCUMENTS this eviction failure mode (lines 26-29). FIX TRADEOFF (operator decision): scout recommends bumping both 4× (1000→4000, 2048→4096) — LOW RISK (trivial memory: ~4000 Arc ptrs; no correctness change; the Lagged/Compacted recovery paths already exist), but it is TUNING/mitigation not a structural fix for the slow receiver. Structural alt (faster drain / per-watcher backpressure) = much bigger surgery, uncertain payoff. For pre-alpha with bounded conformance bursts, buffer-bump is a reasonable cheap first move — measure via --focus EndpointSlice re-run. RECOMMEND: do cyrd.4 (the bump) first, measure, only pursue structural if it doesn't hold.
DOWNGRADED P3 + likely NOT NEEDED (2026-07-05): the isolation repro (see cyrd.6) REFUTED buffer eviction as the cause of the watch failures — they fail deterministically in 60s on a quiet stack with a single write (zero eviction). The real bug is set-based label-selector parsing (cyrd.6). This buffer-bump may still be a marginal improvement for genuine high-burst cases, but it is NOT the fix for the conformance failures or the wall-clock regression. Do NOT prioritize; revisit only if a real under-load eviction is ever observed AFTER cyrd.6 lands.
close_reason: AUDIT 2026-07-14 (ai/findings/cyrd-service-discovery-audit-2026-07-14.md): confirms the prior 'DOWNGRADED + likely NOT NEEDED' note. Live-reproduced the EndpointSlice tracker wedge in a FULLY ISOLATED, zero-burst scenario (single Service/Deployment, and kube-system/kube-dns wedged 80+ idle minutes with zero writes) — this definitively rules out pure ring/broadcast-buffer eviction under write bursts as the dominant mechanism (RING_CAPACITY=1000/BROADCAST_CAPACITY=2048 are still unchanged in sqlite.rs and were never the bottleneck for these idle/isolated cases). Filed mayor-h0lte as the successor investigation (source-level watch-delivery trace of the actual wedge mechanism). Closing cyrd.4 as superseded by h0lte; the 4x buffer bump this bead proposed remains a cheap, low-risk, independently-testable secondary mitigation worth trying AFTER h0lte's root cause is found and fixed, if any residual burst-eviction contribution remains — but should not be prioritized as a standalone fix.

title: fix(store): TCP_NODELAY on watch-stream connections to reduce controller retry churn
description: The 'not as new as written version' errors (204 in conformance run 0705-1409) occur because KCM's controller checks its informer cache immediately after receiving a PUT response, before the watch event can propagate over TCP (12-50ms window). Enabling TCP_NODELAY on watch-stream HTTP response sockets will eliminate Nagle buffering and reduce the watch-event delivery window from 12-50ms to ~1ms, eliminating most of the retry errors. Root cause from 7lrp scout: sqlite.rs push_event fires synchronously, but TCP socket write is buffered by Nagle. Fix: set TCP_NODELAY on watch response connections. Blast radius: watch stream HTTP response handling only, no store logic changes, no correctness risk.
notes:
2026-07-13: #759 (mayor-tkp2f fix) ALREADY IMPLEMENTED TCP_NODELAY on the apiserver's accepted sockets (crates/apiserver/src/main.rs, helper configure_accepted_socket) — the exact fix this bead proposed. It was applied while chasing the protobuf collision storm; it had ZERO effect on THAT storm (which was a decode-defaults bug, not latency — see protobuf-decode-defaults-break-workload-template-equality), but it IS the latency improvement 7lrp.1 wanted. So the CODE change for 7lrp.1 is likely already on main via #759 — before doing anything here, check main's main.rs for configure_accepted_socket / set_nodelay and DO NOT re-implement it. Remaining 7lrp.1 work (if any): quantify whether it measurably reduced 'not as new as written version' transient counts (the bead's original acceptance metric). May be closeable as done-by-#759 after a measurement.
CROSS-REF 2026-07-14 (cyrd audit, ai/findings/cyrd-service-discovery-audit-2026-07-14.md): mayor-cyrd.5 closed as a likely duplicate of this bead — its cited symptom ('read version N not as new as written N+1 for statefulsets.apps') was re-confirmed still live on current main (same pattern for replicasets.apps, transient/self-healing). Whoever picks this up next should remeasure whether #759/tkp2f's TCP_NODELAY already closed the gap; if not, cyrd.5's per-prefix-bookmark angle may need to be revived.
close_reason: Verified-duplicate: TCP_NODELAY already applied to every accepted connection via configure_accepted_socket (crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:3373-3375), called from the TCP accept loop (line 3389) — covers watch-stream sockets along with everything else, no per-handler distinction needed. Has its own regression test (configure_accepted_socket_enables_tcp_nodelay, line 3496) asserting nodelay is enabled. Landed via an earlier session's fix (referenced as #759/tkp2f in prior dashboard notes) before this session began. Closing with no new PR — confirmed via direct grep, no code change needed.

title: perf(proto): pre-size serde_json::Map with capacity hints in gen adapters

title: perf(proto): replace 440+ .to_string() on static JSON field names in gen adapters
description: From protobuf typegen adapter perf audit (2026-07-05; original worktree beads+doc lost on worktree removal — re-filed from the audit's return summary). HOT path, MED severity, est. 5-10% decode latency, ZERO clarity cost. The gen adapters call .to_string() on ~440 static string literals (JSON field names like "metadata","spec",...) on every decode. These are 'static &str' → use a form that avoids per-call heap alloc (e.g. serde_json Map with &'static str keys where the API allows, or a const/interned approach; verify serde_json::Map key type accepts what's cheapest). Sites: core_gen_adapter.rs:327 + ~440 instances across all *_gen_adapter.rs. Every proto PUT/PATCH (all clients + kubelet) hits this. Suggestion from audit — confirm the exact cheapest idiom before applying; must not hurt clarity.
close_reason: Non-win after investigation: serde_json::Map<String, Value> requires owned String keys. .to_string() and .to_owned() on &str are identical at runtime. The json!() macro also allocates string keys — no interning. There is no cheaper idiom for &'static str keys in serde_json::Map without changing the Map type (which would be a clarity regression). Skipping — audit estimate of 5-10% was not validated.

title: perf(apiserver): reduce watch BOOKMARK delivery latency to cut informer sync lag
description:
Separate from 7lrp (which is about whether the residual transient errors fail conformance). This is a standalone quality/perf improvement to the watch delivery path.

## Context
KCM controllers do read-after-write via ConsistencyStore.EnsureReady(), which reads the informer's in-memory LastStoreSyncResourceVersion. That RV lags the apiserver's committed RV by ~1-2 revisions until the trailing BOOKMARK@rv (emitted at crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:~1020) is processed by the client-go informer goroutine. Under write bursts this produces transient "read version N is not as new as written version M" errors (measured: 32 per burst post-#653, self-resolving in ~15s — see bd memory consistency-7lrp-bookmark-latency + ai/findings/7lrp-wal-stale-read-scout-2026-07-04.md).

The dangerous permanent-loop version of this was already fixed by #653. This bead is ONLY the latency reduction — lower bookmark-delivery latency means fewer transient requeues and faster controller convergence generally (helps conformance run wall-clock, not just this one symptom).

## Approach (scout-recommended Option 2)
Force an explicit HTTP flush after each watch event chunk in the apiserver's watch streaming path, reducing BOOKMARK delivery latency from ~10ms to ~1ms. Touches the watch handler in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs (~970-1020 live-broadcast path) and/or the HTTP watch response writer.

Alternative (KCM-side, not our code): 100-200ms backoff before EnsureReady recheck — rejected as it's upstream KCM, not ours to change cleanly.

## Blast radius / caution
Watch streaming path is exercised by EVERY controller + the sonobuoy smoke path. This is NOT cargo-testable alone — needs VM/sonobuoy verification (inject Lima VM protocol when dispatched). Measure bookmark latency + the "is not as new as written version" count before/after on a fresh stack.

## Acceptance
- Measurable reduction in watch BOOKMARK delivery latency (quantify before/after).
- "is not as new as written version" transient count per apps write-burst drops materially from the 32 baseline.
- No watch-delivery regression (all watch/informer-dependent conformance still green).

## Done-when
Not blocking any conformance test on its own (that's 7lrp's question). This is a perf/quality win; schedule after the protobuf typegen EPIC unless a full run shows the transients still flaking sig-apps tests.

title: harden(patch): strategic-merge $patch:delete on UNREGISTERED arrays is stored literally (Unknown merge-key branch ignores delete directive)
description:
Latent gap surfaced while fixing mayor-7gyy (ownerReferences $patch:delete). In crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs, the strategic-merge Unknown/Replace branch (patch.rs:89-98) only handles $patch:REPLACE (via has_replace_directive); a $patch:DELETE directive on any array whose path is NOT registered in merge_key_for_path falls through to target_obj.insert(key, value.clone()) — i.e. the directive element {$patch:delete, <key>:...} is STORED LITERALLY instead of applied or rejected. $patch:delete is only correctly honored inside strategic_merge_array (patch.rs:160-168), reached ONLY for MergeKeyKind::Key(...) paths.

7gyy fixed the ONE confirmed instance (metadata.ownerReferences, which conformance exercises via RS/RC adopt-release). But ANY other strategic-merge array that a client sends $patch:delete for, and that isn't in the merge-key table, will silently store garbage. This is a correctness footgun.

OPTIONS (operator/mayor to decide scope): (a) In the Unknown/Replace branch, detect a $patch:delete directive and ERROR LOUDLY (return PatchError::InvalidDirective) rather than storing it literally — fail-fast surfaces the missing registration. (b) Audit upstream k8s for all metav1/PodSpec/etc. strategic-merge lists with patchStrategy=merge + patchMergeKey and ensure each is registered in merge_key_for_path (systematic). (c) Both: audit + fail-loud as a backstop. Low priority (P3) — no KNOWN conformance failure beyond ownerReferences (fixed in 7gyy/#671), but it's a real latent bug class. Recommend at least (a) as a cheap guard.

Source: patch.rs:89-98 (Unknown branch), patch.rs:160-168 (where delete IS handled), merge_key_for_path patch.rs:211-269 (the registration table). Related: mayor-7gyy (the ownerReferences instance), #671.

title: node proxy: strip port suffix from node name before store lookup
description:
## Problem

GET /api/v1/nodes/lima-node:10250/proxy/pods returns 404 because resolve_node_proxy_target passes the full "lima-node:10250" string to cluster_object_key, but the node is stored as "lima-node".

Sonobuoy dump.go constructs this URL intentionally (line 153: fmt.Sprintf("%v:%v", node, framework.KubeletPort)), so every failure logs:
  Unable to retrieve kubelet pods for node lima-node: Node "lima-node:10250" not found

## Root Cause

Upstream Kubernetes uses SplitSchemeNamePort() to parse the name parameter before the etcd lookup, extracting bare name vs port. Our resolve_node_proxy_target in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs passes node_name directly to cluster_object_key without stripping the :port suffix.

## Fix

In resolve_node_proxy_target, strip the port suffix with rsplit_once(':') before building the store key. The extracted port can be ignored since state.kubelet_port is already configured correctly for our setup. Upstream also uses the port to override daemonEndpoints if they differ, but that is out of scope here.

## Reference

Upstream: pkg/registry/core/node/strategy.go ResourceLocation() -> utilnet.SplitSchemeNamePort()
Affected handler: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:1038

title: fix(store): SQLite WAL stale read wedges kcm controllers (read version N < written M) — DaemonSet/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet status hangs
description:
The apiserver's SQLite store can return a read that is STALE relative to a just-committed write (the WAL read connection lags the write connection under conformance-level write bursts). Upstream controllers do read-after-write with optimistic concurrency; when the read comes back with an older resourceVersion than they just wrote, they treat it as an error, log "read version: N is not as new as written version: M for group resource X.apps", and stop converging — so the object's .status never reaches the value the conformance test waits on.

CONFIRMED + widespread. Verified via limactl shell lima-node sudo grep /tmp/kcm.log:
- 598 total occurrences of "is not as new as written version" in one run:
    544 replicasets.apps, 40 statefulsets.apps, 13 daemonsets.apps, 1 pods.
- The store code DOCUMENTS this exact failure mode and its mitigation: crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:196-203 ("WAL read connection lagging the write connection ... KCM's RS controller logs 'read version N is not as new as written version M' and requeues in a tight loop for up to 15 minutes"). The stale-read guard (get() ~sqlite.rs:791-806, list() ~820-835) retries via the write connection when obj.revision < last_written_revision — but the guard is NOT fully closing the window under write bursts (a stale read still reached kcm).

WORKED EXAMPLE (namespace daemonsets-8492, reaped at 303s, absent from e2e.log because reaped before Ginkgo timed out):
- Scheduler bound the DS pod (scheduler.log ~09:50:30.335); kubelet ran it to Running/Ready; it never restarted (verified via VM syslog).
- kcm DS controller wrote .status 5x in the first 6.3s (all 200) then went SILENT for ~5min — never published the final numberReady=1/numberAvailable=1/observedGeneration=1 the test waits on.
- Smoking gun at the exact wedge moment (kcm.log):
    E0702 18:50:30.338046 daemon_controller.go:411 "Unhandled Error" err="daemonsets-8492/daemon-set failed with : read version: 3832 is not as new as written version: 3833 for group resource daemonsets.apps"
  (klog local 18:50:30.338046 == 09:50:30.338Z, aligns with the apiserver pod-GET at 09:50:30.338273Z.)

NOTE this is NOT lost writes — the status PUTs return 200 and are persisted; it is a stale READ served after a write, breaking the controller's write->read->write cycle. The DNS namespaces show a sibling symptom in the same family: endpointslice_controller "EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date" and endpoints_controller "resource version mismatch (expected 5469, current 0)".

IMPACT: likely the single largest source of slow/flaky conformance runs (widest blast radius of the three bugs found in this run). Recommend prioritizing over the DNS/Job fixes.

REPRO FOCUS (Go regexp; passed as sonobuoy --e2e-focus). These issue the write->read->write status bursts that trip it. Timing-dependent — may need several runs to observe:
  --focus 'ReplicaSet should validate Replicaset Status endpoints'
  --focus 'StatefulSet.*should validate Statefulset Status endpoints'
  --focus 'Daemon set.*should verify changes to a daemon set status'
Broader net (more reliable to trip, slower):
  --focus 'sig-apps\] (ReplicaSet|StatefulSet|Daemon set)'
Direct (non-sonobuoy) confirmation: watch kcm log during any apps-heavy run for the "is not as new as written version" string:
  limactl shell <VM> sudo grep -c "is not as new as written version" /tmp/kcm.log

ACCEPTANCE:
- Under a conformance write-burst, a read that follows a committed write never returns a lower resourceVersion than the write (the stale-read guard fully closes the window — e.g. serialize reads against the write connection's committed revision, or read from the write connection until the read connection catches up).
- kcm log shows ZERO "is not as new as written version" over a full apps-focus run.
- The three status focus tests pass reliably across repeated runs.

title: fix(admission): webhook timeout propagated as generic string instead of dial error — AdmissionWebhook 'should honor timeout' fails
description:
When an admission webhook exceeds its timeout, the apiserver should return an error that the client can identify as a timeout/dial error. Instead we return the string 'Timeout: request did not complete within requested timeout 1s'. The test expects an HTTP/dial timeout error (i.e. an error that looks like a network-level timeout), not a wrapped Kubernetes Status message.

Repro focus:

title: apiserver/resize: status.resize acknowledgment — most resize specs time out 300s waiting for resize to complete
description: The BULK of resize conformance failures (most of the 53 in the op18 run) are 'Timed out after 300s' — the test resizes a pod, then waits for the kubelet to acknowledge+apply (status.containerStatuses[].allocatedResources/resources reflect new values AND status.resize cleared). INVESTIGATE: what does the kubelet need from u7s to actually apply the cgroup resize + report completion, that u7s isn't providing for these specs? Is status.resize being set/cleared correctly through the lifecycle? Does the kubelet's resize path need the apiserver to accept its status write-back (status subresource carrying allocatedResources)? This is the LARGEST remaining resize gap and likely needs a focused investigation (spike) before a fix — the wjon spike said 'conditional gaps NOT needed' based on 3 passing specs, but the 300s-timeout bulk contradicts that for the broader set. Re-examine. Surface: patch_pod_resize + pod /status handling + possibly the resize state machine.
notes: CLOSURE CORRECTED by mayor: the scout closed this but NO resize-acknowledgment fix shipped -- the DIAGNOSIS changed. The prior wjon-spike was RIGHT: there is no resize-acknowledgment gap (pods that reach Running complete resize correctly, status.resize cleared, allocatedResources/resources written back in 3-5s). title: GC/PDB: disruptedPods cleared by KCM before test read — residual reconcile-race (post #627)
description:
After #627 fixed two REAL u7s PDB bugs (proto status.disruptedPods decode + generation=1 on create), the conformance spec '[sig-apps] DisruptionController should update/patch PodDisruptionBudget status' (disruption.go:187) is STILL FLAKY (verified: 3 runs = PASS/FAIL/FAIL). The remaining failure is a KCM-reconcile race u7s doesn't reproduce the way real k8s does.

VERIFIED CAUSAL CHAIN (from apiserver.log during a failing run):
1. test PUTs status.disruptedPods={pod-0} via the status subresource — WRITE PERSISTS (immediate GET shows it, survives 15s).
2. KCM disruption controller GETs the PDB, sees pod-0 Running (not evicted), and reconciles status.disruptedPods={} (legitimately, per buildDisruptedPodMap which rebuilds from matching pods).
3. test's read-back lands after KCM's reconcile → disruptedPods len:0 → FAIL. When the read beats KCM (timing), it PASSES.

WHY #627's generation=1 fix is INSUFFICIENT: the test's SECOND waitForPdbToBeProcessed (in updatePDBOrDie, AFTER the disruptedPods write) is a no-op because KCM's FIRST reconcile (at create) already set observedGeneration=1, so observedGeneration(1)>=generation(1) is permanently satisfied. The barrier that should make the test wait for KCM to settle after the status write never blocks. Real k8s does NOT bump generation on status updates either — so the mechanism that makes real-k8s's 2nd barrier actually block (and the test deterministic) is UNRESOLVED and is the crux of this bead.

INVESTIGATE (diff against real k8s precisely): why does the test pass reliably upstream? Candidates: (a) does KCM's PDB informer cache get the test's disruptedPods write via WATCH before KCM reconciles, so buildDisruptedPodMap RETAINS the fresh entry (it keeps entries whose deletion deadline hasn't expired) — i.e. is u7s's watch event for the status update delayed/missing/missing-disruptedPods, so KCM's cache rebuilds empty? (b) does real k8s's disruption controller only reconcile on specific triggers u7s over-fires? (c) resourceVersion/observedGeneration semantics that gate KCM's write-back. The earlier scout (worker) leaned toward (a): KCM reads from its informer LISTER (cache), not a live GET, and if u7s's watch hasn't delivered the status-update event to KCM's PDB informer by reconcile time, the cache lacks disruptedPods → rebuilt empty. CONFIRM whether u7s's PDB watch reliably + promptly emits status-subresource updates (incl. disruptedPods) to watchers — that's the most likely real u7s gap.
design: DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED (scout 0701-pdb-disruptedpods-watch-scout.md), watch-emission hypothesis REFUTED. The /status PUT DOES correctly emit a watch MODIFIED carrying disruptedPods (traced status.rs:252 -> store.put -> push_event -> broadcast; no asymmetry vs spec writes). REAL root cause: a reconcile-vs-informer-cache RACE. The test's barrier waitForPdbToBeProcessed (observedGeneration>=generation) is a permanent no-op because generation=1/observedGeneration=1 after KCM's create-reconcile and status writes do NOT bump generation. So after the test writes disruptedPods, nothing makes it wait for KCM to reconcile-post-write; KCM's reconcile (triggered by pod->Running) reads its pdbInformer cache before the cache applies the status-write MODIFIED, buildDisruptedPodMap sees disruptedPods=nil and clears it. e2e timing (0701-2238) confirms the clear happened in the ~2s window. Contributing u7s factor: the global BOOKMARK after every write (sqlite.rs:166-172) may advance KCM's consistency check ahead of the PDB-specific MODIFIED delivery, widening the race vs etcd's ordered delivery. FIX IS NOT OBVIOUS / NEEDS DESIGN DECISION: the scout's Option A (increment generation on PDB /status writes) is REJECTED by mayor — it VIOLATES k8s semantics (generation ticks on spec only), would diverge from upstream and risk other controllers/tests that read generation; it fakes a barrier rather than fixing the race. Option C (fix/suppress the global BOOKMARK so it doesn't advance informer consistency ahead of per-object event delivery) is closer to a REAL cause but the scout says it reduces-not-eliminates the race. The correct fix is a watch-consistency change so u7s's watch delivery/ordering doesn't let KCM's reconcile outrun its own informer cache — a deeper design item, NOT a blind patch. RECOMMEND: human/design decision on the watch-consistency approach before any fix. Do NOT ship generation-faking.
notes: RE-DIAGNOSED 2026-07-02: prior 'superseded by mayor-8phw (OCC)' conclusion was WRONG. With the OCC fix applied, this test STILL fails. VERIFIED root cause is mayor-pxsi: the apiserver proto decoder drops PodDisruptionBudget spec (selector+minAvailable), so KCM's disruption controller matches no pods (expectedPods:0) and buildDisruptedPodMap clears disruptedPods. The reconcile-race / global-bookmark / pod-informer-lag theories in this bead's DESIGN are REFUTED (watch delivery verified correct from source + curl; KCM --v=4 log shows 'No matching PDB for pod'). This bead should close when pxsi lands. Now blocked-by pxsi (not 8phw).
close_reason: Resolved by mayor-pxsi (#644). The symptom tracked here — KCM clearing status.disruptedPods before the test reads it — was caused by the apiserver dropping PodDisruptionBudget.spec on proto-encoded creates: with no spec.selector, the disruption controller matched no pods (expectedPods=0) and buildDisruptedPodMap rebuilt an empty disruptedPods. Once #644 made the apiserver decode spec, KCM matches pod-0 and preserves disruptedPods, and the conformance test passes. The theories in this bead's DESIGN — reconcile-vs-informer-cache race, global-bookmark-on-every-write widening the race, pod-informer lag — were all REFUTED by direct evidence: watch delivery verified correct from source + curl (proper WatchEvent envelopes, correct label filtering); KCM --v=4 showed the controller DID receive pod-0 but couldn't match a selector-less PDB. No watch-consistency change was needed. Closing as fixed (superseded by pxsi).

title: refactor(apiserver): consolidate pod defaulting — apply_pod_create_defaults (pods.rs) + default_pod (defaults.rs) are two paths

- For lead 2: compare the ca.crt bytes in a namespace's kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap against the CA the apiserver actually presents (openssl). If they differ, that's the bug — find where kube-root-ca.crt is populated vs where the serving CA comes from.
- For lead 1: read what RBAC the test's discovery flow needs and whether our escalation check is wrongly denying it.
- Split into precise beads ONCE the real failures are captured. This bead is a holder for the leads so they are not lost.

OPERATIONAL NOTE: this is the 2nd time a worker's e2e.txt was lost because the mayor removed the worktree before extracting the log (1st: the proxy --focus run). Extract/copy e2e results out of the worktree BEFORE git worktree remove.

TWO independent verified root causes, split into: mayor-a31j (RBAC: check_crb/rb_escalation missing the 'escalate' verb bypass — general RBAC gap, generic.rs:511/600) + mayor-p8qh (OIDC endpoints /.well-known/openid-configuration + /openid/v1/jwks not registered — 404). Investigation bead superseded.

title: fix(apiserver): QOS class uses string equality, not Quantity-value equality (1 vs 1000m misclassified)
notes:
Found reviewing PR #600 (mayor-jgwx QOS). compute_qos_class in handlers/pods.rs compares request==limit using raw STRING equality: cpu_req.is_none_or(|r| r == cpu_limit). So a container with requests:{cpu:'1'} and limits:{cpu:'1000m'} (numerically equal) is classified Burstable, when real k8s classifies it Guaranteed. Same for memory ('1Gi' vs '1024Mi', etc.).

Not caught by conformance: node/pods.go:200 uses IDENTICAL request/limit strings, so string equality happens to work and sonobuoy passed 21/21. This is a latent correctness gap for clients using different-but-equal Quantity notations.

Fix: parse both sides as k8s Quantity and compare canonical values before deciding Guaranteed. Check whether a Quantity-parse helper already exists in the codebase (Grep for Quantity parsing — the resource fields are strings like '100m','1Gi'); if not, a minimal milli-cpu / bytes normalizer for cpu+memory suffices (don't pull a dep). Keep it scoped to the QOS comparison.

Acceptance: unit test where requests:{cpu:'1'},limits:{cpu:'1000m'} → Guaranteed (currently Burstable). Low priority — edge case, conformance already green.
close_reason: PR #611 opened: fix(apiserver): QOS class compares resource quantities by value, not string

title: fix(apiserver): prepare_live_event is dead code in bin builds — determine if fan-out should call it or it's test-only
notes:
dead_code warning on every build: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:78 'function prepare_live_event is never used'. Its ONLY call sites are in the #[cfg(test)] module (watch.rs:3156+), so in a non-test bin build it has zero callers.

History: prepare_live_event was extracted in PR #592 (watch fan-out perf — 'once-per-event serialize, selector filtering preserved') as a pure, testable unit. A prior mayor edit (commit 9a8dabcd) changed it from pub(crate) to fn trying to silence the warning — that did NOT fix it (just changed which dead_code variant fires).

INVESTIGATE BEFORE FIXING — two possibilities, very different fixes:
(a) The watch fan-out loop SHOULD call prepare_live_event but doesn't — i.e. #592's extraction was left half-wired and the production path still does inline parse/serialize per-watcher (a latent PERF REGRESSION, the thing #592 set out to fix). If so, wire the fan-out to call prepare_live_event and the warning disappears because it's now used. This is the important case.
(b) It is genuinely only a test helper / was always meant to be test-scoped. If so, annotate #[cfg(test)] (or move it into the test module) so it's not compiled into the bin.

Determine which by reading the watch fan-out send loop (Grep the live-event send path in watch.rs) and comparing what it does vs what prepare_live_event does. If the loop already does the once-per-event serialize inline, then prepare_live_event duplicates it → case (b) + consider deduping. If the loop does per-watcher re-serialization, then #592 is incomplete → case (a), wire it up.

Acceptance: zero dead_code warnings on a plain , AND a one-line note in the PR stating which case it was. If case (a), include before/after of the fan-out path. Cargo-testable (the existing tests at watch.rs:3144+ already cover prepare_live_event's behavior).
close_reason: PR #604 opened — case (b): annotated #[cfg(test)], zero warnings confirmed

title: fix(proto): decode lastTransitionTime in metav1.Condition (Time message, field 4)
notes:
Follow-on from mayor-ujet / PR #597. The Service status proto decoder (decode_service_proto, ServiceStatus->MetaV1Condition) skips field 4 lastTransitionTime because it's a metav1.Time message and we have no Timestamp proto struct. Consequence: a protobuf UpdateStatus that sets a condition persists it WITHOUT lastTransitionTime. The service-status-lifecycle conformance test does not check this field (predicate is type/reason/message only), so it PASSES — but lastTransitionTime is required on metav1.Condition in the real API and other tests/clients may depend on it round-tripping.

Scope: this is broader than one field — metav1.Time appears across many types (managedFields, conditions on Deployment/ReplicaSet/Node/etc.). A proper fix adds a Timestamp/Time proto struct (seconds int64 field 1, nanos int32 field 2) and wires it into condition decoders generally, not just Service. Low priority until a conformance test actually asserts on lastTransitionTime. Pattern to follow: the existing skipped-Time-field policy in other decoders (e.g. CSINode, the pod decoders).
close_reason: PR #599 opened: fix(proto): decode lastTransitionTime in metav1.Condition

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:1315

title: main: EndpointSlice reconciler store.put with None revision generates spurious watch events
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:2146: store.put(&ep_key, ..., None).await passes None as expected revision, meaning every reconciler cycle unconditionally overwrites the Endpoints object even when no change is needed. This generates spurious watch events every 5 seconds, causing all informers watching Endpoints to resync unnecessarily.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:2146

## Done-when
Reconciler reads the stored revision and uses it as the expected revision in put(), or skips the put entirely when the computed target already matches the stored value.
close_reason: store.put now passes stored revision for optimistic concurrency; skips write when already in sync. PR #551.

title: admission: single & and | silently dropped by CEL tokenizer, enabling policy bypass
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:1481-1490: a lone & or | in a CEL expression is silently skipped (no token emitted, no error). A matchCondition expression like 'a & b' tokenizes to ['a', 'b'] — only 'a' is evaluated, 'b' is never reached. An expression ending with '& always_true' evaluates only 'always_true' rather than the intended conjunction.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:1481-1490

## Done-when
Single & and single | emit an Unknown/Error token that causes tokenize_cel() to return None (parse failure), reported as an invalid CEL expression rather than silently discarded.
close_reason: tokenize_cel returns None on lone & or |; 5 regression tests including webhook creation rejection. PR #553.

title: main: EndpointSlice reconciler tokio task has no shutdown signal or backoff
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:268-275 spawns an infinite loop: loop { reconcile_kubernetes_endpointslice().await; sleep(5s).await; }. There is no shutdown channel, no JoinHandle saved, and no exponential backoff on store errors. The task runs indefinitely and cannot be cleanly stopped during graceful shutdown.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:268-275

## Done-when
Task receives a tokio::sync::watch shutdown signal and exits when it fires; persistent store errors trigger exponential backoff rather than fixed 5-second retry.
close_reason: tokio::select! on watch shutdown channel; exponential backoff 5s→300s on errors. PR #551.

title: fix(apiserver): Event firstTimestamp/lastTimestamp/eventTime are zero (0001-01-01) instead of real times
description:
Events are stored and retrievable, but their timestamps are the zero value. In conformance dump output every event prints 'At 0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC - event for ...' (temp/e2e/midway-e2e-job-0a8054fc.log lines 121-124). Real events carry firstTimestamp/lastTimestamp (core/v1 Event) or eventTime (events.k8s.io/v1). Our apiserver appears to drop or never populate these on Event create/round-trip.

IMPACT: kubectl describe and 'kubectl get events' sort/display by timestamp; zero timestamps make event ordering and 'LAST SEEN' columns useless, and break clients that reason about event recency. Lower severity than progress/admission bugs but a real conformance/usability gap.

WHERE TO LOOK: Event create handler + proto/json round-trip for core/v1 Event (firstTimestamp, lastTimestamp) and events.k8s.io/v1 Event (eventTime, series). Check whether the apiserver should default these on CREATE when absent (kube-apiserver does default metadata.creationTimestamp; event timestamps are set by the reporting client, but if the client sets them we must round-trip them — verify which is happening here by capturing a real Event create body).

DONE-WHEN: an Event created with firstTimestamp/lastTimestamp (or eventTime) round-trips those values on GET; 'kubectl get events' shows non-zero LAST SEEN. Regression test asserting the timestamp fields survive create+get (and proto round-trip if that is the drop point).
close_reason: Event timestamps normalized for events.k8s.io/v1 group. PR: #547.

title: fix(scripts): sonobuoy progress stall detector — kill and collect partial results when suite makes no progress
description:
## Problem

If the namespace TTL watchdog (mayor-352r) itself fails to unblock a stuck test (e.g. kubectl delete hangs because the apiserver is completely unresponsive), the entire sonobuoy run can still stall indefinitely. We need a second independent kill switch that operates at the sonobuoy level.

## What to implement

A second background watchdog inside 06-run-sonobuoy.sh that polls sonobuoy's progress and kills the run if no tests complete for 15 minutes.

### Logic (runs every 60s, from inside the VM via limactl shell)

Poll: limactl shell $VM_NAME sudo sonobuoy status --json --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig

Track the sum: result-counts.passed + result-counts.failed (NOT progress.completed — that field was 0 at suite completion in our observations; result-counts is the reliable monotonic counter).

If this sum has not increased in 15 minutes:
1. Log the stall to stdout with timestamp.
2. Kill sonobuoy: limactl shell $VM_NAME sudo sonobuoy delete --all --wait --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig
3. Fall through to the result retrieval section — partial results will be collected.

The 15-minute threshold means: even if the namespace watchdog fires and a stuck spec takes its full 10-minute TTL, this detector does not fire during normal per-spec hangs. It only fires when something is globally wrong.

### Lifecycle

- Start after sonobuoy run begins (not immediately — skip the first 30s while sonobuoy initialises).
- Guard against sonobuoy not yet running: skip iterations where status returns no valid JSON or no plugins array.
- Kill on EXIT trap alongside the namespace watchdog.

### Important: verify sonobuoy status works as expected

Before relying on result-counts, verify during an actual run that the field increments as tests complete. We confirmed result-counts is present in the JSON schema (sonobuoy status --json works against our cluster) but have not observed it incrementing live. The worker should run a focused sonobuoy test and watch the field increment.

## Files to change

scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh only.

## Dependency

Implement after mayor-352r (namespace TTL watchdog) is merged — both modify 06-run-sonobuoy.sh and should not race.

## Acceptance criteria

- If result-counts[passed+failed] does not increase for 15 minutes, sonobuoy is killed and partial results retrieved
- Normal runs are unaffected
- Stall events are logged to stdout with timestamp
- Worker provides evidence of sonobuoy status --json working with incrementing result-counts during a live focused run
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(store): reduce continue token TTL from 5min to 60s
description:
## Problem

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs — CONTINUE_TOKEN_TTL_SECS constant

## Fix
Reduce to 60 seconds. Update the TTL expiry test to use a token age that crosses the new boundary.

## Done when
- CONTINUE_TOKEN_TTL_SECS = 60
- Existing expiry regression test still passes (it uses iat=0 which is always expired)
- cargo test passes

title: release clusterIP sentinel on delete_collection for Services
description: PR #243 wired clusterIP release on delete_namespaced_resource and delete_resource, but delete_collection_namespaced_resource does not release IPs. title: refactor(state): generify AppState over S: Store to enable mock store in handler tests
description:
AppState currently holds Arc<SqliteStore> concretely, making it impossible to inject a mock store in handler unit tests. This blocks deterministic OCC testing at the handler layer (status.rs, cr.rs, resource.rs all have untested wiring between handler logic and store.put's CAS).

Refactor AppState to be generic over S: Store with SqliteStore as the default:

  pub struct AppState<S = SqliteStore> {
      pub store: Arc<S>,
      ...
  }

All handler signatures become State<AppState<S>> with where S: Store bounds. Production code continues to use AppState (= AppState<SqliteStore>) unchanged. Tests can use AppState<MockStore> where MockStore is a thin test-only struct defined inline in the test module that wraps SqliteStore(:memory:) and can be configured to inject StoreError::RevisionMismatch on a specific put call.

Scope:
- crates/apiserver/src/state.rs: add S generic param with default
- crates/apiserver/src/main.rs: no change needed (uses AppState directly, default kicks in)
- All handler files that reference AppState in State<AppState> extractor: add S generic + where S: Store bound
- Add a minimal MockStore in a test module (no new file — define inside status.rs tests or a shared test helper mod)
- Add deterministic OCC tests for put_resource_status and put_namespaced_resource_status using MockStore

The Store trait uses impl Future return types (not object-safe), so Arc<dyn Store> is not viable without async-trait. The generic approach is the right fit.

Success criteria:
1. cargo build --workspace succeeds
2. cargo test --workspace passes
3. Two new deterministic OCC tests exist for put_resource_status and put_namespaced_resource_status that inject RevisionMismatch via MockStore and assert 409 Conflict
4. No behavior change in production paths
design: Option A (generify AppState<S: Store>) chosen over Option B (Arc<dyn Store>) because Store uses impl Future returns which are not object-safe, and over Option C (callback hook) because it is principled and future-proof. MockStore lives in test code only — no new production crate dep.
close_reason: Merged PR #236 — AppState<S = SqliteStore> generic over Store trait, all 14 handler files + auth/stream/admission updated, MockStore + 2 OCC tests in status.rs, 1072 tests pass. Note: compaction_horizon() added to Store trait as implementation side-effect of MockStore completeness.

title: security audit: MED/LOW cluster — information disclosure, DoS surface, crypto hardening
description:
MED/LOW findings from paranoid security audit (May 2026):

**MED-1: SA JWT audience validation allows only default audience**
File: auth.rs:265-266
The JWT audience is hardcoded to https://kubernetes.default.svc. If a token specifies a different audience (as the TokenRequest API allows via spec.audiences), the auth layer will reject it even though the token is valid. More importantly, there is no mechanism to restrict tokens to specific audiences — all tokens work against all endpoints.

**MED-2: GET /api/v1/{resource} catch-all matches list verb, not get**
File: auth.rs:301 + main.rs:226-229
The method_to_verb mapping maps GET to 'get', but Kubernetes differentiates between 'get' (named resource) and 'list' (collection). A user with 'get' permission on pods but not 'list' can list pods by hitting the collection endpoint because the RBAC check uses verb='get'. This is an authorization bypass for the list verb.

**MED-3: RBAC index not updated atomically on write**
File: rbac.rs:86-117, handlers/generic.rs
When a ClusterRole or ClusterRoleBinding is written via the generic handler, apply_object() is called after the store write succeeds. There is a window between the store write and the RBAC index update where the old policy is still active. Under concurrent writes, this can lead to briefly stale authorization decisions.

**MED-4: expiration_seconds in TokenRequest is uncapped**
File: handlers/tokens.rs:37
A user can set spec.expirationSeconds to u64::MAX (18446744073709551615), creating a token that effectively never expires. Kubernetes limits this to 48 hours. The mint path at line 127 computes exp = now + spec.expiration_seconds, which would overflow on very large values (though u64 arithmetic wraps, the resulting exp would be in the distant past, causing immediate rejection — so this is more a correctness issue than a security one).

**LOW-1: No rate limiting on authentication failures**
An attacker can brute-force static bearer tokens at the speed of network I/O. The inflight limiter (50 concurrent) provides some protection, but token validation is fast (HashMap lookup), so a single connection can try thousands of tokens per second.

**LOW-2: Error messages leak internal key format**
File: store/lib.rs:71, status responses
StoreError::NotFound includes the full internal store key (e.g., /registry/pods/default/nginx). This leaks the internal key structure to clients, which could be useful for constructing path traversal attacks.

**LOW-3: No label/annotation size limits**
Labels and annotations parsed from protobuf or JSON bodies have no size limits. A client can set a single annotation to a multi-megabyte string, consuming disproportionate storage and memory.

**LOW-4: Broadcast channel lag yields approximate compaction horizon**
File: store/lib.rs:721-726
When a watch receiver lags behind the broadcast channel, the Compacted event uses the lag count (n) as the horizon instead of the actual compaction_horizon. This is approximate and could cause clients to relist from the wrong revision.

**LOW-5: HTTP/1.1 only, no HTTP/2**
File: main.rs:548
The server uses hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder, meaning only HTTP/1.1 is served. While not a direct security issue, HTTP/2 multiplexing reduces the number of TCP connections needed and provides better DoS resilience.

**LOW-6: TLS cipher suite selection delegated to rustls defaults**
File: tls.rs:283-285
ServerConfig::builder() uses default cipher suites and protocol versions from rustls. While rustls defaults are generally good (no TLS 1.0/1.1, no weak ciphers), the configuration is not explicitly pinned. A future rustls version could change defaults.

**LOW-7: Kubeconfig written with default file permissions**
File: tls.rs:372
The kubeconfig file (containing client cert and key) is written with default permissions, making it potentially world-readable.

title: Full typed protobuf serialization: generate/write Rust proto bindings for core Kubernetes API types
description:
## Goal

Replace the Unknown-envelope-with-JSON shortcut with proper typed protobuf serialization for core Kubernetes API types. This achieves full wire-format compatibility with client-go's proto path and is required for maximum performance (proto is ~2x smaller and faster to decode than JSON).

## Background

The Kubernetes protobuf format uses per-type generated serializers. Each API type (Namespace, Pod, Node, Service, etc.) has a `.proto` definition in the kubernetes/kubernetes repo under `k8s.io/api/{group}/{version}/generated.proto`. The real kube-apiserver uses code-generated `Marshal()`/`Unmarshal()` for each type.

The Unknown-envelope-with-JSON shortcut (current approach) works for CRDs and is spec-compliant — clients are supposed to check `contentType` in the Unknown envelope. However, some kubectl versions may not honour it, which is the root cause of the current wireType 6 bug (mayor-lsu/mayor-cux).

## Scope

Phase 1 — core/v1 types only (required for kubelet + kubectl compat):
- Namespace, Pod, Node, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, ServiceAccount
- Event, Endpoints
- PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim (for storage compat)

Phase 2 — extended (for Argo CD + controller compat):
- apps/v1: Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, DaemonSet
- rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1: ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Role, RoleBinding
- apiextensions.k8s.io/v1: CustomResourceDefinition

## Approach options

**Option A** — Use `prost` crate with Kubernetes proto files:
- Copy `.proto` files from kubernetes/kubernetes into the repo
- Use `prost-build` to generate Rust structs
- Write conversion functions `serde_json::Value → proto struct → bytes`
- Pro: auto-generated, low maintenance. Con: conversion layer is non-trivial, proto files are large.

**Option B** — Hand-write proto serializers for each type:
- Similar to the current `encode_proto_response` but per-type
- Pro: full control, no build deps. Con: ~500 LoC per type × 15 types = significant.

**Option C** — Extend the Unknown envelope shortcut correctly:
- Keep Unknown envelope but ensure contentType is respected by testing against the exact client-go version used in CI
- If client-go truly ignores contentType, file a bug upstream
- Pro: 10x less work. Con: may not achieve full compat.

## Recommendation

Option A (prost) if Option C proves insufficient. Do not start until mayor-oayj (serializer abstraction) is merged and the current wireType 6 bug is resolved — that resolution will clarify whether Option C is viable.

## Blocked by

- mayor-oayj (serializer abstraction — prerequisite)
- Resolution of mayor-lsu (wireType 6 bug — determines if Option C is viable)

## Important finding (2026-05-21)

client-go's RawSerializer (used for write response decoding) bypasses the contentType field in the Unknown envelope entirely. It always tries to decode field 2 (raw) as a typed proto message. The Unknown+JSON shortcut is therefore NOT viable for write responses.

For GET responses (kubelet reads), the contentType path may still work — kubelet uses a different decode path. Monitor kubelet smoke tests after PR #84 merges to confirm GET proto still works.

If GET proto also needs to be real typed proto, mayor-pgdr becomes P1.
